children.translated_text: Now, if it is argued that here the capacity to produce aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) is grounded in the distinctiveness of the word's own form, and therefore it constitutes a figure of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) -- then what exactly is the distinctiveness in the word's own form? Is it repetition (<s>paunaruktya</s>), or the property of expressing a repeated meaning, or the quality of being punned upon (<s>śliṣṭatva</s>) through words that are both split and unsplit (<s>sabhaṅgābhaṅga</s>)? In this regard, the first option does not hold, because there is no actual double utterance of the word, and hence such a character does not appear. Nor does the second option hold, because the relationship of expressed and expression is the relationship of ornament, and the relationship of substrate and superstratum does not obtain there. For this very reason, it has been said that since all meaning-figures (<s>arthālaṅkāras</s>) involve words expressing compared meanings etc., the word would have the status of being their figure. Nor does the third option hold, because the term '<s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s>' (semblance of repetition) is adopted as an etymologically meaningful designation; because the figure has been introduced through the causation of the property called repetition; and because the quality of being punned upon is irrelevant here. Rather, here the meaning-repetition serves merely as the occasion for apprehension. And the relation of occasion and occasioned does not constitute a basis for figurative status -- this is undisputed. Therefore, since repetition is meaning-based, its status as a figure of that [meaning] is proper. Thus, the status of being a speaker's ornament (<s>vaktralaṅkāra</s>) is also refuted, because all [figures] have the nature of excellences (<s>atiśaya</s>), and such a status is tenable for all.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 3d:]

children.text:
vistarabhayāditi /
na tu citratvābhāvāt /
nocyanta iti /
vastutastu saṃbhavantyevetyarthaḥ /
ataścāyaṃ prāyo vākyārthapadārthāśrayatvātprathamaṃ dvidhābhavan samastāsamastapadatvena caturvidhaḥ /

children.translated_text: In order, for example:
"The snow-mountain, renowned everywhere for the falling of your heat,

children.text: himavānavatu sadā vo viśvatra samāgataḥ khyātim' //
children.translated_text: May <s>Himavān</s> always protect you, having attained fame universally."

'Due to fear of prolixity' -- but not because of the absence of figurative character (<s>citratva</s>). 'Are not mentioned' -- but in reality they do indeed exist, that is the meaning. And therefore, this [figure], being primarily based on sentence-meaning and word-meaning, first becomes twofold, and then through the distinction of compound and non-compound words, becomes fourfold.

children.text: 'nadīprakaramulliṅgitavantaṃ manoharahastamatyajantaṃ ca, saparyāṇāṃ ruciṃ vahantaṃ rasarvatra pūjanīyaṃ ca,sakubhbhaṃ sakalaśañcarantaṃ ca, sadānadantaṃ madaparyāviladaśanaṃ ca, karaṭaṃ kamapi bibhrataṃ kavāṭavibhramamuñcantaṃ ca, kuñjarājivardhitaruci vāraṇaraṇaraṇaraṇikākulitaṃ ca, rājamānavisaṃdhāyinaṃ virājamānaṃ ca, śārībhūtaṃ madasalilena śabalībhūtaṃ ca, iti punaruktāśrayam' ityanaṅgalekhāyāṃ hastivarṇane /
children.translated_text: "One who embraces the assemblage of rivers, who has a captivating hand and does not let go, who carries the beauty of worship, who is to be honored everywhere; who has a hump and a pot and moves about, who is always generous with a face wet with rut-fluid; who bears some kind of temple-protuberance and releases the play of door-panels; whose beauty is enhanced by a row of elephants, agitated by the sound of elephant-battle; who destroys the agreements of proud [enemies] and shines resplendent; who is embodied in rut-fluid and mottled thereby" -- thus, based on repetition, in the description of an elephant in the <s>Anaṅgalekhā</s>.
"Alas! Cruel time, dark [in nature], the luminaries of the cow-protector (<s>Govibhāva</s>),
Will cast away the sides of this one who is finished, and will not make radiant the glory of the other king."
The non-compound word [type] has been illustrated by the author himself.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 4:
Verbal repetition (<s>śabdapaunaruktya</s>) is repetition of consonants alone, and repetition of the combination of vowels and consonants. [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 4]

children.text: alaṃkāraprastāve kevalaṃ svarapaunaruktyamacārutvānna gaṇyate iti dvaividhyameva /
children.translated_text: In the context of figures of speech, repetition of vowels alone is not counted because of its lack of beauty, hence only the twofold [division is made].
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 4:]
For example:
"In the <s>indīvara</s> (blue lotus), in the <s>inda</s> (Indra/moon), in the <s>indālama</s>, in the troop of <s>indī</s>,
In the <s>indidira</s>, in the <s>indama</s>, the ascetic is of like intention."
Anticipating the question 'why is repetition of vowels alone not counted?', he says 'in the context of figures' etc.

('In the <s>indāvara</s>...' --------) Here, because of the absence of beauty in vowel-repetition, it does not constitute a figure. Among these, he defines the pair of figures based on consonants alone and on vowel-consonant [combination] -- 'by number' etc.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 5:
<s>Chekānuprāsa</s> (clever alliteration) is [defined as having] a restriction on number, [and comes] first. [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 5]

children.text:
dvayorvyañjanasamudāyayoḥ parasparamanaikadhā sādṛśyaṃ saṃkhyāniyamaḥ /
pūrvaṃ vyañjamasamudāyāśritaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: The mutual non-singular similarity of two consonant-groups is the restriction on number. First, as based on consonant-groups, for example:

children.text: 'kiṃ nāma dardura duradhyavasāya sāyaṃ kāyaṃ nipīḍya ninadaṃ kuruṣe ruṣeva /
children.translated_text: "O frog, why, with dull resolve, do you press your body at evening and croak as if in anger?

children.text: etāni kelirasitāni sitacchadānāmākarṇya kārṇamadhurāṇi na lajjito 'si' //
children.translated_text: Having heard these playful laughter-sounds of the white-winged [geese], sweet to the ear, are you not ashamed?"

children.text:
atra sāyaṃśabdenāsyālaṅkārasya yakāramātrasādṛśyāpekṣayā vṛttyanuprāsena sahaikābhidhānalakṣaṇaḥ saṃkaraḥ /
chekā vidagdhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, due to the <s>sāyam</s> word's similarity of only the <s>ya</s>-consonant with this figure, there is a mixture (<s>saṃkara</s>) characterized by single designation with <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (flowing alliteration). '<s>Chekā</s>' means the clever ones (<s>vidagdhāḥ</s>).
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 5:]

children.text:
ekavacanasya jātyā bahutvaprasaṅgādvahuvacanasya ca tryādīnāṃ svayameva bahutvātsaṃkhyāniyamo dvitva eva saṃbhavatīti dvayorityuktam /
dvayorapyekadhā sādṛśyaṃ vṛttyanuprāsa evetyāśaṅkyāha-anekadheti /
yakāramātretyanena dvayoreva sādṛśyamasya jīvitamiti dhvanitam /
yadyapi cāyaṃ vyañjanamātrapaunaruktyākhyasya sāmānyalakṣaṇasya saṃbhavādanuprāsa evānyairantarbhāvitaḥ tathāpyasya granthakṛtā udbhaṭamatānurodhādiha lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtam -anyathetyādi /
children.translated_text: Since the singular, being generic, occasions plurality, and since the plural itself implies a multitude of three or more, the restriction on number is possible only as duality -- hence 'of two' is stated. Anticipating the objection that even a single similarity between two [groups] would just be <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s>, he says 'in more than one way.' By 'only the <s>ya</s>-consonant,' it is implied that the similarity of exactly two [elements] is the life of this [figure]. And although this [figure], due to being subsumed under the general definition called 'consonant-repetition,' has been included within <s>anuprāsa</s> itself by others, nevertheless the author has formulated its definition here following the view of <s>Udbhaṭa</s> -- 'otherwise' etc.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 6:
<s>Vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (flowing alliteration) is otherwise [i.e., when the conditions for <s>chekānuprāsa</s> are not met]. [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 6]

children.text:
kevalavyañjanamātrasādṛśyamekadhā samudāyasādṛśyaṃ tryādīnāṃ ca parasparasādṛśyamānyathābhāvaḥ /
vṛttistu rasaviṣayo vyāpāraḥ /
tadvatī punarvarṇaracanehavṛttiḥ /
sa ca paruṣakomalamadhyamavarṇārabdhatvāttridhā /
tadupalakṣito 'yamanuprāsaḥ /
yathā-
children.translated_text: Similarity of consonants alone in one way, similarity of groups, and the mutual similarity of three or more -- this is the 'otherwise' condition. <s>Vṛtti</s> (style), however, is the activity pertaining to <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). That which possesses it -- here the arrangement of phonemes -- is called <s>vṛtti</s>. And since it is composed of harsh, soft, and moderate phonemes, it is threefold. This <s>anuprāsa</s> is characterized by that [<s>vṛtti</s>]. For example:

children.text: 'āṭopena paṭīyayasā yadapi sā vāṇī kaverāmukhe khelantī prathame tathāpi kurute no sanmanorañjanam /
children.translated_text: "Even though the poet's speech, playing with great force and vigor, first dances upon his face, it does not produce true delight of the mind.
Not until the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), resounding with the buzzing of ornaments of rich and beautiful qualities, flows in the stream of abundant, flowing <s>rasa</s>-essence."

children.text:
yathā vā-
'sahyāḥ pannagaphūtkṛtānalaśikhā nārācapālyo 'pi vā rākendoḥ kiraṇā viṣadravamuco varṣāsu vā vāyavaḥ /
na tvetāḥ saralāḥ sitāsitarucaḥ sācīkṛtāḥ sālasāḥ sākūtāḥ samadāḥ kuraṅgakadṛśāṃ mānānuvidhdā dṛśaḥ' //
children.translated_text: Or for example: "The flames of serpents' hissing fires, or volleys of arrows, are bearable; the rays of the full moon, or the winds of the rainy season that release streams of poison, [are bearable]; but not these -- the straightforward, light-and-dark-hued, sidelong-glancing, languid, purposeful, intoxicated gazes of the doe-eyed women, animated by the passion of love."
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 6:]

children.text:
etadeva bhedanirdeśaṃ kurvanvyācaṣṭe kevaletyādi /
samudāyaḥ pāriśeṣyād vyañjanadvayarūpaḥ /
ekadheti cātraiva saṃbaddhavyam /
kevalasya tryādīnāṃ cānekadhāpi sādṛśyasyānena vyātpatvāt /
evañca samastāsamastākṣaratvena saṃbhavatītyasya prāyaḥ ṣaṭ prakārāḥ /

children.translated_text: In order, for example:

children.text: 'yayā yayāyyayā yūyaṃ yo yo yaṃ yeyayāyayā /
children.translated_text: "<s>Yayā yayāyyayā yūyaṃ yo yo yaṃ yeyayāyayā</s>,
<s>Yayuyāyi yayeyāya yayeyāyāya yāyayuk</s>."

Expounding the very specification of types, he explains: 'consonants alone' etc. 'Group,' by elimination, consists of two consonants. And 'in one way' should be connected here itself, because this [<s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s>] encompasses even the manifold similarity of single consonants and of three or more. Thus, being possible through compound and non-compound syllables, this has approximately six varieties.
The non-compound syllable [type] has been illustrated by the author himself.
"He gave gifts to the wretched, day by day he resounded;
He censured the joys of the delightful, [being] the one who makes delightful ones rejoice."
"With abundant, cherished, plucked-from-treetop, delightful [offerings],
And with long-lasting, beautiful, brilliant rays -- the mind has long been astonished."
"Then, in the bright fortnight of the <s>Soma</s> month, ever esteemed by the virtuous,
That virtuous woman of supreme intellect, free from darkness, gave birth to a son."
"The lotus-eyed one's body, pure, soft as a lotus, and beautifully radiant,
How much does the lotus adorn -- even one fallen from a lotus, if he is pure!"
For example:
"May the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, praised by <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) and other deities, grant

children.text: sadā sadvasatiṃ devaḥ savitā vitatāṃ satām' //
children.translated_text: Always a good abode to the virtuous, with extended [blessings]."
By the word 'ādi' (etc.), groups of four or more syllables are also included.
As it has been stated:
"That <s>vṛtti</s> (style) which is combined with <s>śa</s>, <s>ṣa</s>, <s>repha</s>-conjuncts, and the <s>ṭa</s>-class,
Is called <s>paruṣā</s> (harsh); and also when combined with <s>hla</s>, <s>hva</s>, <s>hya</s>, etc."
'The arrangement of phonemes here is <s>vṛtti</s> (style)' -- this is said figuratively. 'Threefold' --
"That [<s>vṛtti</s>] combined with identical conjuncts, cerebral-class consonants, and final-position
<s>sparśa</s> (stop consonants) -- the learned consider it <s>upanāgarikā</s> (urbane/moderate)."
"The <s>vṛtti</s> composed of the remaining phonemes, as appropriate, known as <s>komalā</s> (soft),
Is praised as a rustic style by those of refined understanding in poetic works."
<s>Udbhaṭa</s>, <s>Kāvyālaṃkārasaṃgraha</s> 9.14-16
For example:
"These elephants, with terrifying gullet-throats gushing forth unrestrained, striking thunderclaps with <s>ḍiṇḍima</s> drums resounding,
With swarms of bees restless from sipping the rut-fluid, their flanks' interiors scarred at every moment of maturation -- [such are] the elephants!"
Here, by the repetition of <s>la</s>-consonant etc., there is the moderate [style] -- thus the threefold division of <s>vṛtti</s>.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 6a:]

children.text: evaṃ vyañjanamātrāśrayamalaṅkāradvayaṃ lakṣayitvā svaravyañjanāśrayaṃ yamakaṃ lakṣayati-svaretyādi /
children.translated_text: Having thus defined the pair of figures based on consonants alone, he defines <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming repetition), which is based on vowels and consonants -- 'with vowels' etc.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 7:
<s>Yamaka</s> (constrained repetition) is the repetition of the combination of vowels and consonants. [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 7]

children.text:
atra kvacidbhinnārthatvaṃ kvicidabhinnārthatvaṃ kacidekasyānarthakatvamaparasya sārthakatvamiti saṃkṣepataḥ prakāratrayam /
yathā-
children.translated_text: Here, in some cases there is difference of meaning, in some cases identity of meaning, and in some cases one [occurrence] is meaningless while the other is meaningful -- thus, in brief, there are three varieties. For example:
"Whoever beholds her lovely eyes -- [like] a forest-lotus (<s>vanajā</s>),
For him, in his other eyes, charm (<s>ruci</s>) alone does not arise."
This is the case of meaningfulness. The rest should be understood similarly.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 7:]

children.text:
ekasyetyādyupalakṣaṇaparam /
ato bahunāṃ yamakānāṃ kvacitsārthakatvaṃ nirarthakatvaṃ ca sthitaṃ saṃgṛhītameva /
'kvacitsārthakatvaṃ kvacinnirarthakatvam'iti tu pāṭhe prathamameva bhedadvayamuktaṃ syānna tṛtīyaḥ prakāraḥ /
ataśca bhedanirdeśagrantho yathāsthita eva jyāyān /
saṃkṣepata iti /
evañca kāvyātmabhūtarasacarvaṇāpratyūhakāritvātprapañcayituṃ yogyamiti cirantanālaṅkāravanna vibhajya lakṣitamiti bhāvaḥ /
evaṃ citre 'pi jñeyam /
anyaditi /
prakāradvayam /

children.translated_text: Among these, the meaningless [type], for example:
"With the lake full of blooming lotuses, with the beauty of bees and waters, in spring, the <s>nalinī</s> (lotus-pond),
Resembling the deity of the ocean, he bore <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), with the radiance of clearly manifested <s>rāga</s> (color/passion)."

'Of one' etc. is meant as illustrative (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). Therefore, the fact that in many <s>yamakas</s> there is sometimes meaningfulness and sometimes meaninglessness is already included. But in the reading 'sometimes meaningful, sometimes meaningless,' the first two types would have been stated, but not the third variety. Therefore, the text of the specification of types as it stands is preferable. 'In brief' -- and thus, since it does not obstruct the savoring of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), which is the soul of poetry, it is worthy of elaboration; hence, like the ancient figures, it has been defined without further subdivision -- this is the implication. The same should be understood regarding <s>citra</s> (pictorial verse) as well. 'Other' means the [remaining] two varieties.
The case of meaninglessness combined with meaningfulness, for example:
"With ornaments, with persistence, with provision -- [give] to the ascetics the good provision;
With progeny, with progeny, with progeny -- [destroy] the lineage of delusion!"
Here, '<s>tarāga</s>' etc. is meaningless.
Here, '<s>sajjasāhāram</s>' is meaningless.
But the others are meaningful -- hence there is no defect.

children.text:
idaṃ ca sthānaniyamamantareṇa na bhavati /
yaduktam-'padamanekārthamakṣaraṃ cāvṛttaṃ sthānaniyame yamakam' iti /
ata eva sthānaniyamādyamakamityasyānvarthamabhidhānam /
sa ca sthānaniyamo vaivakṣiko na vāstavaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:
"Conquering the bees that are vanquished, [pleasing] the minds of proud women defeated by love, fragrant with the beauty of flowers,
The world bore <s>Śrī</s> (splendor), having prevented the overflow of lotuses, with coppery hue and coppery forests resplendent."

And this [<s>yamaka</s>] does not occur without positional restriction. As it has been said: '<s>Yamaka</s> is a word of multiple meanings or a syllable repeated with positional restriction.' For this very reason, since <s>yamaka</s> has positional restriction, its name is etymologically apt. And that positional restriction is conventional, not absolute.
Or for example:

children.text: 'chindyādbhayārtiṃ tava kārtikeyaḥ śaśī jito yena sa kārtike yaḥ /
children.translated_text: "May <s>Kārtikeya</s>, by whom the moon was conquered, destroy your fear and affliction -- he who [shines] in the month of <s>Kārtika</s>;

children.text: utkhātadanto gaṇanāyakasya svāmī yadanyo gaṇanāya kasya' //
children.translated_text: The master of <s>Gaṇanāyaka</s> (Gaṇeśa), whose tusk was uprooted -- who else is there for [such] counting?"
Here, because the <s>yamaka</s> arrangement occurs in pairs of syllables, the position is fixed.

children.text: atra cārthadvaye yamakadvayamiti sthānaniyamo dvidhaiveti nāsyālaṅkārasya kṣatiḥ kācit /

children.translated_text: And therefore:
"<s>Śru tarasikalarukatarasikalitarujālaharijalahariṇatamaḥ</s>,
<s>Hariṇatamaśca tatastava tatastavaḥ syādyaśorāśiḥ</s> -- may your mass of glory be thus!"
Here, since there are two <s>yamaka</s>-pairs in two meanings, the positional restriction is only twofold -- hence there is no detriment to this figure.

Here, even though there is repetition of the combination of vowels and consonants, due to the absence of positional restriction, this is a semblance of <s>yamaka</s> (<s>yamakābhāsa</s>), [and is actually] <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (flowing alliteration).
START <s>Sūtra</s> 8:
"When the repetition of word and meaning is well-established (<s>praruḍha</s>), it is a defect (<s>doṣa</s>)." [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 8]

children.text:
praruḍhagrahaṇaṃ vakṣyamāṇaprabhedavailakṣaṇyārtham /
yadāhuḥ-'śabdārthayoḥ punarvacanaṃ punaruktamanyatrānuvādāt' /
iti /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>praruḍha</s>' (well-established) is used to distinguish from the varieties to be discussed later. As they have said: 'The repetition of word and meaning is <s>punarnukta</s> (redundancy), except in the case of <s>anuvāda</s> (restatement).'
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 8:]
For example:
"Born in that lineage, of pure intellect, the purest of all,
<s>Dilīpa</s>, the moon among kings -- like the moon in the ocean of milk."
'<s>Praruḍha</s>' (well-established) -- such an appearance is [what constitutes] cessation [of aesthetic pleasure].

children.text:
atrenduriti /
atrinetrakṣīrodajanmatvādindordvitvānnaitatpraruḍhamiti na kāryam, kavisamaye tathātvasyāpratīteḥ /
āhurityākṣapādāḥ /
antatrānuvāditi /
anuvāde hi śabdārthayoḥ punarvacanaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ na doṣāya /
akriyamāṇaṃ punardeṣāya bhavatīti bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example —
'The sun rises red and sets red likewise;
In fortune and misfortune, the great ones maintain a single form.'

Here [the verse begins] 'the moon' (<s>indu</s>). Since the moon is born from the ocean of milk which is the eye of <s>Atri</s>, the duality of the moon does not make this a fully established [figure] — this objection should not be raised, because in poetic convention (<s>kavisamaya</s>) such a state is not recognized. [The author] says 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) — [this is the view of] the <s>Ākṣapādas</s> (Naiyāyikas). 'Here it is a restatement' (<s>anuvāda</s>) — for in a restatement, the repetition of word and meaning is not a fault. However, not making [such repetition] would indeed be a fault — this is the purport.
Here, [the repetition is of] the word 'red' (<s>rakta</s>).
'From heaven [falls] the head of <s>Śarva</s> (Śiva), from <s>Paśupati's</s> head to the mountain, from the lofty mountain to the earth, and from the earth also to the ocean;

children.text: adhodho gaṅgāvadūyamupagatā nūnamathavā vivekabhraṣṭānāṃ bhavati vinipātaḥ śatamukhaḥ' //
children.translated_text: Lower and lower the <s>Gaṅgā</s> has descended — surely, the fall of those who have lost discrimination (<s>viveka</s>) is manifold.'

Here, even though there is repetition of meaning, the non-repetition of the word generates a different cognition, [hence] it is a fault. That itself is not a fully established ornament — [the author] states this with 'the purport' (<s>tātparya</s>) and so forth.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 9-10:
'But when there is a difference of purport (<s>tātparya</s>), it is <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s> (Lāṭa-type alliteration).' // <s>RuAss</s>_9 //
For example —

children.text: 'tālā jaanti guṇā jālā de sahiaehiṃ gheppanti /
children.translated_text: 'Then qualities are born, then they are grasped by the sensitive ones;
Favored by the rays of the sun, lotuses [bloom into] lotuses.'
<s>Tātparya</s> (purport) means being directed toward something else (<s>anyaparatva</s>). It is the purport itself that is differentiated, not the form of the word and meaning.
['Then qualities are born, when they are grasped by the sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>) ones;
Favored by the rays of the sun, lotuses [become] lotuses.']

children.text: 'brūmaḥ kiyannaya kathañcana kālamalpam atrābjapatranayane nayane nimīlya /
children.translated_text: 'We say — somehow closing your lotus-petal eyes for just a short while,
O young woman, know that this golden lotus, having been seized by that passion, I, the enemy of the gods, have come.'
In this and similar cases, even though there is no repetition of case-endings and the like, because there is extensive repetition of both word and meaning, it is indeed <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s>.
'The <s>kāśa</s> grasses appear like <s>kāśa</s> grasses, and the lakes appear like lakes;
They captivated the minds of the young — the submerged ones appeared like submerged ones.'
In cases like this, there is no intermixture (<s>saṃkara</s>) with <s>Ananvaya</s> (self-comparison), which is characterized by a single denotation;
because they have distinct domains — [<s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s>] being based on both word and meaning in mutual dependence, while [<s>Ananvaya</s>] is based on meaning alone.
'In <s>Ananvaya</s>, the identity of words is incidental due to propriety;
But in this <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s>, [word-identity] is directly the motivating factor.'
Thus, there are five ornaments based on repetition (<s>paunaruktya</s>). // <s>RuAss</s>_10 //
This has been explained through direct exposition (<s>nigadavyākhyāta</s>).
<s>RuAssC</s>_9-10:

children.text:
anyaparatvamiti /
ekasya vācyaviśrāntatve 'nyasya lakṣye vyaṅgye vārthevācyaviśrāntirityarthaḥ /
bhidyata iti paryavasāne /
āmukhe hi śabdavadarthasyāpyekatvenaivāvabhāsaḥ /
ata evāha-na śabdārthasvarūpamiti /
evaṃ ca nāyaṃ dvayorvācyaviśrāntatve 'nuvādamātramalaṅkāraḥ /
nahi doṣābhāvamātramalaṅkārasvarūpam /
evaṃ hi satprapaśabdādyabhāvasyāpyalaṅkāratvaprasaṅgaḥ /
yatparamādāvuktaṃ tatparameva punarnocyate ityeva sāmānyena yadyanyaparatvamucyate tadvirodhādivat 'udeti raktiḥ savitā-' ityādau doṣābhāvamātratvepyalaṅkāratvocitasyānyaparatvākhyasyātiśayasyāpi bhāvālaṅkāratvaprasaṅgaḥ /
na caitāvataiva kaścidatiśayapratīyate iti yathoktameva yuktam /
ekaḥ kamalaśabdo vācyaparyavasitaḥ anyaśca saurabhabandhuratvādyanekadharmaniṣṭha iti tātparyabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Directed toward something else' (<s>anyaparatva</s>) means: when one [word or meaning] rests in the expressed sense (<s>vācya</s>), the other rests in the suggested (<s>lakṣya</s>) or implied (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) meaning — this is the sense. 'Is differentiated' means at the conclusion. For at the outset, the meaning, like the word, appears as one only. Therefore [the author] says 'not the form of word and meaning.' And thus, when both rest in the expressed sense, this is mere restatement and not an ornament. For the mere absence of a fault is not the nature of an ornament. For if it were so, even the absence of filler words like <s>pra</s>, <s>pa</s>, etc., would absurdly qualify as an ornament. If <s>anyaparatva</s> (being directed toward another meaning) is stated generally as 'what is stated first is simply not stated again in the same way,' then as with <s>virodha</s> (contradiction) and the like, in 'the sun rises red' and similar cases, even when there is merely an absence of fault, there would absurdly follow the status of ornament for the surplus called <s>anyaparatva</s> which deserves ornament-status. And since no surplus is cognized by that alone, what was stated [by the author] is correct. One <s>kamala</s>-word rests in the expressed meaning, while the other is grounded in multiple properties such as fragrance and beauty — this is the difference of purport (<s>tātparyabheda</s>).
<s>RuAssC</s>_9-10a:

children.text:
brumaḥ kiyaditi /
atra abjaśabdasyāpyapaunaruktyāt lāṭānuprāsatvameveti cintyam /
atra hi dvayorapi nayanaśabdayorvācyaviśrantatvādanyaparatvābhāvānnāsti tātparyabhedaḥ /
sa eva hyasya jīvitam /
anyathā hyanuprāsamātratvaṃ syānnālaṅkāratvam /
athāpi kevalanayanaśabdasyasvārthaviśrāntiḥ saṃsargapadāntargatastaya punaḥ svārthamupasarjanīkṛtya saṃjñinamabhigadhamaśca svārthatyāgātparārtheca vṛttirastyeva lakṣyaniṣ ṭatvamiti cet, naitat /
lakṣaṇāsāmagradhabhāvāt /
atra hyanyapadārthapradhānatvānnayanaśabdasya guṇībhāvaḥ, na mukhyārthabādhaḥ /
svārtha eva viśrānteḥ /
na ca guṇībhāvamukhyārthabādhayorkatvam /
sato hi mukhyārthasya kañcidapekṣya guṇībhāvaḥ /
bādhaḥ punaḥ svasminnevāviśrāntirityanayārmahān bhedaḥ /
nāpyatra kiñcitprayojanaṃ na vā ruḍhiriyamityetatpaunaruktyamātram /

children.translated_text: Similarly —
'Radiant with the beauty of the rays of the white-rayed moon, the splendor of the moon-like mountain-lord is your fame;
The <s>Pauṣa</s>-month lotus — that <s>Kamalā</s> (Lakṣmī) too belongs to you alone and to no other.'

'We say, how much' (<s>brūmaḥ kiyat</s>) — here, since there is also non-repetition of the word <s>abja</s> (lotus), one should consider whether it is indeed <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s>. For here, since both <s>nayana</s>-words (eye-words) rest in the expressed sense, due to the absence of <s>anyaparatva</s>, there is no difference of purport. That alone is its life-force. Otherwise, it would be mere <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) and not an ornament. Now, if [one argues that] the <s>nayana</s>-word alone rests in its own meaning, while being included within a compound word, it again subordinates its own meaning and directly denotes the qualifier, and since through abandoning its own meaning it functions for another's meaning, there is indeed the status of being grounded in the suggested sense — [the reply is]: this is not so, because the conditions for secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) are not fulfilled. For here, due to the predominance of another word's meaning, the <s>nayana</s>-word becomes subordinate — there is no obstruction of the primary meaning, since [the word] rests in its own meaning alone. And subordination and obstruction of primary meaning are not identical. For the subordination of an existing primary meaning is relative to something [else]; but obstruction is non-resting in itself — herein lies the great difference. Nor is there here any purpose [for secondary meaning], nor is this a conventional usage — hence this is mere repetition.

children.text:
ityādāvapi ghajñeyam /
camatkārastvatrānuprāsakṛto 'vaseyaḥ /
nanvananvaye 'pi śabdapaunaruktyaṃ dṛśyata iti tatrāpi kimayamevālaṅkāraḥ kimu sa evetyāśaṅkyaha-ananvaya ityādi /
ānuṣaṅgikamiti /
na punaḥ sākṣātprayojakamityarthaḥ /
śabdaikyaṃ vināpyananvayasya pratipādanāt /
atra hi śabdaikyaṃ kvacidakriyamāṇamanaucityamāvahati kvacinneti bhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: An example of that —

children.text: 'yaccakṣurjagatāṃ sahastrakaravaddhāmnāṃ ca dhāmārkava- nmonnadvāramapāvṛttaṃ ca ravivad dhvāntāntakṛt sūryavat /
children.translated_text: 'That which is the eye of the worlds, the abode of splendors like the thousand-rayed [sun], the open and unclosed door of the lofty, the destroyer of darkness like the sun, like <s>Ravi</s>,

children.text: ātmā sarvaśarīriṇāṃ savitṛvat tigmāṃśuvat kālakṛt sādhvīṃ naḥ sa giraḥ dadātu dinakṛd yonyairatulyopamaḥ' //
children.translated_text: The self of all embodied beings, like <s>Savitṛ</s>, the maker of time like the one of fierce rays — may that sun (<s>Dinakṛt</s>) grant us auspicious words, [he who is] incomparably [compared] with others.'

In this and similar cases, this [principle] should be understood. However, the aesthetic delight (<s>camatkāra</s>) here is to be attributed to <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration). Now, since word-repetition is also seen in <s>Ananvaya</s>, one might doubt whether this itself is the ornament or whether that [<s>Ananvaya</s>] alone is — anticipating this, [the author] says '<s>Ananvaya</s>' and so forth. 'Incidental' (<s>ānuṣaṅgika</s>) means: not directly the motivating factor — this is the meaning. Because <s>Ananvaya</s> can be conveyed even without word-identity. For here, word-identity sometimes, when not employed, brings impropriety, and sometimes does not — this is the purport.

children.text: atra sahastrakarādayo 'nya ivābhāsamānā ananvayapratītiṃ vighnayantīti śabdaikyābhāvo 'naucityamāvahati, na punarananvayasyābhāvam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'thousand-rayed' and other [synonyms], appearing as if different, obstruct the cognition of <s>Ananvaya</s> — thus the absence of word-identity brings impropriety, but not the absence of <s>Ananvaya</s> itself.

'The earth due to [its] stability, the sky due to [its] pervasiveness, the wind due to being the life-breath of all beings, the sun due to illuminating the universe, and the moon (<s>sudhāsūti</s>) simultaneously due to [its] delighting,

children.text: vahniḥ saṃhārakatvājjalamakhilajanāpyāyanāccopamānaṃ satyātmatve 'pi yasya prabhavatu bhavatāṃ so 'ṣṭamūrtiḥ śivāya' //
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> (fire) due to [its] power of destruction, water due to nourishing all people — [all these are] objects of comparison for one whose essential nature is truth; may that <s>Aṣṭamūrti</s> (eight-formed) <s>Śiva</s> be for your welfare.'

children.text:
atra nirvighnamevānanvayasya pratīteḥ śabdaikyabhāvo nānaicityāvahaḥ /
tuśabdo vyatireke /
śākṣāditi /
śabdaikyaṃ vināsyānutthānāt /
etadevopasaṃharati-tadevamityādi /
puna ruktavadābhāsamarthapaunaruktyāśritaṃ,chekānuprāsādayastrayaḥ śabdapaunaruktyāśrayāḥ /
lāṭānuprāsastūbhayāśritaṃ iti pañca paunaruktyāśritā alaṅkārāḥ /
yadyapyukteḥ śabdārthagatatvenoccaraṇābhidhānatayā bhedāt sāmānyābhāvāt kasya pañcaprakāratvaṃ tathāpi tasyā dvayorapyanugamādekatvena pratīteruktisāmānyanibandhanameva prakāriprakārabhāvavacanam /
yaccārthabhedena śabdasyāpi bhinnatvaṃ tadavāstavam /
pratītāvekatayaivāvabhāsāt /
ata evānekārthavargādiṣvapi tathātvenaiva vyavahāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since <s>Ananvaya</s> is cognized without obstruction, the absence of word-identity does not bring impropriety. The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) indicates contrast. 'Directly' (<s>sākṣāt</s>) means: because [<s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s>] cannot arise without word-identity. [The author] concludes with 'thus' (<s>tadevaṃ</s>) and so forth. <s>Punaruktavadābhāsa</s> is based on repetition of meaning; <s>Chekānuprāsa</s> and the other three are based on repetition of words; <s>Lāṭānuprāsa</s> is based on both — thus five ornaments are based on repetition. Although, since <s>ukti</s> (expression) pertains to both word and meaning through utterance and denotation, and due to [their] difference there is no generality, [one may ask] — of what are there five varieties? Nevertheless, since <s>ukti</s> pervades both and is cognized as one, the statement of the type-subtype relationship is grounded in the generality of <s>ukti</s>. And the claim that the word too becomes different through difference of meaning is unfounded, because in cognition it appears as one only. Hence, even in lexicons of multiple meanings and the like, the convention operates precisely in that manner.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 11:
When letters form the shape of a sword and the like, it is <s>Citra</s> (pictorial verse). // <s>RuAss</s>_11 //

children.text:
paunaruktakyaprastāve sthānaviśeṣaśliṣṭavarṇapaunaruktyātmakaṃ citravacanam /
yadyapi lipyakṣarāṇāṃ khaṅgādisaṃniveśaviśiṣṭatvaṃ tathāpi śrotrākāśasamavetavarṇātmakaśabdābhedena teṣāṃ loke pratītervācakaśabdālaṅkāro 'yam /
ādiprahaṇād yathāvyutpattisaṃbhavaṃ padmabandhādiparigrahaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example —
'<s>Bhāsate pratibhāsāra rasābhātā hatāvibhā</s>,
<s>bhāvitātmāśubhāvāde devābhā bata sabhā</s>.'

In the context of repetition, this is a statement about <s>Citra</s> (pictorial verse), which consists of repetition of letters fitted to specific positions. Although the written characters (<s>lipyakṣara</s>) possess the distinctive arrangement of sword-shapes and the like, nevertheless, since in common usage they are cognized as identical with the sound-letters (<s>varṇa</s>) which are present in auditory space (<s>śrotrākāśa</s>), this is an ornament of the signifying word (<s>vācakaśabdālaṅkāra</s>). By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), [the author] includes lotus-pattern (<s>padmabandha</s>) and similar [figures], as far as etymological possibility allows.

children.text:
eṣo 'ṣṭadalapadmabanadhaḥ /
atra digdaleṣu nirgamapraveśābhyāṃ śliṣṭākṣaratvam /
vivigdaleṣu tvanyathā /
karṇikākṣaraṃ tu śliṣṭameva /
children.translated_text: This is an eight-petaled lotus pattern (<s>aṣṭadalapadmabandha</s>). Here, in the directional petals, the letters are connected through entry and exit. In the intermediate petals, however, [the connection is] different. The central letter (<s>karṇikākṣara</s>) is connected throughout.
<s>RuAssC</s>_11:

children.text:
varṇānāmityādi /
uccāraṇakāle sthānaviśeṣaśliṣṭavarṇātmakakhaṅgadisaṃniveśasyā bhāvātponaruktyapratītirnātreti kimāśrayo 'yamalaṅkāra ityāśaṅkyāha-yadyapītyādi /
lipyakṣarāṇāṃ maṣībindurūpāṇāṃ śrūyamāṇatāsatattvavarṇaśabdābhedapratipattyā aupacāriko 'yaṃ śabdālaṅkāra iti tātparyārthaḥ /
ādigrahaṇaṃ saphalayituṃ padmabandhenodāharati-bhāsatetyādi /

children.translated_text: Now, a sword-pattern (<s>khaṅgabandha</s>) as an example —
'He shall become a vessel for the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of liberation, he whose essence is [devoted to] existence (<s>bhava</s>);
He who relieves the suffering of all people, undivided in his renown like the ocean.'

'Of letters' (<s>varṇānām</s>) and so forth. Since in the time of utterance, the arrangement of sword-shapes and the like, consisting of letters connected to specific positions, does not exist, there is no cognition of repetition here — so what is the basis of this ornament? Anticipating this doubt, [the author] says 'although' (<s>yadyapi</s>) and so forth. The purport is that this is a figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>) word-ornament, through the cognition of identity between the ink-dot forms of written characters and the spoken sound-letters (<s>varṇa</s>) whose true nature is auditory. To make the word 'and the like' (<s>ādigrahaṇa</s>) meaningful, [the commentator] illustrates with a lotus-pattern — '<s>bhāsate</s>' and so forth.
'Connected throughout' — in all eight directions, for both entry and exit.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 12:

When there is similarity between the object of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) and the object being compared (<s>upameya</s>), with equal status of difference and identity, it is <s>Upamā</s> (simile). // <s>RuAss</s>_12 //

children.text:
arthālaṅkāraprakaraṇamidam /
upamānopameyayorityapratītopamānopameyaniṣedhārtham /
sādhrmye trayaḥ prakārāḥ /
bhedaprādhānyaṃ vyatirekādivat /
abhedaprādhānyaṃ rūpakādivat /
dvayostulyatvaṃ yathāsyām /
yadāhuḥ-'yatra kiñcitsāmānyaṃ kaściñca viśeṣaḥ sa viṣayaḥ sadṛśatāyāḥ' iti /
upamaivanekaprakāravaicitryeṇānekālaṅkārabūjabhūteti prathamaṃ nirdiṣṭā /
asyāśca pūrṇālutpātvabhedāñcirantanairbahuvidhanvamuktam /
tatrāpi sādhāraṇadharmsya kvacidanurāgāmitayaikarūpyeṇa nirdeśaḥ, kvacidvastuprativastubhāvena pṛthaṅnirdeśaḥ /
pṛthaṅnirdeśe ca saṃbandhibhedamātraṃ prativastūpamāvat, bimbapratibimbabhāvo vā dṛṣṭāntavat /
krameṇodāharaṇam -
children.translated_text: This is the section on ornaments of meaning (<s>arthālaṅkāra</s>). 'Of the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>' is meant to exclude [cases where] the <s>upamāna</s> or <s>upameya</s> is not recognized. In 'similarity' (<s>sādharmya</s>) there are three varieties: predominance of difference, as in <s>Vyatireka</s> (contrast) and the like; predominance of identity, as in <s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and the like; and equal status of both, as in this [<s>Upamā</s>]. As they say: 'Where there is some commonality and also some distinction — that is the domain of similarity.' <s>Upamā</s> itself, through the variety of its many forms, is the seed of many ornaments — hence it is stated first. Its manifold divisions of complete and incomplete forms have been extensively discussed by the ancients. Among those, the common property is sometimes stated in a unified manner through a single form of passionate expression, and sometimes stated separately through the relation of object and counter-object. And in separate statement, there is either mere difference of relata as in <s>Prativastūpamā</s> (counter-object simile), or a reflection-image relation as in <s>Dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration). Examples in order —
'As a lamp [is purified] by the greatness of its flame, as the triple path is the path of the divine,

children.text: saṃskāravatyeva girā manīṣī tayā sa pūtaśca vibhūṣitaśca' //
children.translated_text: As by refined speech the wise one — by her he was both purified and adorned.'
'As she goes, repeatedly turning her neck, bearing that face resembling a lotus with a hundred petals turned back,

children.text: digdho 'mṛtena ca viṣeṇa ca pakṣmalākṣyā gāḍhaṃ nikhāta iva me hṛdaye kaṭākṣaḥ' //
children.translated_text: The sidelong glance of the doe-eyed one, smeared with both nectar and poison, is deeply driven into my heart as if nailed.'
Here, turning and being turned back are differentiated by a difference of relata.
But with regard to the intended property, it is indeed a reflection-image relation.
'This <s>Pāṇḍya</s> king, with a long garland draped on his shoulder, anointed with <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood),
Shines like the king of mountains with its peak reddened by the morning sun, along with the outpouring of its waterfalls.'
Here, the garland and the sandalwood-ointment are stated as reflections of the waterfall and the morning sun [respectively].
<s>RuAssC</s>_12:

children.text:
upamānetyādi /
artheti /
śabdālaṅkāranirṇayānantaramavasaraprātpamityarthaḥ /
nanūpamānopameyayoreva sādharmyaṃ saṃbhavati na kāryakāraṇādikayoriti kiṃ tadupādānenetyāśaṅkyāha-upamānetyādi /
tatropamānasyāpratītatvaṃ liṅgabhedādinā prācyairuktam /

children.translated_text: For example —
'Harsh, stinging, and impurity-giving are the wicked — they torment greatly, like chains of bondage;

children.text: manastu sādhudhvanibhiḥ pade pade haranti santo maṇinūpurā iva' //
children.translated_text: But the virtuous captivate the mind at every step with pleasant sounds, like jeweled anklets.'

'<s>Upamā</s>' and so forth. 'Of meaning' (<s>artha</s>) — this means that after the determination of word-ornaments (<s>śabdālaṅkāra</s>), the appropriate occasion has arrived — this is the sense. Now, [one might object:] similarity belongs only to <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> and not to cause-effect and other relations — so what is the purpose of specifying them? Anticipating this doubt, [the author] says '<s>upamāna</s>' and so forth. Regarding that, the non-recognition of the <s>upamāna</s> has been stated by the ancients through difference of gender and the like.

children.text:
atra kaṇanāderdharmasyopamāne 'nyatāṃ karotīti liṅgabhedo duṣṭaḥ /
yadyapi sādhāraṇadharmasyobhayasaṃbandhasaṃbhave 'pi siddhatvādupamāne tatsaṃbandhasya svayamevāvagamāt tasya na śābdatā yuktetyupamānapāratantryeṇa liṅgādivipariṇāmo na kāryaṃ iti na liṅgabhedāderduṣyatvam,tathāpyupamānavākyasya sākāṅkṣatvātpratītiviśrānteḥ śābdastatsaṃbandha upayukta eva /
nahi prabhāmahatyādāvupamānavākye pūtatvādisaṃbandhaṃ vinā samanvayaviśrāntiḥ syāt /
kevalaṃ samānadharmasyopameye vidhīyamānatvamupamāne cānūdyamānatvamitīyāneva viśeṣaḥ /
tadubhayatrāpi tatsaṃbandhasyāvaśyopayogādupapadyata eva samānadharmasyānugāmitvam /
talliṅgabhedāderapi duṣṭatvaṃ yuktam /
upameyasyāpratītatvamavarṇanīyasyāpi varṇanīyatvam /

children.translated_text: For example:
'Fair-complexioned, with full and robust limbs, the shaved pudendum of the widow
appears like the golden plateau of <s>Meru</s> licked [bare] by the horses of the Sun' --

Here, the grammatical gender disagreement in the expression that the property such as blackness 'makes otherness' in the standard of comparison is faulty. Although the common property, being established by its relation to both [the subject and the standard of comparison], and its relation to the standard being self-evident, one might argue that its verbal expression is not justified and therefore gender-modification and the like should not be required due to dependence on the standard of comparison, and thus gender disagreement and the like would not be faulty -- nevertheless, since the sentence of comparison requires syntactic expectancy, the verbal connection of that relation is indeed useful for the completion of cognition. For in a comparative sentence such as 'the radiance is great,' there would be no syntactic completion without the relation of purity and the like. The only distinction is this: the common property is being predicated of the subject of comparison (<s>upameya</s>) and being restated with respect to the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>). Since the relation of that [common property] is necessarily useful in both cases, the fact that the common property follows [both terms] is well established. Therefore the faultiness of gender disagreement and the like is justified. [There is also the fault of] the non-apprehension of the subject of comparison, and the description of what ought not to be described.
Here, in the description of the form of a slender-limbed woman, the description of the pudendum is an impropriety, thus [illustrating] the non-apprehension of the subject of comparison.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> verse 12a:]

children.text:
bhedābhedatulyatvaṃ vyākhyātuṃ sādharmyasya viṣayavibhāgeṇa vyavasthitiṃ darśayati-sādharmya ityādinā /
etaineva ca tribhiḥ prakāraiḥ sādharmyāśrayaḥ samagra evālaṅkāravargaḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ /
tena vyatirekavadityanena sahoktyādayaḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ rūpakavadityanena pariṇāmotprekṣādayaḥ /
kintu rūpakotprekṣayorabhedaprādhānyasadbhāve 'pyāropādhyavasāyakṛta eva viśeṣaḥ /
yadvakṣyati-'āropādabhede 'dhvavasāyaḥ prakṛṣyate' iti /
ataścādhyavasāyagarbheṣvalaṅkāreṣu śuddhābhedarūpaścaturthaḥ prakāro na kaścidāśaṅkanīyaḥ /
tatrāpyabhedāprādhānyasyaiva bhāvāt /
anayāpyupameyopamādayaḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ sāmānyamityabhedahetukam /
viśeṣa iti bhedahetukaḥ /
evaṃ ca bhedābhedatulyatvaviṣaye yaḥ sādṛśyapratyayo jāyate tasyopamāviṣayatvamuktam /
nanu ca satsvapyanekeṣvarthālaṅkāreṣu prathamamiyameva kiṃ nirdiṣṭetyāśaṅkyāha-upamaivetyādi /

children.translated_text: Many ornaments are based on similarity; this [<s>upamā</s>] is the seed of all of them.
It has been stated thus.
'Similarity is <s>upamā</s>; in difference [it is] complete (<s>pūrṇā</s>), elliptical (<s>luptā</s>), and with superlative (<s>sāgrimā</s>);

children.text: śrautyārthīṃ ca bhaved vākye samāse tadvite tathā' //
children.translated_text: it may be expressed (<s>śrautī</s>) or implied (<s>ārthī</s>), in a sentence, in a compound, or with a suffix likewise' --

In order to explain the equality of difference and non-difference, he shows the division of <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity) by means of subject-matter classification, beginning with '<s>sādharmya</s>' and so forth. And by these three modes alone, the entire group of ornaments (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) based on similarity is comprehended. Thus by the expression 'like <s>vyatireka</s>' (contrast), <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression) and the like are comprehended; by the expression 'like <s>rūpaka</s>' (metaphor), <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) and the like are comprehended. However, in <s>rūpaka</s> and <s>utprekṣā</s>, although the predominance of non-difference exists, the distinction is produced only by <s>āropa</s> (superimposition) and <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determinative judgment). As he will state: 'From superimposition, in non-difference, <s>adhyavasāya</s> is intensified.' Therefore, among ornaments that contain <s>adhyavasāya</s>, a fourth mode of pure non-difference should not be suspected, since even there non-difference is not predominant [in the same way]. By this [classification], <s>upameyopamā</s> (reciprocal comparison) and the like are also comprehended. '<s>Sāmānya</s>' (generality) means caused by non-difference; '<s>viśeṣa</s>' (particularity) means caused by difference. Thus it has been stated that the cognition of resemblance (<s>sādṛśya</s>) that arises in the domain of difference, non-difference, and equality is the province of <s>upamā</s> (simile). Now, anticipating the objection 'Why is this very [figure] mentioned first when there are many other figures of sense?', he says 'Indeed <s>upamā</s> alone' and so forth.
and so forth.

children.text:
ataśca kimasmākaṃ tadāviṣkāraṇeneti bhāvaḥ /
evaṃ ca teṣāṃ gaṇane tathā na vaicitryaṃ kiñciditi sūcitam /
children.translated_text: And therefore, 'What is the point for us in making that explicit?' -- such is the purport. And thus it is indicated that in their enumeration there is no such variety [worth separate treatment].
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> verse 12b:]

children.text:
tatrāpīti /
cirantanokte pūrṇatvādibhedanirdeśe satyapītyarthaḥ /
sādhāraṇadharmasyeti /
dharmaḥ parāśritaḥ, tasya ca tadatadgāmitvāt sādhāraṇatvam /
tadeva copamādyatthāne nimittam /
sa ca catuṣṭayī śabdānāṃ pravṛttiḥ' iti mahābhāṣyaprakriyayā jātiguṇakriyādravyātmakeṣu dharmiṣvevaṃrūpa eva bhavati /
na caitadvirudhyate /
dharmidharmabhāvasya na vāstavatvam /
jātyādyātmano dharmiṇo 'pi kadācidanyāśritatve dharmatvāt /
evaṃ ca tadatiriktaṃ dharmamātramapi sādhāraṇaṃ na kiñcidvācyam /
children.translated_text: Thus no additional property beyond these four can be called 'common,'
since it has been stated that the application of words is solely by means of the fourfold [classification].
'Compassionately did the mighty-armed one enjoy [her], thinking "she will suddenly depart in alarm."
That earth, newly subjected [to his rule], [he treated] like a bride at the first taking of the hand' --

'Even there' -- the meaning is: even though the earlier authorities have stated distinctions such as completeness and so forth. 'Of the common property' -- a property (<s>dharma</s>) is dependent on another; and its being common (<s>sādhāraṇatva</s>) consists in its pertaining to this and that [both subject and standard]. And that alone is the basis for <s>upamā</s> and the like. And that [property], according to the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s> procedure that 'the application of words is fourfold,' exists only in this form among substrata (<s>dharmin</s>) that are of the nature of <s>jāti</s> (universal), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>kriyā</s> (action), and <s>dravya</s> (substance). Nor is this contradicted [by anything]. The relationship of substratum and property (<s>dharmi-dharma-bhāva</s>) is not ultimately real, since even the substratum, being of the nature of universal and the like, sometimes becomes a property when dependent on another.

children.text:
ityādāvupamānādau kriyārūpatvāderyojayituṃ śakyatvāt tasya eva ca samagraviṣayāvagāhanasahiṣṇutvāt /
nanu jāteḥ sādhāraṇadharmatve tajjātīyatvāt tattvaṃ na syāt, na sadṛśatvamiti kathamupamāṅgatvamasyāḥ syāditi cet, na /
bimbapratibimbabhāvāśrayeṇa tathātvābhāvāt /
tatra hyasakṛnnirdeśād dvayorhārādikayorjātyoḥ śvaityādyabhedanimittāvalambanenaikatvamāśritya sādṛśyanimittaṃ sādhāraṇyaṃ syāt /
etacca savistaramupariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: in this and similar examples, since it is of the nature of action and the like in the standard of comparison, it can be connected, and it alone is capable of encompassing the entire range of subject matter. Now, if <s>jāti</s> (universal) were the common property, then since one would belong to the same class, there would be identity rather than similarity -- so how could it serve as a component of <s>upamā</s>? No, [this objection does not hold,] because of the absence of such identity when the relationship of original and reflection (<s>bimba-pratibimba-bhāva</s>) is adopted. For in that case, by repeated mention, taking as the basis the unity of two universals such as necklace-ness and the like, grounded in the non-difference of whiteness and the like, resemblance-based commonality would obtain. And this we shall explain at length further on.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> verse 12c:]
The substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) having the form of universal and the like is illustrated as follows:
'As shade from a dense garden [is relief] from a desert path, as a pool of cool water from a forest fire, as nectar from the ripening of poison,

children.text: pravṛddhādunmādāt prakṛtimiva nistāryavirahā- llabheya tvadbhakti nirūpamarasāṃ śaṅkara kadā' //
children.translated_text: as [return to] natural state from an intensified madness -- when, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, having been rescued from separation, shall I obtain your devotion of incomparable <s>rasa</s>?' --

children.text:
atra cchāyāvāpīsudhāprakṛtīnāmupamānānāṃ jātiguṇadravyakriyātvam /
chāyāyastu jātirūpatvād guṇatvaṃ nāśaṅkanīyam /
upameyasya punaretatsvayamevābhyūhyam /
children.translated_text: Here the standards of comparison -- shade, pool, nectar, and natural state -- are respectively of the nature of <s>jāti</s> (universal), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>dravya</s> (substance), and <s>kriyā</s> (action). Since shade is of the nature of a universal, one should not suspect it to be a quality. As for the subject of comparison, this is to be inferred by the reader.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> verse 12d:]
Of the properties (<s>dharma</s>), the illustration is as follows:
'O <s>Vaidehī</s>, behold the foaming ocean divided by my bridge,
like the autumn sky, clear, with its beautiful stars revealed, [divided] as if by a path of shadow' --

children.text:
atra vibhaktamityasya kriyātvaṃ rāmasetucchāyāpathayordravyatvaṃ phenatārakāṇāṃ jātitvaṃ prasādasya ca guṇatvaṃ dravyātmakākāśāmburāśigattatvenopanibaddham /
evaṃ prakṛtāmeva mahābhāṣyaprakriyāmapahāya ninimittameva prakriyāntaramāśritya yadanyairuktaṃ tadayuktamevetyalaṃ bahunā /
evaṃvidhasya cāsya bhāvābhāvarūpatayā dvaividhyam /
etacca na tathāvaicitryāvahamiti granthakṛtā noktam /
children.translated_text: Here 'divided' has the nature of action; the bridge of <s>Rāma</s> and the path of shadow have the nature of substance; the foam and the stars have the nature of universal; and clarity has the nature of quality, being connected as a quality of the substance-natured sky and ocean. Thus, abandoning this very procedure of the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s> that is under discussion and resorting to another procedure without justification, what has been stated by others is indeed unjustified -- enough of prolixity. And this [common property], being of the nature of presence and absence, has a twofold character. But since this does not produce much variety, the author of the treatise has not mentioned it.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> verse 12e:]

children.text:
aikarūpyeṇoti /
sakṛt /
yadvakṣyati-'tatra sāmānyadharmasyevādyupādāne sakṛntirdeśa upamā' iti /
pṛthaṅnirdeśa iti /
asakṛdityarthaḥ /
yadvakṣyati-
'vastuprativastubhāvenāsakṛnnirdeśe 'pi saiva' iti /
sādhāraṇadharmasyetyatrāpi saṃbandhanīyam /
vastuprativastubhāve 'pi dvaividhyamityāha-pṛthaṅnirdeśe ityādi /
sambandhibhedamātramiti /
na punaḥ svarūpabhedaḥ kaścidityarthaḥ /
yadvakṣyati-asakṛnnirdeśe śuddhasāmānyarūpatvaṃ bimbapratibimbabhāva e vā' iti /
etacca bhedatrayaṃ prāyaḥ sarveṣāmeva sādṛśyāśrayāṇāmalaṅkārāṇāṃ jīvitabhūtatvena saṃbhavatītyagrata eva tatra tatrodāhariṣyāmaḥ /
krameṇeti yathoddeśam /
sambandhibhedāditi /
saṃbandhinoḥ kandharāvṛntayorbhedāt /
na tu hāranirjharādivatsvarūpato bhedaḥ /
vastuta ekatvādvalitatvāvṛttatvayorabhedaḥ /
nanu yadi valitatvāvṛttatvākhyo dharma ānanaśatapattrayoḥ śuddhasāmānyarūpatayopāttastaddharmī kandharāvṛntarūpaḥ punaḥ kiṃrūpatayetyāśaṅkyāha-dharmyabhiprāyeṇetyādi /
evakāraḥ śuddhasāmānyarūpatvavyavacchedakaḥ /
kandharāvṛntayośca yathokte dharmitve 'pyānanaśatapatrtāpekṣayā dharmatvameva yuktam /
āśrayāśrayibhāvena dharmidharmabhāvasya bhāvāt /
ata evāsyāvāstavatvaṃ pūrvamuktam /
ataścānanaśatapatrtāpekṣayā iti na vyākhyeyam /
tayorupamānopameyabhāvavācoyuktereva yuktatvāt /
evaṃ ca sati kandharāvṛntayoḥ svarūpamanabhimataṃ syāt /
anenaiva ca bimbapratibimbabhāvasya svarūpe darśite 'pyasaṃkīrṇaprakaṭanāśayena punaḥ 'pāṇḍyo 'yam' ityādyudāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'In a single form' means: once. As he will state: 'When the common property alone is mentioned first, a single mention is <s>upamā</s>.' 'Separate mention' means: more than once. As he will state: 'Even in multiple mentions in the manner of object and counter-object (<s>vastu-prativastu</s>), it is that same [<s>upamā</s>].' This should be connected with 'of the common property' [in the root text] as well. The twofold nature even in the object-counter-object mode is stated by 'In separate mention' and so forth. 'Merely a difference of the related [terms]' -- meaning: there is no difference of essential nature whatsoever. As he will state: 'In multiple mention, [there is] either pure commonality or the relationship of original and reflection (<s>bimba-pratibimba-bhāva</s>).' And this threefold division applies as the very life-force of practically all ornaments based on resemblance, so we shall illustrate it in each case as we proceed. 'In sequence' means: in the order of enumeration. 'Due to difference of the related [terms]' -- due to the difference of the related terms, namely the neck and the stem; but there is no difference of essential nature as with the necklace and the waterfall. In reality, since curvedness and roundedness are one, there is non-difference [of the properties]. Now, if the property called curvedness-roundedness is taken as pure commonality of the lotus and the face, then in what capacity is the substratum in the form of neck and stem taken? -- anticipating this doubt, he says 'With the intention of the substratum' and so forth. The word 'eva' (alone/only) excludes the [interpretation of] pure commonality. And although the neck and the stem have the status of substrata in the manner described, relative to the face and the lotus, it is appropriate [to regard them] as properties only, since the substratum-property relationship exists by way of the support-supported relation. It is for this very reason that its non-ultimate-reality was stated earlier. Therefore one should not interpret it as 'relative to the face and the lotus,' since it is more fitting that the speech-usage of the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> (standard-subject) relation [applies to the face and lotus]. And in that case, the essential nature of the neck and the stem would not be the intended [focus]. And by this, even though the nature of the <s>bimba-pratibimba-bhāva</s> has been shown, with the intent of making it manifest without confusion, he has again cited the example beginning with '<s>Pāṇḍya</s>.'
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> verse 12f:]

children.text:
hārāṅgarāgayoriti /
svarūpayoriti śeṣaḥ /
na cātra bimbapratibimbabhāvasya viṣayāntaraṃ pradarśya vākyārthaṅgatāmupamāśaṅkya guṇasāmyanāmā caturthaḥ prakāro vācyaḥ /
yāvatā hi sādhāraṇadharmanibandhanamupamāsvarūpam, sa cātra dharmo nirdiṣṭānirdiṣṭatvena dvividhaḥ /
nirdeśapakṣe cāsya traividhyamuktam /
anirdeśapakṣe cāsya na vaicitryaṃ kiñciditi na tadāśrayaṃ bhedajātamuktam /
ataścātra nirdiṣṭaḥ sādhāraṇadharmo vyavasthita iti kā nāma caturthaprakārakalpanā /
vākyārthopamāgandho 'pyatra nāsti /
sa hyanekeṣāṃ dharmiṇāṃ parasparāvacchinnānāṃ tādṛśereva dharmibhiḥ sāmye bhavati /

children.translated_text: For example:
'She who is to be honored like a mother, and a potter-woman, she the protectress from whom safety is known,
a bearer of gems like a female serpent -- [she is] like a hidden treasure' --

'Of the necklace and the body-paint' -- the supplement is: 'of their essential natures.' Nor should a fourth mode called 'equality of qualities' (<s>guṇasāmya</s>) be proposed here by showing another domain of the <s>bimba-pratibimba-bhāva</s> and suspecting it to be a sentence-level <s>upamā</s> (<s>vākyārtha-upamā</s>). For the essential nature of <s>upamā</s> is grounded in the common property; and that property here is of two kinds, stated and unstated. In the case of statement, its threefold nature has been described. In the case of non-statement, since there is no variety in it, no set of distinctions based on it has been mentioned. Therefore, since the common property is established as stated here, what is the point of imagining a fourth mode? There is not even a trace of sentence-level <s>upamā</s> here. For that [sentence-level <s>upamā</s>] occurs when the similarity of several substrata, mutually distinct from one another, obtains with [other] substrata of the same kind.

children.text:
atra janayitryādīnāṃ ratnasūtyādīnyupamānānyupāttāni /
eteṣāṃ dharmitvaṃ ca sphuṭameva /
bimbapratibimbabhāvaḥ punardharmiviśeṣapratipādanonmukhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bhavati /
parasparāvacchinnatvaṃ yathātreva /
atra hi hārāṅgarāgayoḥ pāṇḍyasya viśiṣṭatāpādanāyaivopādānam /
indumatīṃ prati tasya viśiṣṭālambanavibhāvatvena vivakṣitatvāt /
ataśca tayoḥ parasparonmukhatvātsvātmanyevāviśrāntiriti kā kathopameyatāyāḥ /
evaṃ pāṇḍyasyādgirājena hāranirjharādidharmanimittaivopamā, tāvanmātreṇaiva sādṛśyaparyavasānāt /
tacca hārādeḥ sādhāraṇadharmasya bimbapratibimbatvād dṛṣṭāntanyāyasyaitatsūdāharaṇameva /
children.translated_text: Here the standards of comparison for the mother and the like -- gem-bearer and the like -- have been employed. And the substratum-status of these is quite evident. The <s>bimba-pratibimba-bhāva</s> (original-reflection relationship), on the other hand, pertains to properties that are oriented toward indicating a specific substratum. The mutual distinctness [of the compared terms] is just as seen here. For here the necklace and body-paint are employed precisely for establishing the distinction of <s>Pāṇḍya</s>, since he is intended as the distinguished <s>ālambana-vibhāva</s> (foundational stimulus) with respect to <s>Indumatī</s>. Therefore, since these two face each other, they do not rest in themselves alone -- so what possibility is there of [them being] subjects of comparison? Thus the <s>upamā</s> of <s>Pāṇḍya</s> with the mountain-king (<s>Adrirāja</s>) is caused only by the properties of necklace-waterfall and the like, since the resemblance culminates in just that much. And since the common property of the necklace and the like has the character of original and reflection, this [discussion] itself serves as the illustrated instance of the principle of <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (exemplification).
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> verse 12g:]

children.text:
nanu hāranirjharayostadatadgāmitvābhāvātkathaṃ sādhāraṇadharmateti cet,ucyate- asyāstāvaddharmasya sādhāraṇyaṃ jīvitam /
tacca dharmasyaikatve bhavati /
na ca vastuto 'tra dharmasyaikatvam /
nahi ya eva mukhagato lāvaṇyādirdharmaḥ sa eva candrādau, tasyānvayāsaṃbhavāt /
api tu tajjātīyo 'trānyo 'sti dharmaḥ /
evaṃ dharmayorbhedātsādhāraṇatvābhāvādupamāyāḥ svarūpaniṣpattireva na syāt /
atha dharmayorapi sādṛśyamabhyupagamyate tattatrāpi sādṛśyanimittamanyadanveṣyam /
tatrāpyanyadityanavasthā syāt /
tataśca dharmayorvastuto bhede 'pi pratītāvekatāvasāyādbhede 'pyabheda ityetannimittamekatvamāśrayaṇīyam /
anyathā hyapamāyā utthānameva na syāt /
evamihāpi hāranirjharādīnāṃ vastuprativastutayopāttānāṃ vastuto bhede 'pyabhedavivakṣetyekatvaṃ grāhyam /
anyathā hyeṣāṃ pāṇḍyādrirājayoraupabhyasamutthāne nimittatvameva na syāt /
na caiṣāmaupamyaṃ yuktamiti samanantaramevoktam /
ata evātra bimbapratibimbabhāvavyapadeśaḥ /
loko hi darpaṇādau bimbātpratibimbasya bhede 'pi madīyamevātra vadanaṃ saṃkrāntamityabhedenābhimanyate /
anyathā hi pratibimbagadarśane kṛśo 'ha sthūlo 'hamityādyabhimāno nodiyāt bhūṣaṇavinyāsādau ca nāyikā nādriyeran /

children.translated_text: Even by the eastern [rhetoricians] --
'That sage, marked with the sacrificial thread and wearing a garment of black antelope skin,
shone like the Sun embraced by a portion of a dark rain-cloud' --

Now, if [one objects that] since the necklace and the waterfall do not pertain to this and that [i.e., are not shared between both], how can they be a common property? -- it is replied: The commonality of this property is its very life. And that [commonality] exists when the property is one. But here there is no real oneness of the property. For it is not the case that the very same property of beauty and the like that resides in the face also resides in the moon, since the connection of that [same property to both] is impossible. Rather, there is another property here belonging to the same class. Thus, since the two properties are different, commonality would be absent, and the very essential nature of <s>upamā</s> would not be established. If, then, resemblance between the two properties is also accepted, then yet another basis for that resemblance must be sought -- and for that too another, leading to infinite regress. Therefore, although the two properties are in reality different, because in cognition there is a determination of oneness, one must resort to a unity grounded in the principle 'non-difference despite difference.' Otherwise, <s>upamā</s> could never arise at all. Similarly here too, although the necklace, waterfall, and the like employed as object and counter-object are in reality different, since non-difference is intended, their oneness must be accepted. Otherwise, these [properties] would have no capacity whatsoever to serve as the basis for the <s>upamā</s> between <s>Pāṇḍya</s> and the mountain-king. Nor is it appropriate [to say] that these have a relation of similarity -- as was stated just a moment ago. It is for this very reason that the designation <s>bimba-pratibimba-bhāva</s> (original-reflection relationship) [is used] here. For in the world, although the reflection in a mirror and the like is different from the original, one determines with non-difference: 'This is my very face that has transferred [into the mirror].' Otherwise, upon seeing a fat reflection, the thought 'I am thin' or 'I am fat' and such self-identification would not arise, and women would not attend to the arrangement of ornaments and the like [using mirrors].
thus.
Likewise --
He, wearing yellow garments and holding the <s>Śārṅga</s> (bow), <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> attained a form terrifying to <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love),
Like a cloud merging with the moon at night, bearing a rainbow of a hundred joys.

children.text:
ityatra mauñjītaḍitoḥ śaṅkhaśaśinośca vastuto bhede 'pyabhedavivakṣāmevāśrityasādhāraṇadharmasya hīnatvamādhikyaṃ coktam /
ata eva cātra pūrvaṃ granthakṛtā vastuprativastubhāvavad vastudvayasya prācyoktameva vyavahāraṃ darśayituṃ prativastūpamāvad dṛṣṭāntavacceti taduktamevadṛṣṭāntadvayaṃ dattam /
evaṃ cātrābhedavivakṣaiva jīvitam /
children.translated_text: Here, although there is an actual difference between the girdle-cord and the lightning, and between the conch and the moon, the deficiency and excess of the uncommon property are stated by resorting to the intention of non-difference. For this very reason, the author of the text, in order to show the conventional usage of the two objects as previously stated by earlier authorities—like <s>vastuprativastubhāva</s> (object-counterpart relation)—has given those very two illustrations as examples of <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart-simile) and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustrative example). Thus, the intention of non-difference is the very life of this figure.
RuAssC_12h:
For example:

children.text: 'vidyutvantaṃ lalitavanitāḥ sendracāpaṃ sacitrāḥ saṃgītāya prahatamurajāḥ snigdhagambhīraghoṣam /
children.translated_text: The graceful women [are like] those bearing lightning, the colorful ones [are like] those bearing <s>Indra</s>'s bow, those producing music with beaten drums [are like] those with deep, resonant thunder,

children.text: antastoyaṃ maṇimayabhuvastuṅgamabhraṃlihāgrāḥ prāsādāstvāṃ tulayitumalaṃ yatra taistairviśeṣaiḥ' //
children.translated_text: The palaces, with water within, with jewel-encrusted floors, with lofty peaks touching the clouds, are able to rival you (the cloud) with each of those particular qualities.
And this [figure] is very abundantly found in literary examples.

children.text:
atra vidyudvanitādīnāṃ meghaprāsādaviṣiṣṭatādhāyakatayā dharmatvenaivopādānam /
ata eva taistairviśeṣairityuktam /
teṣāṃ sakṛnnirdeśābhāvānnānugāmitā /
ekārthatvābhāvānna śudhdasāmānyarūpatvamiti pāriśeṣyādvimbapratibimbabhāva eva /
eteṣāṃ cābhedenaiva pratīteḥ sādhāraṇatvam /
evaṃ hārāderapi jñeyam /
abhedapratītiścātra sādṛśyanimittā /
na caitāvataivaipāmupamānopameyatvaṃ vācyam /
tathātvāvivakṣaṇāt /
sādṛśyasya ca sitatvādiguṇayogitvaṃ nāma nimittam /
evamabhedapratītimukhenātra hārādeḥ samānadharmatvam /
kvacinnimittāntareṇāpyabhedapratītirbhavati /

children.translated_text: For example:
He who is approved by both, learned, like medicine for one who is afflicted,
Even a beloved one, if corrupt, should be abandoned—like a thumb bitten by a snake.

Here, the lightning, women, and so forth are employed as properties precisely because they bestow the quality of being distinguished upon the cloud and the palace. For this very reason it is said 'with each of those particular qualities.' Because there is no single collective mention of them, there is no <s>anugāmitā</s> (recurrence). Because there is no unity of meaning, it is not pure <s>sāmānyarūpatva</s> (generic form). Therefore, by elimination, it is indeed <s>vimbapratibimbabhāva</s> (image-reflection relation). And their commonality arises from the cognition of non-difference itself. The same should be understood regarding necklaces and the like. The cognition of non-difference here is caused by similarity. But one should not thereby say that these are <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison), because there is no intention of such a relation. And the cause of similarity is the possession of qualities such as whiteness—this is the basis. Thus, through the medium of the cognition of non-difference, necklaces and such have the status of common properties. Sometimes the cognition of non-difference arises from other causes as well.

Here, in the latter half-verse, the fact that 'bitten' and 'corrupt' both produce harm—their having the same functional effect—is the cause of [the cognition of] non-difference. Enough of elaboration.
RuAssC_12i:

children.text: iyaṃ ca dvayopari prakṛtayoraprakṛtayoścaupamye samuccitā bhavati /

children.translated_text: In order, for example:
When she, of noble speech, spoke, her voice was as if nectar were flowing,
While another's voice, raised by another, with harsh sounds, was like a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) being struck discordantly.
And this [figure] occurs as combined (<s>samuccita</s>) over two [types]—the primary subjects and the non-primary subjects—in the domain of comparison.
For example:
With lotus-petals as lips, with filaments as teeth, they shine,
With swarms of bees as locks of hair, with lotuses as faces—such are the lotus-pools.

Here, in relation to the noble lady, the 'one raised by another' and the 'discordant lute'—which are non-primary subjects—are combined in the quality of producing harsh sound. This [figure] also admits of <s>ekadeśavivartin</s> (partial variation).

children.text:
atra nalinīnāṃ nāyikā upamānatvena nopāttā ityekadeśavivartitvam /
iyaṃ ca sādṛśyadāḍharyārthaṃ kavipratibhākalpite sādharmye kalpitā bhavati /
tacca kvacidupameyagatatvena kvacidupamānenāpi kalpitamiti dvidhātvamasyāḥ /
yaduktam-
'upameyasya vaiśiṣṭyamupamānasya vā kvacit' iti /
vaidharmyeṇāpi sādharmyamiti tṛtīyaḥ prakāraḥ punarasyā na vācyaḥ /
asyopamāyāmeva saṃbhavāddāḍharyapratipādanapratīteśca /
children.translated_text: Here, because the heroines are not taken as the standard of comparison for the lotus-pools, it is a case of partial variation. And this [figure] occurs as devised through poetic imagination for the purpose of strengthening similarity. And that [imagined similarity] is of two kinds: sometimes attributed to the <s>upameya</s> (object compared), sometimes devised through the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison). As stated: 'The distinction of the <s>upameya</s>, or sometimes of the <s>upamāna</s>.' A third variety—similarity through dissimilarity—should not be separately stated for this figure, because it is possible within <s>upamā</s> (simile) itself, and the understanding of strengthening is [already] conveyed.
RuAssC_12j:
In order, for example:
Bow to him, to the lotus of the navel of <s>Hari</s>, delighting in the beauty of the sky,

children.text: chappaachampiagatto malo vva candammi jattha vihī' //
children.translated_text: Where <s>Brahmā</s> (the Creator), his body covered by a six-legged bee, is like a spot on the moon.
(Bow to him, to the lotus of the navel of <s>Hari</s>, delighting in the beauty of the sky,

children.text: ṣaṭpadācchāditagātro mala iva candre yatra vidhiḥ') //
children.translated_text: Where <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), his body covered by a six-legged bee, is like a spot on the moon.)
Here, the quality of being covered by a six-legged bee is imagined for the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison).
She, slightly bent forward by her breasts, wearing a garment of the color of the rising sun,
Bowing under clusters of newly appeared blossoms—like a moving, sprouting creeper.

children.text:
" atropamānagatatvena saṃcāriṇītvaṃ kalpitam /
na cāsyāḥ pṛthaglakṣaṇaṃ vācyam,dvayoraupamyapratīteḥ /
sāmānyalakṣaṇasyātrāpyanugamāt /
athātra kalpanāstīti cet, na /
evaṃ hi pratibhedaṃ lakṣaṇakaraṇaprasaṅgaḥ /
samuccitatvāderviśeṣāntarasyāpi bhāvāt /
athopamānaguṇaviśiṣṭopameyāvagamaphalatvenopamāyāḥ pratibhaṭabhūtavastvantarābhāvaprayojanatvena cāsyāḥ pṛthagalaṅkāratvamiti cet, na /
atropameyasyopamānopamānaguṇaviśiṣṭatayaiva pratīteḥ phalabhedābhāvāt /
tathā hi'āvarjitā' ityādau bhagavatyā latāyāḥ sādṛśyasya saṃcāriṇītvenābhāvo mā prasāṅkṣīditi tayoḥ sādharmyaṃmeva druḍayituṃ kavinā latāyāḥ saṃcāriṇītvaṃ kalpitam /
nanvatra bhagavatyā anyadupamānaṃ nāstīti pratīyate /
ananvayādivadupamānāntaraniṣedhasya vākyārthatvāt /
maivam /
evamupameyasyāpi vaiśiṣṭyakalpane upameyāntaraniṣedhaphalatvaṃ vācyam /
samānanyāyatvāt /
tadyathā dṛḍharope rūpake viṣayaviṣayiṇorabhedameva draḍhayituṃ kasyaciddharmasya hānirādhikyaṃ vā kalpyate, tathehāpi sāmānyadārḍhyayaiva kalpitatvaṃ jñeyam /
atrāpyabhedālaṅkārākhyālaṅkārāntaratvaṃ na vācyam /
rūpakeṇaivāsyā vicchritteḥ saṃgṛhītatvāt /
viṣayaviṣayiṇorabhedo hi rūpakasatattvam /
sa eva cātra dārḍhyena pratīyata iti ko nāmāsya rūpakātpṛthagbhāvaḥ /
abhedamātrapratītau rūpakam, niyatadharmahānāvanyataḥ sarvato 'pyabhedapratītāvabheda iti pratītibhedo 'pyastīti cet, na /
evaṃ hyasti tāvadabhedapratītiratrānugatā /
yastu vaśeṣaḥ sa pṛthagbhedatve vyavasthāpako 'stu na pṛthagalaṅkāratve /
nahiśābaleyatāmātreṇa gotvamaścatvavyapadeśyaṃ bhavati /

children.translated_text: Thus:
<s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), having assumed a bodily form; the <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring), being perpetual;
The lover stole the heart; the ever-full <s>Sudhākara</s> (Moon).

Here, the quality of 'moving about' is imagined as attributed to the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison). But a separate definition should not be stated for this [figure], because the understanding of comparison applies to both. The general definition applies here as well. If one objects that there is imagination here [making it different]—no. For then there would be the consequence of having to create definitions for every sub-variety, since there are other distinctions such as the combined form and so forth. And if one argues that <s>upamā</s> has the purpose of apprehending the <s>upameya</s> as qualified by the qualities of the <s>upamāna</s>, while this [figure] has the purpose of denying the existence of any rival object, and therefore it is a separate <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure)—no. Because here the <s>upameya</s> is cognized precisely as qualified by the qualities of the <s>upamāna</s>, there is no difference of result. For in the verse 'She, slightly bent forward...' and so forth, in order to strengthen the similarity between the noble lady and the creeper—lest the similarity be absent due to the [creeper's] quality of 'moving about'—the poet has imagined the quality of moving for the creeper. If one says that it is understood here that there is no other <s>upamāna</s> for the noble lady, and that, like <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison), the denial of another standard of comparison is the sentence-meaning—this is wrong. For by the same reasoning, when distinction is imagined for the <s>upameya</s>, one would have to say that the denial of another <s>upameya</s> is the result—the logic being identical. Just as in a firmly established <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), in order to strengthen the identity of the subject and the predicate, the diminution or excess of some property is imagined, so too here the imagination should be understood as being for the purpose of strengthening the commonality. Here too, one should not claim that it is a different <s>alaṅkāra</s> called <s>abheda</s> (non-difference), because it is already comprehended by the extension of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) itself. For the identity of the subject and predicate is the essential nature of <s>rūpaka</s>. And that very [identity] is here cognized with firmness—so what difference could this have from <s>rūpaka</s>? If one argues that in the mere cognition of non-difference it is <s>rūpaka</s>, while in the diminution of a specific property it is something else, and when non-difference is cognized from all sides it is <s>abheda</s>—thus there is a difference in cognition—no. For in that case, the cognition of non-difference is indeed present here as a common element. Whatever distinction there is, let it serve as the basis for classification within [the figure], not for establishing a separate <s>alaṅkāra</s>. For one does not designate cow-ness or horse-ness merely on the basis of being a Śābalēya (spotted one).

children.text:
ityādau gṛhītavigrahattvāderniyatasya dharmasyādhikye 'pyalaṅkārāntaraprasaṅgaḥ /
iyaṃ ca mālātvādinānantabhedeti tadgranthavistarabhayānna prapañcitam /
children.translated_text: Here too, even in the excess of a specific property such as 'having assumed a bodily form' and the like, the consequence of [positing] a separate <s>alaṅkāra</s> would follow. This [figure] also has infinite varieties through garland-form and so forth, which are not elaborated here for fear of expanding the text.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 13:
When a single entity is both <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison), it is <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison). || 13 ||

children.text:
vācyābhiprāyeṇa pūrvaṃrūpānugamaḥ /
ekasya tu viruddhadharmasaṃsargo dvitīyasavrahyacārinivṛttyarthaḥ /
ata evānanvaya iti yogo 'pyatra saṃbhravati /
yathā-
'yuddhe 'rjuno 'rjuna iva prathitapratāpo bhīmo 'pi bhīma iva vairiṣu bhīmakarmā /
nyagrodhavartinamayādhipatiṃ kuruṇāmutprāsanārthamiva jagmaturādareṇa' //
children.translated_text: From the perspective of verbal expression, there is conformity to the preceding form. But the conjunction of contradictory properties in a single entity serves the purpose of negating a second companion. For this very reason, the term <s>ananvaya</s> ('without parallel') also applies here. For example: '<s>Arjuna</s> in battle, like <s>Arjuna</s> himself, of celebrated prowess; <s>Bhīma</s> too, like <s>Bhīma</s> himself, of terrible deeds against enemies; the two went with reverence to the king of the <s>Kurus</s> who dwelt beneath the banyan tree, as if to gain his favor.'
RuAssC_13:

children.text:
ekasyaivetyādi /
nanu sādṛśyāśrayāṇāmalaṅkārāṇāṃ lakṣayutuṃ prastutatvātsādṛśyasyobhayaniṣṭhatvenaiva saṃbhavādekasya ca tadabhāvātkathamihātadāśrayasyāpyasya vacanamityāśaṅkyāha-vācyābhiprāyeṇetyādi /
children.translated_text: 'Of a single entity alone' and so forth. Now, since the figures based on similarity are being defined, and since similarity naturally requires two terms, and a single entity lacks this—how can a figure not based on similarity be mentioned here? Anticipating this objection, he says: 'From the perspective of verbal expression' and so forth.
RuAssC_13a:

children.text:
pūrvarūpeti /
sādṛśyāśrayatvasyetyarthaḥ /
astveva hyatra śābdī sādṛśyapratītiḥ /
mukhaṃ candra ivetyādivadevātropamānopameyatvasya vācyatayopanibandhanāt /
ata evāha-vācyābhiprāyeṇeti /
na punarvastvabhiprāyeṇetyarthaḥ /
vastuto hyekasyaiva sādhyasiddhadharmarūpatvāsaṃbhavādupamānopameyatve 'pi virodhaḥ syāt /
itthaṃ śābdameva sādṛśyānugamamāśrityehāsya lakṣaṇam /
nanu yadyevamekasyopamānopameyatvaṃ virudhyate tatkiṃ vastuviruddhena niṣphalena caitenetyāśaṅkyāha-ekasyetyādi /
children.translated_text: 'Conformity to the preceding form'—meaning: [conformity] to the property of being based on similarity. For indeed there is here a verbal cognition of similarity, just as in 'The face is like the moon' and so forth, since being <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is established as expressly stated. For this very reason he says 'from the perspective of verbal expression'—meaning: not from the perspective of reality. For in reality, since a single entity cannot have the nature of both established and to-be-established properties, there would be a contradiction even in being <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>. Thus, relying only on the verbal [appearance of] conformity to similarity, the definition here [is given]. Now, if one objects: if being <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> of a single entity is contradictory, then what is the point of this [figure] which contradicts reality and is fruitless?—anticipating this, he says: 'Of a single entity' and so forth.
RuAssC_13b:
For example:
By his command alone, while I protect the subjects, this old age with hair whitening near the ears,
Which instructs me as if [I were still in] the embryonic form—even today that partiality of the guru toward me [persists].
