Thus, the negation of a second companion is indeed the validating evidence that establishes its status as an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of speech). Otherwise, it would not be an <s>alaṅkāra</s>.

children.text:
atra yathaiva garbharūpaṃ māṃ gururanvaśāttathaivādyāpyanuśāstīti satyapyekasyopamānopameyatve dvitīyasabrahmacāri nivṛttipratipattyabhāvānnāyamalaṅkāraḥ /
ekasyaivāsthābhedena ca siddhasādhyadharmasaṃbhavānnopamānopameyatvarūpaviruddhadharmasaṃsargaḥ /
ata eveti /
viruddhadharmaṃsaṃyogāt /
ekasyaiva siddhasādhyarūpeṇopamānopameyatvenāvidyabhāno 'nvayaḥ saṃbandho yatra sa tathoktaḥ /
arjunādanyo yuddhe prathitapratāpo nāstīti dvitāyasabrahmacārinivṛttiratra jīvitabhūtā pratīyata eva /
children.translated_text: That there is no one other than <s>Arjuna</s> of celebrated prowess in battle—this negation of a second companion is indeed understood here as the essential element.
For this very reason, because the <s>upamāna</s>-forms of <s>Kārtavīrya</s> and <s>Hiṃstramattva</s> are not cognized, this is a pure example [of <s>ananvaya</s>].
In this world, though filled with thousands of beautiful women,
Only the left half of hers imitates the right half.

Here, although there is the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation of a single entity—'just as the <s>guru</s> instructed me when I was in embryonic form, so too he instructs me even now'—because there is no apprehension of the negation of a second companion, this is not [an instance of] this <s>alaṅkāra</s>. And because, through the difference of temporal states of a single entity, the existence of established and to-be-established properties is possible, there is no conjunction of contradictory properties that constitutes being <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>. 'For this very reason'—because of the conjunction of contradictory properties. <s>Ananvaya</s> is so called because there is a relation (<s>anvaya</s>) in which a single entity, through [its] non-existent [dual] appearance, is both <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> in the form of established and to-be-established [properties].
(In this world, though filled with thousands of beautiful women,
Only the left half of hers imitates the right half.)

children.text:
ityādau cānanvayodāharaṇatvaṃ na vācyam /
atrānyādhanānyārdhasyopamīyamānatvenopamāyā abhidhīyamānatvāt /
asya hyupamānāntaraniṣedhaparyavasāyyabhidhīyamānamekasyaivopamānopameyatvaṃ svarūpam /
na ca tadatra śabdenābhidhīyate 'pi tu vyajyata iti pratīyamānataiva yukteti na vācyatvamasyetivācyam /
evaṃ hyalaṅkādadhvanerviṣayāpahāraḥ syāt /

children.translated_text: Similarly:
By their scent, even <s>Airāvaṇa</s> and other elephants who bear the front rank of war-elephants have not been trained in friendliness toward [this elephant's] cheek,
The truth is that this bull among herds [displays] his lordship of the herd in his own reflections upon the jewel-walled surfaces of <s>Kacatrinayana</s>'s mountain.

And in cases like this, one should not say that it is an example of <s>ananvaya</s>. Here, because one half is being compared to another half, <s>upamā</s> (simile) is being directly expressed. For the essential nature of <s>ananvaya</s> is that the being <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> of a single entity culminates in the negation of any other standard of comparison—and that is what is directly expressed. But here this is not expressed verbally; rather, it is suggested. One should not say that what is merely suggested is rightly [classified as] directly stated. For [to do so] would be to encroach upon the domain of the <s>alaṅkāra</s> of the path of suggestion.

children.text:
ityatrāpyananvayo na vācyaḥ /
svīyapratibimbaireva sādṛśyapratītestadgandhasyāpyabhāvāt /
yadi nāma caitatpratīyeta tadapyasya pratīyamānatvaṃ syānna vācyatvam /

children.translated_text: By the principle stated above.

children.text: evaṃ ca tadekadeśenāvasitabhedena vetyapāsya upamānatayā kalpitena tenaiva sādṛśyamananvaya ityeva tvayā sūtraṇīyam /
children.translated_text: Thus, setting aside 'with a part of that, the difference being ascertained,' the <s>sūtra</s> should be formulated by you as: '<s>ananvaya</s> is similarity with that very [entity] imagined as the standard of comparison.'
He whose name, uttered with reverence by the assembly, as if swallowing their energies,
Even enemies applaud—that man is truly a man.

Here too, <s>ananvaya</s> should not be stated as directly expressed. Because the cognition of similarity arises only from one's own reflections, even the suggestion of that [self-comparison] is absent. Even if this were cognized, it would be in the mode of suggestion, not direct statement.

children.text:
ityatra puṃsaḥ puṃstvāropādananvayarūpakamiti yadanyairuktaṃ tadayuktam /
ekasyaiva vidhyanuvādabhāvenāvasthānādāropābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Here, what others have said—that the attribution of manliness to a man is <s>ananvayarūpaka</s> (self-comparison metaphor)—is incorrect. Because, since a single entity exists in the relation of injunction and restatement, there is no attribution [of something new].
START <s>Sūtra</s> 14:
When two [entities serve] alternately in that [relation of upamāna and upameya], it is <s>upameyopamā</s> (mutual simile). || 14 ||

children.text:
tacchabdenopamānopameyatvapratyavamarśaḥ /
paryāyo yaugapadyābhāvaḥ /
ata evātra vākyabhedaḥ /
iyaṃ ca dharmasya sādhāraṇye vastuprativastunirdeśe ca dvidhā /

children.translated_text: In the first case, for example:

children.text: 'khamiva jalaṃ jalamiva khaṃ haṃsaścandra iva haṃsa iva candraḥ /
children.translated_text: The sky is like the water, the water is like the sky; the <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) is like the moon, the moon is like the <s>haṃsa</s>;
The stars are in the form of <s>kumudas</s> (night-lotuses), the <s>kumudas</s> are in the form of stars.

By the word 'that' (<s>tad</s>), the reference is to the relation of being <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>. 'Alternately' means the absence of simultaneity. For this very reason, there is a difference of sentences here. And this [figure] is of two kinds: when the property is common, and when there is the specification of object and counter-object.
In the second case, for example:

children.text:
'sacchāyābhbhojavadanāḥ sacchāyavadanāmbujā /
vāpyo 'ṅganā ivābhānti yatra vāpya ivāṅganāḥ' //
children.translated_text: 'The pools with beautiful faces like lotuses, the pools with lotus-like faces — the pools shine like women and the women like pools.'
<s>RuAssC</s> 14:
[The commentary begins] with '<s>dvayoḥ</s>' and so on.
'<s>Dvayī</s>' refers to the pair of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison), not to the numeral two.
Therefore, [in the verse:] 'The face of the beloved, the lotus, and the moon — formerly there was a mutual relation of being standards of comparison for one another;
but now, when they are afflicted by old age, frost, and <s>Rāhu</s> respectively, a different mutual relation of mutual dissimilarity has arisen.'

children.text:
ityatra trayāṇāmapyupamānopameyatvaṃ sthitamasyā evāṅgam /
tacchabdeneti tasminnityanena /
yaugapadyābhāva iti kramarūpatvāt /
ata iti yaugapadyābhāvāt /
sa ca vākyabhedaḥ śābda ārthaśca /

children.translated_text: Of these, the verbal [division] is as follows:
'With dust raised by chariots and with elephants resembling clouds,
making the surface of the earth like the sky, and the sky like the surface of the earth.'

Here, the status of all three as both <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is established as a component of this very [figure]. 'By that word' means 'by that which is constant.' 'Absence of simultaneity' means because it has the nature of sequence. 'Therefore' means because of the absence of simultaneity. And that division of sentences is both verbal (<s>śābda</s>) and semantic (<s>ārtha</s>).

children.text: atra bhuvastalaṃ vyomeva kuvaṃnniti vākyapariniṣpatteḥ sphuṭa eva śābdo vākyabhedaḥ /

children.translated_text: The semantic [division] is as follows:
'From the refuge of your feet alone, both the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and devotion, being eternal,
beautiful with mutual resemblance, attain a state worthy of veneration.'
Here, since the sentence is completed as 'making the surface of the earth like the sky,' the verbal sentence-division is clearly evident.

children.text:
atra sphuṭe 'pi śābde ekavākyatve gaṅgābhaktivadbhaktiśca gaṅgāvad vandyetyastyevārtho vākyabhedaḥ /
asyāśco pamānāntaratiraskāra eva phalam /
ata evopameyenopamā ityasyā anvarthābhidhānam /
yatra punarupamānāntaratiraskāro na pratīyate tatra nāyamalaṅkāraḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: 'savitā vidhavati vidhurapi savitarati tathā dinanti yāminyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sun acts like the moon, and the moon acts like the sun; thus days act like nights,
and nights act like days, for one whose mind is overcome by happiness and sorrow.'

Here, even though there is clear verbal unity in a single sentence, there is indeed a semantic sentence-division in the sense that devotion is like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is like devotion, and both are worthy of veneration. The purpose of this [figure] is indeed the concealment of another standard of comparison. For this very reason, its name '<s>Upameyenopamā</s>' (comparison through the object of comparison) is fitting. But where concealment of another standard of comparison is not implied, this figure does not apply.

children.text: na hyatra vidhusavitrādīnāmupamānāntaratiraskaraṇaṃ vivakṣitaṃ kiṃ tu sukhaduḥkhavaśīkṛtamanasāmevaṃ viparītaṃ bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: For here the concealment of the moon, sun, and others as alternative standards of comparison is not intended; rather, [the meaning is] that for those whose minds are overcome by happiness and sorrow, things appear thus reversed.
<s>RuAssC</s> 14a:

children.text:
sādhāraṇya iti /
etacca dharmasya nirdeśānirdeśarūpapakṣadvayayāgūrakatvenoktam /
tatra nirdeśapakṣesādhāraṇyamasti tathāpyatra sakṛntirdeśenaivānugatatvāttadupalambhaḥ sphuṭa ityatra bhāvaḥ /
anirdeśapakṣe tu vāstavameva sādhāraṇyam /
yadanusāraṃ khamiva jalamityādyadāhṛtam /

children.translated_text: When the <s>dharma</s> is carried through [the comparison], as follows:

children.text: 'kamaleva matirmatiriva kamalā tanuriva vibhā vibheva tanuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The intellect is like a lotus, the lotus like the intellect; the body is like radiance, radiance like the body;

children.text: dharaṇīva dhṛtirdhṛtiriva dharaṇī satataṃ vibhāti bata yasya' //
children.translated_text: the earth is like steadfastness, steadfastness like the earth — thus always shines [the glory] of that person.'

[The commentary on] '<s>sādhāraṇya</s>' (commonality) and so on. This is stated with reference to the twofold classification of the <s>dharma</s> (property) as expressed and unexpressed. In the case of expression, commonality exists, and even so, since it is conveyed by a single mention, its apprehension is clear — this is the purport here. In the case of non-expression, however, the commonality is real. Following which, [the example] 'like water, like the sky' and so forth was cited.

children.text:
atra vibhātīti sakṛnnirdiṣṭam /
vastuprativastunirdeśaśca pūrvavadihāpi śuddhasāmānyarūpatvabimbapratibimbabhāvābhyāṃ dvidhā /
tatra bimbapratibimbabhāvo granthakṛtaivodāhṛtaḥ /
tatra hyabhbhojavadanayorbimbapratibimbabhāvaḥ /

children.translated_text: Pure generic identity is as follows:
'When both opened simultaneously with that charming [glance], both at once ascended to the scale of mutual comparison —
the eye with its quivering, rough pupil within, and the lotus with its trembling bee.'

Here '<s>vibhāti</s>' (shines) is mentioned only once. And the expression of object and counter-object here too, as before, is twofold through pure generic identity (<s>śuddhasāmānyarūpatva</s>) and the relation of image and reflection (<s>bimbapratibimbabhāva</s>). Of these, the image-reflection relation is illustrated by the author himself. For there, there is the image-reflection relation between the lotus and the face.

children.text:
(atra) pratpandamānapracalitatvena śuddhasāmānyarūpatvam /
tārakabhramarayostu bimbapratibimbabhāvaḥ /
unmeṣābhiprāyeṇa cānugāmiteti bhedatrayasyāpyetadudāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: Here, through the trembling and quivering, there is pure generic identity. But between the pupil and the bee, there is the image-reflection relation. And through the intention of opening, there is the carrying through [of the property] — thus this is an example of all three distinctions.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 15:
<s>Smaraṇam</s> (Remembrance) is the recollection of another object arising from the experience of a similar one. // <s>RuAss</s> 15 //
The 'other object' is indeed a similar one. Since there is no invariable concomitance, it is not inference (<s>anumāna</s>). For example:
'Seeing the child of surpassing splendor beyond gods and demons, of exactly similar form,
I remember <s>Raghunandana</s> (Rāma), holding his bow, when the son of <s>Kuśika</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>) was destroying the enemies of sacrifice.'
But recollection without similarity is not this figure. For example:
'Here on the bank of the <s>Godā</s>, having returned from the hunt, my fatigue dispelled by the breeze from the waves,
I remember sleeping in the <s>Vānīra</s>-tree bowers, with my head resting on your lap in privacy.'
Here, the attribution of the qualifications of the agent — such as having returned from the hunt — to the state of what is remembered rather than to the state of the rememberer, is inappropriate.
<s>RuAssC</s>_

children.text:
sadṛśeti /
vastvantaramiti smaryamāṇam /
sadṛśameveti /
sādṛśyasyobhayaniṣṭhatvāt /
ataśca smaryamāṇenānubhūyamānasya,anubhūyamānena vā smaryamāṇasya sādṛśyaparikalpanamayamalaṅkāraḥ /

children.translated_text: As it has been said:
'Just as the cognition of similarity produced by what is seen extends to what is remembered,
so too that [cognition] produced by what is remembered extends to what is seen.'

[The commentary on] '<s>sadṛśa</s>' (similar) and so on. 'Another object' refers to what is being remembered. 'Indeed a similar one' — because similarity belongs to both [the perceived and remembered]. Therefore, this figure consists in the attribution of similarity between the remembered and the perceived, or between the perceived and the remembered.
Thus.

children.text:
tatrādyaḥ prakāro granthakṛdudāharaṇe /
tatra hi śiśoreva raghunandanena sādṛśyaṃ vivakṣitam /

children.translated_text: The second type is as follows:
'On its bank, a pleasure-hill made of smooth sapphires with piled-up peaks, beautiful with its wrapping of golden plantains,

children.text: maṅgehinyāḥ priya iti sakhe cetasā kātareṇa prekṣyopāntasphuritataḍitaṃ tvāṃ tameva smarāmi' //
children.translated_text: O friend, dear to <s>Maṅgehinī</s> — seeing you with lightning flashing at your side, with anxious heart I remember that very [hill].'
Of these, the first type is [illustrated] in the author's example. For there, the similarity of the child with <s>Raghunandana</s> is intended.

children.text:
atrānubhūyamānena meghena smaryamāṇasya krīḍāśailasya sādṛśyaparikalpanam /
evaṃ cātra sādṛśyasyobhayasaṃbandhe 'pyanubhūyamānenaiva punaḥ smaryamāṇapratītirbhavatītyavaseyam /
nanu yadyevaṃ tatparasmātparapratipatteḥ kiṃ nedamanumānamityāśaṅkyāha-avinābhāvityādi /
avinībhāvastādātmyānnityasāhacaryāhuḥ /
anubhūyamānasmaryamāṇayośca tadabhāvaḥ /
śiśuraghunandanayoḥ sādṛśyaparikalpane cātiśacitasurātpurabhāvatvādidharmo 'nugāmitayā nirdiṣṭaḥ /
vastuprativastubhāvenāpi dharmasyāyaṃ bhavati /

children.translated_text: Of these, through pure generic identity, as follows:
'May <s>Nandaka</s> (the sword of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) bestow upon you dense joy, containing within it the reflection of exuberant beauty,
constantly causing <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) to remember the playful <s>Rādhā</s> through the sport in the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>.'

Here there is the attribution of similarity of the remembered pleasure-hill to the perceived cloud. Thus, here it should be understood that although similarity belongs to both, it is through the perceived alone that the cognition of the remembered arises. Now, if this is so, then since the cognition of one thing from another [arises], why is this not inference (<s>anumāna</s>)? — anticipating this objection, he says: 'absence of invariable concomitance' and so on. Invariable concomitance means constant co-occurrence due to identity of nature. And between the perceived and the remembered, that is absent. In attributing similarity between the child and <s>Raghunandana</s>, properties such as surpassing the splendor of gods are indicated as carrying through. This [figure] also occurs through the object-and-counter-object relation of the <s>dharma</s>.
Through the image-reflection relation, as follows:
'O beautiful one, gazing at the sky sealed by the full moon marked with an auspicious spot,
I remember you, with the smoke-streak of the wedding fire meeting your cheek.'
Here there is identity between the exuberance and the playfulness.

children.text:
atra meghalavadhūmalekhādīnāṃ bimbapratibimbabhāvaḥ /
etadeva sādṛśyanimittatvaṃ draḍhayituṃ pratyudāharati-sādṛśyamityādinā /
sadṛśānubhavābhāvāttatsmṛterna sādṛśyahetukatvam /
smartavyadaśābhāvitva iti /
smartavyadaśābhāvitvaṃ vācyaṃ sadanādṛśyetyarthaḥ /
ata eva vācyasyāvacanam /
smartṛdaśābhāvitvamityatyavācyasya vacanam /
yadyapi smartṛdaśāyāmatītatvāt kartṛviśeṣaṇānāṃ mṛgayānivṛttitvādīnāmapyatītakālāvacchinnānāṃ tadbhāvitvaṃ tathāpi vartamānakālāvacchinnasya smarturviśeṣaṇabhāvenopanibandhātteṣāṃ tadavacchinnataiva pratīyata iti yathoktameva dūṣaṇadvayaṃ yuktamiti sahṛdayā eva pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: Here there is the image-reflection relation between the auspicious spot and the smoke-streak, and so on. To strengthen this very point that similarity is the cause, he gives a counter-example with '<s>sādṛśya</s>' and so on. Because there is no experience of a similar thing, the remembrance there is not caused by similarity. 'Attribution to the state of what is remembered' — attribution to the state of what is remembered should be stated as what is visible; this is the meaning. Hence there is non-statement of what should be stated. 'Attribution to the state of the rememberer' — this is the statement of what should not be stated. Although in the state of the rememberer, the qualifications of the agent — such as having returned from the hunt — being delimited by past time also have the quality of belonging to that [past state], nevertheless, since they are connected as qualifications of the rememberer who is delimited by the present time, their belonging to that [present] delimitation alone is understood — thus the twofold criticism as stated is appropriate, and the sensitive critics alone are the authority.
<s>RuAss</s> 15/1:

children.text:
preyolaṅkārasya tu sādṛśyavyatiriktanimittotthāpitā smṛtirviṣayaḥ /
yathā
'aho kope 'pi kāntaṃ mukham' iti /

children.translated_text: Even there, when it is pervaded by <s>vibhāva</s> (determinants) and other [factors], and thus expressible only by its own words, as follows:
'Here on the bank of the <s>Godā</s>' and so on.

children.text: 'yairdṛṣṭo 'si tadā lalāṭapatitaprāsaprahāro yudhi sphītāsṛkstrutipāṭalīkṛtapurobhāgaḥ parān pātayan /
children.translated_text: 'When they saw you then in battle, struck by a spear fallen on the forehead, your front made red by the streaming of copious blood, felling enemies —

children.text: teṣāṃ duḥsahakāmadehadahanaprodbhatanetrānala- jvālālībharabhāsvare smaripāvastaṃ gataṃ kautukam' //
children.translated_text: for them, gazing at the blazing fire-flames of the eyes born from the unbearable burning of the body by <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), that wonder has now set.'
The <s>Preyolaṅkāra</s> (figure of endearment), however, has as its domain remembrance aroused by a cause other than similarity. For example: 'Ah, even in anger, the face is lovely.'

children.text:
ityādau sadṛśavastvantarānubhave 'śakyavastvantarakaraṇātmā viśeṣālaṅkāraḥ, kāraṇasya kriyāsāmānyātmano darśine 'pi saṃbhavāt /
matāntare kāvyaliṅgametat /
tadete sādṛśyāśrayeṇa bhedābhedatulyatvenālaṅkārā nirṇītāḥ" /
children.translated_text: In such cases, when there is experience of a similar other object, the special figure (<s>Viśeṣālaṅkāra</s>) consists in the production of an impossible other object, because the cause, being of the nature of action in general, is possible even for the observer. In another school, this is [considered] <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason). 'Thus these figures are determined as equal in terms of difference and non-difference based on similarity.'
<s>RuAssC</s> 15/1:

children.text:
pratyudāharaṇāntaramapi darśayati-preyolaṅkārasyetyādinā /
tuśabdaścārthe /
sādṛśyavyatiriktaṃ saṃskārādinimittam /
tatrāpīti /
evaṃ sthite 'pi satītyarthaḥ /
vibhāvādyāgūritatve preyolaṅkārasya sādṛśyavyatiriktanimittatotthāpitā smṛtirviṣaya iti saṃbandhaḥ /
tatra vibhāvādyāgūritatve smṛtiryathā-'aho kope 'pi kāntaṃ mukham' iti /
svaśabdamātrapratipādyatve yathodāhṛtam 'atrānugodam'- ityādau /
atra ca yathā preyolaṅkāro bhāvadhvaneścāsya yathā bhinnaviṣayatvaṃ tathāgra eva vakṣyāmaḥ /
evaṃ ca pratyudāharaṇadvayasyāpi prayojanaṃ bhinnaviṣayatvāt /
kvacicca sādṛśyanimittāpi smṛtiravākyārthatvānnāsminparyavasyatītyāha-'yairdṛṣṭo 'si-' ityādi /
vastvatra jayāpīḍadarśanam /
vastvantaraṃ tu bhagavallakṣaṇam /
atra tvaddarśanamabhilaṣatāṃ janānāṃ na tvaddarśanāvātpirevābhūdyāvatteṣāmasaṃbhāvyaṃ bhagavadrśanamapi jātamityaśakyavastvantarakaraṇam /
viśeṣālaṅkārasya hyaśakyavastvantarakaraṇaṃ rūpam, iha punaraśakyavastvantaradarśanaṃ sthitamiti kathamatra viśeṣālaṅkāra ityāśaṅkyāha-karaṇasyetyādi /
etacca gamyagamakabhāvamāśrityānyaiḥ kāvyaliṅgatvenābhyupagatamiti darśayitumāha-matāntara ityādi /
etaditi smaraṇam /
matāntara ityaudbhaṭe /

children.translated_text: As it has been said:
'When one thing that has been heard becomes the cause of the remembrance or experience of another,
that is called <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason).'

He also shows another counter-example with '<s>Preyolaṅkārasya</s>' and so on. The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) is used in the sense of 'and.' '<s>Sādṛśyavyatirikta</s>' means a cause such as mental impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) and the like, different from similarity. '<s>Tatrāpi</s>' means 'even when this is the case.' When pervaded by <s>vibhāva</s> and other [factors], the relation is: the domain of <s>Preyolaṅkāra</s> is remembrance aroused by a cause other than similarity. There, remembrance when pervaded by <s>vibhāva</s> and others is as [in the example]: 'Ah, even in anger, the face is lovely.' When expressible only by its own words, as illustrated: 'Here on the bank of the <s>Godā</s>' and so on. And here, just as there is the <s>Preyolaṅkāra</s>, and just as it has a different domain from <s>Bhāvadhvani</s> (suggested emotion), we shall explain later. Thus, both counter-examples serve a purpose because of [their] different domains. And sometimes, even remembrance caused by similarity does not culminate in this [figure] because it is not the sentence-meaning — he says with 'those who saw you' and so on. The real object here is the seeing of <s>Jayāpīḍa</s>. The other object is the form of the Lord. Here, for those who desire to see you, not only did the fulfillment from seeing you occur, but even the inconceivable vision of the Lord arose — this is the production of an impossible other object. For the form of <s>Viśeṣālaṅkāra</s> is the production of an impossible other object; here, however, what is established is the impossible seeing of another object — so how can <s>Viśeṣālaṅkāra</s> apply here? Anticipating this objection, he says: 'of the cause' and so on. And this, being accepted by others as <s>Kāvyaliṅga</s> based on the relation of signified and signifier, he shows by saying 'in another school' and so on. 'This' refers to <s>Smaraṇa</s> (remembrance). 'In another school' means in [the school of] <s>Udbhaṭa</s>.
Thus.

children.text:
iha punargamyagamakabhāvādanubhūyamānasmaryamāṇavyavahāro 'pi viśiṣyata iti pṛthagalaṅkāratayaitaduktam /
etadusaṃharannanyadavatārayati-tadeta ityādi /
eta ityupamādyāścatvāro 'laṅkārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, however, because of the relation of signified and signifier, the usage of perceived and remembered is also distinguished, and therefore this is stated as a separate figure. Concluding this and introducing another [topic], he says '<s>tadete</s>' and so on. 'These' refers to the four figures beginning with <s>Upamā</s> (simile).
START <s>Sūtra</s> 16:
When non-difference is predominant, in superimposition (<s>āropa</s>), when there is no denial of the object of superimposition, it is <s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor). // <s>RuAss</s> 16 //

children.text:
abhedasya prādhānyādbhedasya vastutaḥ sadbhāvaḥ /
anyatrānyāvāpa āropaḥ /
tasya viṣayaviṣayyavaṣṭabdhatvādviṣayasyāpahnave 'pahnutiḥ /
anyathā tu viṣayiṇā viṣayasya rūpavataḥ karaṇādrūpakam /
sādharmye tvanugatameva /
yadāhuḥ-
'upamaiva turobhūtabhedā rūpakamiṣyate' iti āropādabhede 'dhyavasāyaḥ prakṛṣyate iti paścāttanmūlālaṅkāravibhāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the predominance of non-difference, difference has real existence [in fact]. The placing of one thing upon another is superimposition (<s>āropa</s>). Since that [superimposition] is anchored in both object and substratum, denial of the object [of superimposition] is <s>Apahṇuti</s> (concealment). Otherwise, the fashioning of the object, which has form, by the substratum, is <s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor). In [the case of] common properties, it is simply carried through. As they say: '<s>Upamā</s> (simile) itself, with difference thoroughly effaced, is considered <s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor).' From superimposition, when non-difference is [established], determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is intensified — thus the subsequent classification of figures based on that [principle].
<s>RuAssC</s> 16:

children.text:
saṃpratīti /
bhedābhedatulyatvāśrayālaṅkārānantaramabhedapradhānaṃ lakṣayitumucitatvādavasaraprātpāvityarthaḥ /
tatra tāvatprathamaṃ rūpakaṃ lakṣyati-abhedaprādhānya ityādi /
vastuta iti /
na tu pratītitaḥ /
sadbhāva iti /
pradhānāprādhānayoḥ saṃbandhiśabdatvāt /
anyatrānyāvāpa āropa iti /
anyatreti prakṛte mukhādau /
anyasyetyaprakṛtasya candrādeḥ /
sa ca sāmānādhikaraṇyena vaiyādhikaraṇyena ca nirdeśe bhavati /
na tu sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdeśa eva saḥ /
evaṃ hi-'yātāḥ kaṇādatāṃ kecit' ityādāvāropasadbhāve 'pi na sāmānādhikaraṇyamastītyavyātpiḥ syāt /
āryaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyamastīti nāvyātpirita cet, na /
bhinnayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdeśo[a. ra. sū.26]hyāropalakṣaṇam /
na ca tadatra nirdiṣṭam /
vaiyadhikaraṇyena nirdeśāttasyārtāvaseyatvāt /
arthāvasāyo nirdeśaśca naikaṃ rūpam /
vipratiṣedhāt /
nīlaropaḥ prasajyata ityativyātpiḥ syāt /
na cārope bhinnayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdeśa ucyata ityasaṃbhavo 'pi /
iti na niravadyametadāparopalakṣam /
yadyevaṃ tatkiṃ śabde śabdāntaramarthe vārthāntaramāropyata iti ced brumaḥ /
tatra na śabde śabdāntarāropaḥ /
mukhaśabdādeścandraśabdādirūpatvenāpratīteranyonyaviviktasvāntarūpolambhāditi bhavadbhirevoktatvāt /
kiṃ tvarther'thāntarāropaḥ /
sa ca prayojanaparatayā tathā nirdeśyate na bhrāntyā /
ata eva hyuktikāyāmiva rajatāropo na mukhe candrāropaḥ /
tasya svarasata evotthānena bhramarūpatvāt /
ata eva tatrāropaviṣayasyāropyamāṇenācchrāditatvena pratītiḥ /
iha punarjānāna eva kaścicandraviviktaṃmukhaṃ tatra prayojanaparatayā candrārthamāropayati /
ata evoktamāropaviṣayānapahnava iti /
bhavadbhirapyanenaivāśayena 'pratipādanabhrāmo 'yaṃ na bhrāntā pratipattirityādyuktam /
tasyetyāropasya viṣayaḥ prakṛtaḥ viṣayī cāprakṛtaḥ /
tābhyāmavaṣṭabdhatvaṃ yuktatvam /
yaduktam-'sāropānyā tu yatroktau viṣayī viṣayastathā' iti /
children.translated_text: Now the understanding [is as follows]: After the ornaments based on difference, non-difference, and equality, since it is appropriate to define that which has predominance of non-difference, the meaning is that the occasion has arrived. There, first, <s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is defined — beginning with 'predominance of non-difference' and so on. 'In reality' means not merely in cognition. 'Existence' — because the terms 'primary' and 'secondary' are relational words. 'Superimposition of one upon another' — 'upon another' means upon the subject at hand, such as a face; 'of another' means of an unrelated thing such as the moon. And this superimposition occurs through both co-referential and non-co-referential expression. It is not the case that superimposition occurs only through co-referential expression. For otherwise, in cases like 'some have attained the state of <s>Kaṇāda</s>,' even though superimposition exists, there would be no co-referential expression, leading to under-extension. If one objects that there is indeed co-referential expression, no — [the definition states] 'expression of two different things through co-reference' [<s>Alaṃkāra Rahasya Sūtra</s> 26] is the characteristic of superimposition. But that is not expressed here, since it must be inferred from the non-co-referential expression. Inferring the meaning and expressing it are not the same thing, because they are contradictory. There would be over-extension in that even blue-ness could be superimposed. Nor is there impossibility in saying that in superimposition two different things are expressed through co-reference. Thus this definition of superimposition is not flawless. If so, then is a word superimposed upon another word, or a meaning upon another meaning? We say: there is no superimposition of one word upon another word, because you yourselves have stated that the word 'face' etc. is not cognized as having the form of the word 'moon' etc., and each is apprehended in its own distinct inner form. Rather, there is superimposition of one meaning upon another meaning. And this is expressed thus purposefully, not through error. Therefore, just as in the case of shell-silver, the superimposition of silver is not like the superimposition of the moon upon the face, for that [shell-silver illusion] arises spontaneously and has the nature of error. Hence in that case, the object of superimposition is concealed by the superimposed thing in cognition. But here, someone who fully knows the face as distinct from the moon, purposefully superimposes the meaning of the moon upon the face. Therefore it has been said 'without concealment of the object of superimposition.' You yourselves too, with this very intent, have said 'this is an error of expression, not an erroneous cognition' and so on. 'Of that' — the object of superimposition is the subject (<s>prakṛta</s>), and the superimposed thing is the non-subject (<s>aprakṛta</s>). Being grounded in both of them constitutes propriety. As has been stated: 'But another [figure] with superimposition is where both the superimposed and the locus are mentioned.'
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> Commentary, verse 16a:]

children.text:
anyatheti /
anapahnave /
evamanenāpahnutirūpakayorbhedo 'pyuktaḥ /
āhuriti daṇḍyādayaḥ /
ataśca sādharmyasadbhāvāttadanuyāyubhedatrayānuprāṇitatvamapyasya jñeyam /

children.translated_text: For example:
'The ear of the elephant of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Cupid) — a conch marked with dark <s>dāna</s>-water (ichor),

children.text: vyomānokahapuṣpagucchamalibhiḥ saṃchādyamānodaraṃ paśyaitacchraśinaḥ sudhāsahacaraṃ bimbaṃ kalaṅkāṅkitam' //
children.translated_text: a pillow of <s>Rati</s> (Love's consort) stained with a mass of collyrium — behold this disc of the moon, companion of nectar, marked with the dark spot, its belly covered by flower-clusters from the sky-garden by bees!'

'Otherwise' means without concealment. Thus by this, the difference between <s>Apahnuti</s> (denial) and <s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor) has also been stated. 'They say' refers to <s>Daṇḍin</s> and others. And therefore, since similarity exists, it should be known that this [figure] is also animated by the three types of sub-divisions following that [similarity].

children.text:
atra kalaṅkasya dānāmbvādibhiḥ pratibimbanam /
lācchritatvāṅkitatvayoḥ śuddhasāmānyarūpatvam /
sudhārahacaratvasyānugatatvādanugāmiteti bhedatrayānuprāṇitatvam /
anena ca sādṛśyanimitta evāropo rūpakamityuktaṃ bhavati /
keṣāñcidapi saṃbandhāntaraheturapyāropo rūpakāṅgameveti matam /
yadāhālaṅkārabhāṣyakāraḥ-'lakṣaṇāparamārthaṃ yāvatā rūpakasvarūpam' ityupakramya 'sāropānyā ca sādṛśyādvā saṃbandhāntarādvā' ityādi /

children.translated_text: That is illustrated as follows:
'A morsel of nectar, a mass of beauty, a fountain of the juice of delight, a cart of whiteness, a reservoir of moonlight, a peak of snow,

children.text: manasijavṛsī śṛṅgāraśrīvimānamaho nu bho niravadhisukhaśraddhā dṛṣṭeḥ kṛtī mṛgaketanaḥ' //
children.translated_text: a bull of <s>Manasija</s> (the Mind-born, i.e., Cupid), the aerial palace of the splendor of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) — ah indeed! an unlimited faith of happiness for the eyes, a meritorious one — the Moon!'

Here, the dark spot (<s>kalaṅka</s>) is reflected through <s>dāna</s>-water (ichor) and so on. The states of being marked and stained have the nature of pure similarity. The companionship with nectar (<s>sudhā</s>) has the nature of concomitance, being a following attribute — thus it is animated by the three types of sub-divisions. And by this it is stated that superimposition based on similarity alone constitutes <s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor). Some hold the view that superimposition caused by other relations too is merely a limb of <s>Rūpaka</s>. As the author of the <s>Alaṃkārabhāṣya</s> has said, beginning with 'The essential nature of <s>Rūpaka</s> is the ultimate meaning of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification)' and then 'And another [type] with superimposition arises either from similarity or from another relation' and so on.

children.text:
atrendurūpe kāraṇe kāryapupāyāḥ śraddhāyā āropaḥ /
granthakṛtāpyalaṅkārānusāriṇyā-atra 'śraddhāhetutvācchraddhe' tyabhidhāya 'viśeṣaṇaikasminnanekavastvāropānmālārūpakamityabhidadhatāyameva pakṣaḥ kaṭākṣitaḥ /
nanu cādhyavasāyagarbhāṇāmapyalaṅkārāṇāmabhedaprādhānye sati prathamāropagarbhā alaṅkārāḥ kimiti lakṣitā ityāśaṅkyāha-āropādityādi /
children.translated_text: Here, there is superimposition of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) — which is an effect — upon the moon, which is a cause in terms of form. The author of the treatise too, following the [tradition of] poetic ornaments, having stated 'because it is the cause of faith, it is faith [itself],' and then declaring 'because of the superimposition of many things upon a single qualifier, it is <s>Mālārūpaka</s> (garland-metaphor),' has glanced at this very position. Now, if one objects: even among ornaments that contain determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), when there is predominance of non-difference, why are only those ornaments containing primary superimposition defined? — anticipating this, he says 'from superimposition' and so on.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, verse 16/1:]

children.text:
idaṃ tu niravayavaṃ sāvayavaṃ paramparitamiti trividham /
ādyaṃ kevalaṃ māvārūpakañcate dvidhā /
dvitīyaṃ samastavastuviṣayamekadeśavivarti ceti dvidhaiva /
tṛtīyaṃ śliṣṭaśabdanibandhanatvena dvividhaṃ satpratyekaṃ kevalamālārūpakatvāccaturvidham /
tadevamaṣṭau rūpakabhedāḥ /
anye tū pratyekaṃ vākyoktasamāsoktādibhedāḥ saṃbhavanti te 'nyato draṣṭavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, this [<s>Rūpaka</s>] is threefold: without parts (<s>niravayava</s>), with parts (<s>sāvayava</s>), and chained (<s>paramparita</s>). The first is of two kinds: simple (<s>kevala</s>) and garland (<s>mālā</s>) <s>Rūpaka</s>. The second is also of two kinds: pertaining to the whole object (<s>samastavastuviṣaya</s>) and partially transformative (<s>ekadeśavivarti</s>). The third, being based on words with double meaning (<s>śliṣṭaśabda</s>), is of two kinds, and each of those is of two kinds as simple and garland <s>Rūpaka</s>, thus fourfold. Thus there are eight varieties of <s>Rūpaka</s>. Other sub-divisions such as statement-based (<s>vākyokta</s>), compound-based (<s>samāsokta</s>), etc. may exist for each, but they should be examined elsewhere.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> Commentary, verse 16/1:]

children.text:
caśabdo 'nyālaṅkārāpekṣayā bhedasamuccārthaḥ /
viṣayadyotakastuśabdaḥ /
avayavebhyo niṣkrānta āropyamāṇo yatra tattathoktam /
sahāvayavairāropyamāṇo vartate yatra tattathoktam /
paramparayaikasya māhātmyādaparasyārūpaṇātvamāyātaṃ yatra tattathoktam /
ādyamiti niravayavam /
mālā caikasyānekasya vānekāropādbhavati /
evaṃ paramparitatvena mālārūpakaṃ jñeyam /
dvitīyamiti sāvayavam /
samastamāropyamāṇātmakaṃ vastvabhidhāyā viṣayo yatra tattathoktam /
ekadeśa āropaviṣayāṇām; arthastadātmaka evāropyamāṇaprayojanapratipādanāya tadrūpatayā vivar tate pariṇamati yatra tattathoktam /
tṛtīyamiti paramparitam /
yadyapi śleṣanibandhane 'sminguṇakriyātmakadharmanibandhanasya sādṛśyasyāsaṃbhava eva tathāpi śabdamātrakṛtamevābhedādhyavasāyataḥ sādṛśyaṃ grāhyam /
anya iti etadbhedāṣṭakavyatiriktāḥ /
saṃbhavantīti cirantanālaṅkāragrantheṣveva /
na punarlakṣyanta iti bhāvaḥ /
tatra hi teṣāṃ tattve 'pyetadbhedāṣṭakakṛtameva vaicitryaṃ pratīyate /

children.translated_text: And for example:

children.text: 'pādaḥ kūrmo 'tra yaṣṭirbhujagapatirayaṃ bhājanaṃ bhūtadhātrī tailāpūrāḥ samudrāḥ kanakagirirayaṃ vṛttavartiprarohaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The foot is a tortoise here, the staff is <s>Bhujagapati</s> (the Serpent-King), the vessel is the Earth-bearer, the oil-fillings are the oceans, the golden mountain is the wick-holder growing round,

children.text: arciścaṇḍāṃśuruccairgaganamalinimā kajjalaṃ dahyamānā vairiśreṇī pataṅgā jvalati narapate tvatpratāpapradīpaḥ' //
children.translated_text: the flame is the fierce-rayed Sun, the sky's darkness is the lampblack being consumed, the enemy-hosts are the moths — O King, your <s>Pratāpa</s> (valor)-lamp blazes!'

The word 'ca' (and) is for the purpose of enumerating distinctions with respect to other ornaments. The word 'tu' (but) indicates the subject matter. Where the superimposed entity emerges free from its parts, that is called thus [niravayava]. Where it exists together with its parts being superimposed, that is called thus [sāvayava]. Where, through a chain, the attribution of one leads to the attribution of another through its prominence, that is called thus [paramparita]. 'The first' means the partless one. A garland (<s>mālā</s>) arises from multiple superimpositions upon one or upon many [subjects]. Thus garland-<s>Rūpaka</s> should be understood through the chained nature as well. 'The second' means the one with parts. Where the object consisting entirely of superimposed things is described and then the locus [is stated], that is called thus [samastavastuviṣaya]. Where one part of the objects of superimposition — whose meaning is identical with them — transforms, i.e., changes into that form for the purpose of conveying the superimposed thing's purpose, that is called thus [ekadeśavivarti]. 'The third' means the chained one. Although in one based on <s>Śleṣa</s> (double meaning), similarity based on quality, action, or essential attribute is indeed impossible, nevertheless, similarity created merely by the word itself should be accepted on the basis of the determination of non-difference. 'Others' means those beyond this eightfold division. 'They exist' means in ancient treatises on poetic ornaments. The implication is that they are not defined [separately here], for in those [older works], even though those [sub-types] truly exist, the variety is perceived as being produced by this very eightfold division.
Here, even though there is statement-based expression (<s>vākyārthokta</s>), the variety is produced precisely by the whole-object scope (<s>samastavastuviṣaya</s>).
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, verse 16/2:]
Examples in order:

children.text: 'dāse kṛtāgāsi bhavatyucitaḥ prabhūṇāṃ pādaprahāra iti sundari nāsmi dūye /
children.translated_text: 'O beautiful one, the kick of the foot is proper for masters toward an offending servant — so I do not grieve;

children.text: udyatkaṭhorapulakāṅkurakaṇṭakāgrair- yatkhidyate tava padaṃ nanu sā vyathā me' //
children.translated_text: rather, that pain is mine, because your foot is hurt by the sharp tips of the thorn-like erect and hard <s>pulaka</s> (goosebumps)!'

'A new stream of nectar for the sacrificial gods, a sickle for cutting darkness, the face of a <s>Cakravāka</s> bird distressed [by separation from] the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a creeper of lotus-stalks,

children.text: dvirbhāvaḥ smarakārmukasya kimapi prāṇeśvarīsāgasā- māśātanturudañcati pratipadi prāleyabhānostanuḥ' //
children.translated_text: a doubling of <s>Smara's</s> (Cupid's) bow — something indescribable through the beloved's transgression — a thread of hope rises on the first day of the bright fortnight: the body of the snow-rayed [Moon]!'
'In the broad leaf-plate of the sky's surface, with abundant food of a mass of radiance brilliant as <s>Kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers,
smeared with the thick buffalo-milk of the waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — I have eaten, O King, [this feast of] the <s>Kalikāla</s> (dark age)!'
'This line of the dark <s>Tamāla</s> (tree) forest on the border, which is the sword-flesh-creeper of your mountain, appears with the luster of the night,

children.text: indutviṣo yudhi haṭhena tavārikīrtī- rānīya yatra ramate taruṇaḥ pratāpaḥ' //
children.translated_text: where your youthful <s>Pratāpa</s> (valor) delights, having forcefully brought in battle the fame of your enemy, [white as] moonbeams!'
In '<s>kṣitibhṛta</s>' (mountain/king) here, the word has double meaning (<s>śliṣṭa</s>).
The chained type (<s>paramparita</s>):

children.text: 'kiṃ padmamya ruciṃ na hanti nayanānandaṃ vidhatte na vā vṛddhiṃ vā jhaṣaketanasya kurute nālokamātreṇa kim /
children.translated_text: 'Does not this lotus destroy beauty, or does it not bestow delight to the eyes, or does it not increase [the power of] the Fish-bannered one (<s>Jhaṣaketana</s>, i.e., Cupid) by mere sight?

children.text: vaktrendau tava satyayaṃ yadaparaḥ śītāṃśurabhyudgato darpaḥ syādamṛtena cidiha tadapyastyeva bimbādhare' //
children.translated_text: When in the moon that is your face, this other cool-rayed one (Moon) has risen, there would be pride through nectar — and if so, that too indeed exists in your <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip!'

Here, the attribution of the lip-nectar (<s>adharāmṛta</s>) as <s>pīyūṣa</s> (divine nectar) is a <s>Rūpaka</s> based on a word with double meaning (<s>śliṣṭaśabda</s>), caused by the metaphorical identification of the face with the moon.
'O swan of the lake of learned minds, O lotus that blooms at the sun of enemy-destruction, O fire of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> that accepts the offering in the sacrifice of the deep-blue-and-red [battle],

children.text: satyaprītividhānadakṣa vijayaprāgbhāvabhīma prabho sāmrājyaṃ varavīra vatsaraśataṃ vairiñcamuccaiḥ kriyāḥ' //
children.translated_text: O one skilled in bestowing the gift of truth and love, O <s>Bhīma</s> in the prior existence of victory, O Lord! May you perform the lofty rites of <s>Brahmā</s> for a hundred years of sovereignty, O best of heroes!'

children.text: atra tvameva haṃsa ityāropaṇapūrvako mānasameva mānasamityādyāropa iti śliṣṭaśabdaṃ mālāparamparitam /
children.translated_text: Here, the chain of superimpositions with double-meaning words (<s>śliṣṭaśabda</s>) constitutes garland-chained <s>Rūpaka</s> (<s>mālāparamparita</s>): 'you yourself are the swan' is a prior superimposition, and 'the lake [of minds] is indeed the lake' and so on are subsequent superimpositions.
'I seek refuge with my mind, speech, and body in the compassionate world-lord, <s>Jagannātha</s>,
the pair of feet of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), which is a raft for crossing the ocean of birth, old age, and death!'
'The couch of royal fortune, a wave of the ocean of valor made of green gems, a cloth-strip of the <s>dāna</s>-water (ichor) of the fierce victory-elephant that has broken the enemy's lineage,

a dark rain-cloud [made of] the blue water [flowing from] the swan of the fame of <s>Murala</s>'s lord, trembling from the terror of battle — the sword of the sovereign of <s>Mālava</s> is victorious, O cleaver of the earth!'

children.text:
atra kṣmāsauvidalla iti paramparitamapyekadeśavivarti /
evamādayo 'nye 'pi bhedā leśataḥ sūcitā eva /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>kṣmāsauvidalla</s>' (cleaver of the earth) is chained (<s>paramparita</s>) and also partially transformative (<s>ekadeśavivarti</s>). Thus these and other varieties have been indicated in brief.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> Commentary, verse 16/2:]

children.text:
krameṇeti yathoddeśam /
dvirbhāvaḥ smarakārmukasyetyatra ca vākyārthaparyālācanayendoḥ smarakārmutvāropapratīteḥ kuṭilatvādyanekadharmanimittaṃ sādṛśyameva saṃbandhaḥ /
indoścaikasya bahava āropā iti mālārūpakam /

children.translated_text: But for the case of many [subjects], for example:

children.text: 'bāhū bālamṛṇālike kucitaṭī māṇikyaharmyaṃ rater- muktāśailaśilā nitambaphalakaṃ hāsaḥ sudhānirjharaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Her arms are young lotus-stalks, the surface of her breasts is a ruby palace of <s>Rati</s> (Love), her pearl-mountain-stone is the slab of her hips, her laughter is a waterfall of nectar,

children.text: vācaḥ kokilakūcitāni cikurāścetobhavaścāmaraṃ tasyāstrastakuraṅgaśāvakadṛśaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na lokottaram' //
children.translated_text: her words are the cooing of cuckoos, her locks are the fly-whisks of the Mind-born (<s>Cetobhava</s>, i.e., Cupid) — of that woman with eyes like startled fawn-calves, what is not extraordinary?'

'In order' means as per the enumeration. In the verse 'a doubling of <s>Smara's</s> bow,' when the sentential meaning is examined, the superimposition of the moon as <s>Smara's</s> (Cupid's) bow is cognized based on similarity grounded in multiple properties such as curvature and so on. And since there are many superimpositions upon the single moon, it is <s>Mālārūpaka</s> (garland-metaphor).
For example:

children.text: 'netre puṣkarasodare madhumatī vāṇī vipāśā mati- śceto yāti nadīnatāṃ kalayate śoṇatvamasyādharaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Her eyes are <s>Puṣkara</s> (lotus/a sacred lake), her speech is <s>Madhumatī</s> (sweet/a river name), her intellect is <s>Vipāśā</s> (unfettered/a river name), her mind flows like a river, her lip assumes the redness of <s>Śoṇa</s> (the Śoṇa river),

children.text: cāritraṃ nanu pāpasūdanamaho māmeṣa tīrthāśrayaḥ snātuṃ vācchati bhūpatiḥ paramitīvoṣṇodakaṃ vastragati' //
children.translated_text: her conduct indeed destroys sin — ah, this king, being a sacred-ford-dweller, wishes to bathe [in these rivers]! Such is the hot water [of tears] and the cloth [offered at the ford]!'
Here, from multiple superimpositions upon multiple [subjects], it is a garland of <s>Rūpaka</s> (<s>rūpakamālā</s>). And this is also seen as based on <s>Śleṣa</s> (double meaning).

children.text: atrānekeṣāṃ śliṣṭā aneka āropitī iti śliṣṭārtharūpakamālā /
children.translated_text: Here, the multiple superimpositions upon multiple [subjects] with double-meaning words constitute a garland of <s>Rūpaka</s> with double-meaning (<s>śliṣṭārtharūpakamālā</s>).
In the verse beginning with '<s>ābhāti</s>,' some consider it <s>Samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) — therefore a different illustrative verse is cited.
For example:
'Gathering the flower-beauty of your wisdom, incomparably fragrant and sweet, which has blossomed in the garden-rows of your sense-fields,

children.text: bhavodyāne bhaktyā tava saha viśeṣollasitayā viharttu vyagraḥ syāmanusṛkatavive kapriyasakhaḥ' //
children.translated_text: I would eagerly sport in your garden with devotion, specially delighted, like a bee, your dear companion!'
Since the superimposition of <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion) as the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) is non-verbal, it is the partially transformative type (<s>ekadeśavivarti</s>).
The reading '<s>pīyūṣasya adharāmṛtena śliṣṭaśabdanirūpaṇam</s>' (attribution of nectar through lip-nectar with double-meaning words) should be understood as a corruption introduced by a scribe.

children.text:
adharāmṛtasya hi pūyūṣeṇa nirūpaṇamatra sthitam /
ataśca
'adharāmṛtasya pīyūṣeṇa śliṣṭaśabdanirūpam' iti pāṭho grāhyaḥ /
atra ca pīyūṣavadamṛtaśabdasyādhararasāvācakatvamanye manyanta ityudārahaṇāntaramudāhriyate /

children.translated_text: For example:
'O one who illuminated the three worlds with extraordinary and supreme light,
"Is there anyone, O god, who does not praise you, the pearl-jewel of a noble lineage?"

For indeed, the attribution here is of the lip-nectar (<s>adharāmṛta</s>) through <s>pīyūṣa</s> (divine nectar). Therefore the reading to be accepted is '<s>adharāmṛtasya pīyūṣeṇa śliṣṭaśabdanirūpam</s>' (attribution of lip-nectar through <s>pīyūṣa</s> with double-meaning). And here, some consider that, like <s>pīyūṣa</s>, the word <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) also does not denote lip-juice — therefore another illustrative verse is cited.

children.text:
atra muktāratnamittayaropapūrvako vaṃśa eva vaṃśa ityāropa iti śliṣṭaśabdaṃ kevalaparamparitam /
vidvadityādo haṃsarūpaṇāmahātmyānmānasarūpeṇeti paramparitam /
evamarṇavarūpaṇā taraṇḍāropasya heturiti paramparitam /
paryaṅka ityatraikasya bahava āropā iti mālāparamparitam /

children.translated_text: But for multiple [subjects], for example:
"<s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) is the crescent-moon-mark on the chest of the earth-bearer; <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>'s (Śiva's) throat is the cloud, and the lightning is <s>Gaurī</s>;

children.text: śakrākṣipaśvākararājahaṃsī śacī ca vo yacchratu maṅgalāni' //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>'s (Indra's) eye is the cow, and the royal swan is <s>Śacī</s> -- may she grant you auspiciousness!"

Here, '<s>muktāratna</s>' (pearl-jewel) is the basis of superimposition upon '<s>vaṃśa</s>' (lineage/bamboo) itself as '<s>vaṃśa</s>' -- thus it is <s>śliṣṭaśabda</s> (punning word) with simple chaining. In 'vidvat' etc., through the glory of the superimposition of the swan-form, [it is] chained as 'in the form of <s>Mānasa</s>' (lake/mind). Similarly, the superimposition of color-form is the cause of the <s>taraṇḍa</s> (raft) superimposition -- thus it is chained. In '<s>paryaṅka</s>' (couch), multiple superimpositions upon a single [subject] constitute a chained garland.

children.text:
atra bahūnāmanekāropātparamparitamālā /
evamādaya iti /
paramparitamapyekadeśavivartīttyevaṃprakāraḥ /
sūcitā iti /
etatpradarśanādeva /
tataśca sāvayavaṃ dvividhamapi śliṣṭaṃ dṛśyate /

children.translated_text: Among these, the one pertaining to the entire object, for example:
"With parting lip-petals, with abundantly thick filaments of gleaming tooth-edges,
In the moonlight of joy, a smile was [produced] by the <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus), exhaling a sweet fragrance."

Here, because of multiple superimpositions upon many [subjects], it is a chained garland. 'And so forth' -- thus it is stated. The chained [type] too is a variety of <s>ekadeśavivartī</s> (partially transformed) -- of such a nature. 'Indicated' -- by this very demonstration. And thus, the composite type is seen in two varieties as <s>śliṣṭa</s> (blended) with its parts.
In <s>Setubandha</s> 416:
('With parting lip-petals, with abundantly thick filaments of gleaming tooth-edges,
In the moonlight of joy, a smile was [produced] by the <s>kumuda</s>, exhaling a sweet fragrance.')
The <s>ekadeśavivartī</s> (partially transformed) type, for example:

"Studded with half-scattered star-pearls, anointed with moonlight-sandal-water, with the hand of the venerable sage holding a <s>karaka</s> (water vessel) -- a washed <s>ākāśaliṅga</s> (sky-<s>liṅga</s>);

children.text: toyādhāre pratīci cyutavati dinakṛdvimbanirmālyapadme tasyārcāṇḍarīkaṃ vyadhita himakaraṃ satvaraṃ mūrdhni kālaḥ' //
children.translated_text: When in the west the rain-cloud departed, and the sun-disc became a discarded-offering lotus, then <s>Kāla</s> (Time) swiftly placed the moon as a worship-offering upon his head."
Here, the <s>śliṣṭatva</s> (blended nature) belongs to <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus).

children.text:
atra kālaviṣaye pūjakādirāropyamāṇo na śābda ityekadeśavivartitvam /
toyādhārasya samudranirmālyodakabhāṇḍavācakatvākatvācchrilaṣṭatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the case of <s>Kāla</s> (Time), the worshipper etc. being superimposed is not verbal -- hence the <s>ekadeśavivartitva</s> (partially transformed nature). The word '<s>toyādhāra</s>' (water-bearer) denotes both the ocean and a water vessel for discarded offerings -- hence the <s>śliṣṭatva</s> (blended nature).
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 16/2a:]

children.text: kvaciccābhedameva draḍhayituṃ virṣāyaṇo niṣedhapūrvamāropyamāṇatvena tadīyasya vā bhedahetordharmasya hānikalpanenādhikyena vā dṛḍhāropatvenāpīdaṃ dṛśyate /

children.translated_text: In order, for example:
"She who is dear to strife, who always shows contempt even to elders and respected relatives,

children.text: jāyā nijā yā nanu saiva kṛtyā kṛtyā na kṛtyā saralasya dhārmeḥ' //
children.translated_text: His own wife -- she is indeed a <s>kṛtyā</s> (sorceress); a <s>kṛtyā</s> is not a <s>kṛtyā</s> [compared] to an honest man's wife."

And sometimes, in order to strengthen the non-difference itself, through superimposition preceded by denial of what is to be superimposed according to <s>Viṣāyaṇa</s>'s [method], or by the diminishment of the property that causes difference, or by excess, this is also seen as firm superimposition.

children.text:
atra kṛtyā niṣedhapūrvaṃ jāyāyāmāropitā /
tanniṣedhena hi jāyāyā kṛtyayā dāḍharyena sāmyaṃ pratīyate /
kṛtyā tathā na svakarmaṇi vyāpriyate yatheyaṃ tatkarmaṇīti hyatra vākyārthaḥ /
atra ca yadanye viśeṣālaṅkāramāhustadabhedālaṅkāranirākaṇādeva nirākṛtamiti na punarāyasyate /

children.translated_text: Through diminishment, for example:
"Of the forest-dwelling women's companions, with brilliance clinging to the laps of cave-dwellings,
Where the herbs at night become lamps of love-making, unfilled with oil."

Here, '<s>kṛtyā</s>' (sorceress) is superimposed upon the wife through denial. For by denying [that the actual kṛtyā is a kṛtyā], the firm identity of the wife with the <s>kṛtyā</s> is understood. The sentence-meaning here is: the <s>kṛtyā</s> does not engage in her own activity as this [wife] does in that [destructive] activity. And here, what others call the figure <s>viśeṣālaṅkāra</s> (distinction) has already been refuted through the rejection of the <s>abhedālaṅkāra</s> (non-difference figure), so it is not labored over again.
Through excess, for example:
"He is indeed the fourth sacred fire; or even the fifth <s>Āmnāya</s> (Veda);

children.text: api vā jaṅgamaṃ tīrthaṃ dharmo vā mūrtisaṃcaraḥ' //
children.translated_text: Or even a mobile <s>tīrtha</s> (holy place); or <s>dharma</s> itself moving in bodily form."
Here, through 'unfilled with oil,' there is the device of diminishment.
Here, the excess lies in the property of being the fourth etc.
"Of the miser and the sword -- [both] with firmly clenched fist, seated in a sheath, and naturally dirty --
The difference between the miser and the sword is merely in appearance."

children.text:
ityatrāpi dṛḍharopameva rūpakaṃ jñeyam /
atra hi kṛpāṇasyeti samuccīyamānatvenanirdeśācchrābdasyāropasyāpratīterapyākāramātreṇa bhedasyoktervākyārthaparyālocanamāhātmyātvariśiṣṭasamastadharmāntarasadbhāvābhyanujñānāpyaryavasāne dāḍharyena viṣayaviṣayiṇorabhedapratipattiḥ /
saiva ca rūpakasatattvamiti pūrvamevoktam /
anye 'pi bhedāḥ svayamevābhyahyodāhāryāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here too, this should be understood as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) with firm superimposition. For here, because '<s>kṛpāṇasya</s>' (of the sword) is mentioned as being conjoined [with the miser], verbal superimposition is not apprehended; yet by merely stating difference in appearance alone, through the power of sentence-meaning contemplation, the acknowledgment of all other distinguished common properties [leads to], at the conclusion, firm apprehension of non-difference between the subject and the object of comparison. And that alone is the true nature of <s>rūpaka</s> -- as was stated before. Other varieties too should be illustrated by oneself from one's own [examples].
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 16/3:]
For example:
"A desert of the waters of generosity, a wall-painting of the sky of good conduct, a dark fourteenth night of the moonlight of virtue, a dog's-tail-tuft of the yoga of straightforwardness --

children.text: yaireṣāpi durāśayā kaliyuge rājāvalī sevitā teṣāṃ śūlini bhaktimātrasulabhe sevā kiyatkauśalam' //
children.translated_text: Those by whom even this ill-intentioned line of kings in the <s>Kali</s> age was served -- for them, when the Trident-bearer (<s>Śiva</s>) is obtainable by devotion alone, what skill is there in such service?"
This is also seen through dissimilarity.

children.text: atra cāropyamāṇasya dharmitvādāviṣṭaliṅgasaṃkhyātve 'pi kvacitsvato 'saṃbhavatsaṃkhyāyogasyāpi viṣayasaṃkhyātvam pratyekamāropāt /

children.translated_text: For example: 'somewhere, with matted locks and bark garments, cheeks [that are] forest fires' -- and so forth.
For the sage <s>Kapila</s> does not have plurality.
"Delusion, the death of the moth of the mind, <s>pralaya</s> (dissolution), fainting, darkness, bodily decay,

children.text: maraṇaṃ ca jaladabhujagajaṃ prasahya kurute viṣaṃ viyoginīnām' //
children.translated_text: And death like a cloud-serpent -- poison forcibly brings [all these] upon women in separation."

And here, although the superimposed [term] has manifested gender and number, in some cases, due to the impossibility of the number arising from itself, the number of the subject [is adopted] because of individual superimposition upon each.

children.text:
ityatra niyatasaṃkhyākakāryaviśeṣotthāpito garalārthaprabhāvito viṣaśabde śleṣa eva /
jaladabhujagajamiti rūpakasādhakamiti pūrve siddhatvābhāvānna tannicanvanaṃ viṣaśabde śliṣṭaśabdaṃ paramparitamiti śleṣa evātretyāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the word '<s>viṣa</s>' (poison), whose effects of a definite number are generated, and whose potency establishes the meaning of poison, there is indeed <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning). 'Cloud-serpent' serves as the basis of the <s>rūpaka</s> -- but since its prior establishment is lacking, the earlier [commentators] say: 'In the word viṣa, there is <s>śliṣṭaśabda</s> (punning word) with chaining -- hence this is <s>śleṣa</s> alone.'
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 16/3:]

children.text:
vaidharmyeṇāpīti /
na kevalaṃ sādharmyeṇetyarthaḥ /
asya ca vicchittiviśeṣāntaraṃ darśayitumāha-atretyādi /
āviṣṭaliṅgatve 'pītyanena dharmiṇaḥ svarūpamātraparyavasitatve 'pi dharmyantarasaṃbandhinaḥ saṃkhyātmano dharmāntarasyāpi svīkāra ityāveditam /
asaṃbhavatsaṃkhyāyogatyeti /
yadyapyekādivyavahārahetuḥ saṃkhyeti nītyā ekasminnapi dravye tadyogaḥ saṃbhavati tathāpyanekadravyavartitvādyabhiprāyeṇaitaduktam /
pratyekamāropāditi ayamagniḥ kapilo 'yamagniḥ kapila ityevaṃrūpāt /
ataścāropyamāṇasya kṛpilamunerbahutvāyogādviṣayasaṃkhyatvam /
śliṣṭatānibandhanasya paramparitasya śleṣādvailakṣaṇyaṃ dyotayitumāha-bhramimiti /
prabhāvita iti /
prathamameva pratītigācarīkṛta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Through dissimilarity too' -- not merely through similarity, is the meaning. To show a further distinctive feature of this, he says 'here' etc. 'Even though manifested gender' -- by this it is indicated that even though [the superimposed term] is restricted to merely its own form, a property of number belonging to a different qualified [entity] is also accepted. 'Due to the impossibility of number arising' -- although according to the principle that number such as 'one' etc. is the cause of conventional usage, its connection is possible even in a single substance, nevertheless this is stated with the intention that [number] pertains to multiple substances. 'Because of individual superimposition' means: in the form 'this fire is <s>Kapila</s>, this fire is <s>Kapila</s>.' And thus, because plurality cannot belong to <s>Kapila</s> the sage who is being superimposed, the number of the subject [is adopted]. To show the distinctive feature of <s>śleṣa</s> from chained [metaphor] which is based on blending, he says '<s>bhrami</s>' etc. 'Established' means: brought into the range of apprehension at the very outset, is the meaning.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 16/3a:]

children.text:
pūrvaṃ siddhatvābhāvāditi /
rūpakasya śleṣahetutvāt /
tannibandhanimiti rūpakanibandhanam /
iti śabdo hetau /
ataśca śleṣa evātrālaṅkāro na paramparitaṃ rūpakamityatra tātparyam /
cintyaṃ caitat /
yataḥ śleṣastāvadvāccayordvayoḥ prakṛtayoraprakṛtayoḥ prakṛtāprakṛtayośca bhavati /
atra ca na dvayoḥ prakṛtatvaṃ nāpyaprakṛtatvam /
varṣāsamaye jaladasyeva jalasya varṇanīyatvāt /
prakṛtāprakṛtayośca viśeṣaṇasāmya eva śleṣo bhavati iha tu viśeṣyasyāpi sāmyamiti śabdaśaktyutthitasya dhvanerayaṃ viṣayo na śleṣasya /
ataśca nātra śleṣālaṅkāraḥ /
nāpi dhvaniḥ /
jaladabhujagajamiti rūpakamāhātmyācchabdaśakyā garalārthasyābhidhānāt /
evamatra śliṣṭaśabdanibandhanaṃ [rūpakamevālaṅkāraḥ] jaladabhujagajamiti rūpakāntareṇāpi garalārtho yadi pratīyate tatsa dhvanervaṣayaḥ syādityuktaṃm /
sthite tu jaladabhujagajamiti rūpake tanmāhātmyādeva viṣaśabde śliṣṭaśabdanibandhanaṃ rūpakam /
anyathā hi jaladabhujagajamiti rūpakaṃ vyarthaṃ syāt /
tena vinā hi garalārthaḥ pratīyatata ityalaṃ bahunā /
children.translated_text: 'Because of the lack of prior establishment' -- because <s>rūpaka</s> is the cause of <s>śleṣa</s>. 'Its basis' means the basis of <s>rūpaka</s>. The word '<s>iti</s>' is in the causal sense. And thus, the purport is that the figure here is <s>śleṣa</s> alone, not chained <s>rūpaka</s>. But this should be examined. For <s>śleṣa</s> indeed occurs between two expressed meanings, two contextual subjects, two non-contextual subjects, or one contextual and one non-contextual. And here, there is neither dual contextuality nor dual non-contextuality -- because in the rainy season, water like that of a cloud is the subject to be described. And <s>śleṣa</s> of contextual and non-contextual occurs only in similarity of qualification; but here there is similarity of the qualified too -- hence this is the domain of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) arising from the power of words, not of <s>śleṣa</s>. Therefore, there is no <s>śleṣālaṅkāra</s> (figure of double meaning) here. Nor is it <s>dhvani</s> [alone] -- because the meaning of poison is expressed through the power of words due to the power of the <s>rūpaka</s> 'cloud-serpent.' Thus, here the figure is <s>śliṣṭaśabda</s>-based <s>rūpaka</s> alone. If the meaning of poison is apprehended through another <s>rūpaka</s> besides 'cloud-serpent,' then that would be the domain of <s>dhvani</s> -- this is what is stated. But when the <s>rūpaka</s> 'cloud-serpent' is established, through its power alone, in the word '<s>viṣa</s>' there is <s>śliṣṭaśabda</s>-based <s>rūpaka</s>. Otherwise, the <s>rūpaka</s> 'cloud-serpent' would be purposeless -- for without it, the meaning of poison would be apprehended. Enough of this elaboration.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 17:
When the superimposed [term] serves the contextual [meaning], it is <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation). [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 17]

children.text:
āropyamāṇaṃ rūpake prakṛtopayogitvābhāvātprakṛtoparañjakatvenaiva kevalenānvayaṃ bhajate pariṇāme tu prakṛtātmatayā āropyamāṇasyopayoga iti prakṛtamāropyamāṇarūpatvena pariṇamiti /
āgamānugamavigamakhyātyabhāvātsāṃkhyīyapariṇāmavaisakṣaṇyam /
tasya sāmānādhikaraṇyavaiyadhikaraṇyaprayogād dvaividhyam /

children.translated_text: The first type, for example:

"Having crossed the divine river <s>Amaradhunī</s> (Ganges), the stream [that serves as] the garland on <s>Bhūteśa</s>'s (Śiva's) head, he, the third [<s>Rāma</s>], offered to the boatman that ferry-fare which was [in the form of] friendship with <s>Saumitri</s> (Lakṣmaṇa).

children.text: vyāmagrāhyastanībhiḥ śabarayuvatibhiḥ kautukodañcadakṣaṃ kṛcchrādanvīyamānastvaritamaya giriṃ citrakūṭaṃ pratasthe' //
children.translated_text: Followed with difficulty by <s>Śabara</s> (tribal) women with curiosity-widened eyes, their arms spanning to embrace him, he swiftly departed for <s>Citrakūṭa</s> mountain."

In <s>rūpaka</s>, the superimposed [term], due to the absence of serving the contextual meaning, partakes of connection merely through embellishing the contextual meaning alone. But in <s>pariṇāma</s>, there is the usefulness of the superimposed in the form of the contextual -- thus the contextual is transformed by taking on the form of the superimposed. Due to the absence of the principles of manifestation, conformity, and disappearance, it differs from the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [concept of] <s>pariṇāma</s>. Through its usage in co-referential and non-co-referential constructions, it is twofold.

children.text:
atra saumittrimaittrī prakṛtā āropyamāṇasamānādhikaraṇātararūpatvena pariṇatā /
ātarasya maittrīrūpatayā prakṛte upayogāt /
tadatra yathā samāsoktāvāronyamāṇaṃ prakṛtopayogi taccāropaviṣayātmatayā tatra sthitam, ata eva tatra tadvyavahārasamāropaḥ evamihāpi jñeyam, kevalaṃ tatra viṣayasyaiva prayogaḥ, viṣayiṇo gamyamānatvāt /
iha tu dvayorapyabhidhānam, tādātmyāt tu tayoḥ pariṇāmitvam /

children.translated_text: The second type, for example:
"Then, with speeches that had attained maturity, were eloquent, and had taken a circuitous path,
He first made an approach to the king of the earth, and then afterwards with horses and other [gifts]."

Here, the contextual friendship with <s>Saumitri</s> is transformed by taking the co-referential form of '<s>ātara</s>' (ferry-fare). Because the ferry-fare serves the contextual [meaning] by being in the form of friendship. And here, just as in <s>samāsokti</s> the superimposed serves the contextual and that [superimposed] remains in the form of the object of superimposition -- hence the superimposition of that convention upon it -- so too should it be understood here; only there, just the subject is expressed, the object of comparison being understood [implicitly]. But here, both are expressed, and because of their identity, it is <s>pariṇāma</s>.

children.text:
rājasaṃghaṭane tūpāyanamucitam /
taccātra vacorūpamiti vacasāṃ vyadhikaraṇopāyanarūpatvena pariṇāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the context of meeting a king, an offering (<s>upāyana</s>) is appropriate. And here, that [offering] takes the form of speech -- thus there is <s>pariṇāma</s> through the speeches being transformed into a non-co-referential offering.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 17:]

children.text:
āropyamāṇasyetyādi /
āropyāropaviṣayabhāvasāmye 'pi rūpakādvailakṣaṇyaṃ darśayannetadeva vyācaṣṭe-āropyamāṇamityādinā /
prakṛtoparañjakatveneti /
yaduktam-viṣayiṇā viṣayasya rūpavataḥ kāraṇādrūpakamiti /
prakṛtātmatayeti /
prakṛtāṅgatayetyarthaḥ /
upayoga iti /
tena vinā prakṛtārthasyāniṣpatteḥ /
pariṇamatīti /
prakṛtamaprakṛtavyavahāraviśiṣṭatayāvatiṣṭate /
prakṛtasvarūpamātrāvasthāne prakaraṇārthāniṣpatteḥ /
evamatra prakaraṇopayogitvābhāvādityāropyamāṇasyopayoga iti cānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ prakṛtopayogitvasyāsādhāraṇatvaṃ darśitam /
asādhāraṇatvasya hi dharmasya tattavyavasthāpakatvāllakṣaṇatvam /
ataśca nāstyevālaṅkārāntareṣu prakṛtayogitvam /

children.translated_text: Thus:
"Wishing for you something else would be redundant, since all blessings have already come to you.
May you obtain a son worthy of your own virtues -- praiseworthy like you, as [your] father [was] to you."

'Of the superimposed' etc. Showing the distinctive feature from <s>rūpaka</s> despite the similarity in the superimposition and the object-of-superimposition relationship, he explains this very [definition] beginning with 'the superimposed' etc. 'Through embellishing the contextual' -- as was stated: '<s>rūpaka</s> arises from the subject's [being endowed with] the form of the object of comparison.' 'In the form of the contextual' means: as a component of the contextual, is the meaning. 'Usefulness' -- because without it, the contextual meaning would not be accomplished. 'Is transformed' means: the contextual stands as qualified by the convention of the non-contextual. Because if the contextual were to remain in its own form alone, the contextual meaning would not be accomplished. Thus, through positive and negative concomitance, the uniqueness of 'serving the contextual meaning' is demonstrated. And uniqueness of a property establishes it as a defining characteristic. Therefore, there is no serving of the contextual in other figures at all.
In this case, it is in <s>upamā</s> (simile).
'Meanwhile, as if to narrate the news of <s>Sarasvatī</s>'s descent, the sun descended to the middle world' -- in such cases, it is in <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).
"With peaks trembling from the agitation of <s>Mandara</s>-clouds, with the swan-group of the crescent-moon [playing] upon it,
With the emerald-servant gaze, like-<s>cakravāka</s>-birds gazing upon the peak."

children.text:
ityatra ca rūpake tathānyālaṅkāreṣvaucityameva nopayogaḥ /
ocityaṃ hi siddhasya sataḥ prakṛtārthopalambhakaṃ bhavati /
upayogaḥ punaḥ siddhāveva prakṛtārthahetutāṃ bhajate ityanayormahānbhedaḥ /

children.translated_text: Thus:
"In <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison), verbal identity is merely propriety as an incidental element;
But in this <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (repetition with different meaning), it is directly the motivating [factor]."

And here in <s>rūpaka</s>, as well as in other figures, there is merely propriety (<s>aucitya</s>), not usefulness (<s>upayoga</s>). For propriety serves to make apprehensible something that already exists as established in the contextual meaning. Usefulness, however, serves as the cause of the contextual meaning in its very establishment -- thus there is a great difference between these two.

children.text:
ityatraikasyaiva śabdaikyasyaucityopayogābhyāṃ bheda uktaḥ /
ataścaucityopayogayorbhedabhajānudbhiḥ sarvatraiva prakṛtopayogitvamanyairyaduktaṃ tadayuktam /

children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>pariṇāma</s> is indeed distinct from <s>rūpaka</s>.

children.text: iha punaḥ aprakṛtārthasya prakṛtārthāropamantareṇa siddhireva na bhavatīti prakṛtopayogitaiva jīvitam /
children.translated_text: Here, however, the meaning of the non-primary subject (<s>aprakṛtārtha</s>) cannot be established without superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) onto the primary subject (<s>prakṛtārtha</s>); therefore, usefulness to the primary subject (<s>prakṛtopayogitā</s>) is its very life.

children.text: 'dāho 'mbhaḥ prasṛtipacaḥ pracayavān bāṣpaḥ praṇālecitaḥ śvāsāḥ preṅkhitadīpradīpalatikāḥ pāṇḍimni magnaṃ vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The burning, the flowing of water, the dense vapor, the tears channeled through ducts, the sighs like flickering lamp-flames, the body immersed in pallor —

children.text: kiṃ vānyatkathayāmi rātrimakhilāṃ tvanbhārgavātāyane hastacchrattraniruddhacandramahasastasyāḥ sthitirvartate' //
children.translated_text: What more shall I say? The whole night at the window facing your direction, she remains like the moon's radiance blocked by an outstretched hand-parasol.'

Here, the difference of verbal identity alone is stated through propriety and usefulness. Therefore, what others have stated -- that serving the contextual meaning is present everywhere -- is incorrect, because propriety and usefulness are different categories.

children.text: atra hi cchratrtāropamantareṇa candrātaparodha eva na bhavatīti tasya prakṛtopayogitvam /

children.translated_text: And thus, the primary subject transforms as if it were the non-primary; this is called <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).

children.text: yadyevaṃ tarhi sāṃkhyīyapariṇāmādasya ko viśeṣa ityāśaṅkyaha-āgametyādi /
children.translated_text: If so, then what is the difference between this and the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> concept of <s>pariṇāma</s>? Anticipating this objection, he says 'āgama' etc.
'When this [substance], abandoning one property, takes on another,
yet the substrate (<s>dharmī</s>) does not deviate from its essential nature — that is called <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).'
Here indeed, without the superimposition of the parasol (<s>chatra</s>), the obstruction of moonlight cannot be established; hence its usefulness to the primary subject (<s>prakṛtopayogitva</s>).

children.text:
iti sāṃkhyīyapariṇāmalakṣaṇam /
maitrtīrūpatayeti /
maitryātmatayetyarthaḥ /
upayogāditi /
ātaramantareṇa taraṇāyogāt /
ataśca prakṛte yata ātarasyopayogastataśca prakṛtāyā eva maitryāstatkāryakāritvāttadvyavahārāropaḥ /
etadeva dṛṣṭāntamukhenāpi pratipādayati-tadatretyādinā /
atreti pariṇāme /
samāsoktau cāropyamāṇasya prakṛtopayuktatvam /
prakṛtasiddhyarthamevāprakṛtasyākṣepāt /
āropyamāṇamapi tatra prakṛtāvacchedakatvena sthitaṃ na punarācchādakatvenetyāha-taccetyādi /
ata eveti /
āropaviṣayātmakatvādeva /
tatreti samāsoktau /
etadeva prakṛte yojayati-evamityādi /
yadyevaṃ tarhi samāsoktipariṇāmayoḥ ko viśeṣa ityāśaṅkyāha-kevalamityādi /
tayorityāṃbhadhīyamānayordvayoḥ /
ucitamiti /
upayuktatayeti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
This is the definition of <s>pariṇāma</s> according to <s>Sāṃkhya</s>.
'In the form of friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>)' means 'having the nature of friendliness.'
'Due to usefulness' means: because crossing is impossible without the ford (<s>ātara</s>).
And thus, since the ford is useful to the primary subject, and since friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) itself — being the primary subject — produces the effect of the ford, the conventional usage of the ford is superimposed upon it.
This very point is also demonstrated through an illustration, beginning with 'tad atra' etc.
'Here' means: in <s>pariṇāma</s>.
In <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) too, what is superimposed has usefulness to the primary subject, since the non-primary is invoked precisely for establishing the primary.
The superimposed element, even there, stands as a delimiter of the primary subject, not as a concealer — this he states beginning with 'tac ca' etc.
'For this very reason' means: precisely because it has the nature of being the object of superimposition.
'There' means: in <s>samāsokti</s>.
This very point he applies to the present topic, beginning with 'evam' etc.
If so, then what is the difference between <s>samāsokti</s> and <s>pariṇāma</s>? Anticipating this objection, he says 'kevalam' etc.
'Of those two' means: of the two being discussed.
'Appropriate' means: by way of being useful. This is to be supplied.
START Sūtra 18:
When the object (<s>viṣaya</s>) is in a state of being doubted, it is <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt). // <s>RuAss</s>_18 //

children.text:
'abhedaprādhānye āropa ityeva /
viṣayaḥ prakṛto 'rtaḥ, yadbhittitvenāprakṛtaḥ saṃdihyate /
aprakṛte saṃdehe viṣayo 'pi saṃdihyata eva /
tena prakṛtāprakṛtagatatvena kavipratibhotthāpite saṃdehe saṃdehālaṅkāraḥ' /
children.translated_text:
'When identity (<s>abheda</s>) predominates, it is superimposition (<s>āropa</s>)' — just so.
The object (<s>viṣaya</s>) is the primary meaning (<s>prakṛtārtha</s>); the non-primary (<s>aprakṛta</s>) is doubted as being its substrate.
When the non-primary is doubted, the object too is thereby doubted.
Thus, when doubt is aroused by the poet's imagination (<s>kavipratibhā</s>) with respect to both the primary and non-primary subjects, it is the figure of speech called <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt).'
Commentary on <s>RuAss</s>_18:

children.text:
viṣayasyetyādi /
viṣayaviṣayiṇoḥ saṃbandhiśabdatvādviṣayasyokterviṣayiṇo 'pyākṣepādatra grahaṇam /
tena viṣayasya viṣayiṇaśca saṃdehapratītiviṣayatva sūtrārthaḥ /
nanu viṣayaśabdena viṣayiśabdasya saṃbandhiśabdatvādākṣepe 'pi vinā vacanamākṣepamātrādviṣayiṇaḥ kathaṃ saṃdihyamānatā labhyata iti cet, na /
aniyatobhayāṃśāvalambivimarśarūpatvādvipayamātragatatvenāsaṃbhavātsaṃdehasyānyathānupapattyā viṣayiṇastatsaṃbandhitvaṃ labhyata eveti yathāsūtritameva jyāyaḥ /
etadeva vibhajya vyācaṣṭe-viṣaya ityādinā /
yadbhittitveneti /
anyathā hyaprakṛtasya nirviṣayatvamaprantutābhidhānalakṣaṇo vā doṣaḥ syāditi bhāvaḥ /
tena viṣayabhittitayā vipayiṇāmeva tathāmāvo bhavatītyāśaṅkyāha-aprakṛtetyādi /
viṣayo 'pīti /
na kevalaṃ viṣayiṇa eva saṃdihyamānatvaṃ yāvadviṣayasyāpātyapiśabdāthaḥ /
tena kvacidviṣayiṇāmeva saṃdihyamānatve kvacicca viṣayaviṣayiṇorapyalaṅkāro bhavet /
ubhayatrāpi sāmānyalakṣaṇānugamāt /
aniyatobhayāṃśāvalambī hi vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
sa ca viṣayiṇāmeva bhavati /
viṣayavipayiṇoreva saṃdihyamānatvāt /
ata eva ca prakṛtāprakṛtagatatveneti yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojyam /
pratibhotyāpita iti /
na punaḥ svarasotyāpitaḥ, sthāṇurvā puruṣo vetyevamādirūpa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
'The object (<s>viṣaya</s>)' etc.
Since <s>viṣaya</s> (object) and <s>viṣayin</s> (subject) are correlative terms, by mentioning the object, the subject too is implicitly included.
Thus, the meaning of the sūtra is that both the object and the subject are within the scope of the cognition of doubt.
Objection: Even though the term <s>viṣayin</s> is a correlative of <s>viṣaya</s> and hence implied, how can the state of being doubted be obtained for the subject merely by implication without explicit statement? Reply: No [this is not a problem], because doubt has the nature of deliberation that rests indeterminately on both alternatives; since it cannot belong to the object alone, by the principle of otherwise-inexplicability, the subject's connection to it is indeed obtained. Therefore, the sūtra as formulated is best.
This very point he explains analytically, beginning with 'viṣaya' etc.
'As its substrate' — for otherwise, the non-primary would be objectless, or there would be the defect of being a mere verbal expression without reference; this is the import.
Anticipating that doubt pertains only to the subjects by virtue of having the object as substrate, he says 'aprakṛta' etc.
'The object too' — not only are the subjects doubted, but the object also is [doubted]; this is the meaning of the word 'api'.
Thus, sometimes only the subjects are doubted, and sometimes both the object and the subjects; in both cases the figure of speech applies, since the general definition holds for both.
For deliberation that rests indeterminately on both alternatives is what constitutes doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), and that belongs only to the subjects, since it is the object and the subjects that are in a state of being doubted.
And for this very reason, 'with respect to both primary and non-primary' should be construed as appropriate to each case.
'Aroused by imagination (<s>pratibhā</s>)' — not spontaneously arisen, not of the form 'Is it a post or a person?' and such; this is the meaning.
Commentary on <s>RuAss</s>_18/1:

children.text:
sa ca trividhaḥ /
śuddho niścayagarbho niścayāntaśca /
śuddho yatra saṃśaya eva paryavasānam /

children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: 'kiṃ tāruṇyataroriyaṃ rasabharodbhinnā navā vallarī līlāprocchalitasya kiṃ laharikā lāvaṇyavārāṃnidheḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is this a fresh creeper bursting forth with the weight of sap from the tree of youth? Is it a playful wave of the ocean of charm?

children.text: udgāḍhotkalikāvatāṃ svasamayopanyāsavistrambhiṇaḥ kiṃ sākṣādupadeśayaṣṭirathavā devasya śṛṅgāriṇaḥ' //
children.translated_text: Is it directly the teaching-staff of the god of love (<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>), full of buds ready to bloom, emboldened by the arrival of its own season?'

And this [doubt as a figure of speech] is of three kinds: pure (<s>śuddha</s>), containing certainty (<s>niścayagarbha</s>), and ending in certainty (<s>niścayānta</s>).
Pure (<s>śuddha</s>) is where doubt alone is the final conclusion.
For example:
