children.text: 'ayaṃ mārtaṇḍaḥ kiṃ sa khalu turagaiḥ satpabhiritaḥ kṛśānuḥ kiṃ sākṣātprasarati diśo naiṣa niyatam /
children.translated_text: 'Is this the sun? Indeed, does he travel with seven horses? Is it fire (<s>Kṛśānu</s>)? Does it directly spread across the directions? No, that is certain.

children.text: kṛtāntaḥ kiṃ sākṣānmahiṣavahano 'sāviti cirāt samalokyājau tvāṃ vidadhati vikalpānpratibhaṭāḥ' //
children.translated_text: Is it <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death) himself, riding a buffalo?' — Thus, after long observation, the adversaries on the battlefield form various conjectures about you.'
<s>Niścayagarbha</s> (containing certainty) is that which begins with doubt, has certainty in the middle, and ends with doubt.

children.text: niścayānto yatra saṃśaya upakramo niścaye paryavasānam /

children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: 'induḥ kiṃ kva kalaṅkaḥ sarasijametatkimambu kutra gatam /
children.translated_text: 'Is it the moon? Then where is the dark spot? Is this a lotus? Then where has the water gone?
It is the face, O doe-eyed one — this is subsequently ascertained through graceful and charming words.'
<s>Niścayānta</s> (ending in certainty) is that which begins with doubt and concludes with certainty.
For example:

children.text: 'rañjitā nu vividhāstaruśailā nāmitaṃ tu gaganaṃ mthagitaṃ nu /
children.translated_text: 'Are the various trees and mountains tinged with color? Is the sky bowed down? Is it veiled?

children.text: pūritā nu viṣameṣu dharitrī saṃhṛtā nu kakubhastimireṇa' //
children.translated_text: Are the uneven grounds of the earth filled up? Or are the directions gathered together by darkness?'
Sometimes the things being superimposed are seen as having different substrates.

children.text:
atrāropaviṣaye timire rāgādi tarvādibhinnāśrayatvenāropitam /
kecittvadhyavasāyāśrayatvena saṃdehaprakāramāhuḥ /
anye tu nuśabdasya saṃbhāvanādyotatvādutprekṣāprakāramimamācakṣate /
children.translated_text:
Here, redness and other qualities are superimposed upon darkness (the object of superimposition) as belonging to different substrates such as trees.
Some, however, describe this as a variety of <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt) based on <s>adhyavasāya</s> (cognitive determination).
Others explain this as a variety of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), since the particle 'nu' indicates supposition.
Commentary on <s>RuAss</s>_18/1:

children.text:
etadeva bhedatrayaṃ vivṛṇvannudāharati-śuddha ityādi /
atra prakṛtāyāstanvyāḥ saṃdehapratītiviṣayatvābhāvādviṣayiṇāṃ mañjaryādīnāmeva saṃdehaḥ /

children.translated_text: Where both the object and subjects [are doubted], for example:

children.text: 'kiṃ paṅkajaṃ kimu sudhākarabimbametaktaṃ vā mukhaṃ klamaharaṃ madirekṣaṇāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is it a lotus? Or is this the orb of the nectar-rayed moon? Or is it the fatigue-dispelling face of the intoxicant-eyed woman?
For in the middle of this [face/lotus/moon] is seen a darkness resembling the eyes — an imitation of a pair of bees, a pair of young deer, and a pair of beautiful eyes.'

Elaborating on this threefold classification, he illustrates beginning with 'śuddha' etc.
Here, since the slender woman who is the primary subject is not within the scope of doubt-cognition, the doubt pertains only to the subjects (<s>viṣayins</s>) such as the vine and others.
Sometimes it occurs in the manner of <s>vastu</s> (object) and <s>prativastu</s> (counter-object), as in:
'Is this a lotus adorned with dark bees, or is it a face with beautiful dark hair?
Thus the world is in doubt about you, O slender one, when you have descended to the lake.'
Here, the common property of dispelling fatigue and the like is taken up as the connecting attribute.

children.text:
atrāsitatvasunīlatvayoḥ śuddhasāmānyarūpatvam /
alikacānāṃ ca bimbapratibimbabhāvaḥ /
evaṃ cāsya sādṛśyanimittatvātsamānadharmānekadharmanimittatvena dvibhedattvaṃ na vyākāryam /
sādṛśyanimittatvenaivāsya saṃgrahasiddheḥ /
vipratapattyādinimittāntaravaccārutvābhāvācca /
bhinnāśrayatveneti vaiyadhikaraṇyena /
children.translated_text:
Here, darkness and dark-blue color have the nature of a pure common property. And the bees and the hair stand in the relation of original and reflection.
Thus, since this [figure] is caused by similarity, the twofold division based on having one common property or many common properties need not be elaborated, since it is already included under similarity as the cause.
Moreover, there is no charm [in such classification] with causes other than similarity such as <s>vipratipatti</s> (contradiction).
'Having different substrates' means: by way of belonging to different loci.
Commentary on <s>RuAss</s>_18/1a:

children.text:
avautrapakṣantaramāha-kecityādi /
anena ca saṃdehasyādhyavasāyamūlatvamapi granthakṛtaivoktam /
tenādhyavasāyāśrayo 'pyayaṃ svarūpahetuphalānāṃ saṃdihyamānatvena tridhā bhavati /
tatra svarūpasaṃdeho yathā-'rañjitā' ityādyeva /

children.translated_text: Or as in:

children.text: 'etattarkaya kairavaklamahare śṛṅgāradīkṣāgurau dikkāntāmukure cakorasuhṛdi prauḍhe tuṣāparatviṣi /
children.translated_text: 'Consider this, regarding him who removes the distress of night-lotuses, who is the preceptor of initiation into <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), who is the mirror of the lady quarters of the sky, the friend of the <s>cakora</s> bird, resplendent with the brilliance of frost —

children.text: karpūraiḥ kimapūri kiṃ malayajairālepi kiṃ pāradai- rakṣāli sphaṭikopalaiḥ kimaghaṭi dyāvāpṛthivyorvapuḥ' //
children.translated_text: Was the body of heaven and earth filled with camphor? Or smeared with sandalwood paste? Or sprinkled with mercury? Or studded with crystal stones?'

He presents the alternative view beginning with 'kecit' etc.
By this, the author himself has stated that <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt) can be rooted in <s>adhyavasāya</s> (cognitive determination).
Hence, even when rooted in cognitive determination, this [figure] is threefold according to whether the essence, the cause, or the result is doubted.
Among these, doubt regarding the essence (<s>svarūpa</s>) is illustrated by 'rañjitā' etc. itself.
Doubt regarding the cause (<s>hetu</s>), for example:

children.text: 'divi tvakṣaraṇāmbujasmṛtividhau gāḍhāvadhānaspṛśāṃ dhanyānāṃ prasaranti saṃtatatayā ye bāṣpadhārābharāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For those blessed ones in heaven who, with deep attentiveness toward the remembrance of the imperishable lotus, shed copious streams of tears continuously —
Are those [tears] from the intensity of contemplating worldly existence meditated upon for a long time? Or from the joy of beholding the moon-like face of liberation attained?'
Here, because the whiteness of moonlight is cognitively determined as filling with camphor and so forth, this [figure] is rooted in <s>adhyavasāya</s> (cognitive determination).
Doubt regarding the result (<s>phala</s>), for example:

children.text: 'nṛttānte pārijātaṃ kimu vighaṭayituṃ spraṣṭumākāśagaṅgāṃ kiṃsvidvā candrasūryau kimu vidalayituṃ ścetaraktābjabuddhathā /
children.translated_text: 'At the end of the dance, is it to pluck the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree? Or to touch the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>? Or is it to shatter the sun and moon, thinking them to be red and blue lotuses?

children.text: labdhuṃ nakṣatramālābharaṇabharamuta svargajaṃ vābhiyoddhuṃ dūrodastaḥ samastastava gaṇapatinā svastaye so 'stu hastaḥ' //
children.translated_text: Or to seize the garland of stars as an ornament? Or to fight the celestial elephant? — That hand of your <s>Gaṇapati</s> (lord of attendants), raised far upward, may it be for your welfare!'
Here, regarding the cause of the tears — joy — two causes are cognitively determined: separation from <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and the direct encounter with <s>mukti</s> (liberation).

children.text:
atra kariṇo niṣpādanasya vighaṭanādiphalamadhyavasitam /
atraivādiśabdavannuśabdasya saṃbhāvanādyotakatvātpakṣāntaramapi darśayitumāha-anya ityādi /
ataśca rañjitā ivetyarthaḥ /
pūrvatrārthe tu nuśabdo vitakaṃmātra evamyākhyeyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Here, the results of the elephant's reaching up — plucking and so forth — are cognitively determined.
Just as with the word 'ādi' (etc.) here, because the particle 'nu' indicates supposition, he shows the alternative view beginning with 'anye' etc.
Thus the meaning is: 'as if tinged with color' etc.
In the former interpretation, however, the particle 'nu' should be explained as indicating mere conjecture.
START Sūtra 19:
The cognition of another object due to resemblance is <s>bhrāntimān</s> (the figure of delusion). // <s>RuAss</s>_19 //

children.text:
asamyagjñānatvasādharmyātsaṃdehānantaramasya lakṣaṇam /
bhrāntiścittadharmaḥ /
sa vidyate yasminbhaṇitiprakāre sa bhrāntimān /
sādṛśyaprayuktā ca bhrāntirasya viṣayaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: 'oṣṭhe bimbaphalāśayālamalakeṣūtpākajambūdhiyā karṇolaṅkṛtibhāji dāḍimaphalabhrāntyā ca śoṇe bhaṇau /
children.translated_text: 'Mistaking the lip for a <s>bimba</s> fruit, the dark locks for ripe <s>jambū</s> berries, the ear-ornament for a pomegranate on account of its redness,

children.text: niṣpattyā sakṛdutpalacchadadṛśāmāttaklamānāṃ marau rājangṛrjararājapañjaraśukaiḥ sadyastṛṣā mūrcchitam' //
children.translated_text: and mistaking the eyes — resembling <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) petals — of those [women] who were fatigued in the desert, the parrots in the cage of the great king <s>Gūrjara</s> immediately died of thirst.'

Because it shares the property of being erroneous cognition (<s>asamyagjñāna</s>), this is defined immediately after <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt).
<s>Bhrānti</s> (delusion) is a property of the mind. That mode of expression in which it is present is called <s>bhrāntimān</s>.
And the delusion caused by resemblance (<s>sādṛśya</s>) is its subject matter.
For example:
'By <s>Dāmodara</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), whose blow pulverized the entire chest,
<s>Cāṇūra</s> the wrestler saw a hundred moons in the sky.'
However, delusion caused by a severe blow to vital points and the like is not the subject matter of this figure of speech.

children.text:
sādṛśyahetukāpi bhrāntirvicchittyarthe kavipratibhotthāpitaiva gṛhyate,yathodāhṛtam, na svarasotthāpitā śuktikārajatavat /
evaṃ sthāṇurvā syātpuruṣo vā syāditi saṃśaye 'pi boddhavyam /
children.translated_text:
Even delusion caused by resemblance is understood [as a figure of speech] only when aroused by the poet's imagination (<s>kavipratibhā</s>) for the purpose of poetic charm, as illustrated above — not when it arises spontaneously, like [the illusion of] silver in mother-of-pearl.
The same should be understood regarding the doubt 'Is it a post or a person?'
Commentary on <s>RuAss</s>_19:

children.text:
asamyagjñānatvasādharmyāditi na punarāropagarbhatvasājātyāllakṣitamiti bhāvaḥ /
āropo hi viṣayaviṣiyiṇoryugapadekapramātṛviṣayīkṛtatve bhavatīti nāropagarbho bhramaḥ kvacidapi saṃbhavati, śuktikādīnāṃ śuktikādirūpatayāvagame rajatādyabhimānābhāvāt /
nanu bhrāntiścittadharmaḥ sa yasyāsti sa bhrāntimāniti vaktuṃ nyāyyaṃ tatkathamalaṅkārasyaitadabhidhānamityāśaṅkyāha - bhrāntirityādi /
sa iti bhaṇitiprakāraḥ ataśaacālaṅkāre bhrāntimacchrabda upacarita iti bhāvaḥ /
sādṛśyaprayukteti /

children.translated_text: But not [as in]:

children.text: 'prāsāde sā pathi pathi ca sā pṛṣṭhataḥ sā puraḥ sā paryaṅke sā diśi diśi ca sā tadviyogāturasya /
children.translated_text: 'She on the terrace, she on every path, she behind, she before, she on the couch, she in every direction — for one tormented by separation from her,

children.text: haṃho cetaḥ prakṛtiraparā nāsti te kāpi sā sā sā sā sā sā jagati sakale ko 'yamadvaitavādaḥ' //
children.translated_text: Alas, O heart! You have no other nature — she, she, she, she, she, she pervades the entire world! What is this doctrine of non-duality (<s>advaitavāda</s>)?'

'Because it shares the property of being erroneous cognition' — and not because it belongs to the same class as superimposition-containing [figures]; this is the import.
For superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) occurs when both object and subject are simultaneously apprehended by a single cognizer; hence delusion containing superimposition is never possible anywhere, since when shells and the like are cognized as shells, there is no apprehension of silver and the like.
Objection: <s>Bhrānti</s> (delusion) is a property of the mind; how then can this term be applied to a figure of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>)? Anticipating this, he says '<s>bhrānti</s>' etc.
'That' refers to the mode of expression. Hence, the word <s>bhrāntimat</s> is used figuratively with respect to the <s>alaṅkāra</s>; this is the import.
'Caused by resemblance' —

children.text:
ityatraikasyā eva parimitāyā api yoṣito gāḍhānurāgahetukaṃ tanmayatānusaṃdhānaṃ prāsādādāvanekatra yugapatpratītau nimittamiti bhrāntimadalaṅkāraḥ /
sa hi prāsādādervallabhārūpatvena pratītau syāt /
anyasyānyarvallabhātvena pratīyata iti sphuṭa evāyaṃ viśeṣālaṅkārasya viṣayaḥ /
athaprāsādādāvabhūtāyā api vallabhāyā darśanād bhrāntiriti cet,naitat /
evaṃ hyatra bhrāntimātraṃ syānnālaṅkāraḥ /
gāḍhānurāgātmakanimittasāmarthyātsvarasata eva prāsādādāvasatyā api yuvatyāḥ pratītisamullāsāḥ /
kavipratibhānirvartitvābhāvāt /
'devamapi harṣaṃ pitṛśokavihnalīkṛtaṃ śriyaṃ śāpa iti mahīṃ mahāpātakamiti rājyaṃ roga iti bhogānbhujagā iti nilayaṃ niraya ityādi manyamānam' ityādāvapi na bhrāntimadalaṅkāraḥ /

children.translated_text: Because it was stated immediately after that 'since in perceiving [something] as having the form of mother-of-pearl etc., there is no arising of the notion of silver etc.'

children.text: iha punarviṣayarūpāṃ śriyamavagamyāpi śrīharṣeṇa pitṛśokavihvalīkṛtatvācchāpatvena bhāmyata iti viṣamālaṅkāro ñyāyān /
children.translated_text: Here, however, even though <s>Śrīharṣa</s> perceives glory in the form of a real object, because he was distressed by grief for his father, he is deluded into perceiving it as a curse -- therefore the figure <s>viṣama</s> (incongruity) is more appropriate.

children.text: 'dutuṃ vācchati dakṣiṇe 'pi nayane vāmaḥ karaḥ kajjalaṃ bhaujaṅgaṃ ca bhujo 'ṅgadaṃ ghaṭayituṃ vāme 'pi vāmetaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "The left hand wishes to apply collyrium even to the right eye, and the other-than-left [right hand] wishes to fasten the serpent-armlet even to the left arm.

children.text: itthaṃ svaṃ svamaśikṣitaṃ bhagavatorardhaṃ vapuḥ paśyatoḥ sādhārasmitalācchitaṃ diśatu no vaktraṃ manovācchitam' //
children.translated_text: Thus, as both halves of the Lord's body observe their own respective untrained [half], may his face, adorned with a common smile, grant us our heart's desire."

Here, even though the beloved is singular and limited, the absorption and identification arising from intense love becomes the cause of simultaneous perception in multiple places such as the palace etc. -- thus it is the figure <s>bhrāntimat</s> (based on delusion). For that [figure] would apply when the palace etc. is perceived as having the form of the beloved. That another [thing] is perceived as the form of another's beloved -- this is clearly the domain of the figure <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction). If one objects that 'the delusion arises from seeing the beloved even in the palace etc. where she does not exist' -- that is not correct. For in that case there would be mere delusion here, not a figure of speech. Due to the power of the cause, namely intense love, the perception of the young woman spontaneously arises even in the palace etc. where she is not actually present. Because it is not produced by poetic imagination. In 'considering even the god <s>Harṣa</s>, distressed by grief for his father, as glory, a curse; the earth as a great sin; the kingdom as disease; pleasures as serpents; the abode as hell' etc. -- even there, it is not the figure <s>bhrāntimat</s> (based on delusion).

children.text:
ityatrāpi saṃskāra evālaṅkāro na bhrāntimān /
atra hi bhagavatyā netradvayāñjanadānasatatābhyāsādvāmanetrāñjanadānānantaraṃ dakṣiṇanetrāñjanadānavāsanānurodho jāyata iti saṃskārasyaiva vākyārthatvam /
athātra saṃskāraprabodhaṃ vinā tadabhāvādañjanadānanaitat /
pratyutātra hi bhagavadardhasya tathātvenaivāvagamādañjanasaṃskāro na prarohamupāgata iti kārasyaiva skhaladgatitvāttatkārthasya bhramasyotpāda eva na saṃbhavatīti na bhrāntimato 'vakāśaḥ /
praruḍha eva hi saṃskāro bhramaḥ /
svātmamātrāvasthitastu saṃskārālaṅkāraḥ /
ata eva dātuṃ vācchratītyuktam /
evaṃ cātra netradvayābjanadānasatatābhyāsahetukaḥ saṃskāra eva pratīyate na tu tannimittako 'pi bhramaḥ paramaḥ /
parameśvarārdhasya tathātvenaivāvagamāttadgandhasyāpyabhāvāt /
ata evāśikṣitaṃ smitalācchitaṃ cetyuktam /
avāntara evānayorviśeṣo 'laṅkārabhāṣya evokta iti tata evānusartavya iti /
evaṃ casādṛśyanimittaivabhrāntiralaṅkāraviṣayo na nimittāntarotthāpiteti na lakṣaṇasyāvyāpakatvaṃ vācyam /
evaṃ sādṛśyanimittakatvādasya sādhāraṇadharmasyāpi trayī gatiḥ /

children.translated_text: Among these, 'following along' (<s>anugāmitā</s>) is illustrated as follows --
"Mistaking [her eye] for a blue lotus, with widened eyes,
See, the foolish bee chases the doe-eyed maiden!"

Here too, the figure is <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression), not <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion). For here, due to the constant practice of applying collyrium to both eyes of the goddess, after applying collyrium to the left eye, there arises a conformity with the latent impression of applying collyrium to the right eye -- thus the <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) alone is the meaning of the sentence. Now, if one says that without the awakening of the <s>saṃskāra</s>, since it would not exist, this is not the application of collyrium -- on the contrary, here, because the Lord's half [of the body] is perceived precisely as such [i.e., as his own], the collyrium-impression has not sprouted forth, and therefore, since the action itself proceeds haltingly, the arising of error which would be the purpose of that action is simply impossible -- hence there is no scope for <s>bhrāntimat</s>. For <s>bhrama</s> (error) is indeed a <s>saṃskāra</s> that has sprouted. But one that remains confined to itself alone is the figure <s>saṃskāra</s>. Hence the text says 'wishes to apply' [indicating intention, not actual error]. And thus, here what is perceived is only the <s>saṃskāra</s> caused by the constant practice of applying collyrium to both eyes, but not the error caused by it, which would be supreme [delusion]. Because of the complete absence of even a trace of that, since the Lord's half is perceived precisely as such. Hence the text says 'untrained' and 'adorned with a smile.' The subsidiary distinction between these two [figures] has been stated in the <s>Alaṅkārabhāṣya</s> itself -- hence one should follow that [work]. And thus, only delusion caused by similarity is the domain of this figure, not delusion produced by other causes -- hence one should not claim that the definition is too narrow. Similarly, because this [figure] is caused by similarity, the common property also has three modes:
The pure generic form (<s>śuddhasāmānyarūpatva</s>) is illustrated as follows --
"This <s>Ahimaruci</s> (the moon), heading toward the west, with a disc reddish like the beak of an angry parrot,
Is swiftly gazed upon by the sharks of the ocean, out of greed for a fresh, blood-red lump of flesh."
Here, the property of 'being widened' is indicated as the following-along [quality].
The relation of original and reflection (<s>bimbapratibimbabhāva</s>) is illustrated as follows --
[Prakrit:] "The moon-rays, stolen by the blue sapphire radiance of the ear-ornaments, are wiped away
From the face of the proud woman, with tears mixed with collyrium, by the beloved out of suspicion."
Here, the properties of coppery-redness and reddishness have the nature of pure generic similarity.
[Sanskrit reconstruction:] "The moon-rays, stolen by the blue sapphire radiance of the ear-ornaments, are wiped away
From the face of the proud woman, with tears mixed with collyrium, by the beloved out of suspicion."

children.text:
atra sakajjalatvendralakiraṇāhatatvayorbimbabhāvaḥ /
sādṛśyanimittakatvameva cāsya draḍhayituṃ pratyudāharati-gāḍhetyādinā /
sādṛśyanimittakatve 'pi kavipratibhotthāpitaiva bhrāntirasyaiva viṣayo na punarvāstavītyāha-sādṛśyetyādi /
udāhṛtamiti /
oṣṭhebimbaphalāśayetyādi /
etadeva saṃdehe 'pi yojayati-evamityādi /
saṃśaya iti /
arthādāropagarbha eva /
tatraiva hyasya sādṛśyaṃ nimittam /
adhyavasāyamūle hi saṃdehe sādṛśyātsambandhāntarādvā viṣayaviṣayiṇoḥ saṃdihyamānatvaṃ syāt yathodāhṛtaṃ prāk /
evamāropagarbhatva eva sādṛśyaṃ vinā nāyamalaṅkāra ityavagantavyam /
tasmādaviśeṣeṇaiva sādharmyaṃ vihāyāpi nimittāntaramavasambya nāsyālaṅkāratvaṃ vācyam /
sādṛśye 'pi kavipratibhotthāpitasyaivālaṅkāratvaṃ na punaḥ svārasikasyeti /
children.translated_text: Here, the properties of being mixed with collyrium and being struck by sapphire rays stand in the relation of original and reflection. And to firmly establish that this [figure] is indeed caused by similarity, he gives a counter-example beginning with 'gāḍha' etc. Even though caused by similarity, the delusion is one that is produced by poetic imagination alone -- this is its domain, not real [delusion] -- thus he says beginning with 'sādṛśya' etc. 'Has been illustrated' refers to 'the lip, the <s>bimba</s> fruit, the expectation' etc. He applies the same to doubt as well, beginning with 'evam' etc. 'Doubt' means: it is essentially embedded in superimposition. For in that [superimposition] alone lies its similarity as cause. In doubt rooted in identification, the uncertainty between the object and the subject-of-comparison would arise either from similarity or from some other relation, as was illustrated earlier. Thus, one should understand that this figure does not exist without similarity even when embedded in superimposition. Therefore, without any distinction, even by abandoning shared properties and relying on other causes, one should not assert that this constitutes the figure. Even in [cases involving] similarity, only [delusion] produced by poetic imagination constitutes the figure, not spontaneous [delusion] --
START <s>Sūtra</s> 20:
The perception of even a single [thing] in multiple ways due to the force of grounds is <s>ullekha</s> (multiple delineation). [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 20]

children.text:
yatraikaṃ vastvanekadhā gṛhyate sa rūpabāhulyollekhanādullekhaḥ /
na cedaṃ nirnimittamullekhamātram, api tu nānāvidhadharmayogitvākhyanimittavaśādetatkriyate /
tatra rucyarthitvavyutpattayo yathāyogaṃ prayojikāḥ /

children.translated_text: Thus it has been stated --
"According to taste, according to desire, according to linguistic convention, the appearance is differentiated
In a single object, accomplished through [different] modes of apprehension."

Where a single object is perceived in multiple ways, that is <s>ullekha</s>, from the delineation of multiplicity of forms. And this is not mere groundless delineation; rather, it is done due to the force of grounds called possession of various kinds of properties. Among these, taste, desire, and linguistic convention are the motivating factors as appropriate.
Thus.

children.text:
yathā-
'yastapovanamit.i munibhiḥ kāmāyatanamiti veśyābhiḥ saṃgītaśāleti lāsakaiḥ' ityādi harṣacarite śrīkaṇṭhākhyajanapadavarṇane /
atra hyeka eva śrīkaṇṭhākhyojanapadastattadguṇayogāttapovanādyanekarūpatayā nirūpitaḥ /
ruccarthitvavyutpattayaśca prāyaśaḥ samastavyastā yojayituṃ śakyante /
nanvetanmadhye 'vajravañjaramiti śaraṇāgatairasuravivaramiti vātikaiḥ' ityādau rūpakālaṅkārayoga iti kathamayamullekhālaṅkāraviṣayaḥ /
satyam /
asti tāvat 'tapovanam' ityādau rūpakavivikto 'sya viṣayaḥ /
yatra vastutastadrūpatāyāḥ saṃbhavaḥ /
yatra tu rūpakaṃ vyavasthitaṃ tatra cediyamapi bhaṅgiḥ saṃbhāvinī tatsaṃkaro 'stu /
na tvetāvatāsyābhāvaḥ śakyate vaktum /
tataśca na doṣaḥ kaścit /
evaṃ hi tatra viṣaye bhrāntimadalaṅkāro 'stu atadrūpasya tadrūpatāpratītinibandhanatvāt /
naitat /
anaikadhāgrahaṇākhyasyāpūrvasyātiśayasyābhāvāt, taddhetukatvāccāsyālaṅkārasya /
saṃkarapratītistvaṅgīkṛtaiva yadyevam, abhede bheda ityevaṃrūpātiśayoktiratrāstu /

children.translated_text: This is not a defect.

children.text: grahītṛbhedākhyena viṣayavibhāgenānekadhātvoṭṭaṅkanāttasya ca vicchittyantararūpatvāt sarvathā nāsyāntarbhāvaḥ śakyakriya iti niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the stamping of multiplicity through the division of the domain known as difference of perceivers, and because that [multiplicity] is of the nature of a distinct charm -- the conclusion is that its subsumption [under other figures] is in no way possible.

children.text: yathā vā- 'ṇārāaṇot ti pariṇaavaāhiṃ sirivallahot ti taruṇīhiṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] "'<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!' -- thus [confirmed] by those of mature age; '<s>Śrīvallabha</s> (beloved of <s>Śrī</s>)!' -- thus by young women;

children.text: bālāhiṃ uṇa kodūhaleṇa eme a saccavio' //
children.translated_text: By children, however, out of curiosity, [he was] confirmed just so."

For example -- 'Which [place] is called a grove of asceticism by sages, an abode of pleasure by courtesans, a concert-hall by dancers' etc. -- in the <s>Harṣacarita</s>'s description of the region called <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>. Here, the single region called <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> is described as having multiple forms such as a grove of asceticism etc., due to the possession of respective qualities. And taste, desire, and linguistic convention can generally be applied individually or collectively. Now, if one objects that in passages like 'a diamond cage by refugees, a demon's lair by madmen' etc. within this, there is the presence of the figure <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), so how is this the domain of the figure <s>ullekha</s>? True. There is indeed a domain of this [<s>ullekha</s>] that is distinct from <s>rūpaka</s> in 'a grove of asceticism' etc., where the actual nature of that form is possible. But where <s>rūpaka</s> is established, if this mode [of <s>ullekha</s>] is also possible there, let there be combination [of figures]. But this does not mean its [<s>ullekha</s>'s] non-existence can be asserted thereby. Hence there is no defect whatsoever. For in that domain, let the figure <s>bhrāntimat</s> (delusion) apply, since the perception of what is not of that form as being of that form is the basis? Not so. Because of the absence of the novel excellence called 'perception in multiple ways,' and because this figure [<s>ullekha</s>] is caused by that [multiple perception]. The perception of combination is indeed accepted; if so, let the figure <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) in the form of 'difference in what is non-different' apply here.
[Sanskrit reconstruction:] "'<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!' -- thus [confirmed] by those of mature age; '<s>Śrīvallabha</s> (beloved of <s>Śrī</s>)!' -- thus by young women;
By children, however, out of curiosity, [he was] confirmed just like that."

evam
'garurvacasi pṛthururasi arjuno yaśasi' ityādāvavaseyam /
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ-pūrvatra grahītṛbhedenānekadhātvollekhaḥ, iha tu viṣayabhedena /
nanvanekadhātvollekhane gurvādirūpatayā śleṣa iti kathamalaṅkārāntaramatra sthāpyate /
satyam /
anekadhātvanimittaṃ tu vicchittyantaramatra dṛśyate iti tatpratibhotpattihetuḥ śleṣo 'tra syāt /
na tu sarvathā tadabhāvaḥ /
ataścālaṅkārāntaraṃ yadevaṃvidhe viṣaye śleṣābhāve 'pi vicchittisadbhāvaḥ /
tasmādevamādāvullekha eva śreyān /
evamalaṅkārāntaravicchittyāśrayeṇāpyayamalaṅkāro nidarśanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in '<s>guru</s> (heavy/venerable) in speech, <s>pṛthu</s> (broad/great) in chest, <s>arjuna</s> (white/heroic) in fame' etc., the same should be understood. But the distinction is this: in the former, the <s>ullekha</s> (multiple delineation) involves multiplicity through difference of perceivers, while here it involves difference of objects. Now, if one objects that in the delineation of multiplicity, [there is] <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) through forms like <s>guru</s> etc., then how is this established as a separate figure? True. The multiplicity has no [other] cause, but a distinct charm is seen here -- thus <s>śleṣa</s> would be the cause that gives rise to the perception of that [charm]. But it is not the case that this [figure] is entirely absent. And therefore, it is a separate figure because even in the absence of <s>śleṣa</s> in such a domain, the charm is present. Hence, in such cases, <s>ullekha</s> alone is preferable. Thus, this figure should also be illustrated with reference to the charm dependent on other figures.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 20:]

children.translated_text: As they state --
"Therefore, every cognition that grasps universals etc., whether barren of verbal investigation
Or connected with it, is accepted as perception."

'Of even a single' etc. 'Perception in multiple ways' -- and not 'imagination in multiple ways.' For perception is possible in both spontaneous and produced cognition, not merely in spontaneous [cognition] alone.
Thus.

children.translated_text: That is as follows —

children.text: 'savrīḍā dayitānane sakaruṇā mātaṅgacarmāmbare satrāsā bhujage savismayarasā candre 'mṛtasyandini /
children.translated_text: 'Bashful upon the beloved's face, compassionate upon the elephant-hide garment, fearful upon the serpent, filled with wonder upon the moon dripping with nectar,

children.text: serṣyā jahvasutāvalokanavidhau dīnā kapālodare pārvatyā navasaṃgamapraṇayinī dṛṣṭiḥ śivāyāstu vaḥ' //
children.translated_text: jealous in the act of beholding the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s> (the <s>Gaṅgā</s>), dejected at the sight of the bowl of skulls — may the glance of <s>Pārvatī</s>, enamored of the new union, be auspicious for you!'

The fabrication of repetition and the like, since apprehension leads to a single conclusion — in natural apprehension this does not arise, and since it pervades both cases, what was stated in the <s>sūtra</s> is indeed correct. 'On account of the abundance of forms' — hence even when not explicit, the cognition of another entity is indeed present. Otherwise, the apprehension of one thing in multiple ways would simply not occur. And therefore its definition comes immediately after <s>bhrāntimat</s> (that which involves illusion). And the apprehension of one thing in multiple ways does not occur independently, but rather through the force of particular purposes — thus he says 'na cedam' and so on. 'Etad' refers to the apprehension of one thing in multiple ways. Since the object of cognition comes within the scope of undivided apprehension as possessing various kinds of properties, how can the apprehension in multiple ways pertaining to individual properties be justified? Anticipating this, he says 'tatra' and so on. 'Tatra' means in the apprehension of multiple aspects. Independent differentiation is <s>ruci</s> (taste/inclination). Eagerness directed toward practical purposes is <s>arthitva</s> (purposefulness). Reliance on the conventions of the learned is <s>vyutpatti</s> (linguistic competence). This has been stated in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>. 'On account of the conjunction of such and such qualities' means on account of the connection with various properties such as seclusion and the like. The purposefulness of sages is directed toward the subject of the hermitage. The purposefulness of courtesans is directed toward the subject of the abode of pleasure. Similarly, the linguistic competence and purposefulness of dancers is directed toward the subject of the music hall. By the word 'generally,' it is indicated that <s>ruci</s> (taste) is not present here. Now, the passage describing the land called <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> that was brought as an illustration — there is also a connection with another <s>alaṃkāra</s> (figure) therein, so how can this be exclusively its domain? He addresses this with 'nanu' and so on. Having accepted this very point, he provides a response with 'satyam abhi' and so on. The word 'tāvat' serves to indicate the disagreement regarding the absence of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). 'Of having that form' means of having the form of a hermitage and the like. Here too, what others have said — that since the <s>sāropā lakṣaṇā</s> (figurative expression with transfer) obtains by virtue of the part-whole relationship, one should suspect the figure of <s>rūpaka</s>, and therefore the seclusion aspect is to be reconsidered — that is incorrect. Because there is no part-whole relationship, the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> itself does not obtain. For in the land called <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, a hermitage does not exist anywhere as a part in the manner of part-whole, such that it could be superimposed on the whole by the sages. Rather, because <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> possesses such and such qualities like seclusion and the like, through the medium of hermitage-like qualities, sages and others have such an appearance according to their respective habitual tendencies through purposefulness and the like. Even if there were an intention of a part-whole relationship, that would be merely <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (figurative usage), not <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). Even though the <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is the ultimate reality, the subject's being given form constitutes its nature as an <s>alaṃkāra</s> (ornament). Otherwise it would be mere <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. Nor is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> ultimately <s>rūpaka</s>. And here, through the superimposition of hermitage and the like, there is no special excellence of the object of superimposition, since its having that form is actually possible. Therefore, it is established that the domain of this figure is distinct from <s>rūpaka</s>. Not only is this distinct from other <s>alaṃkāras</s> in its domain, but even where there is a conjunction with the <s>rūpaka</s> figure, this too can occur — to show this he says 'yatra' and so on. 'This too is a mode' — one having the form of apprehending one thing in multiple ways. 'This much' means merely by the employment of <s>rūpaka</s>. 'And from that' means from the combination of <s>rūpaka</s> and <s>ullekha</s>. Now, where there is no conjunction of <s>rūpaka</s>, a conjunction with another <s>alaṃkāra</s> is possible — he states this with 'evaṃ hi' and so on. 'Not having that form' — even though not having the form of a hermitage, because its being represented as having the form of a hermitage is the basis. 'Grasping that in the absence of that is error' — this indeed is the true nature of error. 'Of something unprecedented' — of that which cannot occur in <s>bhrāntimat</s>. 'Because it is the cause of that' — because it is the cause of the special excellence called apprehension in multiple ways. And if here <s>bhrāntimat</s> also exists, then let there simply be a combination of this with it — he says 'saṃkare' and so on. 'If so' — the special nature of <s>bhrāntimat</s> or its combination with this — that is the meaning. 'This' refers to the existence of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). 'From that' — because of the difference among apprehenders, the distinction is merely a difference of <s>vicchitti</s> (charm/striking quality). Indeed, the difference of <s>vicchitti</s> is the cause of distinction among all <s>alaṃkāras</s>. Thus, having refuted various doubts and established precisely this conclusion, he again illustrates with 'ṇāpāaṇo' and so on. And here the mention of being <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like, for the learned and others respectively, expresses <s>vyutpatti</s> (competence) and <s>arthitva</s> (purposefulness) in order. 'Because it is the cause of the arising of that cognition.' Because <s>ullekha</s> is produced here without <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning). 'The absence of that' means the absence of <s>ullekha</s>. 'Therefore' — because even in the absence of <s>śleṣa</s>, this <s>vicchitti</s> is possible. 'Of such a kind' means having the form of difference of subject.
Here, the varied perception of a single glance is described according to the difference of objects.
(Section marker: RuAssC_20a)
There, the first kind is based on <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt), as follows —

children.text: 'kiṃ bhānuḥ kimu citrabhānuriti yaṃ niścinvate vairiṇaḥ kiṃ cintāmaṇireṣa kalpaviṭapī kiṃ veti cāśāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is it the sun, or is it the fire? — thus his enemies deliberate about him. Is it the wish-fulfilling gem or the wish-granting tree? — thus those who come with hopes.

children.text: kiṃ puṣpākara eṣa puṣpaviśikhaḥ kiṃ veti rāmājanaḥ kiṃ rāmaḥ kimu jāmadagnya iti vā yaṃ dhanvino manvate' //
children.translated_text: Is it the spring season or is it the flower-arrowed <s>Kāma</s>? — thus the women. Is it <s>Rāma</s> or is it <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>)? — thus the archers consider.'
Thus this figure, though of two kinds, can be based on <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and the like as well as on other <s>alaṃkāras</s> — he states this with 'evam alaṃkārāntare' and so on.
And this same figure based on <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is as follows —

children.text: 'vajraṃ saurājyasākṣī parikalitamahāḥ śaktimārdrāparādho daṇḍaṃ khaḍgaṃ ripustrīprasabhaharaṇavitkūpavāpyādidṛśvā /
children.translated_text: 'The thunderbolt — a witness of righteous sovereignty; the great <s>śakti</s> (spear) — seized upon one who has committed offense while still wet; the rod; the sword — knower of forcible abduction of enemies' wives; having seen wells, tanks and the like;

children.text: pāśāṃ pāṇāvapaśyandhvajamapi balavitkoṣavedī gadāṃ ca svācchrandyajñastriśūlaṃ likhati karatale deva citrākṛteste' //
children.translated_text: seeing the noose in his hand, and the banner too — knower of strength, versed in treasuries, and the mace — O lord, the painter draws images of you on the palm as one who knows the science of sacrifices, the trident!'
Here, the varied perception of a single person through doubted multiple identities is described.

children.text: atra tvamedendra ityādyatiśayoktyā lokapālābhedo rājña upalabhyate ityekasyānekadhātvollekhanam /

children.translated_text: And based on <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) through difference of subject, as follows —
'On the mountain-peak it is the crimson of spring; on the trees, fresh shoots; beneath the coral, the ocean; on the heads of the elephants of the quarters, freshly applied dense sindūra powder;

children.text: sīmni vyognaśca henmaḥ suraśikharibhuvo jāyate yaḥ prakāśaḥ śoṇimnāsau kharāṃśoruṣasi diśatu vaḥ śarma raśmipratānaḥ' //
children.translated_text: at the boundary it is gleaming gold; the radiance that arises from the abode of <s>Meru</s> (the mountain of the gods) — may that reddish expanse of rays of the fierce-rayed sun at dawn grant you well-being!'
Here, through the hyperbole 'you are <s>Indra</s>' and so on, the non-difference of the king from the world-guardians is perceived — thus the varied perception of one in multiple ways.

children.text:
atraikasyaiva viṣayabhedena rūpakāśrayaṃ nānātvam /
'kārakāntara' ityapapāṭhaḥ /
prakṛtekārakavicchrittyāśrayasyaivānuktatvāt /
ayaṃ svarūpahetuphalollekhanarūpatvāttridhā /
tatra svarūpollekhaḥ samanantaramevodāhṛtaḥ /

children.translated_text: The varied perception of cause is as follows —
'For the sake of creation, always there is <s>dharma</s> (righteousness); for the sake of preservation, there are subjects; even though a destroyer,
and for the sake of destruction too — people know you as born of themselves.'

Here, the multiplicity of a single thing through difference of subject is based on <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). '<s>Kārakāntara</s>' is a misreading, since only the <s>vicchitti</s> (charm) based on the subject and the agent has been discussed. This figure is threefold, being of the nature of varied perception of essence, cause, and effect. Among these, the varied perception of essence has just been illustrated.
The varied perception of effect is as follows —

children.text: 'dharmāyaiva vidanti pārthiva yathāśāstraṃ prajāḥ pālitā arthāyaiva ca jānate 'ntaravidaḥ koṣaikadeśatya ye /
children.translated_text: 'O king, people know your protection of subjects according to <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) as being for the sake of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) alone; those who know the inner workings, being a portion of the treasury, know it as being for the sake of <s>artha</s> (wealth) alone;

children.text: kāmāyaiva kṛtārthatāmupagatā nārthaśca niścinvate mokṣāyaiva ca veda janma bhavataḥ kaścidvipaścijjanaḥ' //
children.translated_text: those who have attained fulfillment determine it not as for the sake of <s>artha</s> but for <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) alone; and some wise person knows your birth as being for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) alone.'
Here, the varied perception of the causes of a single birth in multiple ways is described.
Here, the varied perception of the fruits of a single birth in multiple ways is described.
(Beginning of Sūtra 21)
<s>Apahṇuti</s> (concealment) is the denial of the subject. (RuAss_21)

children.text:
vastvantarapratītirityeva prakrāntāpahnavavaidharmyeṇedamucyate /
āropaprastāvādāropaviṣayāpahnutāvāropyamāṇapratītāvapahnutyākhyo 'laṃṅkāraḥ /
tasya ca trayī bandhacchāyā, apahnavapūrvaka āropaḥ, āropapūrvako 'pahnavaḥ /
chalādiśabdairasatyatvapratipādakairvāpahnavanirdeśaḥ /
pūrvoktabhedadvaye vākyabhedaḥ /
tṛtīyabhede tvekavākyatvam /

children.translated_text: The first type is as follows —

children.text: 'yadetaccandrāntarjaladalavalīlāṃ prakurute tadācaṣṭe lokaḥ śaśaka iti no māṃ prati tathā /
children.translated_text: 'That which produces the play of water-lily petals inside the moon — the world calls it a rabbit, but not so in my view.
I rather consider it to be the scar-mark formed by the wound-brands from the falling glances, like firebrands, of young women pining in separation from your enemy.'

The term 'cognition of another entity' having already been introduced — this is stated by way of difference from denial. In the context of superimposition, when there is denial of the object of superimposition and cognition of the thing superimposed, the figure called <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment) arises. Its stylistic pattern is threefold: superimposition preceded by denial, denial preceded by superimposition, and expression through words indicating unreality such as 'chala' (deception) and the like. In the first two types there is a division of sentences; in the third type there is a single sentence.

children.text: atraindavasya śaśasyāpahnave upakṣitpe śaśakaprativastukiṇavata indorāropo nānvayaghaṭanāṃ puṣyatīti na niravadyam /
children.translated_text: Here, when the denial of the rabbit (the mark on the moon) is implied, the superimposition of the scar-mark upon the moon as a counter-entity to the rabbit does not support syntactic connection — hence it is not flawless.

children.text: tattu yathā 'pūrṇendoḥ paripoṣakāntavapuṣaḥ sphāraprabhābhāsvaraṃ nedaṃ maṇḍalamabhyayudeni gaganābhoge jigīṣorjagat /
children.translated_text: Rather it should be as follows: 'This brilliant orb of the full moon, of beauty complete in fullness, radiant with expansive splendor, does not rise in the expanse of the sky to conquer the world.
Rather, it is the upraised royal parasol of <s>Bhāra</s>, now bearing the beauty of a pale surface, of one whose sole instrument is the effort to crush the pride of people swollen with arrogance.'
The second type is as follows —
'He who always dwells above the beautiful blue lotus groves that are the eyes of celestial <s>Apsaras</s> women, having subdued them through self-restraint,

children.text: na tu rucirakalāpe vartate yo mayūre vitaratu sa kumāro brahmacaryaśriyaṃ vaḥ' //
children.translated_text: yet does not abide in the beautiful-tailed peacock — may that <s>Kumāra</s> (<s>Skanda</s>) bestow upon you the splendor of celibacy!'
The third type is as follows —
'Trembling with agitation, the <s>Gurjara</s> women who have fled their houses, their high breasts swaying, the swinging beautiful garlands of pearls scattering pearl-drops with a jingling sound,

children.text: sārdhaṃ tvadripubhistvadīyaśasāṃ śūnye marau dhāvatāṃ bhraṣṭaṃ rājamṛgāṅkaṃ! kundamukulasthūlaiḥ śramāmbhaḥkaṇaiḥ' //
children.translated_text: fleeing along with your enemies through the desolate desert of your fame — the royal moon-mark has fallen, O lord, with drops of sweat thick as <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) buds!'

children.text:
atra śūnya ityasya sthāne manyeśabdaprayoge sāpahnavotprekṣā ittayapi sthāpayiṣyate, ' ahaṃ tvinduṃ manye ' iti tu vākyabhede manyeśabdaprayogenotprekṣeti ca vakṣyate /
etasminnapi bhedo 'pahnavāropayoḥ paurvāparyaprayogaviparyaye bhedadvayaṃ sadapi na pūrvavaccitratāvahamiti na bhedatvena gaṇitam /
tatrāpahnuvapūrvake ārope nirantaramudāhṛtam /

children.translated_text: In the type where denial follows superimposition, as follows —
'White with the gleaming of moonlight-ashes, bearing star-bones, fond of the pleasure of disappearing, assuming the <s>Kāpālika</s> vow,

children.text: dvīpāddvīpaṃ bhramati dadhatī candramudākāpāne nyastaṃ siddhāñjanaparimalaṃ lāñcanasya cchalena' //
children.translated_text: she wanders from island to island, carrying the moon placed in the skull-bowl as an ointment-collyrium, under the pretext of the mark (on the moon).'

Here, if instead of 'desolate' the word 'manye' (I think) were used, it would be established as <s>apahṇuti</s> combined with <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), and 'ahaṃ tv induṃ manye' — with the use of 'manye' in a division of sentences — will also be explained as <s>utprekṣā</s>. In this too there is a distinction: when the order of denial and superimposition is reversed, the two types, though present, do not produce the same striking effect as before, and hence are not counted as separate types. Among these, the type where superimposition follows denial has been illustrated immediately above.
Sometimes the unreality is expressed through words like 'vapu' (form/appearance) that denote the form of another entity, as follows —

children.text: 'amuṣmiṃllāvaṇyāmṛtasarasi nūnaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ smaraḥ śarvapluṣṭaḥ pṛthujaghanabhāge nipatitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In this lake of nectar that is her beauty, surely <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), burnt by <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), fell upon the broad region of her hips.

children.text: yadaṅgāṅgārāṇāṃ praśamapiśunā nābhikuhare khikhā dhūmasyeyaṃ pariṇamati romāvalivapuḥ' //
children.translated_text: For this line of hair, indicative of the pacification of the embers of his limbs in the cavity of the navel, assumes the appearance of a streak of smoke.'
Thus.

children.text:
viṣayasyetyādi /
vastvantareti /
bhrāntimatāṃ'nuvartata iti śeṣaḥ /
ata eva kecana maṇḍūkaplutinyāyenānuvartanasyānucitatvād bhrāntimadanantaramapahnutirgranthakṛtā lakṣitā ullekhaścatiśayoktyanantaramiti granthaṃ viparyāsitavantaḥ /
na caitat /
yata ullekhastāvadatiśayoktyanantaraṃ granthakṛtā na lakṣitaḥ /
yadvakṣyati-'evamadhyavasāyāśrayeṇālaṅkāradvayamuktvā gamyamānaupamyāśrayā alaṅkārā idānīmucyante /
tatrāpi padārthavākyārthagatatvena teṣāṃ dvaividhyai'pi padārthagatamalaṅkāradvayaṃ krameṇocyate' iti /
tasmādvastvantarapratīterbhāvādbhrāntimadanantaramevāsya granthakṛtā lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtam /
ata eva collekhe 'pi tatsaṃbhavādvastvantarapratīternirantaramevānuvartanādihaivāsyā lakṣaṇamucitamiti yathāsthita eva granthaḥ sādhuḥ /
yadyevaṃ tardhullekhāpahlatyorihaiva viparyayeṇa kiṃ na lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtamityāśaṅkyāha-prakrāntetyādi /
idamityapahnutilakṣaṇam /
tadevavyācaṣṭe - āripetyādinā /
viṣayasyāpahnaveviṣayiṇo 'nyasya vidhirityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: By this —
"They do not call poison 'poison'; rather, [misappropriated] <s>brahmasva</s> (brahmin's property) is called poison.
Poison kills only one person, but <s>brahmasva</s> [destroys] along with one's lineage."

"Of the subject" and so forth.
"Of another entity" — the rest [of the sentence] is "follows [the pattern] of those possessing <s>bhrānti</s> (erroneous cognition)."
For this very reason, some, [arguing] that the continuation [of treatment] is improper according to the <s>maṇḍūkapluti-nyāya</s> (frog-leap principle), have rearranged the text so that <s>apahnutī</s> (concealment) is placed after <s>bhrāntimat</s> (as recognized by the author) and <s>ullekha</s> (delineation) after <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).
But this is not correct.
Because <s>ullekha</s> has not been placed by the author after <s>atiśayokti</s>.
As he will state: "Having thus described two <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) based on <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination), the <s>alaṅkāras</s> based on implied resemblance are now described.
Among these too, since they are found in word-meaning and sentence-meaning, there is a twofold division" — and the two <s>alaṅkāras</s> pertaining to word-meaning are described in order.
Therefore, since the cognition of another entity does occur, the author has defined this [figure] right after <s>bhrāntimat</s>.
For this very reason, since the cognition of another entity is possible in <s>ullekha</s> as well, the definition of this [figure] is appropriate right here as a continuous [treatment] — thus the text as it stands is correct.
If so, then why has the definition of <s>ullekha</s> and <s>apahnutī</s> not been given here in reverse order? Anticipating this, he says "of the ongoing" and so forth.
"This" refers to the definition of <s>apahnutī</s>.
He explains that very thing with "of the denying" and so forth.
The meaning is: in the denial of the subject, there is the establishment of another, the <s>viṣayin</s> (predicate).

children.text:
ityatra viṣayasya niṣedhapūrvaṃ brahmasvaviṣaya āropyamāṇatvād dṛḍhāropaṃ rūpakameva nāpahnutiḥ /
apahnuterhi niṣedhyaviṣayabhittitayaivānyasya viṣayiṇo vidhānaṃ lakṣaṇam /
atra tu niṣedhyasyaiva viṣasya brahmasvaviṣaye āropyamāṇatvādvidhānam /
atha
'atra mukhyasya viṣasya niṣedheāropyamāṇatvāt brahmasvaviṣasya gauṇasya vidhānam' - [alaṅkāraratnākare pṛ.42] iti cet, tatra brahyasvaviṣasya gauṇasya vidhānamiti bhaṇiteḥ kor'thaḥ /
kiṃ brahmasyeti /
tatra nādyaḥ pakṣaḥ /
viṣādinyāyena brahmasvaviṣātmanaḥ kasyacidvastuno bahirasaṃbhavāt /
tatrāpyasya brahmasvaṃ viṣaṃ ceti na bhedenoktiḥ syāt /
nāpi gauṇatā svārtha eva pravṛtteḥ /
anyadanyatra vartamānāṃ gauṇamityucyate /
na cātra brahmasvaviṣamanyatra kutracidvartate yenāsya gauṇatā syāt /
evaṃ dvitīye 'pi pakṣe na gauṇatvaṃ yuktam /
nāpyatrobhayavidhiḥ /
brahmasvavṛttyabhāvānmukhyārthabādhādguṇeṣu vartanāt /
tṛtīye 'pi na gauṇasya sato viṣasya vidhānam /
brahmasvavṛttyabhāvānmukhaayārthabādhādhādguṇeṣu vartanāt vihitasya tastaya gauṇatvāt /
evaṃ brahmasvatya dāḍharyena viṣasābhyapratītipratipipādayiṣayā tatra niṣedhapūrvaṃ viṣamāropitamiti dṛḍhāropameva rūpakaṃ yuktam /
na brahmasvaṃ viṣamidamiti punarucyamāne 'pahnutiḥ syāt /
tasmāt 'mukhyasya ve' tyapāsta viṣayasyāpahnuve 'nyavidhirapahnutirityeva lakṣaṇaṃ kāryam /
children.translated_text:
Here, because the <s>brahmasva</s>-subject is being superimposed upon the subject of poison through prior negation, this is indeed <s>dṛḍhāropa-rūpaka</s> (firm-superimposition metaphor), not <s>apahnutī</s>.
For the definition of <s>apahnutī</s> is precisely the establishment of another, the <s>viṣayin</s>, on the basis of the denied subject alone.
But here, the establishment is due to the superimposition of the very thing denied — poison — onto the domain of <s>brahmasva</s>.
Now, if [one objects]: "Here, with the negation of the primary [meaning] poison, there is the establishment of the secondary <s>brahmasva</s>-poison through superimposition" — [as stated in the <s>Alaṅkāraratnākara</s>, p. 42] — then what is the meaning of the statement "establishment of the secondary <s>brahmasva</s>-poison"?
Does it mean "of <s>brahmasva</s>" [alone]?
The first alternative is not [valid].
Because there is no external existence of any entity having the nature of both <s>brahmasva</s> and poison, by the principle of poison and the like.
Even there, the statement "this is <s>brahmasva</s> and poison" would not express a distinction.
Nor is there secondariness (<s>gauṇatā</s>), since the word is employed in its own meaning.
That which operates in something other [than its primary referent] is called secondary.
And here <s>brahmasva</s>-poison does not operate in anything else, so that its secondariness would obtain.
Likewise, secondariness is not justified in the second alternative either.
Nor is there a combined predication of both here.
Because of the absence of the function of <s>brahmasva</s> [as poison], due to the obstruction of the primary meaning, the operation is in the secondary qualities.
In the third [alternative] too, there is no establishment of poison as secondary.
Because of the absence of the function of <s>brahmasva</s> [as poison], due to the obstruction of the primary meaning, what is established operates in the secondary qualities, hence its secondariness.
Thus, in order to demonstrate the firm identity of <s>brahmasva</s> with poison, poison is superimposed there through prior negation — hence firm-superimposition <s>rūpaka</s> alone is appropriate.
<s>Apahnutī</s> would occur only if it were further stated "this <s>brahmasva</s> is not poison."
Therefore, setting aside "of the primary, etc.," the definition should be made as: "In the denial of the subject, the establishment of another is <s>apahnutī</s>."
<s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 21a:

children.text:
tasyetyapahnutyākhyasyālaṅkārasya /
vākyabheda iti ekavākyamiti cānena yathāsaṃbhavaṃ bhedatrayasya svarūpanirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ /
na niravadyamiti /
yathoktakramanirvāhābhāvāt /
ata evodāharaṇāntaramāha-pūrṇendorityādi /
manyeśabdasya prayoga iti saṃbhāvanādyotakatvāt /
notprekṣeti /
sādhyavasāyādyutprekṣāsāmagrayabhāvāt /
vakṣyata iti /
utprekṣāyām /
tayā cāsyā ivādiśabdavanmanyeśabdo 'pi pratipādakaḥ /
kintūtprekṣāsāmagrayabhāve manyeśabdaprayogo vitarkameva pratipādayatīti /
ataścātra 'avātpaḥ prāgalbhyam-ityādāvapahnatyatudāharaṇatvamabhidadhataḥsamāne 'pi nyāye 'no māṃ prati tathā' ityanena śaśakapakṣasya nirākṛtatvādanyasyānyarūpatayā saṃbhāvanāyā abhāvān manya-ityanena kiṇapakṣasyaiva niścitatvādatiśayoktitvameveti manyante (alaṅkāraratnakarakārādayaḥ) /
teṣāṃ pūrvāparavicārakuśalānāṃ kimabhidadhmaḥ /
evamanyairatrānyatra codāharaṇādau bahuprakāraṃ skhalitaṃ tat punargrunthavistararabhayād,asmaddarśanadattdūṣaṇodbharaṇasyaiva pratighajñātatvāt,asmābhiḥ pratipadyena na dūṣitam /
children.translated_text:
"Of that" — of the <s>alaṅkāra</s> called <s>apahnutī</s>.
"Distinction of sentences" and "a single sentence" — by this, the indication of the three-fold nature is made according to applicability.
"Not faultless" — because the stated order cannot be maintained.
Therefore he gives another example — "of the full moon" and so forth.
Because of the use of the word <s>manye</s> (I think) — since it indicates supposition.
"Not <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy)" — because there is no agreement with <s>sādhyavasāya</s> (determination) and other [elements] of <s>utprekṣā</s>.
"He will state" — in [the section on] <s>utprekṣā</s>.
And the word <s>manye</s> is an indicator of that [<s>utprekṣā</s>], just like the words <s>iva</s> and the like.
However, in the absence of agreement with <s>utprekṣā</s>, the use of the word <s>manye</s> indicates <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) alone.
And therefore, while stating that this is an example of <s>apahnutī</s> in "boldness of the waterless [cloud]" and so forth, since the hare-alternative has been rejected by the statement "not so towards me," and since the <s>kiṇa</s> (spot)-alternative alone is ascertained by <s>manye</s> due to the absence of imagining one thing as another — [some, namely] the author of the <s>Alaṅkāraratnākara</s> and others, consider this to be <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) alone.
What shall we say of those who are skilled in examining the preceding and following [context]?
Thus, many errors of this kind in examples and elsewhere by others have not been refuted by us point by point, out of fear of prolixity of the text, and because the elicitation of objections given by our exposition is itself well-known.
<s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 21b:

children.text:
etasminniti chalādiśabdapratipādye /
saṃbhāvamātraṃ punardarśayitumetadudāhṛtam /
vastvantararūpatābhidhāyīti /
vapuḥśabdasya śarīrārthābhidhāyitvāt /
atra punarupamānasyopameyarūpatāpariṇatau pariṇāma iti pariṇamālaṅkāratvaṃ syāt /
iha punaḥ śarvapluṣṭamadananipatanānumāpakatvena romāvalyapahnave dhūmaśikhāyā evaṃ prādhānyaṃ vivakṣitamiti na pariṇāmaḥ nāpi rūpakam /
vyājārthaparyavasāyivapuḥ śabdabalādāropaviṣayāpahnutāvāropyamāṇasya pratīteḥ /
āropaviṣayānapahnave hi rūpakamiti pūrvamevoktam /
athātrāpi bhinnayoḥ sāmānādhikharaṇyāyogādekatarasya niṣedhaprātpavāropyamāṇasya ca niṣedhānupapatterāropaviṣayasyaiva paryavasāne niṣedhaḥ pratīyata iti cet, naitat /
atra hi mukhādau candrādervṛtyabhāvād bādhitaḥ saṃścandrārthaḥ svātmasahacāriṇo guṇāṃllakṣayati na tu mukhāderviṣayasya niṣedhaḥ pratīyate /
mukhaśabdādeḥ svārtha eva pravṛtteḥ /
paryavasāne hyatra mukhādi candradiguṇaviṣiṣṭaṃ pratīyate /
na tu mukhāderbādhaḥ /
na mukhamityevamādeḥ pratyavamarśābhāvāt /
nāpi nidarśanā /
saṃbandhavighaṭanādyabhāvāt /
children.translated_text:
"In this" — that which is denoted by the words <s>chala</s> (deceit) and the like.
"Mere supposition is again shown" — this has been cited [as an example].
"Denoting the nature of another entity" — because the word <s>vapus</s> (body/form) denotes the meaning of body.
Here, however, when the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) is transformed into the nature of the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison), there would be <s>pariṇāma-alaṅkāra</s> (transformation).
But here, since the primacy of the smoke-streak is intended as indicative of the burning of <s>Madana</s> (Kāmadeva) by <s>Śarva</s> (Śiva), and thus for the denial of the hair-line, this is neither <s>pariṇāma</s> nor <s>rūpaka</s>.
By the force of the word <s>vapus</s>, which resolves into the meaning of pretext, from the cognition of that which is superimposed in the denial of the object of superimposition — [this is <s>apahnutī</s>].
For it has been stated earlier that <s>rūpaka</s> occurs when the object of superimposition is not denied.
Now if [one argues] that here too, since co-referentiality of two distinct things is impossible, one of them must be negated, and since what is superimposed cannot be negated, the negation is ultimately understood of the object of superimposition itself — this is not so.
For here, since the moon and the like have no [actual] function in the face and so forth, the obstructed moon-meaning indicates the qualities accompanying its own nature, but the negation of the subject — face and so forth — is not cognized.
Because the word <s>mukha</s> (face) and the like are employed in their own meaning.
For ultimately here, the face and the like are cognized as qualified by the qualities of the moon and so forth.
There is no sublation of the face and the like.
Because there is no reflective awareness of the form "this is not a face."
Nor is this <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration).
Because of the absence of disconnection of relation and the like.
<s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 21c:
For example —

children.text: 'maddhāhvorvyavahāramujjhatu latā kaṇṭhasthale tāvake mā kārṣīratisāhasaṃ priyatame dāsastava prāṇiti /
children.translated_text: "Let the creeper abandon the practice of embracing your neck! Do not commit such recklessness, O beloved — [this] servant is your very life-breath.

children.text: nītā vṛddhimamī tvayaiva kusumairbāṣpāyamāṇā drumā gṛhṇanti kṣurikāmivālipaṭalavyājena pāśacchide' //
children.translated_text: These trees, brought to growth by you alone through [their] flowers, weeping as it were, take up a razor-like [sharpness] under the pretext of a row of bees, for cutting [their] bonds."
And by the word <s>ādi</s> (et cetera), unreality is sometimes conveyed by the third [type] as well.

children.text:
atra kusumairiti tṛtīyayāpahṇavanibandhanam /
āropagarbhatvācceyaṃ sādṛśyādvā bhavati saṃbandhāntarādvā /
sādṛśye 'pyasyāḥ sādhāraṇadharmasya trayī gatiḥ /

children.translated_text: Among these, the [type involving] concomitance is as follows —
"They say that this moon bears a dark stain resembling a young <s>tamāla</s> tree, soft and dark.
But that is untrue — this sky appears [thus] because of the wound-opening made by the tooth of the cruel <s>Vidhuntuda</s> (Rāhu) being displayed."

Here, the instrumental case "with flowers" forms the basis of the denial.
And this [<s>apahnutī</s>], being pregnant with superimposition, arises either from similarity or from another relation.
When based on similarity, the common property of this [figure] has a threefold course.
The [type involving] pure generic similarity is as follows —
"This is a <s>pārijāta</s> tree from <s>Surendra</s>'s (Indra's) garden, brought to earth by <s>Hariṇa</s> (Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa).
This excellent flower is not recognized — it has the pride of originating from the land of <s>Kaśmīra</s>."
Here, the darkness resembling the <s>tamāla</s> tree is taken up as a concomitant [property].
The [type involving] the relation of original and reflection is as follows —

children.text: 'na syotsmābharaṇaṃ nabho na militacchāyāpatho vāmbudo no tārāprakāro na cedamamṛtajyotiṣmato maṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: "This is not a jewel-ornament of moonlight in the sky, nor a mass of clouds with merged shadows, nor a collection of stars, nor the disc of that which possesses immortal radiance.

children.text: kṣīrakṣobhamayo 'pyapāṃnidhirasau netrāhinā mandaraḥ pṛkto 'yaṃ maṇipūga eṣa kalaśaścāyaṃ sudhānirjharaḥ' //
children.translated_text: That ocean, though made of churned milk, [is not the ocean]; this is not <s>Mandara</s> mountain stirred by the serpent of the eye; this is a heap of gems, this is a pitcher, and this is a stream of <s>sudhā</s> (nectar)."
Here, there is pure generic similarity between the acts of taking away and bringing.
From another relation, as follows —
"Among the creeper-laden branches swaying in a kind of swinging play, agitated by the haughty gusts of the <s>Malaya</s> mountain breeze,

children.text: vācālatvaṃ nanu yadabhavat kānane kokilānāṃ maunitvaṃ tatpathikahariṇīlocanānāṃ vabalga' //
children.translated_text: the garrulousness that arose in the <s>koel</s> birds in the forest — that indeed became the silence of the eyes of the traveler's doe-eyed [beloved]. How wonderful!"
Here, the quality of being a moonlight-ornament is indicated as a reflection of the quality of being made of churned milk.

children.text:
atra kokilavācālatvasya kāraṇasya niṣedhe pathikastrāmaunitvasya kāryasya vidhiḥ /
evamāropagarbheyaṃ saprapañcaṃ darśitā /

children.translated_text: The [type] pregnant with <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) is now shown, as follows —
"Not because of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s beauty, nor because she made the gods' nectar-drink the eldest [of drinks] by granting refuge to the gods,

children.text: yadevaṃ bālendordiśi vidiśi vandyatvamuditaṃ sphuṭaṃ tvetatkāntāmukhakamaladāsyādupanatam' //
children.translated_text: nor because of being the crest-jewel of the Lord — the fact that the young moon is worshipped in every direction is clearly due to its servitude to the lotus-face of the beloved."

Here, in the denial of the cause — the garrulousness of the <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoos) — there is the establishment of the effect — the silence of the traveler's wife.
Thus this [<s>apahnutī</s>] pregnant with superimposition has been shown in detail.
Or, for example —
"The divine moon, the source of nectar, rises daily with fifteen digits for the purpose of satisfying the gods, ancestors, and humans — thus it is said.
But this [moon] wanders about, reaching your reflection by the device of [approaching] your cheek, intent on gathering the nectar of your lip."
Here, when the cause of being worshipped is [attributed to] glory and the like, another cause is determined by swallowing [the real one].

children.translated_text: <s>Adhyavasāya</s> (ascertainment) — and not <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) — [is the basis of <s>utprekṣā</s>]. For here, cognitions are of two kinds by virtue of being of the nature of certainty and non-certainty. Certainty (<s>niścaya</s>) is one that does not deviate from the object; the distinction into correct, incorrect, and otherwise [as merely] incorrect is not to be accepted here, since only the mere occurrence of cognition is what has been undertaken for examination here, and since [this distinction] is useful [only] in the investigation of validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>). Non-certainty (<s>aniścaya</s>) is of two kinds, having the form of doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) and conjecture (<s>tarka</s>). Therefore one should not say that what is non-certain is simply doubtful, since even the cognition of supposition (<s>saṃbhāvanāpratyaya</s>), which has the nature of <s>tarka</s>, while being non-certain, lacks the quality of being doubtful. <s>Utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), being designated by words like <s>saṃbhāvanā</s> (supposition), has <s>tarka</s>-cognition as its basis — therefore it does not have doubt as its basis, since [doubt] has a different definition. Now, if one objects that cognition characterized by non-determination is doubt, and that since <s>tarka</s> is not different from doubt due to the non-difference of being non-determinate cognition, [<s>utprekṣā</s>] has doubt as its basis — that is not so. Despite the non-difference of being non-determinate cognition, doubt and <s>tarka</s> have different forms. For example: "Is it a post or a person?" — the general consideration of both alternatives is doubt. "It must be a person" — through seeing a cause favorable to one alternative, the apparent refutation of the other alternative is <s>tarka</s>. "This is indeed a person" — the determination of one alternative without any contact with the other is certainty (<s>niścaya</s>). Thus, with the testimony of the sensitive reader (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), there is a threefold division of cognitions. Granted, there is indeed a threefold division of cognitions, but if [one argues that] due to the non-difference of being non-determinate cognition, <s>tarka</s> is a variety of doubt — that is not so. For by this reasoning, due to the non-difference of being incorrect cognition, error (<s>bhrama</s>) too would be a variety of doubt. If one says there is a distinction between them through having the nature of certainty or non-certainty regarding the object — well then, what is the proof that no [such distinction exists] here? For doubt arises as a deliberation of the form "what is it?" dependent on both alternatives without commitment to either; <s>tarka</s>, however, arises by refuting one alternative and supporting the other through the appropriateness of favorable causes such as seeing water-play and so on. For in another place, the post-alternative remains in full competition, whereas in the water-play ground it does not remain so, but becomes weakened; yet because it is possible [the perception is] an error, it does not entirely cease — and for this very reason certainty is possible even without a proving means of knowledge (<s>sādhakapramāṇa</s>). For certainty does not arise merely from the refutation of the opposing side; it arises from the presence of both proving and refuting means of knowledge. Therefore, the deliberation "what is it?" that depends on both alternatives without commitment is doubt; but that which depends on one alternative is <s>tarka</s>. If one objects that even with dependence on one alternative, doubt is possible, [as stated] "what is the special means of this fruitless [cognition]?" — that is not so. Why? Because without definitely accepting the other alternative, the dependence on one alternative has no firm ground. And from external observation: just as particular persons come to the path of memory, particular posts do not come so — thus <s>tarka</s>, born from the memory of one particular, is distinguished from doubt, which is born from the memory of both particulars. The further subtle arguments for establishing the distinction between these two are extremely profound and have not been stated here since they are not relevant to the present topic. Therefore, the cognition of supposition (<s>saṃbhāvanāpratyaya</s>), which occupies the middle ground between doubt and certainty, having the character of both, must necessarily be accepted — hanging suspended like <s>Triśaṅku</s>.
(Reference marker <s>RuAssC</s> 22b)

children.translated_text: Therefore:
"Because of the absence of certainty when <s>iva</s> ('as if') and the like [are used], because of the adoption of the object,
<s>utprekṣā</s> is not [based] on <s>adhyavasāya</s> in some cases, but rather on doubt" —

Even so, since <s>utprekṣā</s> has as its basis the cognition of supposition (<s>saṃbhāvanāpratyaya</s>) which is non-certain in nature, how can it have <s>adhyavasāya</s> (ascertainment) as its basis? For the nature of [<s>adhyavasāya</s>] is the swallowing up of the object (<s>viṣaya</s>) and the certainty of the superimposed entity (<s>viṣayin</s>). And neither of these is possible here — because of the adoption of the object [as merely possible] and the absence of certainty — so it is said. To this we reply: here <s>adhyavasāya</s> is of two kinds — natural (<s>svārasika</s>) and produced (<s>utpādita</s>). In the natural kind, the object is not apprehended [as an obstacle]; the cause is that, by the power of [the cause], the cognition of the superimposed entity naturally arises spontaneously. For one who has apprehended the true nature of a shell could never have the cognition "this is silver." In the other [produced] kind, however, even having apprehended the object, through making it internal, one produces the cognition of the superimposed entity by the force of a self-dependent conceptualization. For one who knows the object as distinct from the superimposed entity, the cognition of that kind, directed toward a purpose, being natural, is reproduced (<s>anūdyate</s>) by the speaker, not produced (<s>utpādyate</s>). As they say: "That in which another's cognition of the nature of error is reproduced — that is [called] erroneous" (<s>bhrāntimān</s>). But the naturalness here is desired as arising precisely from the poet's creative intuition (<s>kavipratibhā</s>). For otherwise it would be mere error, as was stated earlier. The other [type] is the domain of <s>utprekṣā</s>. And that is of two kinds — established (<s>siddha</s>) and to-be-established (<s>sādhya</s>). The established is where, because the object has been swallowed up through non-adoption, the ascertained [superimposed entity] has primacy. The to-be-established is where, because of the initial adoption [of the object], [and] because [the cognition] has the nature of supposition, the object is being swallowed up, and hence the activity of ascertainment itself has primacy. Therefore he says: "primacy of the activity" (<s>vyāpāraprādhānya</s>). And for this very reason, here sometimes there is non-adoption of the object — because the ascertainment useful for the expressed meaning is undertaken as something to be established. And sometimes, even without adoption of the object, there is no [mere] establishment — because through the initial adoption of <s>iva</s> ("as if"), [the object] is being swallowed up, and thus it contains superimposition (<s>āropagarbhatva</s>), which need not be explicitly stated. In that [other figure, <s>āropa</s>], the object is cognized as the superimposed entity. Here, however, because the object is being swallowed up, only the superimposed entity is cognized. Now, if [one objects that] the swallowing of the object is the definition of <s>adhyavasāya</s>, but here the object is [merely] being swallowed up, so how is there <s>adhyavasāya</s>? — that is not so. As stated in "that is <s>adhyavasāyikā</s>, where the object is made internal by the superimposed entity" and so on — the definition of <s>adhyavasāya</s> is the making-internal of the object by the superimposed entity. And that occurs either through the swallowing of the object or through its being-swallowed — so there is no distinction. And the being-swallowed too, following the previously stated principle, occurs whether the object is adopted or not adopted — so there is no distinction. Thus, in the established <s>adhyavasāya</s>, the ascertained [entity] has primacy; in the to-be-established, the essential nature [of the process] has primacy — this is proven. And the author of the text himself will distinguish and state this later — so let it be understood from there. That very quality of being-to-be-established which belongs to <s>adhyavasāya</s> is precisely the quality of being supposition (<s>saṃbhāvanātmakatva</s>). For supposition manifests through the weakening of one alternative and the strengthening of the other — thus its equivalence with to-be-established <s>adhyavasāya</s>, which too arises through the weakening of the object and the strengthening of the superimposed entity. For this very reason, even the word denoting the superimposed entity has [grammatical] truth. Because the to-be-established <s>adhyavasāya</s> in its essential nature manifests through the strengthening of the superimposed entity. As you yourselves have stated: "And in supposition, because of the strengthening of what is being supposed, not because of the weakening of the other." Here, because of the strengthening of the superimposed entity, there is difference from doubt. For doubt has as its definition the deliberation "what is it?" dependent on both alternatives without commitment — and because of the weakening of the <s>saṃbhāvanā</s>-object, there is difference from certainty too. For regarding the object, through the presence of a refuting [cognition], one [alternative] would be weakened, or through the presence of a proving [cognition], the other alternative would be established. And <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) has the nature of certainty — hence its difference [from <s>utprekṣā</s>]. As for what the author of the text will say, "the to-be-established is where the superimposed entity is cognized as unreal" and so on — that should be understood with reference to the actual state of affairs (<s>vastuvṛtta</s>). Thus, because the object is being swallowed up and because there is certainty of the superimposed entity, the basis of [<s>utprekṣā</s>] in <s>adhyavasāya</s> is established — and the definition as stated is one whose designation has been carefully considered.
this and similar statements are indeed incorrect. Enough of this extended discussion.

prāyaśca svarūpotprakṣāyā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ bhedanirdeśa /
eṣā cārthāśrayati dharmaviṣaye śliṣṭaśabdahetukā kvacitpadārthānvayavelāyāṃ sādṛśyābhivānādupakrāntāpyupamāvākyārthatātparyasāmarythābhimantṛvyāpāropārohakrameṇotprekṣāyāṃ paryavasyati /
kvacicchalādiśabdaprayoge sāpahnavātprekṣā bhavati /
ataścoktavakṣyamāṇaprakāravaicitryeṇānantyamasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [<s>adhyavasāya</s>] is of two kinds — to-be-established (<s>sādhya</s>) and established (<s>siddha</s>). The to-be-established is where the superimposed entity (<s>viṣayin</s>) is cognized as unreal. And the unreality [means]: the attribute (<s>dharma</s>) belonging to the superimposed entity is cognized as possible in the superimposed entity and impossible in the object, since the attribute has the form of quality, action, or substance. When there is the cognition of the possibility and impossibility [of the attribute], that which is the locus of possibility is cognized as unreal in that [context], [being there] in a non-ultimate sense; while the other [the object] is [cognized as having] reality in the ultimate sense. The ascertainment in the reality-cognition of that which is unreal is the to-be-established [<s>adhyavasāya</s>]. Therefore there is primacy of the activity (<s>vyāpāra</s>). The established is where, for the superimposed entity which is actually unreal, there is the cognition of reality. And the reality [arises] from the absence of the previously mentioned cause of unreality. Therefore there is primacy of the ascertained [entity]. In the to-be-established, where the primacy is of the activity, <s>adhyavasāya</s> is expressed by words such as <s>saṃbhāvana</s> (supposition), <s>abhimāna</s> (conceit), <s>tarka</s> (conjecture), <s>ūha</s> (reasoning), and <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). Thus, the supposition (<s>saṃbhāvana</s>) of the subject (<s>prakṛta</s>) as something other than itself (<s>aprakṛta</s>), through connection with qualities and actions belonging to what is not the subject — that is <s>utprekṣā</s>. And the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) [form of <s>utprekṣā</s>] is indicated by [particles like] <s>iva</s> and the like. In the suggested (<s>pratīyamānā</s>) [form], however, there is no use of <s>iva</s> and the like. And it is fourfold, according to whether the ascertained [entity] is a universal (<s>jāti</s>), action (<s>kriyā</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), or substance (<s>dravya</s>) that is not the subject. Even though the subject may be connected with these distinctions, there is no variety [from that side], so they are not counted. And for each, through the duality of being in the form of positive supposition or negative supposition (<s>bhāvābhāvābhimāna</s>), there are eight varieties. And for each of the eight, since the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) has the form of quality or action, there are sixteen divisions. And for each of those, through adoption or non-adoption of the cause, there are thirty-two sub-divisions. And for each of those, through having the nature of supposing a cause (<s>hetu</s>), essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>), or result (<s>phala</s>), there are ninety-six divisions. This is the system of expressed <s>utprekṣā</s>. Even there, since substance mostly has only supposition of essential nature, the divisions of cause-supposition and result-supposition should be removed from that. For the suggested [form], although in outline there are this many divisions, still, since the non-adoption of the cause is not possible in it, this type has fewer divisions by those [categories]. Because when <s>iva</s> and the like are not adopted, and the cause is not mentioned, the supposing does not come about. And mostly the division-exposition of essential-nature-supposition [is given] as applicable. And this [<s>utprekṣā</s>], resting on meaning, relating to attributes, and caused by words with double meaning (<s>śliṣṭaśabda</s>), sometimes at the stage of word-meaning connection, even though begun through the expression of similarity (<s>sādṛśyābhidhāna</s>) as a simile (<s>upamā</s>), culminates in <s>utprekṣā</s> through the progressive ascent of the activity of the one who conceives, by the force of the purport of the simile-sentence. Sometimes, with the use of words like <s>chala</s> (pretext) and the like, it becomes <s>utprekṣā</s> containing concealment (<s>apahnavā</s>). Therefore, through the variety of types stated and to be stated, this [figure] has infinity.
(Reference marker <s>RuAssC</s> 22/1)

children.text:
etadeva vyācaṣṭe - viṣayetyādinā /
abhedapratipattiriti viṣayāntaḥkaraṇāt /
saṃbhāvanāpratyayātmakatve 'pi sādhyādhyavasāyasya vastvabhiprāyeṇa tadvailakṣaṇyaṃ pradarśayitumāha-sādhya ityādi /
viṣayapariśodhanadvāreṇa pramāṇānugrāhakatvātsaṃbhāvanāpratyayasya puruṣeṇanena bhavitavyamityatra vastuvṛttena puruṣasya satyatvam /
iha punastatra tasya prayojanaparatayādhyavasīyamānatvātsaṃvanāviṣaye saṃbhāvyamānasya vastuto na satyatvamityāha-asatyatayā pratītiriti /
atraiva nimittamāha-asatyatvaṃ cetyādiṣa /
viṣaya upanibandha iti /
tadgatadharmābhedenādhyavasita ityarthaḥ /
anenasaprayojanatvamevopodvalitam /
dharma iti viṣayigataḥ /
sa eva cotprekṣaṇe nimittam /
tasyeti dharmasya /
saṃbhāvanāśrayasyeti viṣayiṇaḥ /
tatreti saṃbhāvanāśraye viṣaye /
itarasyeti asaṃbhavāśrayasya viṣayasya /
yasyeti viṣayiṇaḥ /
ataṃśceti /
adhyavasāyasya sādhyamānatvāt /
asatyasyāpīti /
