vastuto viṣayiṇastatrāsaṃbhavāt /
satyatāpratītiriti /
niścayasvabhāvatvādatiśayokteḥ /
asatyatvanimittasyanti dharmasaṃcārādeḥ /
ataśceti dharmasaṃcārātrigīyamāṇatāyāḥ prādhānyābhāvāt /
adhyavasitaprādhānyamiti viṣayasya nigīrṇatvādviṣayiṇa eva prādhānyamityarthaḥ /
sādhyatvasiddhatvayośca samanantaramevasvarūpamupapāditamitīha na punarāyastam /
tatreti dvayanirdhāraṇe /
adhyavasāya ityādiśabdairuccata iti saṃbandhaḥ /
etadevopasaṃharati-tadevamityādi /
yadāhuḥ-'vivayitvena saṃbhāvanamuprekṣā' iti /
pratīyamānāyāmiti /
ivādyaprayogācchabdānuktatvādūhyāyāṃ na vyaṅgayāyām,alaṅkāraprabhedānāṃ pratipipādayiṣitatvād vyaṅgyabhedābhidhānasyāprastutatvāt /
evaṃ vācyā pratīyamānā cotprekṣā bhavatītyanuvādadvāreṇa vidhiḥ /
sā ceti /
vaicitryamiti /
tasya nigīrthamāṇatvenāprādhānyāt /
pratyekamiti jātyādīnām /
nimittasyeti dharmasya /
tadvaśādeva hi prakṛtagatatvenāprakṛtopanibandhaḥ /
hetusvarūpaphalalakṣaṇamevāsyā bhedatrayaṃ jīvitabhūtamiti tadeva viśrāntidhāmatayā paścāduddiṣṭam /
jātyādibhedagaṇanaṃ punaravaicitryāvahamapi cirantanānurodhātkṛtam /
ata eva granthakṛtā prātipadyena nodāhṛtam /
asmābhiśca nodāhariṣyate /
eṣeti /
samanantaroktā /
tatrāpīti /
satyāmapi samanantaroddaṣṭāyāṃ bhedagaṇamāyām /
prāyaḥśabdena ca hetuphalayoḥ kutrāpi saṃbhavo 'stīti darśitam /
ata evālaṅkārānusāriṇyāṃ granthakṛtānayorapi saṃbhavo darśitaḥ /
tadevaṃ dravyasya hetuphalayoḥ saṃbhave prāguktaiva saṃkhyā jyāyasī /
anyathā tvetadbhedaṣoḍaśakatyābhāvādaśītirbhedāḥ /
asyāśca vakṣyamāṇanītyā hetuphalayornimittānupādānāsaṃbhavāccatuḥṣaṣṭireva bhedāḥ saṃbhavanti /
etāvanta iti ṣaṇṇavatiḥ /
ayaṃ prakāra iti /
pratīyamānotprekṣālakṣaṇaḥ /
prāya iti /
vācyā yathā svarūpotprekṣā lakṣayeṣu pracurā tatheyaṃ na bhavatītyarthaḥ /
na punaratyantamevāsyā abhāvo ścāṣṭacatvārriśadbhedāḥ saṃbhavanti /
taduktamalaṅkārānusāriṇyām-'pratīyamānotprekṣābhedā aṣ catvāriṃśat' iti /
arthāśrayāpīti /
arthāśrayasya yadyapi śabdahetukatvaṃ na kvāpyupayuktaṃ tathāpi śliṣṭaśabdahetukatvamasyāḥ kvacidvaicitryamāvahatītyarthaḥ /
upamā utprekṣāyāṃ paryavasyatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
ānantyamiti bahu prakāratvam /
children.translated_text:
He explains this very [point] with '<s>viṣaya</s>' (object) and so on.
'Non-difference cognition' — because of the subsumption of the object [into another]. Even though it has the nature of a presumptive cognition (<s>saṃbhāvanāpratyaya</s>), in order to show its distinction from the determination of what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) in terms of actual reality, he says '<s>sādhya</s>' and so on. The presumptive cognition, through the method of examining the object, supports the means of knowledge — therefore in the statement 'this must be a man,' the man is real in terms of actual fact. But here, because [the object] is determined with the purpose of serving a poetic aim at the site of presumption, the presumed object is not actually real — thus he says 'cognition as unreal.' He states the reason for this: 'And the unreality' and so on. 'The object is the basis' — meaning: determined through non-difference of attributes belonging to it. By this, the purposefulness itself is reinforced. 'Attribute' refers to [the attribute] belonging to the described object (<s>viṣayin</s>). And that itself is the ground of the imaginative fancy (<s>utprekṣaṇa</s>). 'Of that' — of the attribute. 'Of the locus of presumption' — of the described object. 'Therein' — in the object that is the locus of presumption. 'Of the other' — of the object that is the locus of impossibility. 'Of which' — of the described object. 'And therefore' — because the determination is being proved. 'Even of the unreal' — because the described object does not actually exist there. 'Cognition as real' — because <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) has the nature of certainty. 'Of the ground of unreality' — such as the transfer of attributes and so on. 'And therefore' — because of the non-prominence of what is being expressed through the transfer of attributes. 'Prominence of what is determined' — meaning: because the object is absorbed, the prominence belongs to the described object alone. And the nature of provability and provedness has been established immediately [before], so it is not repeated here. 'Therein' — in determining the two. 'By <s>adhyavasāya</s>' and the rest — words [like 'is declared'] connect with 'higher.' He concludes this very [discussion] with 'Thus indeed' and so on. As they say: '<s>Utprekṣā</s> (imaginative fancy) is the presumption of the described-object-nature.' 'When suggested' — because of the use of '<s>iva</s>' and the like, since it is not stated by the word [directly], it is to be inferred, not suggested in the technical sense [of <s>dhvani</s>], since the varieties of figures of speech are what is intended to be taught and the mention of varieties of the suggested is not the topic here. Thus, 'expressed and suggested <s>utprekṣā</s> both exist' — a rule through the door of restatement. 'And it' — 'variety' — because of the non-prominence due to [the object's] being absorbed. 'Individually' — of species and the rest. 'Of the ground' — of the attribute. 'By the force of that alone, it is the basis of the non-subject through being present in the subject.' The threefold division characterized by cause (<s>hetu</s>), intrinsic nature (<s>svarūpa</s>), and result (<s>phala</s>), which is the very life of this [figure], is pointed out afterward as the resting-place. The enumeration of divisions by species and the rest, though not productive of variety, was done in deference to the ancients. For precisely this reason, the author of the treatise did not illustrate [them] word by word. Nor shall we illustrate [them]. 'This' — [refers to] what was stated immediately before. 'Even therein' — even though the enumeration of divisions was stated immediately before. By the word '<s>prāyaḥ</s>' (mostly), it is shown that somewhere in the case of cause and result there is possibility. For precisely this reason, in the <s>Alaṅkārānusāriṇī</s>, the author of the treatise has shown the possibility of these two as well. Thus, when substance has the possibility of cause and result, the previously stated number is greater. Otherwise, because of the absence of this group of sixteen divisions, there would be eighty divisions. And according to the rule to be stated, because of the impossibility of cause and result having a ground, only sixty-four divisions are possible. 'This many' — ninety-six. 'This manner' — characterized by suggested <s>utprekṣā</s>. '<s>Prāyaḥ</s>' (mostly) — meaning: just as expressed <s>svarūpotprekṣā</s> is abundant in examples, so this [suggested] is not. But it is not that it is entirely absent — forty-eight divisions are possible. As stated in the <s>Alaṅkārānusāriṇī</s>: 'The divisions of suggested <s>utprekṣā</s> are forty-eight.' 'Even object-based' — although the word-causation of the object-based [type] is not employed anywhere, nevertheless, the causation of words with double meaning (<s>śliṣṭa</s>) sometimes produces variety — this is the meaning. '<s>Upamā</s> (simile) culminates in <s>utprekṣā</s>' — this is the connection. 'Infinity' means multiplicity of kinds.
Therein, <s>utprekṣā</s> of species (<s>jātyutprekṣā</s>) — for example:

children.text: 'sa vaḥ pāyādindurnavabisalatākoṭikuṭilaḥ- smārāreryo mūrdhni jvalanakapiśo bhāti nihitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'May that moon protect you — curved at the tip like a fresh lotus-stalk tendril, which blazes fire-brown placed on the head of the Enemy of <s>Smara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: stravanmandākinyāḥ pratidivasasiktena payasā kapālenonmuktaḥ sphaṭikadhavalenāṅkura iva' //
children.translated_text: as if it were a sprout released from a skull white as crystal, daily watered by the flowing water of the <s>Mandākinī</s> (heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>).'
Now this [<s>utprekṣā</s>] is illustrated by a mere indication.
Here, because the word '<s>aṅkura</s>' (sprout) is a species-term, it is the species that is fancied.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of action (<s>kriyotprekṣā</s>) — for example:
'The sky seems to smear (<s>limpatīva</s>) darkness on [all] limbs, seems to rain down collyrium.'
Here the actions of smearing and raining are fancied as belonging to darkness and the sky respectively.
But in the second half: 'Like the service of a wicked person, one's sight has become fruitless.'
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of quality (<s>guṇotprekṣā</s>) — for example:

children.text: 'saiṣā sthalī yatra vicinvatā tvāṃ bhraṣṭaṃ mayā nūpuramekamurvyām /
children.translated_text: 'This is the ground where, searching for you, one of my anklets fell from my foot on the earth;
it appeared to have bound itself in silence, as if from the sorrow of separation from your lotus-foot.'
Here it is a simile (<s>upamā</s>) only, not <s>utprekṣā</s>.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of substance (<s>dravyotprekṣā</s>) — for example:
'Seeing this nether world empty of the festival for the eyes, devoid of the deer-marked [moon],
the women here, with the pretext of their own faces, have created a moon-made creation in the sky, as it were.'
Here 'sorrow' (<s>duḥkha</s>) is the quality.

children.text:
atra candrasyaikatvād dravyatvam /
etāni bhāvābhimāne udāharaṇāni /
children.translated_text: Here, because the moon is a single entity, it has the nature of substance. These are examples of positive attribution (<s>bhāvābhimāna</s>).
(RuAssC_22/2:)

children.text:
sāṃpratamiti prātpāvasaram /
diṅmātreṇeti /
anena jātyādibhedānāmanavaklatpirdhvanitā /
tamogatatveneti /
tamogatavyāpanādidharmanigaraṇenetyarthaḥ /
atra hi tamaso dharmiṇo 'nyadharmadharmitvaṃ nigīryānyadharmadharmitvamavasthāpitamityagra eva vakṣyāmaḥ /
dravyotprekṣeti /
dravyasya svarūpeṇotprekṣaṇam /

children.translated_text: Of that very [substance], <s>utprekṣā</s> of cause (<s>hetūtprekṣā</s>) — for example:

children.text: 'jayati śiśiratāyāḥ kāraṇaṃ sā himādre- stripuraharakirīṭādāpatantī dyusindhuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Victorious is that celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), falling from the crown of the Destroyer of the Three Cities (<s>Śiva</s>), the cause of coldness on <s>Himādri</s> (the Himālaya),

children.text: satatasahanivāsī kṣīrasindhoḥ prasūto- himakara iva hetuḥ śvaityaśaityasya yasyāḥ' //
children.translated_text: as if the moon, born of the Milk Ocean, ever dwelling in it, were the cause of her whiteness and coolness.'

'Now' means 'at the present occasion.' 'By a mere indication' — by this, the non-labored [treatment] of the divisions by species and the rest is implied. 'As belonging to darkness' — meaning: by the absorption of the other attribute-substratum through [attributes] such as the pervading nature belonging to darkness. For here, another attribute-substratum of the attributive entity darkness is absorbed and another attribute-substratum is established — as we shall explain further ahead. '<s>Dravyotprekṣā</s>' — the fancying of a substance in its intrinsic nature.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of result (<s>phalotprekṣā</s>) — for example:
'In the midst of water, facing the sun, grey with dust,
the night-lotuses (<s>kumudinīs</s>) perform austerities — as if for the sake of the moon, day after day.'
Here the visible moon is fancied as a cause.
Here the [word for] moon has the nature of substance. He extends the exemplification of positive attribution to these — with 'these' and so on.
In the case of negative attribution (<s>abhāvābhimāna</s>) — for example:
'Alas! Her two cheek-surfaces, having become such,
not seeing each other, have attained such endurance, as it were.'

children.text:
atrāpaśyantāviti kriyāyā abhāvābhimānaḥ /
evaṃ jātyādāvapyūdyam /
guṇasya nimittatvaṃ yathā-
'navabisalatākoṭikuṭilaḥ' ityatrodāhṛte kuṭilatvasya /
kriyāyā yathā- r'idṛkṣāṃ kṣāmatāṃ gatau' ityatra kṣāmatāgamanasya /
nimittopādānasyaite udāharaṇe /

children.translated_text: When [the ground is] not employed, 'The sky seems to smear (<s>limpatīva</s>) darkness on limbs' and the like are the examples.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> of cause (<s>hetūtprekṣā</s>) — for example, 'as if from the sorrow of separation, it had bound itself in silence' and the like.

children.text: svārūpotprekṣā yathā - 'kuberajuṣṭāṃ diśamuṣṇaraśmau gantuṃ pravṛtte samayaṃ vilaṅghya /
children.translated_text: <s>Utprekṣā</s> of intrinsic nature (<s>svarūpotprekṣā</s>) — for example: 'When the hot-rayed one [the sun] set forth to go to the direction inhabited by <s>Kubera</s>, transgressing the [proper] season,

children.text: dig dakṣiṇā gandhavahaṃ mukhena vyalīkaniḥ śvāsamivotsasarja' //
children.translated_text: the southern direction, as if with its mouth, released a false sigh through the scent-bearer [the wind].'

Here, 'not seeing' — the negative attribution is of an action. Similarly, it should be inferred for species and the rest too. The ground being a quality — for example, in the [verse] cited above '<s>navabisalatākoṭikuṭilaḥ</s>' (curved like the tip of a fresh lotus-stalk), [the quality] of curvature [serves as the ground]. Of an action — for example, in 'having attained such endurance,' the attainment of endurance [serves as the ground]. These are examples where the ground is employed. When the ground is not employed — 'The sky seems to smear darkness on [all] limbs' and the like are the examples.

children.text: phalotprekṣā yathā - 'colasya yadbhītipalāyitasya bhālatvacaṃ kaṇṭakino vanāntāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Utprekṣā</s> of result (<s>phalotprekṣā</s>) — for example: 'The thorny forest-borders, [observing] the bark-cloth of the <s>Cola</s> [king] who had fled in fear,
were splitting open, as if to see the letters — "What else will he experience now?"'
Suggested <s>utprekṣā</s> (<s>pratīyamānotprekṣā</s>) — for example:
'<s>Mahilāsahasabharie tuha hiae suhaa sā asāantī</s>
<s>aṇudiṇamaṇaṇṇaambhā aṅgaṃ taṇuaṃpi taṇuei</s>'
Thus the illustrative direction for expressed <s>utprekṣā</s> has been given.
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'Dwelling in your heart which is filled with a thousand women, O fortunate one, she,
day by day, having no other occupation, makes thin even the thin body.'

children.text:
atra-
amāantītyavartamāneveti tanūkaraṇahetutvenotprekṣitam /
evaṃ bhedāntareṣvapi jñeyam /
children.translated_text: Here — '<s>amāantī</s>' (not dwelling) [implies] 'as if not existing' — the thinning is fancied as having its cause in non-dwelling. Similarly, this should be understood in other sub-divisions as well.
(RuAssC_22/3:)

children.text:
abhyūhyamiti abhāvābhimānodāharaṇam /
nimittopādānasyeti /
kuṭilatvasya kṣāmatāgamanasya ca sākṣānnirdeśāt /
anupādāna iti /
tirodhāyakatvādernimittasya gamyamānatvāt /
bhedāntareṣviti svarūpaphalādikeṣu /
jñeyamiti pratīyamānatvāt /

children.translated_text: Therein, <s>utprekṣā</s> of intrinsic nature (<s>svarūpotprekṣā</s>) — for example:
'<s>malaasamīrasamāgamasaṃtosapaṇiccārābhisavvatto</s>
<s>vidhyāiha calakisalajakarāhi sāhāhi mahulacchrī</s>'

'To be inferred' — this is an example of negative attribution. 'Where the ground is employed' — because curvature and the attainment of endurance are directly stated. 'Where [the ground is] not employed' — because the ground, such as the capacity to conceal, is understood [implicitly]. 'In other sub-divisions' — in intrinsic nature, result, and the rest. 'Should be understood' — because it is suggested.
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'Everywhere, with the robe-garments of the joy of meeting the <s>Malaya</s> breeze,
the beauty of the <s>Madhūka</s> tree speaks forth with branches as trembling tender-shoot hands.'

children.text:
atra madhulakṣmīgatatvena calakisalayakaratvādi nigīrya vyāharaṇakriyā svarūpenotprekṣitā /
tadaunmukhyotpādakatvādi ca nimittamanupāttam /
yatpunaruddeśe pratīyamānotprekṣāyāṃ nimittānupādānaṃ na saṃbhavatītyuktaṃ tatra prāyastasyāḥ svarūpotprekṣaṇasyāsaṃbhavo nimittam /
granthakṛto hi pratīyamānoprekṣā hetuphalarūpaiva bhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ /
hetuphalotprekṣaṇayoścavakṣyamāṇanītyā nimittānupādānaṃ na saṃbhavatītyāśayenaitaduktam /
tena pratīyamānāpi svarūpotprekṣā nimittopādānānupādānābhyāmeva bhavati /
tatra nimittānupādāne udāhṛtā /

children.translated_text: With employment [of ground] — for example:
'This darkness, having spread everywhere, concealing the world,
smears all the limbs of people with thick brushes of ambrosia.'

Here, through being attributed to the beauty of <s>Madhūka</s>, the action of speaking is fancied in its intrinsic nature, having absorbed [the quality of] having trembling tender-shoot hands and so on. And the ground, such as the capacity to produce eagerness toward it, is not employed. Now, as for the statement that in the outline of suggested <s>utprekṣā</s>, the non-employment of the ground is impossible — the reason there is that mostly the fancying of intrinsic nature is not possible [for the suggested type]. For the author's view is that suggested <s>utprekṣā</s> takes only the form of cause and result. And according to the rule to be stated, the non-employment of ground is impossible for the fancying of cause and result — with this intention, that [statement] was made. Therefore, even the suggested <s>svarūpotprekṣā</s> exists [only] through employment and non-employment of the ground. Therein, [the case] without employment of ground has been illustrated.

children.text: atra prasāritvādi nigīrya tamāgatatvena lepanakriyā svarūpeṇetprekṣitā tirodhāyakatvādi ca nimittam /
children.translated_text: Here, having absorbed the spreading and so on, the action of smearing is fancied in its intrinsic nature as belonging to darkness, and the concealing nature and so on is the ground.
'This is the fourth [fire], the sacrificial fire, or the fifth Veda,

children.text: api vā jaṅgamaṃ tīrdhaṃ dharmo vā mūrtisaṃcaraḥ' //
children.translated_text: or a moving sacred ford, or <s>dharma</s> itself walking in embodied form.'

children.text:
ityādau tu vāmanatamate viśeṣoktiḥ-'bhūtalakārtikeyaḥ'itivat /
granthakṛnmate tu dṛḍhāropaṃ rūpakam /
yadvakṣati-yā tvekahānikalpanāyāṃ sāmyadāḍharthaṃ viśeṣoktiriti viśeṣoktirlakṣitā sāsmaddarśane rūpakabheda eveti /
ata evātra tatsāmagrababhāvādutprekṣodāharaṇatvaṃ na vācyam /
evam 'aparaḥ pākaśāsano rājā' ityatrāpi dṛḍhāropameva rūpakam /
etaccālaṅkārānusāriṇyāmutprekṣāvicāre granthakṛtaiva darśitam /

children.translated_text: <s>Utprekṣā</s> of result (<s>phalotprekṣā</s>) — for example:
'<s>gijjante maṅgalagāhiāhi varagottakaraṇṇae</s>
<s>sottaṃ viṇiggao uai hāentabahuāhi romaṅkṣo</s>'

In [passages] like this, in the view of <s>Vāmana</s>, it is <s>viśeṣokti</s> (particular statement) — like 'the <s>Kārtikeya</s> on earth.' But in the author's view, it is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) with firm superimposition. As he will state: 'That which, when similarity is asserted for the purpose of one-sided attribution, is identified as <s>viśeṣokti</s> — that, in our view, is a sub-type of <s>rūpaka</s> itself.' Therefore, since the totality of that [figure] is absent here, it should not be called an example of <s>utprekṣā</s>. Similarly, in 'He is another <s>Indra</s>, the king,' it is also <s>rūpaka</s> with firm superimposition. And this was shown by the author of the treatise himself in the examination of <s>utprekṣā</s> in the <s>Alaṅkārānusāriṇī</s>.
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'As the auspicious songs are grasped by the singers, for the one whose ears are given by the noble family,

children.text: śrotuṃ vinirgataḥ paśyata bhaviṣyadvadhvā hi romāñcaḥ') //
children.translated_text: look — the goose-flesh of the future bride has emerged, as if to listen!'
Here 'as if to listen' — the result is fancied.
[<s>Utprekṣā</s>] based on a word with double meaning (<s>śliṣṭaśabdahetu</s>) — for example: 'He who was celebrated on the surface of the earth through song, being renowned for having no equal,
became supremely the field of <s>Smara's</s> arrows, through a pride-first [gait] of those who had gone [to him].'
Here, in the domain of attributes, the word '<s>mārgaṇa</s>' has a double meaning [both 'arrow' and 'seeking'].
(RuAssC_22/4:)
'Double-meaning' — because of [the word's] also denoting 'arrow.'

children.text: upamopakramotprekṣā yathā - 'kastūrītilakanti bhālaphalake devyā mukhāmbhoruhe rolambanti tamālabālamukulottaṃsanti maulāvapi /
children.translated_text: An <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) beginning with <s>upamā</s> (simile), for example: 'On the forehead-surface of the goddess's lotus-face, they appear as musk-<s>tilaka</s> marks; on the crown, they hang down like young <s>tamāla</s>-bud ornaments;

children.text: yāḥ karṇe vikacotpalanti kucayoraṅke ca kālāguru- sthāsanti prathayantu tāstava śivaṃ śrīkaṇṭhakaṇṭhatviśaṣaḥ' //
children.translated_text: at the ears they bloom like opened <s>utpala</s> lotuses, and at the breasts and lap they become dark <s>aguru</s> (aloe) — may those marks of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>'s throat bestow auspiciousness upon you.'

children.text:
atra yadyapi 'sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kkip' ityupamānātkkibvidhāvāmukhe upamāpratītistathāpyupamānasya prakṛte saṃbhavaucityātsaṃbhāvanotthane utprekṣāyāṃ paryavasānam /
yathā vā virahavaṇaṃne 'keyūrāyitamaṅgadaiḥ' ityādau /
eṣāpi samastopamāpratīpādakaviṣaye 'pi harṣacaritavārtite sāhityamīmāṃsāyāṃ ca teṣu teṣu pradeśeṣudāhṛtā, iha tu granthavistarabhayānna prapañcitā /
children.translated_text:
Here, although by the rule '<s>sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kkip</s>' (the <s>kkip</s> suffix is applied to all nominal stems) there is apprehension of <s>upamā</s> (simile) at the beginning through the <s>kvip</s>-formation from the standard of comparison, nevertheless, due to the propriety of the standard of comparison being possible in the subject, the conclusion rests in <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) arising from supposition.
Similarly in the description of separation, as in '<s>keyūrāyitam aṅgadaiḥ</s>' (the armlets became as if bracelets) and so forth.
This type has also been cited in the <s>Harshacarita</s>-based discussion and in the <s>Sāhityamīmāṃsā</s>, in those respective passages, in the context of all simile-establishing expressions; but here it has not been elaborated for fear of prolixity.
<s>RuAssC</s> 22/5:

children.text:
āmukha iti na punaḥ paryavasāne /
upamāpratītiriti /
tadarthameva kvipaḥ pravṛtteḥ /
ata evātra vācakābhāvānnotprekṣātvamiti na vācyam /
nahi vācakasaṃbhavāsaṃbhavāsaṃbhavamātramevālaṅkārāṇāṃ bhāvābhāvaprayojakam /
evaṃ hi vyājastutau nindādervācyatve 'pyavācyasya stutyādeḥ pratītiralaṅkāratvaparyavasāyinī na syāt /
tasmādvākyārtha eva praruḍho 'laṅkārāṇāṃ svarūpapratiṣṭāpakaṃ pramāṇam /
vākyārthasya ca padārthānvayavelāto 'nyaiva pratipattiḥ /
saṃbhavaucityāditi /
kastūrītilakāderviṣayiṇo bhālaphalakādau saṃbhave yathaucityaṃ na tathākaṇṭhatviḍāderviṣayasyetyarthaḥ /
ata evātropamāyāḥ prakṛtasyāprakṛtakastūrīlilakādirūpatayā pariṇāmātpariṇāmagarbhatvaṃ yadanyairuktaṃ tatteṣāṃ pariṇāmasvarūpānabhijñātvam /
na aucityameva tasya svarūpaṃ kiṃ tu yathoktaṃ prakṛtopayogitvam /
aucityaṃ ca notprekṣāyāṃ viruddham /
tasya sarvatraiva bhāvāt /
utprekṣāyāṃ paryavasānamiti /
kaṇṭhatviṣāmeva kastūrītilakatvādipratīterviṣayiṇo viṣayanigaraṇenābhedapratipatteḥ sādṛśyāvagamābhāvāt /
sādṛśyaṃ jhubhayaniṣṭam /
na cātra prakṛtāprakṛtayoḥ saṃlpadhitayā pratītiḥ /
yathā vetyanenāsyā lakṣye prācuryaṃ darśitam /
samastopamāpratipādakaviṣaye dṛśyamānā /

children.translated_text: That is as follows —
'May that staff-footed one, uprooting the staff-foot of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, protect you —
whose crescent moon gleaming before him attains the semblance of the tip of a balance-beam.'

'At the beginning' means not at the conclusion.
'Apprehension of <s>upamā</s>' — because the <s>kvip</s> suffix is employed precisely for that purpose.
Therefore it should not be objected that this is <s>utprekṣā</s> due to the absence of an explicit indicator; for the mere presence or absence of an explicit indicator is not the sole determinant of the existence or non-existence of figures of speech.
For in that case, even in <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise), where censure and the like are expressly stated, the apprehension of the unexpressed praise and the like, which culminates in the status of a figure, would not obtain.
Therefore, the sentence-meaning itself, as conventionally established, is the valid means for establishing the essential nature of figures.
And the cognition of the sentence-meaning is something distinct from the point of word-meaning connection.
'Due to the propriety of possibility' — the meaning is that where musk-<s>tilaka</s> and the like, which are the objects of comparison, are possible on the forehead-surface and similar locations as befitting, the same does not apply to the throat-lustre and the like, which are the subjects.
Therefore, what others have stated — that this involves <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation) because the subject transforms into the form of the non-subject, namely musk-<s>tilaka</s> and the like — that shows their unfamiliarity with the true nature of <s>pariṇāma</s>.
Propriety alone is not its essential nature; rather, as stated, it is serviceability to the subject.
And propriety is not incompatible with <s>utprekṣā</s>, since it is present everywhere.
'The conclusion rests in <s>utprekṣā</s>' — because the apprehension of the throat-lustre and the like as musk-<s>tilaka</s> marks results in a cognition of non-difference through the subsumption of the object by the correlate, and hence there is no cognition of similarity.
Similarity requires both terms to be apprehended.
But here the subject and the non-subject are not cognized as jointly present.
By the word '<s>yathā</s>' (as, for example), the abundance of this type in actual literary instances is shown.
'In the domain of all simile-establishing expressions' — as observed.

children.text: atra satyapi tulāśabde candralekhāyā eva tulākoṭitvapratīterutprekṣātvam /
children.translated_text: Here, despite the presence of the word '<s>tulā</s>' (balance/scale), since the crescent moon itself is apprehended as being a balance-tip, it is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).
<s>RuAss</s> 22/6:
An <s>utprekṣā</s> combined with <s>apahṇava</s> (denial/concealment), for example —
'When the city-women rushed to the bank in alarm due to the collision with the whale,
the <s>Siprā</s> river shines as if bursting into laughter of pearls, under the pretext of its glistening foam-mass.'

children.text:
atrevaśabdamāhātmyātsaṃbhāvanaṃ chalaśabdaprayogāccāpahnavo gamyate /
evaṃ chadmādiśabdaprayoge 'pi jñeyam /
'apara iva pākaśāsanaḥ' ityādāvaparaśabdāprayoge upamaiveyam /
tatprayoge tu prakṛtasya rājñaḥ pākaśāsanatvapratītāvadhyavasāyasaṃbhāvādivaśabdena ca tasya sādhyatvapratīterutprekṣaiveyam /
ivaśabādāprayoge siddhatvādadhyavasāyasyātiśayoktiḥ /
ivāparaśabdayoraprayoge tu rūpakam /
tadevaṃ prakāravaicitryeṇāvasthitāyā utprekṣāyā hetūtprekṣāyāṃ yasya prakṛtasaṃbandhino dharmasya heturutprekṣate sa dharmo 'dhyavasāyavaśādabhinna utprekṣāyāṃ nimittatvenāśrīyate /
sa ca vācya eva niyamena bhavati /
anyathā kaṃ prati hetuḥ syāt /
yathā-'apaśyantāvivānyonyam' ityādau /
atra kapolayoḥ prakṛtayoḥ saṃbandhitvenopāttasya kṣāmatāgamanasya heturadarśanamutprekṣitam /
hetuphalaṃ ca kṣāmatāgamanaṃ tatra nimittam /
evam 'adṛśyata tvaccaraṇāravindaviśleṣaduḥkhādiva baddhamaunam'ityatra nūpuragatasya maunitvasya heturduḥkhitvam /
tadutprekṣaṇe maunitvameva nimittaṃ jñeyam /
evaṃ sarvatra /
children.translated_text:
Here, by the force of the word '<s>iva</s>' (as if), supposition is understood, and by the use of the word '<s>chala</s>' (pretext), <s>apahṇava</s> (concealment) is understood.
The same should be known when words like '<s>chadma</s>' (guise) and the like are used.
In cases like '<s>apara iva Pākaśāsanaḥ</s>' (as if another <s>Indra</s>), when the word '<s>apara</s>' (another) is not used, it is simply <s>upamā</s> (simile).
But when that word is used, since the subject (the king) is apprehended as being <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) through <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determinative identification), and the word '<s>iva</s>' indicates that this is to be supposed, it is indeed <s>utprekṣā</s>.
When the word '<s>iva</s>' is not used, since the identification becomes established fact, it is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) through <s>adhyavasāya</s>.
When both '<s>iva</s>' and '<s>apara</s>' are absent, it is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).
Thus, regarding <s>utprekṣā</s> as established in its variety of forms: in <s>hetūtprekṣā</s> (fancy regarding cause), the property whose cause is imagined — that property, being non-different through <s>adhyavasāya</s> — is relied upon as the ground in the <s>utprekṣā</s>.
And that ground must necessarily be expressly stated;
otherwise, for whom would the cause apply?
As in '<s>apaśyantāv ivānyonyam</s>' (as if not seeing each other) and so forth.
Here, for the cheeks as the subjects, the cause of the thinness-onset that is connected with them is imagined to be 'not seeing' (i.e., separation).
And the effect of the cause — the onset of thinness — serves as the ground there.
Similarly in '<s>adṛśyata tvac-caraṇāravinda-viśleṣa-duḥkhād iva baddhamaunam</s>' (it appeared as if bound in silence from the grief of separation from your lotus-feet), the cause of the silence belonging to the anklet is the state of being grieved.
When that cause is imagined, the silence itself should be understood as the ground.
The same applies everywhere.
<s>RuAssC</s> 22/6:
With the use of the word '<s>chadma</s>' (guise), for example —
'Your breast-region, adorned with a mass of sweat-drops as if with a pretext of concealment, shines
as though <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), though priceless, has offered <s>arghya</s> (oblation) to it.'

children.text:
asyāśca tattacchrabdaprayogāprayogābhyāṃ pratītibhedādalaṅkāraiḥ saha vibhāgaṃ darśiyitumāha-apara ityādi /
tatprayoga ityaparaśabdaprayoge /
ivaśabdasya saṃbhāvanādyotakasyāprayogāt siddhatvam /
ata eva cātra viṣayasyānupādānameva /
tadupādāne hi dṛḍhāropaṃ rūpakamiti samanantaramevoktam /
anyatra punaḥ sarvatra viṣayopādānameva nyāyyam /
taditthaṃ bhedavaicitryeṇāvasthitāyā utprekṣāyā hetusvarūpaphalānāṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃsvarūpaṃ darśayati-tadevamityādinā /
sa dharma iti yaṃ pratyeva heturutprekṣyate /
adhyavasāyavaśāditi bhede 'pyabhedāśrayaṇāt /
abhinna ityaprakṛtasaṃbandhinā dharmeṇa /
sa iti nimittatvenāśrito dharmaḥ /
niyameneti /
avācyaḥ punarna kadācidbhavatītyarthaḥ /
anyatheti avācyatve /
kaṃ pratiheturiti /
tasyaiva phalarūpatvāt /
nahi ya pratyeva heturutprekṣyate tasyaivāvācyatvaṃ yuktam /
sādhyamantareṇa sādhanasya nirviṣayatvāpatteḥ /
yadi cāsya nimittamātratvameva syātadvācyatvamavācyatva syāt /
evameka eva dharmo hetorutprekṣyamāṇasya nimittaṃ phalañceti siddham /
etadeva darśayati-apaśyantāvityādinā /
tatretihetūtprekṣaṇe /
nimittamiti tadvinotprekṣaṇasyāniṣpatteḥ /
dvividhamatra kṣāmatāgamana tapojanitamadarśanajanitaṃ ca /
tayoradhyavasāyavaśādabhinnatvenāśrayaṇam /
ataśca hetoreka eva dharmo nimittaṃ phalaṃ ca /
vastutastu tapojanitasya nimittatvamanyasya tu hetuphalarūpatvam /
ata eva netaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ /
dvayorapi bhinnatvāt /
maunitvameveti /
na punaranyatkiñcidityarthaḥ /
ataśca niścalatvādijanitasya duḥkhajanitasya ca maunitvasyābhedenāśrayaṇam /
sarvatretyanena samastalakṣyāviruddhatva hetūtprekṣāsvarūpakathanasyoktam /
evaṃ hetūtprekṣāyā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ svarūpaṃ pradarśya svarūpotprekṣāyā api darśiyati-svarūpotprekṣāyābhimityādinā /
children.translated_text:
And to show the distinction of this figure from other figures through the use or non-use of the respective words, he says '<s>apara</s>' and so forth.
'With the use of that word' means with the use of the word '<s>apara</s>'.
Since the word '<s>iva</s>', which indicates supposition, is not used, the identification becomes established.
And precisely for this reason, the object of comparison is not mentioned here.
For if it were mentioned, then with firm superimposition it would be <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), as stated immediately after.
But elsewhere, in all other cases, mention of the object of comparison alone is proper.
Thus, having shown how <s>utprekṣā</s> is established through variety of distinctions, he demonstrates the essential nature of cause, intrinsic nature, and result as applicable, beginning with '<s>tad evam</s>' and so forth.
'That property' — namely, that with respect to which a cause is imagined.
'Through the force of <s>adhyavasāya</s>' — because non-difference is resorted to even when there is difference.
'Non-different' — with the property belonging to the non-subject.
'That' refers to the property relied upon as the ground.
'Necessarily' — meaning that it is never unexpressed.
'Otherwise' means if it were unexpressed.
'For whom would the cause apply?' — because it itself has the nature of an effect.
For it is not proper that the very thing for which a cause is imagined should itself be unexpressed.
Because the means of proof would become objectless without the thing to be proved.
And if its role were merely that of a ground, then what is expressly stated would be unexpressed — a contradiction.
Thus it is established that one and the same property is both the ground and the effect of the cause being imagined.
This is demonstrated with '<s>apaśyantau</s>' and so forth.
'There' refers to the imagining of the cause.
'The ground' — because without it, the imagining would not be accomplished.
Here, the onset of thinness is of two kinds: that born of austerity and that born of not-seeing.
Of these two, non-difference is resorted to through the force of <s>adhyavasāya</s>.
Therefore, for the cause, one and the same property is both the ground and the effect.
But in reality, what is born of austerity has the status of ground, and the other has the status of cause-and-effect.
Hence there is no fault of mutual dependence,
since the two are in fact different.
'Silence itself' — meaning nothing else.
Therefore, the silence born of immobility and that born of grief are resorted to as non-different.
'Everywhere' — by this word it is stated that the explanation of the essential nature of <s>hetūtprekṣā</s> is not contradicted by any literary instance.
Having thus demonstrated the essential nature of <s>hetūtprekṣā</s> as applicable, he now shows that of <s>svarūpotprekṣā</s> (fancy regarding intrinsic nature) as well, beginning with '<s>svarūpotprekṣāyām abhimat</s>' and so forth.
<s>RuAss</s> 22/7:

children.text:
svarūpotprekṣāyāṃ yatra dharmī dharmyantaragatatvenotpekṣyate tatrāpi nimittabhūto dharmaḥ kkacinnirdiśyate /
yathā-'sa vaḥ pāyādunduḥ' ityādau /
atra kuṭulatvādi nirdiṣṭameva /
'veleva rāgasāgarasya' ityādau saṃkṣobhakāritvādi gamyamānam /
yatra ca dharma eva dharmigatatvenotprekṣyate tatrāpi nimittasyopādānānupādānābhyam /

children.translated_text: When it is mentioned, for example —
'Having received consecration, while this one takes his stand against enemies,
the earth, with its authority being overturned, trembled as if overwhelmed with fear.'

In <s>svarūpotprekṣā</s> (fancy regarding intrinsic nature), where the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is imagined as being another subject, there too the property serving as the ground is sometimes expressly stated.
As in '<s>sa vaḥ pāyād unduḥ</s>' (may it protect you) and so forth.
There, crookedness and similar properties are expressly stated.
In '<s>velā iva rāga-sāgarasya</s>' (like the shore of the ocean of passion) and so forth, the property of causing agitation and the like is implied.
And where a property alone is imagined as belonging to another subject, there too the ground may or may not be mentioned.

children.text:
atra bhūgatatvena bhayavihvalitatvākhyadharmotprekṣāyāṃ kampādinimittamupāttama /
anupādāne yathā-'lipmatīva tamo 'ṅgāni' ityādau /
atra tamotatatvena lepanakriyākartṛtvopekṣāyāṃ vyāpanādi nimittaṃ gamyamānam /
vyāpanādau tūtprekṣāviṣaye nimittamanyadanveṣyaṃ syāt /
na ca viṣayasya gamyamānatvaṃ yuktam /
tasyotprekṣitādhāratvena prastutasyābhidhātumucitatvāt /
tasmād yathoktameva sādhu /
children.translated_text:
Here, in the <s>utprekṣā</s> of the property called 'being overwhelmed with fear' as belonging to the earth, trembling and the like serve as the expressly stated ground.
When not mentioned, as in '<s>limpati iva tamo 'ṅgāni</s>' (as if darkness smears the limbs) and so forth.
Here, in the <s>utprekṣā</s> of darkness having the agency of the action of smearing, the pervasion and the like serve as the implied ground.
But if <s>utprekṣā</s> were applied to pervasion and the like as the object, then yet another ground would have to be sought.
And it is not proper for the object of comparison to be implied,
since it, being the substratum of what is imagined, is appropriately expressed as the subject under discussion.
Therefore, what has been stated is correct.
<s>RuAssC</s> 22/7:

children.text:
yadyapyuddeśata evaitatsvarūpotprekṣāyāṃ nimittopādānatvānupādānatvamavagamyate tathāpi hetūtprekṣāyāṃ yathā nimittopādānameva saṃbhavati tathātrāpi na saṃbhāṣyamityāśayena punarihaitaduktam /
yadā cātra dharmo dharmyantaragatatvenotprekṣyate tadā tatra nimittasya kīdṛgrapatvaṃ bhavatītyāśaṅkyāha-yatretyādi /
dharma eveti /
na punardharmī dharmigatatveneti /
dharmibhittitayetyarthaḥ /
atra hi dharmiṇo 'nyadharmadharmitvaṃ nigīryāntadharmadharmitvamavasthāpyate /
ata evātra dharmībhittibhūtatayā viṣayaḥ /
dharmiṇaṃ vinā kevalasyaiva dharmasyavyavasthāpayitumaśakyatvādvathavasyāpyamānatve vā dharmitvameva syāt /
vastutastu dharmaṃ evotprekṣāviṣayaḥ /
yannigaraṇenābhedapratipattirviṣayiṇo 'vasīyate /
sa ca nigīryamāṇodharmaḥ kvacidupātto bhavati kvaciccānupāttaḥ /

children.translated_text: With regard to '<s>prāpyābhiṣekam</s>' and so forth, others consider it to be <s>hetūtprekṣā</s> — therefore another example is cited:
'<s>Navarosadalia-ghaṇaniravalaṃba-saṃghaḍia-taḍikaḍapyavva</s> —
the mane-binding on the neck of <s>Narahari</s> is victorious, with its fierce mane like a flash of lightning joined to a dense, newly-angered splitting cloud.'

Although the mention or non-mention of the ground in <s>svarūpotprekṣā</s> is understood from the initial statement itself, nevertheless, since in <s>hetūtprekṣā</s> only mention of the ground is possible, to show that the same applies here as well, this is stated again.
When a property is imagined as belonging to another subject, what is the role of the ground therein? — anticipating this doubt, he says '<s>yatra</s>' and so forth.
'A property alone' — not a subject imagined as being another subject.
'As having the subject as foundation' — this is the meaning.
For here, the subject's possession of one set of properties is subsumed, and its possession of another set of properties is established.
Precisely for this reason, here the subject, serving as the foundation, functions as the object of comparison.
Since a property alone, without a subject, cannot be established — or if it were forced into independence, it would itself become a subject.
But in reality, the property alone is the object of <s>utprekṣā</s>.
That by whose subsumption the non-difference of the correlate is determined — that subsumed property is sometimes mentioned and sometimes not mentioned.
('<s>Nararoṣadalita-ghananiravalamba-saṃghaṭita-taḍitkaṭapraḥ</s> —
the mane-binding on the neck of <s>Narahari</s> (Man-Lion) is victorious, like a canopy of lightning joined to a dense cloud split by fresh fury.')

children.text:
atra kandharābandhadharmiṇi sakesaratvaṃ nigīrya sataḍitkaṭapratvamutprekṣitam /
kaḍāratvaṃ ca nimittamupāttam /
nigīryamāṇaśca dharmo dharmigatatvenopāttaḥ /
lepanakriyākartṛtvotprekṣāyāmiti,arthādāśaṅkitāyām /
evaṃ hi tamolepanamiveti pratītiḥ syāt /
na cātra tathetyāśaṅkyāha-vyāpanādāvityādi /
nimittamanyaditi tirodhāyakatvādi /
tena tamasi dharmiṇivyāpanādvidharmaṃ nigīrya lepanakriyākartṛtvarūpo dharmaṃ utprekṣita ityarthaḥ /
yadāha śrīmammaṭaḥ-
'vyāpanādi lepanādirūpatayā saṃbhāvitam' iti /
yatra ca dharmāntaranigaraṇena dharma eva dharmibhittitayotprekṣyate tatra bhittibhūtatvādviṣayarūpasya dharmiṇaḥ samanantaroktanīttyā gamyamānattvaṃ na yujyam ityāha-na cetyādi /
viṣayasyeti /
nigīryamāṇotprekṣyamāṇayordharmayobhittibhūtasya dharmiṇa ityarthaḥ /
na tu nigīryamāṇasyeti vyākhyeyam /
tasya hyupādānānupādānābhyāṃ dvaividhyaṃ bhavatīti samanantaramevoktam /
taccodāhṛtam /

children.translated_text: Or, for example —
'That which is like a white lotus, and which, pure as it is, like a pair of blue lotuses has arisen on a single stalk,
having reached that treasure-house of ruby-lustre as its root, my eyes have been truly conquered by the power of fortune.'

Here, in the subject which is the neck-binding, the property of having a mane is subsumed, and the property of having a lightning-canopy is imagined.
And the quality of being fierce (<s>kaḍāra</s>) is the expressly stated ground.
The subsumed property is mentioned as belonging to the subject.
As for the objection that in the <s>utprekṣā</s> of the agency of the action of smearing — this is to be understood as a hypothetical objection.
For thus the apprehension would be 'as if darkness smears' — but that is not the case here. Anticipating this, he says '<s>vyāpanādi</s>' and so forth.
'Another ground' refers to the property of being a concealer and the like.
Thus, regarding darkness as a subject, by subsuming the property of pervasion and the like, the property in the form of agency of the action of smearing is imagined — this is the meaning.
As the illustrious <s>Mammaṭa</s> states:
'Pervasion and the like are supposed to have the form of smearing and the like.'
And where, by the subsumption of one property, another property alone is imagined with the subject as foundation, there — since it serves as the foundation — the subject, which has the nature of the object, should not be considered implied, according to the principle just stated. He says '<s>na ca</s>' and so forth.
'Of the object' — meaning of the subject which serves as the foundation of both the subsumed and the imagined properties.
This should not be interpreted as referring to the subsumed property;
for its twofold classification through mention and non-mention has been stated immediately before.
And that has been illustrated.

children.text:
atra mukhādīnāmutprekṣāviṣayāṇāmanupādānādgamyamānatvam /
tasyeti dharmirūpasya viṣayasya /
utprekṣitādhāratveneti /
utprekṣitādhāratveneti /
utprekṣitasya lepanārdharmasya vyāpanādidharmanigaraṇenotprekṣāviṣayīkṛtasyādhāratvena bhittibhūtayetyarthaḥ /
dharmiṇamantareṇa dharmasyāviśrānteḥ /
prastutasyeti /
avaśyābhidheyasyetyarthaḥ /
evaṃ hetuphalotprekṣayorapi dharmigatatvenaivānyadharmahetukatvaṃ nigīryānyadharmahetutvamanyadharmaphalatvaṃ cādhyavasīyate /
ataśca sa dharmī vācya eva bhavati /
yathoktopapatteḥ /
nigīryamāṇaḥ punardharma evopādānānupādānābhyāṃ dvidhā /
tattu yathā- eṣā sthalītyādi /
atra nūpurasya dharmiṇo baddhamaunatve niścalatvādi dharmahetukatvaṃ nigīryamāṇaścānupātto dharmaḥ /

children.translated_text: When the property is explicitly mentioned, the example is as follows —
'The <s>cakravāka</s> bird, eager for sweet words to his beloved,
pulled the lotus-fiber stalk standing near his beak, as if in the delusion that it was the thread of a mechanical device for separating the two from each other.'

Here, because the subjects of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) such as face etc. are not explicitly mentioned, they are understood implicitly. 'Of that' refers to the subject-matter in the form of the <s>dharmin</s> (substantive). 'By being the substratum of the imagined' — by being the ground, like a wall, for the imagined property (<s>dharma</s>) of smearing etc., which has been made the object of <s>utprekṣā</s> through the absorption of other properties such as pervading. Since a property cannot rest without a substantive, 'of what is being presented' means what must necessarily be expressed. Similarly, in <s>hetu-utprekṣā</s> (causal fancy) and <s>phala-utprekṣā</s> (resultant fancy) also, the being-caused-by-another-property is absorbed by virtue of belonging to the substantive, and the being-a-cause-of-another-property and being-a-result-of-another-property are determined through superimposition. Therefore that substantive must indeed be stated, as demonstrated by the reasoning given above. The absorbed property, however, is of two kinds depending on whether it is explicitly mentioned or not. That is illustrated as follows — 'This is a ground' etc. Here the property of being bound in silence, namely motionlessness etc., which is the cause pertaining to the <s>dharmin</s> (substantive) anklet, is absorbed, and the property is not explicitly mentioned.

children.text:
atra cakravākasyāvarṣaṇe cāṭusamutsukahetutvaṃ nigīryaṃ bhrāntihetutvamadhyavasitam /
nigīryamāṇaśca dharma upāttaḥ /

children.translated_text: When the property is not explicitly mentioned, the example is as follows —
'The <s>kumudinī</s> (night-lily) flowers, full of delight, blossomed at that time,
as if to behold the withering of the <s>nalinī</s> (day-lotus) due to separation from her lord (the sun).'

Here, the actual cause of the <s>cakravāka</s>'s pulling — namely eagerness for sweet words — is absorbed, and causation through delusion is superimposed. The absorbed property is explicitly mentioned.

children.text:
atra kumudinīnāmunmīlane candrodayahetukatvaṃ nigīrya darśanaṃ phalatvenotprekṣitam /
nigīryamāṇaśca dharmo 'nupāttaḥ /
tadevaṃ hetusvarūpayoryathāsaṃbhavaṃ svarūpaṃ darśayitvā phalotprekṣāyā api darśayatiphalotprekṣāyāmityādinā /
children.translated_text: Here, the actual cause of the <s>kumudinī</s> flowers' blooming — namely moonrise — is absorbed, and 'beholding' is imagined as the result. The absorbed property is not explicitly mentioned. Having thus shown the nature of both cause and essential form as applicable, he now shows it for <s>phala-utprekṣā</s> (resultant fancy) also, beginning with 'In <s>phala-utprekṣā</s>' and so on.
<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 22/8:

children.text:
phalotprekṣāyāṃ yadeva tasya kāraṇaṃ tadeva nimittam /
tasyānupādāne kasya tatphalatvenoktaṃ syāt /
tasmāttatra tasya nimittasyopādānameva na prakārāntaram /

children.translated_text: For example —
'As if for the turning back of the ancient horses
stationed on chariots, the sun proceeded toward the northern direction, the birthplace of excellent horses.'

In <s>phala-utprekṣā</s> (resultant fancy), what is the cause of that result is itself the basis. If that basis is not mentioned, of what would that result be stated? Therefore in that case, the mention of the basis is itself required, and there is no other alternative.
Here, the going northward — which is the cause of the result of horse-replacement — is itself the basis and is explicitly mentioned.
Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 22/8:

children.text:
tasyeti phalasya /
evacca hetūtprekṣaghāvicāragranthavivṛteravagatārthamiti granthavistarabhayānna punarāyasyate /
tadevaṃ granthakṛdātmanaḥ ślāghāṃ kaṭākṣayannetadupasaṃharati /
children.translated_text: 'Of that' means of the result. And indeed, since the meaning has been understood from the elaboration of the investigation section on <s>hetu-utprekṣā</s> (causal fancy), he does not belabor the point again for fear of prolixity. Thus, the author of the treatise, casting a sidelong glance at his own commendation, concludes this section.
<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 22/9:

children.text:
tadasāvutprekṣāyāḥ kakṣyāvibhāgaḥ pracuratayā sthito 'pi lakṣye duravadhāratvādiha na prapañcitaḥ /
tasyāścevādiśabdavanmanyeśabdo 'pi pratipādakaḥ /
kiṃ tūtprekṣāsāmagrathabhāve manyeśabdaprayogo vitarkameva pratipādayati /
yathodāhṛtaṃ prāk 'ahaṃ tvinduṃ manye tvadariviraha' ityādi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this classification of grades of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), though abundantly present in literary works, has not been elaborated here because of the difficulty of determining it. And the word <s>manye</s> ('I think'), like the word <s>iva</s> ('as if'), is also an indicator of <s>utprekṣā</s>. However, in the absence of the complete apparatus of <s>utprekṣā</s>, the use of the word <s>manye</s> conveys only <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture). As was illustrated earlier: 'I think the moon is your enemy's absence' and so on.
Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 22/9:

children.text:
tadasāvityādi /
asyāśca vācakavyavasthāṃ darśayati-tasyāścetyādi /
utprekṣāyāmagrathabhāva iti saṃbhāvanāpratyayātmakatvābhāvāt /
prāgiti,apahṇutau /
evanivaśabdo 'pi kvacidvitarkameva pratipādayati /

children.translated_text: For example —

children.text: 'vṛttānupūrve ca na cātidīrghe jaḍghe śume sṛṣṭavatastadīye /
children.translated_text: 'Her legs, neither too round nor too long, being beautiful and well-proportioned, having been created by <s>Vidhātṛ</s> (the Creator),
it was as if the effort of the Creator in fashioning the remaining limbs was devoted to producing elegance.'

'Therefore this' and so on. He shows the convention of its indicator words: 'of that' and so on. 'In the absence of the apparatus of <s>utprekṣā</s>' means the absence of the nature of the presumptive suffix. 'Earlier' refers to the section on <s>apahṇuti</s> (denial). Similarly, the word <s>iva</s> ('as if') also sometimes conveys only <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture).
For identity-in-difference, an example from <s>Pṛthvīrājavijaya</s> —
'By the soldiers seizing with utmost devotion the successive rows of <s>Bāṇaliṅgas</s> (Śiva-liṅgas from the <s>Narmadā</s>),
A <s>Narmadā</s> was as it were created that was not actually the <s>Narmadā</s> river.'
And this figure is also seen in the variety of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) that consists of identity-in-difference and so on.
For connection-in-disconnection, an example —

'May that non-duality be yours, for the nourishment of the non-duality of consciousness — of Him whose body is twofold, being the beloved of <s>Ramā</s> enriched by her son, and of <s>Bhṛtputrī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>),

children.text: yatrākārṣṇyaṃ nija iva vidandakṣiṇārdhaprabhābhirdehe 'nyeṣāmapi puraripuḥ kārṣṇyamantaḥ pramārṣṭi' //
children.translated_text: where the Enemy of the Cities (<s>Śiva</s>), treating the blackness of the right half as his own, wipes away the blackness from the bodies of others too with the radiance of that half.'
Here, despite the non-difference of the <s>Narmadā</s>, difference is expressed.
For connection-in-disconnection, an example —
'As if washed with milk and resembling the moon, as if cleansed with indigo dye and resembling cloth,
as if the sun were scratched out with a chisel — the spring moonlight expanded.'
Here, despite the connection with blackness, disconnection is expressed.
For the simultaneity of cause and effect, an example —
'He arose together with fame, grew together with prosperity,
was born together with splendor, and rose together with generosity.'
Here, despite the disconnection of actually being washed with milk etc., connection is expressed.
For the reversal of temporal sequence, an example —
'The arrows fly forth first, as it were; the bow is strung afterward, as it were;

children.text: anvakprahārā iva saṃghaṭante prāṇāndviṣaḥ pūrvamiva tyajanti' //
children.translated_text: the blows seem to follow, and the enemies' lives seem to depart beforehand.'
This figure is also seen in the reversal of cause and effect, as in —
'This river, the birth of the moon, with its continuous worship of the Lord's speech, noble, single-pointed, with creepers releasing flowers within its pure interior,

children.text: yasyāḥ pāṇḍurapuṇḍarokapaṭalavyājena tīradvaye śaścatpārvaṇacandramaṇḍalaśatānīva prasūte jalam' //
children.translated_text: whose waters, under the pretext of beds of white lotuses on both banks, seem to produce hundreds of ever-present full-moon discs.'
This is also seen with reversal of sequence, as in —
'Resplendent with his lower lip showing teeth in an undiminished, proud smile,

children.text: samutthitaḥ kṣīravipāṇḍurāṇi pītveva sadyo dviṣatāṃ yaśāṃsi' //
children.translated_text: he arose and immediately seemed to drink the milk-white fame of his enemies.'
Here there is a reversal of cause and effect, since the moon is born from the <s>Narmadā</s> river.

children.text:
atra samutthānānantarabhāvino yaśaḥ pānasya pūrvanirddeśātkramikaviparyayaḥ /
atraiva 'pibannivoccaiḥ' iti pāṭhe tu kramikayoḥ samakālabhāvitvam /
children.translated_text: Here, the prior mention of the drinking of fame, which actually follows the rising, constitutes a reversal of sequence. In the alternative reading 'as if drinking aloud,' there is simultaneity of the two sequential events.
Beginning of <s>Sūtra</s> 23:
Having thus determined <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) with respect to the potentiality of superimposition, he now defines <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) with respect to its accomplished state —
When the superimposed identification predominates, it is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). // <s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 23 //

children.text:
adhyavasāne trayaṃ saṃbhavati- svarūpaṃ viṣayo viṣayī ca /
viṣayasya hi viṣayiṇāntarnigīrṇatve 'dhyavasāyasya svarūpotthānam /
tatra sādhyatve svarūpaprādhānyam /
siddhatve tvadhyavamitaprādhānyam /
viṣayaprādhānyamadhyavasāye naiva saṃbhavati /
adhyavasitaprādhānye cātiśayoktiḥ /
anyāśca pañcaprakārāḥ /
bhede 'bhedaḥ /
abhede bhedaḥ /
saṃbandhe 'saṃbandhaḥ /
asaṃbandhe saṃbandhaḥ /
kāryakāraṇapaurvāparyavidhvaṃsaśca /
children.translated_text: In superimposition, three things are possible: the essential nature, the object (<s>viṣaya</s>), and the subject (<s>viṣayin</s>). When the object is absorbed within the subject, the essential nature of the superimposition arises. When it is in the potential state, the essential nature predominates. When it is in the accomplished state, the superimposed identification predominates. The predominance of the object is simply not possible in superimposition. When the superimposed identification predominates, it is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). And there are five other varieties: identity-in-difference; difference-in-identity; disconnection-in-connection; connection-in-disconnection; and the destruction of the temporal sequence of cause and effect.
Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 23:

children.text:
etadupasaṃharannanyadavatārayati - evamityādi /
tāmeva lakṣayutumāha-adhyavasitetyādi /
etadeva vyākhyātumadhyavasāyasya tāvadyathāsaṃbhavaṃ svarūpaṃ darśayati-adhyavasāna iti /
parasparaniṣṭhatvānupapatteradhyavasāyasya kiṃ viṣayaviṣayibhyāmityāśaṅkyāha-viṣayasya hītyādi /
viṣayaviṣayibhyāmantareṇādhyavasāya eva na bhavatītyarthaḥ /
eṣāmeva viṣayavibhāgaṃ darśayati-tatretyādinā /
tatreti trayanirdhāraṇe /
svarūpaprādhānyamiti adhyavasāyaprādhānyam /
adhyavasitaprādhānyamiti viṣayiprādhānyam /
sādhyatvaṃ coprekṣāyāmeva nirṇītam /
naiva saṃbhavatīti-adhyavasāyasvarūpānudayāt /
tadevaṃ viṣayiṇaḥ prādhānyavivakṣāyāmalaṅkāre bhavatītyāha-adhyavasitetyādi /

children.translated_text: And it has been stated elsewhere —
'When the cognition of the potentiality of superimposition arises, this is accepted (as <s>utprekṣā</s>);
but when the cognition of its accomplished state arises, there is the understanding of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).'

While concluding this, he introduces the next topic — 'thus' and so on. To define that, he says 'the superimposed' and so on. To explain this, he first shows the nature of superimposition as applicable — 'in superimposition' and so on. Anticipating the question: since mutual dependence is untenable, does superimposition arise from the object and subject? — he says 'of the object indeed' and so on. The meaning is that without object and subject, superimposition itself does not occur. He shows the distribution of these — with 'there' and so on. 'There' is for the determination of the three. 'Predominance of essential nature' means predominance of superimposition. 'Predominance of the superimposed' means predominance of the subject. And the potentiality has already been determined in <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). 'Is simply not possible' — because the essential nature of superimposition would not arise. Thus, when the predominance of the subject is intended in the figure, he says 'the superimposed' and so on.
Thus.

children.text:
pañceti nyūnādhikasaṃkhyānirāsārtham /
ata eva kāryakāraṇapaurvāparyavidhvaṃsatya caturthabhedāntarbhāvo na vācyaḥ /
evaṃ hi bhedāntarāṇāmapi tadantarbhāva eva syāt /
abhedādyasaṃbandhe 'pi saṃbandhopanibandhanāt /
atha bhavatvetaditi cet /
na /
'atra ca yadyapi sarvatrabhede 'bhedādau vastuto /
āsabandhe saṃbandha eva varṇayituṃ śakyate tathāpyavāntarabhedavivakṣayānyairlakṣitatvādviviktasyāsaṃbandhe saṃbandhasya darśitatvācca vibhāgenanirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ' iti bhavadbhirevoktatvāt /
tatsamānanyāyatvātkathamasyāpi caturthabhedāntarbhāvo nyāyyaḥ /
atha 'yadi kāryakāraṇayoḥ paurvāparyavidhvaṃsātsamānakālatādyabhāve 'pi tathopanibandhe pañcamo 'tra prakāra iṣyate taddeśakālayoḥ padārthasaṃbandhe viśeṣābhāvādbhinnadeśatvābhāve 'pi tathopanibandhe ṣaṣṭo 'pi bhedaḥ parigaṇanīya iti nirviṣayatvādasaṃgaterabhāvaḥ prasajyata' iti cet /
nautat /
yasmādatiśayoktāvatiśayākhyaprayojanapratipipādayiṣayā viṣayanigaraṇena viṣayiprādhānyaṃ vivakṣitam, asagatau tu viruddhatvapratyāyanāya kāryakāraṇayobhinnadeśatvamityubhavrāpyasti tāvannirvivādo lakṣaṇabhedaḥ /
kāryakāraṇapaurvāparyavidhvaṃse ca vallabhakartṛkasya hṛdayādhiṣṭānasya kāraṇasya smarakartṛkasya ca kāryasya pūrvāparībhāvaṃ nigīrya 'tvaddarśanenaiva viṣayāntaravaimukhyena tvanabhilāṣaparaiva jātetyatiśayaprayojanapratipādanārthamanyathātvamadhyavasitamityati śayoktibhedatvamevāsya nyāyyaṃ na tvasaṃgatibhedatvam /

children.translated_text: In that regard —
'The leader of her retinue bound the hair-knot of the doe-eyed woman with <s>campaka</s>-flower garlands;
and anger became firmly established in the hearts of the rival women with eyes like those of a <s>sāraṅga</s> deer.'

'Five' is stated to exclude a lesser or greater number. For this very reason, the inclusion of the destruction of the temporal sequence of cause and effect within the fourth variety should not be asserted. For if so, then other varieties too would be included within it. Since disconnection-in-identity etc. is also based on connection. If one says 'let it be so,' no — because 'although everywhere in difference-in-identity etc. there is actually connection-in-disconnection, which can be described as connection, nevertheless, because other scholars have distinguished it and because connection-in-disconnection has been separately demonstrated, the classification is made distinctly' — this was stated by you yourselves. By the same reasoning, how is the inclusion of this too within the fourth variety justified? If one argues that 'when, despite the absence of simultaneity etc. in the temporal sequence of cause and effect, it is represented as such, a fifth variety is accepted, then since there is no difference in the relation of objects to place and time, a sixth variety should also be enumerated for the representation of non-different location as different location' — this would make the position groundless and lead to absurdity. But that is not so. Because in <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), the predominance of the subject through the absorption of the object is intended for the purpose of conveying exaggeration; and in disconnection, the different location of cause and effect is intended to convey contradiction. Both of these are undisputed differences in definition. And in the destruction of the temporal sequence of cause and effect, the prior-posterior relation of the cause authored by the beloved and the effect authored by <s>Smara</s> (Love) is absorbed, and 'by your very sight, through aversion to other objects, the longing directed toward you alone arose' — this alternative state is superimposed for the purpose of conveying exaggeration. Therefore it is proper that this be a variety of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), not a variety of disconnection.

children.text:
ityādau dhammille bandhaścitteṣu ca manyusthairyamiti kāryakāraṇayorbhinnadeśatvam /
yatraiva bandhastatraiva tatkāryasya sthairyasyopapatterviruddhatvapratyāyakam /
virodhasya cātrābhāsamānatvam /
dhammillabandhamanyusthairyayorvastuto 'pi kāyakāraṇabhāvasadbhāvākhyasya bādhakapratyayasyollāsāt /
na ca bādhodaye 'pi virodhāpratītiḥ /
dvicandrapratītivadanupapadyamānatayā skhaladgatitvena tatpratīteravasthānāt /
na cātiśayoktau skhaladgatitvam /
niścayasvabhāvatvādasyā anupapadyamānatvaśaṅkāyā apyabhāvāt /
nahi kāryakāraṇayoḥ paurvāparyavidhvaṃsa upapadyata ityatra vivakṣitaṃ kintvevaṃ phalametaditi /
children.translated_text: For what is intended here is not 'the destruction of the temporal sequence of cause and effect is untenable,' but rather 'such is the result of this.'

children.text: ata evāsaṃgateratiśayākteśca svarūpabhedo 'pīti kāryakāraṇayoḥ paurvāparyavidhvaṃsenāsaṃgatirbhinnadeśatvam cātiśayoktiriti yathoktameva yuktam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the essential difference between <s>asaṃgati</s> (disconnection) and <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is also established. Thus, the destruction of the temporal sequence of cause and effect is disconnection, and different location is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — this is exactly as stated and is proper.
And for this very reason: 'The reversal of the temporal sequence and the simultaneous arising
of cause and effect — these two are sprouts of apparent contradiction.'

In this verse, the binding of the hair-knot and the firmness of anger in the hearts represent different locations for cause and effect. Since the binding would produce its effect of firmness only in the same location, representing it in a different location conveys contradiction. And the contradiction here is only apparent; because the actual cause-effect relation between the binding of the hair-knot and the firmness of anger is contradicted by a sublating cognition that affirms the existence of a cause-effect relation. Nor does the cognition of contradiction fail even when sublation arises; for, like the perception of two moons, that cognition persists in a faltering manner due to its being untenable. Nor is there faltering in <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), because this figure is of the nature of certainty, and there is no possibility even of doubt regarding its untenability.

children.text:
ityādyapi yadanyairuktaṃ tadayuktameveti na nyūnaprakāratvam /
kecicca sarvālaṅkāraṇāmapyatiśayoktereva prabhedatvādasyā bahuprakāratāmācakṣate /
tathā hyupamāyāmapyastyetadbhedatvam /
nyūnaguṇasya mukhāderadhikaguṇena candrādinā sābhye 'tiśayānatipātāt,atiśayaṃ vinā ca gauriva gavaya ityādāvanalaṅkāratvāt /
ataścātiśayasyaiva sarvālaṅkārabījabhūtatvāt 'ekaivātiśayoktiśca kāvyasyālaṅkṛtirmatā' ityuktam /
naitat /
iha hyatiśayasya dvayī gatiḥ yadayaṃ kavipratibhānivartitaḥ sāmānyātmā bhavati,bhede 'pyabheda ityevamādirūpo viśeṣātmā vā /
tatrādyaḥ sarvairevālaṅkārabījatayābhyupagataḥ /
anyathā hi gauriva gavaya ityādāvalaṅkāratvaṃ syāt /
tāvatā punaretatprabhedatvaṃ sarvālaṅkārāṇāṃ na yuktam /
tattve hi viśeṣokyullekhādīnāmapi tatprasaṅgaḥ /
sarvālaṅkārāṇamapi viśeṣoktyullekharūpatvāt /
atha dvitīyapakṣāśrayeṇaitaducyate tadapyuktam /
asyā hyadhyavasitaprādhānyaṃ lakṣaṇam /
taccālaṅkārāṇāṃ na saṃbhavati /
tathātvānavagamāt /
ataścaiṣāmasaṃbhavattatsāmānyatvātkathaṃ tadviśeṣatvamiti bahuprakāratvamasyā nirastam /
children.translated_text: What has been stated by others in passages such as this is indeed incorrect, so there is no deficiency in the number of varieties. Some, however, declare the multiplicity of varieties of this [<s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole)], since all ornaments are indeed sub-types of <s>atiśayokti</s> alone. For in <s>upamā</s> (simile) too, this sub-type status exists. Since in comparing something of lesser quality such as the face with something of greater quality such as the moon, there is no transcendence of exaggeration, and without exaggeration, as in 'the cow is like the <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox),' there would be no ornament. Therefore, since <s>atiśaya</s> (exaggeration) alone is the seed of all ornaments, it has been said: 'Hyperbole alone is considered the ornamentation of poetry.' This is not correct. For here, exaggeration has two courses: either it is of a general nature, produced by the poet's creative imagination, or it is of a specific nature, having the form 'identity despite difference' and the like. Of these, the first is accepted by all as the seed of ornaments. For otherwise, even in 'the cow is like the <s>gavaya</s>,' there would be ornament-status. But merely on that account, the sub-type status of all ornaments under this is not justified. For if that were the case, then <s>viśeṣokti</s> (specific statement), <s>ullekha</s> (indication), and others would also fall under that category, since all ornaments also have the nature of <s>viśeṣokti</s> and <s>ullekha</s>. If this is said based on the second position, that too has been addressed. For the defining characteristic of this [<s>atiśayokti</s>] is the predominance of what is superimposed (<s>adhyavasita</s>). And that is not possible in [other] ornaments, because such a nature is not perceived in them. Therefore, since this is impossible for them, how can they be its sub-types merely due to sharing a general quality? Thus the multiplicity of its varieties has been refuted.
<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, Sūtra 23/1:
There, identity in difference is as follows—
'The lotus is upon the water, and in the lotus are <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotuses), and those are upon a golden creeper;
She is so delicate and beautiful—what is this chain of miraculous events?'
Here, identity of the face and other [features] with the lotus and others, despite their difference, [is expressed].
Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, Sūtra 23/1:

children.text:
mukhādīnāmiti /
na tu vāstavasya saundaryasya kamalādyairiti /
na tu kavisamarpitenasaundaryeṇa /
ata eva ca, 'atrātiśayākhyamityādiḥ' tadabhiprāyeṇaivādhyavasitaprādhānyam- ityantaścottarakāliko granthaḥ svamatijāhyāllekhakairanyathā likhita iti niścinumaḥ /
ayaṃ hi granthakṛtaḥ paścātkaiścidvipaścidbhiḥ patrikābhirlikhita ityavagītā prasiddhiḥ /
tataśca tairanavadhānena granthāntaraprasaṅgatvādanupayuktatvādvā patrikāntarādayamasamañjasaprāyo granthakhaṇḍo likhita iti /
na punarekatraiva tadaiva mukhādīnāṃ kamalādyairbhede 'pyabheda ityuktvāpi 'na tu vadanādīnāṅkamalādibhirabhedādhyavasāyo yojanīya' ityādi vacanaṃ pūrvāparaparāhatamasya vaiduṣyaśālinogranthakārasya saṃbhāvyam /
children.translated_text: 'Of the face and other [features]'—but not of the actual beauty with the lotus and others; rather, not with the beauty attributed by the poet. And precisely because of this, we determine that the passage from 'here what is called <s>atiśaya</s>' up to 'the predominance of what is superimposed' is a later text that has been written differently by scribes due to their own lack of intelligence. For it is well-known that this work of the author was later copied onto manuscripts by certain scholars. And so, through their inattention, because of its being connected to another text or because of its irrelevance, this largely inconsistent portion of the text was written from another manuscript. For it is not conceivable that the learned author, having said in one and the same place 'identity despite difference of the face and other [features] with the lotus and others,' would then also say 'but the superimposition of identity of the face and others with the lotus and others should not be construed'—such a self-contradictory statement is not to be attributed to this erudite author.
<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, Sūtra 23/2:
Difference in identity is as follows—
'Different is the beauty, and some other quality of appearance;
The dark one is beyond the ordinary, her outline indeed cannot exist [elsewhere].'
('Different is the beauty, and some other quality of appearance;
The dark one is beyond the ordinary <s>Prajāpati</s>'s [creation], her outline indeed cannot exist [elsewhere].')
Here, despite identity of charm and other [qualities], difference is [expressed] by [describing them as] 'other.'

children.text: yathā vā-- 'maggialaddhaṃmi valāmoḍiacuṃbieṃ apyaṇā a uvaṇamie /
children.translated_text: Or as follows—'When obtained on the road, kissed by force, and brought near by oneself,
In the single lip of the beloved, different flavors arise one after another.'
('When obtained on the road, kissed by force, and brought near by oneself,
In the single lip of the beloved, different flavors arise one after another.')
Connection in disconnection is as follows—

children.text: 'lāvaṇyadraviṇavyayo na gaṇitaḥ kleśo mahānsvīkṛtaḥ svacchandaṃ carato janasya hṛdaye cintājvaro nirmitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The expenditure of the wealth of beauty was not counted, great toil was undertaken, in the heart of the freely moving person a fever of anxiety was produced;

children.text: eṣāpi svaguṇānurūparamaṇābhāvād varākī hatā ko 'rthaścetasi vedhasā vinihitastanvyāstanuṃ tanvatā' //
children.translated_text: She too, poor thing, is ruined for want of a lover matching her own qualities—what purpose did the Creator have in mind when fashioning the slender one's body?'
Here, although the flavor of the beloved's lip is undivided, there is a suggestion of difference through the division of conditions.
Here, despite the connection of the expenditure of the wealth of beauty, disconnection is composed for the purpose of establishing the excellence of the slender woman's beauty.

children.text: yathā vā-- 'asyāḥ sargavidhau prajāpatipabhūccandro nu kāntipradaḥ śṛṅgāraikarasaḥ svayaṃ nu madano māso nu puṣkākaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Or as follows—'In the creation of this [woman], was the moon the giver of radiance to <s>Prajāpati</s>? Was <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) himself, the sole essence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment)? Was the month of spring the creator?

children.text: vedābhyāsajaḍaḥ kathaṃ nu viṣayavyāvṛttakautūhalo nirmātuṃ prabhavenmanoharamidaṃ rūpaṃ purāṇo muniḥ' //
children.translated_text: How could the ancient sage, dull from the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, with curiosity turned away from worldly objects, be capable of creating this enchanting form?'
Connection in disconnection is as follows—
'If a flower were set upon a coral, or a pearl were placed upon bright coral,
Then it would imitate the radiance of her bright smile, set around red lips.'
Here, disconnection is stated despite the connection with creation by the ancient <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: atra saṃbhāvanayā saṃbandhaḥ yathā vā- 'dāho 'mbhaḥprasṛtiṃpacaḥ pracayavān bāṣpaḥ praṇālocitaḥ śvāsāḥ preṅkhikatadīpradīpakalikāḥ pāṇṭimni magnaṃ vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the connection is through supposition. Or as follows—'A burning, a flowing of waters, an accumulation of tears, a gazing forth, sighs that are like the flickering of the flame of the lamp, a body sunk in pallor;

children.text: kiṃ tāmyatkathagrāmi rātrimakhilāṃ tvanmārgavātāgrane hastacchattraniruddhacandramahasastasyāḥ sthitirvartate' //
children.translated_text: What is this ailing one speaking of throughout the night? In the presence of the wind from your path, the condition of that woman whose moonlike face has the moon obstructed by the hand-held parasol, persists.'
Here, despite the disconnection of burning and other [states] with the flowing of water and other [states], connection is stated as if established.
Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, Sūtra 23/2:

children.text:
laḍahatvādīnāmiti,ādiśabdād vartanacchāyāyā eva grahaṇam /
tatraivābhede 'pi bhedavivakṣaṇāt /
uttarārdhe hi saṃbandhe 'pyasaṃbandhaḥ /
'lāvaṇyadraviṇavyayo na gaṇitaḥ' ityasya pādatrayī tanvīlāvaṇyaprakarṣapratipādanārthamityetatprayojanadarśanaṃ sarvodāharaṇopalataṇaparam /
saṃbhāvanayeti /
natu vastutaḥ /
ata eva saṃbandhasyāvāstavatvādudāharaṇāntaramāha-dāho 'mbha ityādi /
vāśabdaḥ samuccayārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of charm and other [qualities]'—the word 'and other' includes the quality of appearance itself. For therein, despite identity, difference is intended. In the latter half, however, there is disconnection despite connection. 'The expenditure of the wealth of beauty was not counted'—the indication of the purpose in the three quarters as being for establishing the excellence of the slender woman's beauty applies to all the examples. 'Through supposition'—but not in reality. Precisely because the connection is unreal, another example is given—'A burning, water' and so forth. The word 'or' has a cumulative meaning.
<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, Sūtra 23/3:
Reversal is as follows—
'The heart was first conquered by the flower-arrowed one of <s>Mālatī</s>;
Lastly, O beloved of the beautiful woman, it was beheld by your eyes.'
The destruction of the sequential order of cause and effect is either through reversal of sequence or through simultaneity.

children.text:
tulyakālatvaṃ yathā--
'aviralavilolajaladaḥ kuṭajārjunanīpasurabhivanavātaḥ /
ayamāyātaḥ kālo hanta hṛtāḥ pathikagehinyaḥ' //
children.translated_text: Simultaneity is as follows— 'With dense and trembling clouds, with forest breezes fragrant with <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, and <s>nīpa</s> [flowers], this season has arrived—alas, the wives of travelers are carried away!'
Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, Sūtra 23/3:

children.text:
atra ca kāryakāraṇapaurvāparyavidhvaṃsa ityanena prasiddhayoḥ kāryakāraṇayorvidhvaṃso viparyayastathā paurvāparyasyādipaścātkālabhāvitvena prasiddhasya kramatya vidhvaṃso vyatyayaḥ sahabhāvo vetyapi bhedatrayaṃ tantreṇoktam /
evaṃ ca kāryakāraṇavidhvaṃsasyāpi pañca prakārāḥ /
avāntaraprakāratvātpunareṣāṃ pañcaprakāratvaṃ niyamagarbhīkāreṇa pūrvaṃ vyākhyātam /

children.translated_text: There, reversal of cause and effect is as follows—
'So bright, so much causing the contraction of the radiance of the moon,
The thousand-petaled [lotus] of the lake becomes the cause.'

Here, by 'the destruction of the sequential order of cause and effect,' three sub-types are stated in a compressed manner: the destruction—that is, reversal—of [the relationship between] two things well-known as cause and effect; the destruction—that is, transposition or co-occurrence—of sequential order, meaning what is well-known as occurring in an earlier-and-later temporal sequence. Thus there are also five varieties of the destruction of the cause-and-effect [relationship]. Since these are sub-varieties, the fivefold division of these was previously explained through the method of restrictive inclusion.
('So bright is it, causing the contraction of the radiances of the moon,
The thousand-petaled lotus of the lake becomes the cause.')

children.text:
atrendukānteḥ saṃkoce viparyayeṇa śatapatrasya kāraṇatvamadhyavasitam /
atra bhede 'bheda ityevaṃrūpātiśayoktirhetutvena sthitā /
uttare tvardhe saiva śliṣṭaśabdanibandhanā hetuḥ /
tathābhāvopanibandhaścātra vaktrasya lāvaṇyaprakarṣapratipādanārtham /
kramaviparyayo yathā-
'kupitasyaprathamamandhakārī bhavati vidyā tato bhrukuṭiḥ, ādāvindriyāṇi rāgaḥ samāskandati, caramaṃ cakṣuḥ,ākambhe tapo galati paścātsvedasalilam,pūrvamayaśaḥ sphuratyanantaramadhara' iti /
atra kopakārye vidyābhrukuṭyādīnāmandhakārībhavanādau kramaṃ nigīrya tadviparyayo 'dhyavasitaḥ /

children.translated_text: Simultaneity of that very [sequence] is as follows—
'From the chambers of love, the attendants; smoothly, the jeweled girdle from the hips;
Shame from the hearts—they depart together, simultaneously, of the moon-faced women.'

Here, through reversal, the hundred-petaled [lotus] is superimposed as the cause of the contraction of the moon's radiance. Here, <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) in the form of 'identity despite difference' stands as the basis. In the latter half, however, that very [hyperbole] rests upon an ambiguous word. Likewise, the suggestion of existence is here for the purpose of establishing the excellence of the beauty of the face. Reversal of sequence is as follows— 'When angry, first comes darkness, then the frown of the brow; at the outset the senses, then passion assails; in agitation, austerity melts away, afterwards sweat-water; first infamy appears, then the lip'—thus. Here, in the effects of anger such as the frown becoming darkness, the sequence is swallowed up and its reversal is superimposed.
('From the chambers of love, the attendants; smoothly, the jeweled girdle from the hips;
Shame from the hearts—they depart together, simultaneously, of the moon-faced women.')

children.text:
atra parijanādīnāmapasaraṇe kramikatve 'pi samakālatvamadhyavasitam /
evameṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva bhedānāṃ lokāsabhavadviṣayatvaṃ darśayitumāha /
children.translated_text: Here, although the departure of the attendants and others is sequential, simultaneity is superimposed. Thus, to demonstrate that the domain of all these varieties is what is impossible in ordinary experience, he says:
<s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, Sūtra 23/4:

children.text:
eṣu pañcasu bhedeṣu bhede 'bhedādivacanaṃ lokātikrāntagocaram /
ataścātrātiśayākhyaṃ yatphalaṃ prayojakatvānnimittaṃ tatrābhedādhyavasāyaḥ /
tathā hi 'kamalamanambhasi' ityādau vadanādīnāṃ kamalādyairbhede 'pi vāstavaṃ saundaryaṃ kavisamarpitena saundaryeṇābhedenādhyavasitaṃ bhede 'bhedavacanasya nimittam /
tatra ca siddho 'dhyavasāya ityadhyavasitaprādhānyam /
na tu vadanādīnāṃ kamalādibhirabhedādhyavasāyo yojanīyaḥ, abhede bheda ityādiṣu prakāreṣvaṣyāpteḥ /
tatra hi 'aṇṇaṃ laḍahṛttaṇaaṃ' ityādau sātiśayaṃ laḍahatvaṃ nimittabhūtabhedenādhyavasitam /
evamanyatrāpi jñeyam /
tadabhiprāyeṇaivādhyavasitaprādhānyam /
prakārapañcakamadhyātkāryakāraṇabhāvena yaḥ prakāraḥ sa kāryakāraṇatāśrayālaṅkāraprastāve prapañcārthaṃ lakṣiyiṣyate /
children.translated_text: In these five varieties, the statement of identity in difference and so forth has a domain that transcends ordinary experience. And therefore, what is called <s>atiśaya</s> (exaggeration) is the result, and since it is the motivating factor, it is the cause; therein, the superimposition of identity [is the essence]. Thus, in 'the lotus is upon the water' and so forth, although there is difference between the face and other [features] and the lotus and others, the actual beauty is superimposed through identity with the beauty attributed by the poet—this is the cause of the statement of identity in difference. And therein, the superimposition is established, hence the predominance of what is superimposed. But the superimposition of identity of the face and others with the lotus and others should not be construed, because that would apply also to such varieties as 'difference in identity' and others. For there, in 'different is the beauty' and so forth, the exaggerated charm is superimposed through the difference that serves as the cause. Similarly in other cases too it should be understood. It is with this intention that 'the predominance of what is superimposed' [is stated as the definition]. Among the five varieties, the variety that involves cause-and-effect relationship will be examined in detail in the section on ornaments based on causal relationship.
Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>, <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s>, Sūtra 23/4:

children.text:
eṣvityādi /
eṣviti viṣayasatpamī /
eṣa cāvayavanirdeśaḥ /
lokātikrānteti /
kavipratibhānirmitameva sātiśayaṃ vastveṣāṃ viṣaya ityarthaḥ /
atreti bhedapañcake /
caśabdaḥ prameyāntarasamuccayārthaḥ /
phalamiti /
tasyaiva pratipipādayiṣitatvāt /
tatreti /
vāntavasya sgaindaryasya kavisamarpitena saundaryeṇābhedavacane /
nanu cātra vadanādīnāṃ kamalādyadhyavasāyaḥ pratīyata iti kathametaduktamityāśaṅkyāha-na tvityādi /
kutaśca teṣvavyātpirityāśaṅkayāha-tatra hītyādi /
kamalamanambhasītyatra hi yadi vadanādīnāṃ dharmiṇāmabhedādhyavasāyayojanaṃ kriyate tattasya dhamigatatvenaiveṣṭeriha dharmāṇāṃ na syādavyātpiḥ /
ataśca pūrvatra dharmāṇābhevādhyavasāyo yojanīyo yena sarvatraika eva pakṣaḥ syāditi tātparyārthaḥ /
upalakṣyaṃ caitat /
yāvatā hyadhyavasitaprādhānyamasyā lakṣaṇam /
