children.translated_text: Or for example:
'Born along with fortune, nurtured along with subjects,
grown along with meritorious deeds — she gave birth to that king who was like the ocean.'

[He cites] the half-verse 'Along with the lotuses, the pride of the women contracts.' Without the distinguishing feature [means] without the animating force of <s>atiśayokti</s>. [He cites] the second half-verse 'By breezes that have removed the perspiration with pollen brought from other islands.' 'These' refers to those just mentioned. Since the celestial host's desire is mentioned after Death's, the expression of simultaneity applies to what is actually sequential.
And the nature of pure generality (<s>śuddhasāmānya</s>) in this [figure] is illustrated as follows:
[In Prakrit:] 'Along with the Malaya breeze perfumed with fragrance, of the beloved ones,
the sighs, thick with the delicate scent of tender [mango blossoms], increase.'
Here, the birth of his fortunes occurring after his own birth — this simultaneity is [attributed to] what is actually sequential.
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'Along with the Malaya breeze perfumed with fragrance, of the beloved ones,
the sighs, dense with the delicate scent of tender [mango blossoms], increase.'
The image-reflection relation (<s>bimbapratibimbabhāva</s>) is illustrated as follows:
[In Prakrit:] 'The clusters of the sun's rays, sparkling with the dust of the golden mountain's slopes,
blossom along with the lotus-pools, bold with the abundance of fragrance.'
Here, between fragrance (<s>saurabha</s>) and scent (<s>parimala</s>), there is the nature of pure generality.
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'The clusters of the sun's rays, sparkling with the dust of the golden mountain's slopes,
blossom along with the lotus-pools, bold with the abundance of fragrance.'
Here, the sparkling with the dust of the golden mountain's slopes is presented as image and reflection (<s>bimbapratibimba</s>) of the boldness born of the abundance of fragrance.
START Sūtra 31:
He now defines <s>vinokti</s> (expression through absence), which is the counterpart of <s>sahokti</s>:
The absence of the existence or non-existence of something without something else is <s>vinokti</s> (expression through absence). || 31 ||

children.text:
sattvasya śobhanatvasyābhāvo 'śobhanatvam /
evamasattvasyāśobhanatvasyābhāvaḥ śobhanatvam /
tedve sattvāsattve yatra kasyacidasaṃnidhānānnibadhyete sā dvidhā vinoktiḥ /
atra ca śobhanatvāśobhanatvasattāsattāyāmeva vaktavyāyāmasattāmukhenābhidhānamanyanivṛttiprayuktā tannivṛttiriti khyāpanārtham /
evaṃ cānyānivṛttau vidhireva prakāśito bhavati /
ādyā yathā -
'vinayena vinā kā śrīḥ kā niśā śaśinā vinā /
rahitā satkavitvena kīdṛśī vāgvidagdhatā' //
children.translated_text: The absence of existence means the absence of auspiciousness, i.e., inauspiciousness. Likewise, the absence of non-existence, i.e., of inauspiciousness, means auspiciousness. These two — existence and non-existence — wherever they are predicated due to the absence of something, that twofold [figure] is <s>vinokti</s>. And here, when what is to be expressed is the existence or non-existence of auspiciousness or inauspiciousness, the expression through the mode of non-existence is for the purpose of indicating that the cessation of one entails the cessation of the other. Thus, when the other does not cease, only the positive assertion is manifested. The first type is illustrated as follows: 'What is glory without modesty? What is night without the moon? What kind of eloquence is there devoid of good poetic skill?'

children.translated_text: Others, considering this [figure] to be factual (<s>vāstavatva</s>), [cite]:

children.text: 'tasyāḥ śaityaṃ vinā jyotsnā puṣparddhiḥ saurabhaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: 'Moonlight without its coolness, the abundance of flowers without their fragrance,
and fire without its heat — [each] appears to you [as something else] without you.'

'Counterpart' means 'being on the opposite side.' Hence this definition comes immediately after that [of <s>sahokti</s>]. He states precisely this with '<s>vinā kiñcit</s>' etc. He explains this with 'of existence' etc. 'Of something' means of whatever kind is intended in the given context. Now, if both existence and non-existence can be expressed through the positive mode, why has the expression been made through the negative mode, which creates an imbalance in cognition? — anticipating this dual doubt, he says 'And here' etc. The word 'that' refers back to existence and non-existence. To the question 'What is gained even by the implication that the cessation of one entails the cessation of the other?' he says 'Thus' etc. The meaning is: when the other thing does not cease, only existence or only non-existence obtains. 'The first' means the statement predicated on non-existence. 'What glory?' means 'no glory whatsoever' — the absence of glory is its non-existence. Even when modesty is absent, if the non-existence of glory is stated, that statement culminates in the non-existence of glory, thus the non-existence of glory occasioned by the cessation of modesty is stated. Likewise, when modesty does not cease, only the positive assertion — namely, the existence of glory — is manifested; therefore one must engage in the burden of [cultivating] modesty. The same should be understood in other cases.

children.text:
ityatra vinoktyalaṅkāratvamāhuḥ /
atra hi jyotstrādīnāṃ śaityādinā nityamavibhāve 'pi vinābhāva upanibaddhaḥ /
yadāhālaṅkārabhāṣyakāraḥ-"nityasaṃbaddhānāmasaṃbandhavacana vinoktiḥ" iti vinoktirūpasaṃkhyāsyate' iti /
granthakṛtā punariyaṃ cirantanalakṣitattvāllakṣitā /
children.translated_text: Here, they declare this to be the figure <s>vinokti</s>. For here, even though moonlight etc. are never actually separated from coolness etc., the state of being 'without' is predicated. As the author of the <s>Alaṅkārabhāṣya</s> says: '<s>Vinokti</s> is the statement of non-connection of things that are permanently connected' — thus <s>vinokti</s> of this form is enumerated. But the author [<s>Ruyyaka</s>] has defined it [differently], since the earlier definition had been long-established.
RuAss_31/1:

children.text: atra vināśabdamantareṇāpi vinārthavivakṣā yathākathañcinnimittībhavati yathā sahoktau sahārthavivakṣā /

children.translated_text: Thus:

children.text: 'nirarthakaṃ janma gataṃ nalinyā yathā na dṛṣṭaṃ tuhināṃśubimbam /
children.translated_text: 'The birth of the water-lily has been purposeless, for the disc of the moon was not seen;

children.text: utpattirindorapi niṣphalaiva na yena dṛṣṭā nalinī prabuddhā' //
children.translated_text: and the rising of the moon too has been fruitless, for by it the awakened water-lily was not seen.'

Here, even without the word '<s>vinā</s>' (without), the intention of the meaning of absence can somehow become the occasion [for the figure], just as in <s>sahokti</s> the intention of the meaning of 'together' [can arise without the word <s>saha</s>].

children.text:
ityādau vinoktireva /
tuhināṃśudarśanaṃ nalinījanmano 'śobhanatvapratīteḥ /
iyaṃ ca parasparavinoktibhaṅgyā camatkārātiśayakṛt /
yathodāhṛte viṣaye /
children.translated_text: In this and similar cases, it is indeed <s>vinokti</s>. [This is so] because the non-seeing of the moon produces the cognition of the inauspiciousness of the water-lily's birth. And this [example], through the mode of mutual <s>vinokti</s> (reciprocal expression through absence), creates an excess of wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>). As in the cited example.

children.translated_text: The intention of the meaning of accompaniment without the word <s>saha</s> is illustrated as follows:
'In the blooming <s>karṇikāra</s> tree, which reveals the fault of the fragrance's excess, which touches [one] with its qualities of color like a bard's vow,

children.text: vikasvare kasya na karṇikāre ghrāṇena dṛṣṭervavṛdhe vivādaḥ' //

'Somehow' — although, just as even without the word <s>saha</s> the instrumental case exists for the meaning of accompaniment, so too even without the word <s>vinā</s> the ablative and other cases exist for the meaning of 'without,' nevertheless by the force of reflecting on the sentence-meaning, [the meaning] culminates in that sense — this is his intent.

children.text:

evaṃ ceti /
yasmād vināśabdaṃ vināpi tadarthavivakṣā bhavatītyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Or for example:

children.text: 'haṃsaṇa sarehiṃ viṇā sarāṇa sohāviṇā ṇa haṃsehiṃ /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'Without lakes, there is no beauty of swans; without swans, no [beauty] of lakes;

children.text: aṇṇoṇṇaṃ cia ee appāṇaṃ ṇavaraṃ garuenti' //

Here, 'with the nose' implies 'together with,' and the cognition rests precisely on that [meaning of accompaniment] without the actual use of [the word <s>saha</s>]. 'Thus' — since even without the word <s>vinā</s>, the intention of that meaning arises — this is the meaning. 'As in the cited [example]' refers to 'purposeless' and so forth.

children.text: ('haṃsānāṃ sarobhirvanā sarasāṃ śobhā vinā ca haṃsaiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] 'Without lakes, there is no beauty of swans; without swans, no beauty of lakes;

RuAss_31/2:
The second type is illustrated as follows:
'Without the doe-eyed woman, [yet] brilliant with the radiance of wit in varied conduct,
this prince, with thoughts beautiful as the nectar-rayed [moon], is a friend to him.'
Here, the absence of disagreeableness is expressed through the device of introducing an agreeable object. This <s>vinokti</s> (expression through exclusion) is of two kinds.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 31/2:]
'The second' — means the expression based on agreeableness.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 32:
Now, two figures are stated with reference to the charm of qualifications. Among these, first, relying on similarity of qualifications, he states <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression):
When, through similarity of qualifications, the non-contextual [subject] is implied, it is <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression). [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32]

vācyatvaṃ ca śleṣanirdeśabhaṅgyā pṛthagupādānena vetyapi dvaividhyam /
etad dvibhedamapi śleṣālaṅkārasya viṣayaḥ /
gumyatvaṃ tu prastutaniṣṭhamaprastutapraśaṃsāviṣayaḥ aprastutaniṇṭhaṃ tu samāsoktiviṣayaḥ /
tatra ca nimittaṃ viśeṣaṇasāmyam /
viśeṣyasyāpi sāmye śleṣaprātpeḥ /
viśeṣaṇasāmyāddhi pratīyamānaprastutaṃ prastutāvacchedakatvena pratīyate /
avacchedakatvaṃ ca vyavahārasamāropaḥ /
rūpasamārope tvavacchāditatvena prakṛtasya tadrūpitvād rūpakameva /
children.translated_text: Here, for contextual and non-contextual [subjects], there is a twofold distinction: sometimes they are expressed, sometimes implied. Expressibility too is twofold: through the device of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) indication, or through separate presentation. This twofold [expressibility] is the domain of the figure <s>śleṣa</s>. But implication, when it pertains to the contextual subject, is the domain of <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the non-relevant); when it pertains to the non-contextual subject, it is the domain of <s>samāsokti</s>. And the cause there is similarity of qualifications. For when there is similarity of the qualified [subject] as well, <s>śleṣa</s> would result. Through similarity of qualifications, the contextual [subject] that is implied is cognized as a delimiter of the contextual. And delimitation is superimposition of convention. But in superimposition of form, since the contextual is covered and takes on that very form, it would be <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) itself.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32:]

children.text:
tatretyalāṃradvayamadhyāt /
ādāviti pradhānatayā /
asyā hi viśeṣaṇamātrāvaṣṭabhbhātparikarādviśeṣaṇasāmyāvaṣṭambhatvena viśiṣṭatvam /
viśeṣaṇetyādi /
attyāścālaṅkārāntarebhyo vibhāgaṃ darśayitumupakramate-ihetyādinā /
vācyatvaṃ cātra dvayoḥ prastutayoraprastutayoḥ prastutāprastutayośca bhavati /
gamyatvaṃ punaḥ kvacitprastutasya kvaciccāprastutasya /
prastutāprastutayostu na bhavati /
tādrūpyeṇa vastusadbhāvābhāvāt /
śleṣanirdiśabhaṅgyeti /
prastutayoraprastutayośca /
pṛthagupādāneneti /
prastutayoraprastutayoḥ prastutāprastutayoścaitaditi vācyam /
atra cāprastutasya kiṃhetukaṃ gamyatvamityaṅkyāha-tatra cetyādi /

children.translated_text: 'Tatra' (there) — when the non-contextual is implied.

children.text: viśeṣaṇānāṃ cātra bahutvameva vivakṣitamiti na vācyam /
children.translated_text: And it should not be said that only the multiplicity of qualifications is intended here,
"The night is troubled by wind; the moonlight has trembling charm; the lotus-pond closes its eyes with tears upon the moonstone ground;

children.text: upacitatamonohā bhūmirvyanakti vivarṇatāṃ taditi gahane darśaṃ darśaṃ kathaṃ sakhi jīvyate' //
children.translated_text: The earth, with its accumulated darkness dispelled, reveals its pallor — thus, O friend, glimpsing [him] again and again in that dense [darkness], how does one survive?"

'Tatra' (among these) — from among the two figures. 'First' — as the principal one. For this [<s>samāsokti</s>] is distinguished from <s>parikara</s> (attendant expression) by depending on similarity of qualifications, while [<s>parikara</s>] depends on qualifications alone. 'Viśeṣaṇa' etc. And he begins to show its distinction from other figures with 'iha' (here) etc. And here, expressibility applies to both contextual [subjects], both non-contextual, and one contextual with one non-contextual. But implication applies sometimes to the contextual, sometimes to the non-contextual. It does not apply to both contextual and non-contextual together, because of the absence of actual existence in such identical form. 'Through the device of <s>śleṣa</s> indication' — applies to both contextual and both non-contextual subjects. 'Through separate presentation' — this should be stated for both contextual, both non-contextual, and one contextual with one non-contextual. Here, anticipating the question 'what is the cause of the non-contextual being implied?', he says 'tatra ca' etc.

children.text:
ityatra viśeṣaṇabahutvābhāve 'pi samāsokteḥ sadbhāvāt /
ataśca viśeṣaṇānāṃ sāmyādīti na sūtraṇīyama /
abahutve tasyāvyāpteḥ /
viśeṣaṇasāmyamapi kasmādatra hetutvaṃ bhajata ityāśaṅkyāha-viśeṣeṇetyādi /
aprastutamiti na punaraprastutadharmā eva /
nahyanyadharmisaṃbandhino dharmāḥsvadharmiṇamantareṇānyatrāvatiṣṭante /
nahyanāyake nāyakadharmāṇāmanvayo yujyate /
anyadharmāṇāmanvayatrānvayāsaṃbhavāt /
ata evānyaropyamāṇo 'nyavahāro 'nyatra na saṃbhavatīti tadavinābhāvātsvavyavahāriṇamākṣipatītyākṣipyamāṇenāprastutena dharmiṇaiva prastuto dharmyavacchridyatena punarācchrādyate /
tathātve hyaprastutena prastutasya rūparūpitatvādrūpasamāropaḥ syānna vyavahārasamāropaḥ /
ata evāha-prastutasya rūparūpitatvādrūpasamāropaḥ syānna vyavahārasamāropaḥ /
ata evāha-prastutāvacchedakatveneti /
ata evāprastutasya gamyatve iti sūtritam /
evaṃ samāsoktau vyavahārasamāropādaprastutena prastutasya vaiśiṣṭamlakṣaṇamavacchredakatvaṃ vidhayate /
rūpake tu rūpasamāropādrūpitatvākhyamācchrādakatvamityanirbhedaḥ /
tena 'viśeṣaṇānāṃ sāmyādaprastutadharmāvacchreda' ityapāsyāsmallakṣaṇānuguṇyenaiva viśeṣaṇasāmyādaprastutāvacchedaḥ samāsoktirityeva sūtraṇīyam /
atiśayoktyāśaṅkā punaratra niṣpramāṇikaiva /
viṣayasyopādānādviṣayiṇaścānupādānāt /
children.translated_text: For here, even in the absence of multiplicity of qualifications, <s>samāsokti</s> exists. Therefore, 'through similarity of qualifications' should not be formulated [as requiring multiplicity] in the <s>sūtra</s>, since in the absence of multiplicity it would be too narrow. Anticipating the question 'why does similarity of qualifications serve as the cause here?', he says 'viśeṣaṇa' etc. 'The non-contextual' — means not merely the properties of the non-contextual subject. For properties belonging to one property-bearer do not exist elsewhere without their own property-bearer. For it is not appropriate that the properties of a hero apply to a non-hero. Because properties of another cannot be connected where there is no connection. Hence, a convention superimposed on one cannot exist in another — therefore, through its inseparable connection, it draws in its own bearer of convention; and by the non-contextual [subject] thus drawn in as property-bearer, the contextual subject is delimited and then re-covered. For if it were otherwise, since the contextual would take on the form of the non-contextual, there would be superimposition of form, not superimposition of convention. Hence he says 'as a delimiter of the contextual.' Hence the <s>sūtra</s> states 'when the non-contextual is implied.' Thus, in <s>samāsokti</s>, through superimposition of convention, the non-contextual produces a distinction in the contextual called 'delimitation.' But in <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), through superimposition of form, what is produced is 'concealment' — called identity of form — thus there is no confusion. Therefore, setting aside 'through similarity of qualifications, delimitation by properties of the non-contextual,' the <s>sūtra</s> should be formulated in accordance with our definition as: 'when the non-contextual is implied through similarity of qualifications, it is <s>samāsokti</s>.' The suspicion of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) here is entirely without basis, since the domain [of comparison] is included but the thing compared to is not.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/1:]

children.text: tacca viśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ śliṣṭatayā sādhāraṇyenaupamyagarbhatvena ca bhavat tridhā bhavati tatra śliṣṭatayā yathā - 'upoḍharāgeṇa vilolatārakaṃ tathā gṛhītaṃ śaśinā niśāmukham ṣa yathā samastaṃ timirāṃśukaṃ tayā puro 'pi rāgādgalitaṃ na lakṣitam' //
children.translated_text: And that similarity of qualifications, occurring as conjoined (<s>śliṣṭa</s>), as common (<s>sādhāraṇya</s>), or as containing a simile (<s>aupamyagarbha</s>), is threefold. Among these, with conjunction, for example: 'With the face of the night seized by the moon whose star-eyes are restless with rising passion, her dark veil of darkness slipped away unnoticed due to passion, even in front [of others].'
Here, through the power of the conjoined qualifications of night and moon, the convention of being a hero [and heroine] is cognized.
Because the cognition is of night and moon as possessing the property called hero-status, without abandoning their own forms.

children.text: sādhāraṇyena yathā - 'tanvī manoramā bālā lolākṣī puṣpahāsinī /
children.translated_text: With commonality, for example: 'Slender, charming, young, with restless eyes, smiling like flowers,
She blossoms, O fortunate one, merely from the sight of you.'

children.text:
atra tanvītyādiviśeṣaṇasāmyāllolākṣyā latāvyavahārapratītiḥ /
tatra ca lataikagāmivikāsākhyadharmasasāropaḥ kāraṇam /
anyathā viśeṣaṇasāmyamātreṇa niyatalatāvyavahārasyāpratīteḥ /
vikāsaśca prakṛte upacarito jñeyaḥ /
evaṃ ca kāryasamārope 'pi jñeyā /
iyaṃ ca samāsoktiḥ pūrvāpekṣayāspaṣṭā /
children.translated_text: Here, through the similarity of qualifications like 'slender' etc., the convention of being a creeper is cognized for the restless-eyed [woman]. And there, the superimposition of the property called 'blossoming,' which pertains exclusively to creepers, is the cause. Otherwise, mere similarity of qualifications would not produce the invariable cognition of the creeper-convention. And 'blossoming' in the present context should be understood as figurative. Thus, this should be understood even in cases of superimposition of effect. And this <s>samāsokti</s> is less explicit compared to the previous one.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/1:]

children.text:
taditi aprastutasya gamyatve nimittam /
tatreti nirdhāraṇe /
nāyaketi sarūpayorekaśeṣaḥ /
aparityaktasvarūpayoriti /
rūparūpitatve hi parityaktaṃ svasvarūpaṃ syāt /
tatreti /
latāvyavahārapratītau /
nanu yadi lataikagamyeva vikāsākhyo dharmastatkathaṃ prakṛte saṃgacchata ityāśaṅkyāha-vikāsa ityādi /
etadevānyatrāpi yojayati-evamityādinā /
tadevaṃ sādhāraṇyena samāsokterviśeṣaṇasāmye satyapyaprakṛtasaṃbandhi dharmakāryaṃsamāropamantareṇa tadvayavahārapratītirna bhavatīti siddham /
children.translated_text: 'That' refers to the cause of the non-contextual being implied. 'Tatra' is for specification. '<s>Nāyaka</s>' (hero) — is an <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (elliptical compound) for the two similar [terms, hero and heroine]. 'Without abandoning their own forms' — for if they took on the form [of the hero], their own form would be abandoned. 'Tatra' — in the cognition of the creeper-convention. Now, if the property called 'blossoming' pertains exclusively to creepers, how does it apply to the present context? — anticipating this, he says 'vikāsa' etc. He applies this to other cases as well with 'evam' etc. Thus, it is established that in <s>samāsokti</s> with commonality, even when similarity of qualifications exists, without the superimposition of a property or effect pertaining to the non-contextual, the cognition of that convention does not occur.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/2:]
With simile-containment, for example:
"Adorned with flowers of tooth-radiance, beautiful with hand-shoots,
With a flock of hair-creepers, well-dressed, with deer-like eyes."

children.text:
atra dantaprabhā puṣpāṇīveti suveṣatvavaśādupamāgarbhatvena kṛte samāse paścāddantaprabhāsadṛśaiḥ puṣpaiściteti samāsāntarāśrayaṇena samānaviśeṣaṇamāhātmyāllatāvyavahārapratītiḥ /
atraiva 'parītā hariṇekṣaṇā' iti pāṭhe upamārūpasādhakabāghakābhāvāt saṃkarasamāśrayeṇa kṛte yojane paścāt pūrvavat samāsāntaramahimnā latāpratītijñaṃyā /
rūpakagarbhatvena tu samāsāntarāśrayaṇāt samānaviṣeṣaṇatvaṃ bhavadapi na samāsokteḥ prayojakam /
ekadeśavivartirūpakamukhenaivārthāntarapratītestasyā vaiyarthyāt /
na ca pūrvadarśitopamāsaṃkaraviṣaye eṣa nyāyaḥ /
upamāsaṃkarayorekadeśavivartinorabhāvāt /
taccaikadeśavivartirūpakamaśleṣeṇa śleṣeṇa ca bhavatīti dvividham /

children.translated_text: Without <s>śleṣa</s>, for example:
"Having gazed with lightning-eyes, the cloud at the face of the woman going to her lover's tryst at night,

children.text: dhārānipātaiḥ saha kiṃ nu vāntaścandro 'yamitpārtataraṃ rarāsa' //
children.translated_text: Along with a downpour of rain — has this moon been vomited? — it cried out most piteously."

Here, 'tooth-radiance' being like flowers — through the force of the 'well-dressed' meaning, when a compound is formed containing a simile, and then through resorting to another compound [interpretation] as 'adorned with flowers resembling tooth-radiance,' the cognition of the creeper-convention arises through the power of the common qualifications. In this very [verse], with the reading '<s>parītā hariṇekṣaṇā</s>' (surrounded, deer-eyed), since there is no factor that establishes or prevents either simile or metaphor, when the construction is made by resorting to a mixed [interpretation], thereafter, as before, the creeper-cognition should be understood through the power of the alternative compound. But when there is metaphor-containment, even though commonality of qualifications arises through resorting to an alternative compound, it does not motivate <s>samāsokti</s>. Because the cognition of another meaning would occur through partial-transformation metaphor alone, making [<s>samāsokti</s>] redundant. And this principle does not apply to the domain of simile-mixture shown earlier, because partial-transformation does not exist in simile and mixture. And that partial-transformation metaphor, occurring with and without <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning), is of two kinds.

children.text: atra nirīkṣaṇānuguṇyādvidyunnayanairiti rūpake payodasya draṣṭṛpuruṣanirūpaṇamārtataraṃ rarāsetyatra pratīyamānotprekṣāyā nimittatvaṃ bhajate /

children.translated_text: With <s>śleṣa</s>, for example:
"Raising the elaboration of writing at the site of the enumeration of <s>Madana</s> (Love), with spotted bee-ink marks placed on large leaves of the <s>Vicakila</s> tree,

children.text: kuṭilalipibhiḥ kaṃ kāyasthaṃ na nāma visūtrayan vyadhita virahiprāṇeṣvāyavyayāvadhikaṃ madhuḥ' [śrī. ca. 670] //
children.translated_text: With crooked letters, confusing every <s>kāyastha</s> (scribe / embodied being) — did not <s>Madhu</s> (Spring / honey) inflict upon the lives of the love-sick an excess of income and expenditure?" [<s>Śrīkaṇṭhacarita</s> 670]

Here, through the appropriateness of gazing, in the metaphor 'with lightning-eyes,' the identification of the cloud as the male observer becomes the cause of the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) that is implied in 'cried out most piteously.'

children.text:
atra hi pattralipikāyasthaśabdeṣu śleṣagarbhe rūpakaṃ dvirephamaṣīlavairityetadrūpakanimittam /
asya ca pracuraḥ prayogaviṣaya iti na samāsoktibuddhiḥ kāryā /
children.translated_text: Here, in the words '<s>pattralipikā</s>' (leaf-inscription), '<s>kāyastha</s>' (scribe), there is metaphor containing <s>śleṣa</s>; 'with spotted bee-ink marks' — this is the basis of the metaphor. And since this has abundant scope for application, one should not apply the notion of <s>samāsokti</s>.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/2:]

children.text:
suveṣatvaṃ prakṛtārthaṃ evānuguṇamityupamāyāḥ sādhakam ataśca tatsamāsāśrayaḥ /
samāsāntarāśrayaṇeneti /
yadyapyatropamāsamāsa eva sthitastathāpyupamānopameyayorvyatyayādeva samāsāntaratvamuktam /
pūrvāpekṣavāsyānyayātvāt /
atraiveti dantaprabhetyādau /
upamārūpakasādhakabādhakābhāvāditi /
parrītatvasya hi prakṛtāprakṛtayostathā nānuguṇyamiti sādhakatvābhāvaḥ /
tathā ca na viguṇatvamiti bādhakatvābhāvaḥ /
ataścaikapakṣāśrayābhāvādupamārūpakayoḥ saṃdehasaṃkaraḥ /
tasya samāśraya ubhayasamāsagrahaṇam /
taccaikasminneva vākye na saṃbhavatīti kāmakṣāreṇa tayorgrahaṇam /
saṃkarasamāśrayeṇāpyupamāsamāsayoccane kṛte yadvadayamevālaṅkārastadvadrūpakasamāsayojajane 'pi kimathameva kimutālaṅkārāntaramityāśaṅkyāha-rūpaketyādi /
evacca sākṣādapi rūpakagarbhe samāse yojyam, samānanyāyatvāt /
yadyevaṃ tarjhupamāsamāśraye 'pyekadeśavivartyupamāmukhenaivārthāntarapratīteḥ kiṃ naitadbhavatītyāśaṅkyāha-na cetyādi /
eṣa iti rūpakoktaḥ /
abhāvāditi udbhaṭamatena /
yadāhuḥ -
'na ca rudraṭasyevodbhaṭasyaikadeśavivartirūpakavadupamāsaṃkarāvekadeśinau staḥ' ataścaitattanmatābhiprāyeṇoktam /
granthakṛnmate hi vakṣyamāṇanītyā tayoḥ saṃbhavaḥ /
nanu yadi tayorgranthakṛnmate saṃbhavastadaupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇotthāpitaḥ samāsoktiprakārastarhi na saṃbhavati /
tasyaikadeśavivartirūpakavadekadeśavivartibhyāmupamāsaṃkarābhyāmevārthāntarapratītisiddhervaiyarthyāt /
naitat /
yato 'styeva tāvadaupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇahetukatvaṃ samāsokteḥ /
kintvetadanyabhedasahacaritamevāsyā nimittatāṃ bhajate na punaḥ kevalam /
tathātve hi viśeṣaṇānāmaupamyagarbhatve ekadeśavivartinyā upamāyāḥ prātpiḥ /

children.translated_text: Among these, accompanied by conjunction, for example:
"Stained yellow on their dark garments, dense, captivating, with their charming
Breasts — O friend, at evening these directions with bright passion and trembling stars, who do they not steal away?"

'Well-dressed-ness' is favorable to the contextual meaning alone — this establishes the simile. Hence the compound is based on that. 'Through resorting to another compound' — although here the simile-compound itself stands, nevertheless, because of the transposition of the compared and the object of comparison, the alternative compound status is stated. Because compared to the previous [example], this is of a different type. 'In this very [verse]' — in 'dantaprabha' etc. 'Because of the absence of factors establishing or preventing simile or metaphor' — for 'surrounded-ness' is not favorable to either the contextual or the non-contextual — hence the absence of an establishing factor. And thus, there is no unfavorable quality — hence the absence of a preventing factor. Therefore, in the absence of commitment to either side, there is a doubtful mixture of simile and metaphor. The acceptance of that [mixture] is the taking up of both compounds. And that is not possible in a single sentence, so both are taken up partially. Anticipating the objection 'if in the case of simile-mixture too the construction is made by resorting to an alternative compound, then just as this very figure [<s>samāsokti</s>] results, so too in the case of metaphor-compound construction, why should this not also be the case — or rather, why should it not be yet another figure?', he says 'rūpaka' etc. And thus, this should be applied also when there is direct metaphor-containment in the compound, since the principle is the same. If so, then even in the simile-compound case, since the cognition of another meaning occurs through partial-transformation simile alone, why does this [objection] not apply? — anticipating this, he says 'na ca' etc. 'Eṣa' (this) — the one stated regarding metaphor. 'Absence' — according to <s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s view. As they say: 'Neither partial-transformation <s>rūpaka</s> nor partial simile-mixture exist, as <s>Udbhaṭa</s> [holds], unlike <s>Rudraṭa</s>.' Therefore, this is stated with the intent of that [<s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s] doctrine. But according to the author's view, by the principle to be stated later, their existence is possible. Now, if according to the author's view their existence is possible, then the type of <s>samāsokti</s> arising from simile-containing qualifications would not be possible — since the cognition of another meaning would be accomplished by partial-transformation simile and mixture alone, making it redundant. This is not so, because the simile-containing quality of qualifications is indeed a cause of <s>samāsokti</s>. But this [causality] operates only when accompanied by another variety, not alone. For if it were alone, when qualifications contain simile, partial-transformation simile would result.
Accompanied by commonality, for example:
"Slender, charming, young, with restless eyes, with cluster-like breasts,
She blossoms, O fortunate one, merely from the sight of you."
Here, with the reading '<s>sphuṭasaṃdhyātapakuṅkumaiḥ</s>' (with the <s>kuṅkuma</s> of the bright twilight glow), 'with twilight-glow-<s>kuṅkuma</s>' is a qualification containing simile.
Accompanied by pure superimposition of effect, for example:
"He climbed to the tops of trees, rolled in heaps of flower-pollen,

children.text: latāprasūnāṃśukamācakarṣaṃ krīḍanvane kiṃ na cakāra caitraḥ' //
children.translated_text: Pulled at the flower-garments of creepers — playing in the forest, what did <s>Caitra</s> (Spring) not do?"
Here, '<s>stabakastanī</s>' (she whose breasts are like clusters) is a qualification containing simile.
But when these stand alone, it is simply partial-transformation simile, as in:
"There shone forth, with the trembling lower lip-petal revealing the stamen-like teeth,
The charming face of the woman, with the playful movement of the eyebrows as a bracelet.
Here, '<s>prasūnāṃśuka</s>' (flower-garment) is a qualification containing simile.

children.text:
atra lalitatvamupamāsādhakam /
samāsāntarāśrayāt samānaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ bhavadapi nātra samāsokteḥ prayojakam /
ekadeśavivartyupamāmukhenaivārthāntarapratītestasyā vaicathyāt /
evaṃ dantaprabhetyādāvapi jñeyam /
dantaprabhāḥ puṣpāṇīvetyeva samāse kṛte upamānabhūtāyā latāyāḥ pratītisiddheḥ samāsāntarāśrayeṇāgatāyāstatpratītervyarthatvāt /
aprakṛtāgūraṇe hi kaveḥ saṃrambhaḥ taccānayaiva siddhamiti kiṃ samāsoktyā /
cirantanānurodhāt punaratra granthakṛtāsamāsoktiruktā /
yattu 'yatra samāsoktāyāmupamāyāṃ samāsāntareṇa viśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ yojayituṃ śakyaṃ tatraupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇaprabhāvitā samāsoktiruktā' iti vakṣyati tadapi cirantanānurodhaparameva /
anyathā hi samānanyāyatvādekadeśavivartini rūpake 'pi yatra samānaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ yojayituṃ śakyaṃ tatrāpi samāsoktiriti kiṃ noktam /

children.translated_text: That it has not been stated is indeed proper.

Because of the supremacy of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), the introduction of the non-primary subject through <s>samāsokti</s> would be purposeless, since the cognition [of the intended meaning] is already accomplished through that [metaphor] itself.
"With a moon-like face that delights, with glittering star-like pearls,
With dense darkness as her tresses, the expanse of the sky shines forth."

Here, the charmingness is the basis of <s>upamā</s> (simile). Even though <s>samānaviśeṣaṇatva</s> (common qualification) arises from dependence on another compound, it is not the cause of <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) here, because the meaning is understood only through <s>ekadeśavivartyupamā</s> (partially-transforming simile), and that [samāsokti] would be redundant. The same should be understood in cases like 'dantaprabha' etc. Since the <s>latā</s> (creeper), which is the object of comparison, is already understood when the compound 'the radiance of teeth is like flowers' is formed, the cognition of that [creeper] obtained through dependence on another compound would be purposeless. For the poet's effort lies in the introduction of the non-primary subject, and that is already accomplished through this [simile] alone -- so what need is there for <s>samāsokti</s>? However, following earlier authorities, the author of the treatise has stated <s>samāsokti</s> here. As for what he will state later -- 'where in the <s>samāsokti</s>-based simile, similarity of qualification can be established through another compound, there the <s>samāsokti</s> is effected by <s>aupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇa</s> (qualification containing comparison)' -- that too is merely in deference to earlier authorities. For otherwise, since the principle is the same, why has it not been stated that <s>samāsokti</s> applies also in <s>ekadeśavivarti rūpaka</s> (partially-transforming metaphor) where common qualification can be established?

children.text:
ityādau punarupamāyāḥ sādhakābhāvādekadeśavivarti rūpakameveti na samāsoktibhramaḥ kāryaḥ /
na caivamādāvupamārūpakayoḥ saṃdehasaṃkaro nyāyyaḥ /
tasyālaṅkārasārakārādibhinirākṛtatvāt /
samāsoktilakṣaṇāvalasare kiṃ rūpakanirūpaṇenetyāśaṅkyāha-asyā ityādi /
children.translated_text: In such cases, since there is no basis for simile, it is only <s>ekadeśavivarti rūpaka</s> (partially-transforming metaphor), and one should not mistakenly identify it as <s>samāsokti</s>. And in such cases, a confusion between <s>upamā</s> and <s>rūpaka</s> is not appropriate, as that has been thoroughly refuted by the author of the <s>Alaṅkārasāra</s> and others. Anticipating the objection 'why discuss <s>rūpaka</s> when defining <s>samāsokti</s>?', he says 'asyā' etc.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/2a:]
He enumerates the varieties of this [<s>samāsokti</s>] as stated above, beginning with 'tadevaṃ' etc.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/3:]

children.text:
tadevaṃ śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇasamutthāpitaikā /
sādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇasamutthāpitā tu dharmakāryasamāropābhyāṃ dvibhedā /
aupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇasamutthāpitopamāsaṃkarasamāsābhyāṃ dvibhedā /
rūpakasamāśrayeṇa tu bhedadvayamasyā na viṣayaḥ /
tadevaṃ pañcaprakārā samāsoktiḥ /
iyaṃ ca śuddhakāryasamāropeṇa viśeṣaṇasāmyenobhayamayatvena prathamaṃ tridhā samāsoktiḥ /
viśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ ca pañcaprakāraṃ nirṇītam /
sarvatra cātra vyavahārasamāropa eva jīvitam /
sa ca laukike vastuni laukikavastuvyavahārasamāropaḥ /
śāstrīye vastuni śāstrīyavastuvyavahārasamāropaḥ /
laukike vā śāstrīyavastuvyavahārasamāropaḥ /
śāstrīye vā laukikavastuvyavahāramāropa iti caturdhā bhavati /
tadevaṃ bahuprakārā samāsoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, one [variety] is produced by <s>śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇa</s> (ambiguous qualification). That produced by <s>sādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇa</s> (common qualification) is of two kinds: through <s>dharma</s> (property) and through <s>kāryasamāropa</s> (superimposition of activity). That produced by <s>aupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇa</s> (comparison-containing qualification) is of two kinds: through <s>upamāsaṃkara</s> (mixture of simile) and through <s>samāsa</s> (compound). However, the two varieties through <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) are not within the scope of this [<s>samāsokti</s>]. Thus, <s>samāsokti</s> is of five kinds. And this, firstly, is threefold as <s>samāsokti</s>: through pure <s>kāryasamāropa</s>, through <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> (similarity of qualification), and through a combination of both. And the <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> has been determined to be of five kinds. And in all cases here, the superimposition of conventional usage is the life [of <s>samāsokti</s>]. And that is fourfold: superimposition of worldly usage upon a worldly thing, superimposition of technical usage upon a technical thing, superimposition of technical usage upon a worldly thing, or superimposition of worldly usage upon a technical thing. Thus, <s>samāsokti</s> is of many varieties.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/3:]

children.text:
bhedadvayamiti sākṣātsaṃdihyamānatvena vā /
na viṣaya iti /
yathoktopapatte rūpaka eva viśrānteḥ /
prathamamiti /
etadbhedatrayamasyā mūlabhūtamityarthaḥ /
uktaṃ punaḥ prakārapañcakamasyā avāntarabhedarūpam /
viśeṣaṇasāmyasyaitadbhedatvāt /
yadyapi śuddhakāryasamārope 'pi viśeṣaṇasāmyabhevāsti tathāpyatra śuddha eva kāryasamāropa udbhiktatayā pratīyata iti tasya pṛthagmedatvamuktam /
sarvatreti bhedasatpake /
bahuprakāreti /
laukikādīnāṃ vyavahārāṇāmānantyāt /
children.translated_text: 'Two varieties' means either directly or as being doubtful. 'Not within the scope' means because, as explained, the meaning comes to rest in <s>rūpaka</s> itself. 'Firstly' means that this threefold division is the fundamental one. The fivefold classification mentioned is its subsidiary variety, since <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> constitutes these subdivisions. Although <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> exists also in pure <s>kāryasamāropa</s>, nevertheless, since pure <s>kāryasamāropa</s> is perceived as predominant there, its separate classification has been stated. 'In all cases' refers to the five varieties. 'Of many varieties' is because the worldly and other usages are infinite.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/4:]
Among these, through pure <s>kāryasamāropa</s> (superimposition of activity), for example:

children.text: 'vilikhati kucāvuccairgāḍhaṃ karoti kacagrahaṃ likhati lalite vaktre pattrāvalīmasamañjasām /
children.translated_text: "He sketches on the breasts, tightly grasps the hair, inscribes an improper <s>pattrāvalī</s> (leaf-design) on the lovely face,

children.text: kṣitipa khadiraḥ śroṇībimbād vikarṣati cāṃśukaṃ marubhuvi haṭhāt trasyantīnāṃ tavārimṛgīdṛśām' //
children.translated_text: O king, the <s>khadira</s> (acacia) tree forcibly pulls away the garment from the buttocks of your enemies' deer-eyed women fleeing in terror through the desert."

Here, through the superimposition of the pure activity of drawing a <s>pattrāvalī</s> etc., the cognition of the <s>khadira</s> as a forceful lover is illustrated through <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> (similarity of qualification).
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/4:]
'Illustrated' means by the verse beginning 'upoḍharāgeṇa' etc.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/5:]
Through a combination of both, for example:

children.text: 'nirlūnānyalakāni pāṭitamuraḥ kṛtsno 'dharaḥ khaṇḍitaḥ karṇe rugjanitā kṛtaṃ ca nayane nīlābjakānte kṣatam /
children.translated_text: "The curls are torn off, the chest is split, the lower lip is entirely bitten, pain is inflicted on the ear, and a wound is made on the eye beloved of the blue lotus.

children.text: yāntīnāmatisaṃbhramākulapadanyāsaṃ marau nīrasaiḥ kiṃ kiṃ kaṇṭakibhiḥ kṛtaṃ na tarubhistvadvairivāmabhruvām' //
children.translated_text: As they go with steps confused by excessive haste through the desert, what indeed have the thorny, sapless trees not done to your enemies' lovely-browed women?"

children.text:
atra nīrasaiḥ kaṇṭakibhiriti viśeṣaṇasāmyam /
nirlūnānyalakānītyādiṣu kāryasamāropaḥ /
vyavahārasamāropaprakāracatuṣṭaye krameṇodāharaṇam /

children.translated_text: For example:
"He embraced the sky, quickly kissed the faces of the directions, scratched with his fingertips the crescent moon confined by the clouds.

children.text: antarnimagracarapuṣpaśaro 'titāpāt kiṃ kiṃ cakāra taruṇo na yadīkṣaṇāgniḥ' //
children.translated_text: With <s>Puṣpaśara</s> (the flower-arrowed one, i.e., <s>Kāmadeva</s>) submerged within, what did the youthful fire of the eye not do out of excessive heat?"

Here, 'sapless' and 'thorny' constitute <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> (similarity of qualification). In 'the curls are torn off' etc., there is <s>kāryasamāropa</s> (superimposition of activity). The four types of <s>vyavahārasamāropa</s> (superimposition of conventional usage) are illustrated in order.
A worldly thing is of many varieties through distinctions of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) etc., to be imagined by oneself.
"By those who, seeing you as having one form in all <s>vṛttis</s> (verbal operations), engaged in the designation '<s>asaṃkhyata</s>' (innumerable),

children.text: lopaḥ kṛtaḥ kila paratvajuṣo vibhakte- stairlakṣaṇaṃ tava kṛtaṃ dhruvameva manye' //
children.translated_text: The <s>lopa</s> (elision) of the <s>vibhakti</s> (case-ending) which follows <s>paratva</s> (posteriority) was performed; thus your characteristics were surely established, I think."
Here, there is superimposition of a matter well-known in <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar) upon a matter well-known in <s>āgama</s> (scripture).

children.text: 'sīmānaṃ na jagāma yannayanayornānyena yatsaṃgataṃ na spṛṣṭaṃ vacasā kadācidapi yad dṛṣṭopamānaṃ na yat /
children.translated_text: "That which did not reach the boundary of the eyes, that which was not encountered by another, that which was never touched by speech, that for which no object of comparison was seen,

children.text: arthādāpatitaṃ na yanna ca na yattatkiñcideṇīdṛśāṃ lāvaṇyaṃ jayati pramāṇarahitaṃ cetaścamatkārakam' //
children.translated_text: That which did not arise incidentally, that which is not nothing -- such <s>lāvaṇya</s> (beauty) of these women triumphs, beyond measure, astonishing the mind."

children.text:
atra lāvaṇye laukike vastuni mīmāṃsāśāstraprasiddhavastusamāropaḥ /
evaṃ tarkāyurvedajyotiḥśāstraprasiddhavastusamāropo boddhavyaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:
"Displaying distinction in the matter of <s>Smara</s> (Love) when the cause is established through the playful charm of his own faction,
The <s>pāṇḍitya</s> (scholarship) of the cuckoo in refuting the pride of all young men was unbroken."

Here, there is superimposition of matters well-known in <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> (exegetical) scripture upon <s>lāvaṇya</s>, a worldly thing. Similarly, one should understand the superimposition of matters well-known in <s>Tarka</s> (logic), <s>Āyurveda</s> (medicine), and <s>Jyotiḥśāstra</s> (astrology).
Here, there is superimposition of matters well-known in <s>Tarkaśāstra</s> (logic).
The word '<s>pāṇḍitya</s>' is to be interpreted through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) in the present context.
"There appeared slow, un-pungent, sweet, gravelly darkness, displaying swelling,
And eyes afflicted with <s>timira</s> (dimness of vision) took recourse to the defect born of darkness in the absence of the lord of herbs [the moon]."
Here, there is superimposition of matters well-known in <s>Āyurveda</s> (medicine).

children.text: 'gaṇḍānte madadantināṃ prahṛrataḥ kṣmāmaṇḍale vaidhṛte rakṣāmācarataḥ sadā vidadhato lāṭeṣu yātrotsavam /
children.translated_text: "Of the one who strikes at the cheek-region of rutting elephants, who observes protection in the <s>Vaidhṛta</s> (astrological conjunction) of the earth's circle, who always conducts the festival of military expeditions in <s>Lāṭa</s>,

children.text: pūrvāmatyajataḥ sthitiṃ śubhakarīmāsevyamānasya te vardhante vijayaśriyaḥ kimiva na śreyasvināṃ maṅgalam' //
children.translated_text: Who does not abandon the auspicious former position of ministers, and who is resorted to -- your victories increase; what indeed is not auspicious for the fortunate?"
Here, there is superimposition of matters well-known in <s>Jyotiḥśāstra</s> (astrology).

children.text: 'prasarpattātparyairapi sadanumānaikarasikai- rapi jñeyo no yaḥ parimitagatitvaṃ parijahṛt /
children.translated_text: "He who is unknowable even by spreading implications, even by inferences that are solely devoted to reasoning, having abandoned the nature of being of limited scope,

children.text: apūrvavyāpāro guruvara! budhairityavasito na vācyo no lakṣyastava sahṛdayasyo guṇagaṇaḥ' //
children.translated_text: O great teacher! His unprecedented operation has been determined by the wise -- that collection of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of yours, sympathetic to the sensitive, is neither expressible nor targetable."

children.text:
atra bharatādiśāstraprasiddhavastusamāropaḥ /
tathā hyatra guṇagaṇagatatvena śṛṅgārādirasavyavahāraḥ pratīyate /
yato raso na tātparyaśaktijñeyaḥ /
nāpyanumānaviṣayaḥ /
na śabdairabhidhāvyāpāreṇa vācyīkṛtaḥ /
na lakṣaṇāgocaraḥ /
kiṃ tu vigalitavedyānataratvena parihṛtapārimityo vyañjanalakṣaṇāpūrvavyāpāraviṣayīkṛto 'nukāryānukartṛgatatvapari hāreṇa sahṛdayagata iti prasarpattātparyairityādipadai rasa eva pratīyate /
eva pratīyate /
evamanyadapi jñeyam /
children.translated_text: Here, there is superimposition of matters well-known in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) of <s>Bharata</s> and others. For here, through belonging to a collection of <s>guṇas</s>, the conventional usage of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) and other <s>rasas</s> is implied. Because <s>rasa</s> is not cognizable through the power of <s>tātparya</s> (purport), nor is it the object of <s>anumāna</s> (inference), nor is it made expressible by the denotative operation of words, nor is it within the scope of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification). Rather, through the unprecedented operation characterized as <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion), having transcended the state of being a knowable object, having abandoned limitation, having relinquished belonging to the thing imitated or the imitator -- it resides in the <s>sahṛdaya</s> (sensitive reader). Thus, through the words 'by spreading implications' etc., <s>rasa</s> itself is implied. Similarly, other instances should also be understood.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/5:]

children.text:
krameṇeti yathoddeśam /
mīmāṃsetyatrottaramīmāṃsā vivakṣitā /
tatra kahi nikhilapramāṇāgocaraṃ paramātmasvarūpaṃ darśitam /
tadvyavahārasamāropo 'tra kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In order' means as listed. By '<s>Mīmāṃsā</s>' here, the <s>Uttaramīmāṃsā</s> (Vedānta) is intended. There, the nature of <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), which is beyond all means of knowledge, is shown. The superimposition of that conventional usage is made here.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/5a:]
As has been stated:
"Neither denotation nor purport, neither <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) nor inference,
Is capable of subsuming <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), since the object exists as distinct."
'Not by purport' --
Thus.

children.text:
anukāryo rāmādiḥ /
anukartā naṭādiḥ /
tadgacaraśca na rasaḥ pratīyate /
yaduktam-'nānukārye 'pi rāmādau naṭādau nānukartari /
rasaḥ sacetasāṃ kiṃ tu' iti /
anyaditi /
anyaśāstraprasiddhavastusamāropalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The thing imitated is <s>Rāma</s> etc. The imitator is the actor etc. And <s>rasa</s> is not perceived as residing in them. As has been stated: 'Neither in <s>Rāma</s> etc. who are imitated, nor in the actor etc. who imitates, but <s>rasa</s> [resides] in those who have hearts.' 'Other' refers to the superimposition of matters well-known in other <s>śāstras</s>.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/6:]

children.text: 'paśyantī trapayeva yatra tirayatyātmānamābhyantare yatra truṭyati madhyamāpi madhuradhvanyujjihāsārasāt /
children.translated_text: "Where <s>paśyantī</s> (the 'seeing' level of speech), as if out of modesty, conceals herself within; where even <s>madhyamā</s> (the 'middle' level of speech) breaks down from the desire to utter sweet sounds;

children.text: cāṭūccāraṇacāpalaṃ vidadhatāṃ vāk tatra bāhyā kathaṃ devyā te parayā prabho saha rahaḥkrīḍādṛḍhāliṅgane' //
children.translated_text: How then can <s>vaikharī</s> (external speech), displaying the fickleness of uttering flattery, [function] there -- O lord, in the intimate love-play with your supreme <s>Devī</s> (Goddess)?"

children.text:
atrāgamaprasiddhe vastuni laukikavastuvyavahārasamāropa /
laukikavastuvyavahāraśca rasādibhedād bahubheda ityuktaṃ prāk /
tatra śuddhakāryasamārope kāryasya viśeṣaṇatvamaupacārikamāśritya viśeṣaṇasāmyāditi lakṣaṇaṃ pūrvaśāstrānusāreṇa vihitaṃ yathākathañcid yojyam /
children.translated_text: Here, there is superimposition of worldly conventional usage upon a matter well-known in <s>āgama</s> (scripture). And worldly conventional usage is of many varieties through distinctions of <s>rasa</s> etc., as stated earlier. In the case of pure <s>kāryasamāropa</s>, relying on the metaphorical qualification-status of the activity, the definition 'through <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s>' is applied somehow following earlier treatises.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/6:]

children.text: taditthaṃ saprapañcāṃ samāsoktiṃ pratipādya punarapi sahṛdayānāṃ hṛdayaṅgamīkartuṃ granthakṛdetatpratīrti vibhāgena lakṣye yojayati-iha tvityādinā /
children.translated_text: Having thus explained <s>samāsokti</s> with all its elaborations, the author of the treatise, in order to make it penetrate the hearts of the <s>sahṛdayas</s> (connoisseurs), further applies the distinction of this understanding to examples, beginning with 'iha tu' etc.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/7:]
Here, however --
"With a pale cloud, the autumn, bearing <s>Indra</s>'s bow having the appearance of fresh nail-marks,
Propitiating the blemished moon, caused the heat of the sun to increase greatly."

children.text:
ityatrāsti tāvad raviśaśinornāyakatvapratītiḥ /
na cātra viśeṣaṇasāmyamiti sā kutastyā /
prasādayantī sakalaṅkamindumiti viśeṣaṇasāmyāccharadonāyikātvapratītau tadunuguṇyāt tayoḥ samāsoktyā nāyakatvapratītiriti cet ārdranakhakṣatābhamaindraṃ dhanurdadhānetyetadviśeṣaṇaṃ kathaṃ sāmyena nirdriṣṭam /
na caikadeśavivartinyupamoktā yatsāmarthyānnāyakatvapratītiḥ syāt /
tatkathamatra dhyavasthā /
atrocyate-ekadeśavivartinyupamā yadi pratipadaṃ noktā tat sā kena pratiṣiddhā /
sāmānyalakṣaṇadvāreṇāyātāyāstasyā atrāpi saṃbhavāt /
athātra nopamānatvena nāyakaḥ svasvarūpeṇa pratīyate apitu raviśaśinorevanāyakatvapratītiḥ /
tayoratra nāyakatvāt /
tadatrārdranakhakṣatābhamityatra sthitamapi śrutyopamānatvaṃ vastuparyālocanayā aindre dhanuṣi saṃcāraṇīyam, indracāpābhaṃ nakhakṣataṃ dadhāneti pratīteḥ, yathā 'dadhnā juhoti' ityādau dadhni saṃcaryate vidhiḥ /
evamiyamupamānuprāṇitā samāsoktireva /
iha punaḥ ityatra saraḥśriyāṃ nāyikātvapratītirna samāsoktyā, viśeṣaṇasāmyābhāvāt /
tasmānnāyikātropamānatvena pratīyate na tu saraḥśrīdharmatvena nāyikātvapratītirityekadeśavivartinyupamaivābhyupagamyā,gatyantarāsaṃbhavāt /
yaistunoktā teṣāmapyupasaṃkhyeyaiva /
yatra tu 'keśapāśālivṛndena' ityādau samāsoktāyāmupamāyāṃ samāsantariṇa viśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ yojayituṃ śakyaṃ tatraupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇaprabhāvitā samāsoktireveti na virodhaḥ kaścit /
children.translated_text: Here, there is indeed the cognition of the sun and moon as <s>nāyaka</s> (hero). But there is no <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> (similarity of qualification) here, so how does that [cognition] arise? If one says that from the <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> in 'propitiating the blemished moon,' the cognition of autumn as <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) arises, and in conformity with that, the cognition of those two [sun and moon] as <s>nāyakas</s> through <s>samāsokti</s> -- [then the objection is:] how is the qualification 'bearing <s>Indra</s>'s bow having the appearance of fresh nail-marks' established through similarity? And there is no speaker of <s>ekadeśavivartyupamā</s> (partially-transforming simile) by whose power the cognition of <s>nāyaka</s>-status would arise. Then how is the matter to be settled here? To this it is replied: if the <s>ekadeśavivartyupamā</s> is not stated word by word, then by whom is it prohibited? Since that [simile], arrived at through the general definition, is possible here too. Now, here the <s>nāyaka</s> is not perceived in his own form as the object of comparison, but rather the cognition of <s>nāyaka</s>-status belongs to the sun and moon themselves, because they are the <s>nāyakas</s> here. Therefore, although the qualification 'having the appearance of fresh nail-marks' stands [literally] there, through consideration of the actual meaning, it should be transferred to <s>Indra</s>'s bow, the understanding being 'bearing nail-marks resembling a rainbow' -- just as in 'he offers with curds,' the injunction is transferred to the curds. Thus this is indeed <s>samāsokti</s> animated by simile. Here, however, in 'iha punaḥ,' the cognition of the beauty of the lake as <s>nāyikā</s> is not through <s>samāsokti</s>, due to the absence of <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s>. Therefore, the <s>nāyikā</s> is perceived here as the object of comparison, and it is not that the beauty of the lake is perceived as <s>nāyikā</s> through having the properties [of a nāyikā] -- thus <s>ekadeśavivartyupamā</s> alone must be accepted, there being no other alternative. Those by whom this was not stated should also add it. But where, in cases like 'by the multitude of hair-like bees,' <s>viśeṣaṇasāmya</s> can be established through another compound in the <s>samāsokti</s>-based simile, there it is indeed <s>samāsokti</s> effected by comparison-containing qualification -- hence there is no contradiction whatsoever.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/7:]

children.text:
avipratipattidyotanārthastāvacchrabdaḥ /
kutastyeti /
kimasyā nimittamitibhāvaḥ /
tadānuguṇyāditi /
śarado nāyikātvapratītyanuguṇatvāt /
tayoriti raviśaśinoḥ /
kathamiti /
aprakṛtārthānanuguṇatvāt sāmyāyogāt /
kathamatra vyavastheti /
viśeṣaṇasāmyāyogāt samāsokteraprātperekadeśavivartinyā upamāyā anuktatvāt /
sāmānyalakṣaṇeti /
upamānopameyayoḥ sādharmye bhedābhedatulyatve upameti /
evamekadeśavivartyupamāsāmarythādevātra nāyakakatvapratītiriti bhāvaḥ /
atheti pakṣāntare /
yadi cātra pūrvoktayuktyaivānuguṇyād raviśaśinoḥ samāsoktimukhena nāyakatvapratītistadārdranakhakṣatābhamiti viśeṣaṇaṃ kathaṃ sāmyena yojayituṃ śakyamityāśaṅkyāha-tadatretyādi /
etadeva śāstrāntaraprasiddhadṛṣṭāntamukhena hṛdayaṅgamīkaroti-yathetyādinā /
agnihotraṃ juhuyādityanenotpattividhivākyena hi homo vihitaḥ /
tasya ca punarvidhānamadagdhadahananyāyena yāvadaprātpaṃ tāvad vidherviṣaya ityabhyupagamātra yujyata iti tatrāpyuktatvādupapade dadhni saṃcāryata ityarthaḥ /
upamānuprāṇiteti /
aupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇotthāpitetyarthaḥ /
samāsoktireveti /
na punarekadeśavivartinyupamā /
gatyantaramalaṅkārāntaram /
yairityudbhaṭādibhiḥ /
yatratvityādergranthasya pūrvamevāsmābhirabhiprāya uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'tāvat' is for the purpose of indicating certainty. 'How does it arise?' means: what is the cause of this? 'In conformity with that' means: because of the conformity with the cognition of autumn as <s>nāyikā</s>. 'Of those two' means of the sun and moon. 'How' means: because of the non-conformity with the non-primary meaning, there is no possibility of similarity. 'How is the matter to be settled here?' means: because of the impossibility of similarity of qualification, <s>samāsokti</s> is not obtained, and the <s>ekadeśavivartyupamā</s> (partially-transforming simile) has not been stated [by earlier authorities]. 'General definition' means: when the properties of the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (thing compared) are similar, with equality of difference and non-difference, it is <s>upamā</s>. Thus, through the power of <s>ekadeśavivartyupamā</s> alone, the cognition of <s>nāyaka</s>-status arises here -- this is the purport. 'Now' introduces an alternative position. If the cognition of <s>nāyaka</s>-status of the sun and moon arises through <s>samāsokti</s> by the aforementioned reasoning of conformity, then how can the qualification 'having the appearance of fresh nail-marks' be established through similarity? -- anticipating this objection, he says 'tadatra' etc. He makes this very point penetrate the heart through an example well-known in another <s>śāstra</s>, beginning with 'yathā' etc. For by the injunctive sentence 'one should offer the <s>agnihotra</s>,' the oblation is enjoined. And according to the principle of 'un-burnt burning' [i.e., the injunction applies as far as needed], since it is accepted that the injunction applies wherever it has not yet been obtained, it is appropriate there too -- and since it has been stated [that the injunction applies] in that context also, [the injunction] is transferred to the curds -- this is the meaning. 'Animated by simile' means: produced by comparison-containing qualification. '<s>Samāsokti</s> alone' means: and not <s>ekadeśavivartyupamā</s>. 'Other alternative' means another figure of speech. 'By those' means by <s>Udbhaṭa</s> and others. The purport of the passage beginning 'yatra tu' has already been stated by us earlier.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/8:]

children.text: sā ca samāroktirarthāntaranyāse kacitsamarthyagatatvena kacitsamarthakagatatvena ca bhavati /

children.translated_text: In order, for example:
"When autumn embraced the moon, the rainy season departed with the glances of its lightning stilled.
Of which women, having lost their swelling breasts, does the quality of beauty not perish?"
And that <s>samāsokti</s> occurs in <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration), sometimes through the power of the thing corroborated and sometimes through the power of the corroborating element.
"What concern with women has a heroic man who desires to conquer from an unequal foe?

children.text: anākramya jagat sarve no saṃdhyāṃ bhajate raviḥ' //
children.translated_text: Without first conquering the entire world, the sun does not resort to <s>saṃdhyā</s> (twilight/union)."

children.text:
atropagūḍhatvena śāntataḍitkaṭākṣatvena ca śaśāṅkaśaradornāyakavyavahārapratītau samāsoktyāliṅgita evārtho viśeṣarūpaḥ sāmānyāśrayeṇārthāntaranyāsena samarthyate /
sāmānyasya cātra śleṣavaśādutthānam /

children.translated_text: 'With stilled lightning-glances' is a comparison-containing qualification; the common qualification through another compound is present here.

children.text: asamātpetyādau tu strīśabdasya sāmānyena strītvamātrābhidhānāt sāmānyarūpo 'rtho liṅgaviśeṣanirdeśagarbheṇa kāryāpanibandhanenotthāpitayā samāsoktyā samāropitanāyakavyavahāreṇa ravisaṃdhyāvṛttāntena viśeṣarūpeṇa samarthyate /
children.translated_text: But in 'from an unequal foe' etc., since the word 'strī' (woman) denotes merely womanhood in general, the meaning, which is of the nature of a generality, is corroborated by a particular in the form of the episode of the sun and <s>saṃdhyā</s>, in which <s>nāyaka</s> convention is superimposed through <s>samāsokti</s> produced by the indication of gender-distinction inherent in the binding of the effect.
"With the snake-king's sloughed skin falling due to the force of attraction, appearing as a surrounding halo of the ocean,
As if to relieve the pain of churning, the <s>Mandākinī</s> (Ganges) swiftly coiled around his feet."

Here, when the conventional usage of the moon and autumn as <s>nāyaka</s> (hero) is perceived through their being embraced and through having stilled lightning-glances, the meaning, which is of the nature of a particular, being enveloped by <s>samāsokti</s>, is corroborated through <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> depending on a generality. And the generality here arises through the force of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning).

children.text:
atra nirmokapaṭṭāpahnavena samāropitāyā mandākinyā yadvastuvṛttena pādamūle veṣṭanaṃ taccaraṇamūle veṣṭanatvena śleṣamūlayātiśayoktyādhyavasīyate /
tat tathādhyavasitaṃ manthavyathāvyupaśamārthamivetyutprekṣāmutthāpayati /
sotthāpyamānaivāmburāśimandākinyoḥ patipatnīvyavahārāśrayāṃ samāsoktiṃ garbhīkaroti /
evaṃ cotprekṣāsamāsoktyorekaḥ kālaḥ /
evaṃ 'nakhakṣatānīva vanasthalīnām' ityatrāpi vanasthalīnāṃ nāyikāvyavahāra utprekṣāntarānupraviṣṭasamāsoktimūla eva /
evamiyaṃ samāsoktiranantaprapañcetyanayā diśā svayamutprekṣyā /
children.translated_text: Here, through the concealment of the sloughed snake-skin by <s>apahṇuti</s> (denial), the <s>Mandākinī</s>, upon whom [the identity] is superimposed, -- her coiling at the feet according to actual events is determined as coiling at the feet [of a husband] through <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) based on <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning). That, so determined, gives rise to the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) 'as if to relieve the pain of churning.' And that <s>utprekṣā</s>, being generated, incorporates within itself the <s>samāsokti</s> based on the husband-wife convention of the ocean and <s>Mandākinī</s>. Thus, <s>utprekṣā</s> and <s>samāsokti</s> are simultaneous. Similarly, in 'like nail-marks of the forest-lands,' the convention of <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) for the forest-lands is rooted in <s>samāsokti</s> that has entered into another <s>utprekṣā</s>. Thus, this <s>samāsokti</s> is of infinite elaboration -- in this direction, one should imagine for oneself.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 32/8:]

children.text:
setyuktaprapañcā /
sāmānyasyetyaṅganāśabdasya strītvamātrābhidhānāt /
śleṣadavaśāditi, payodharāṇāṃ hi śliṣṭatvam /
liṅgaviśeṣeti,ravisaṃdhyayoḥ puṃstrīrūpeṇa kāryaṃ bhajanākhyam /
evamanyālaṅkārasaṃmiśratvamapyasyā darśiyati-ākṛṣṭītyādinā /
setyutprekṣā /
ekaḥ kāla iti /
jñatpau samāsoktigabhīṅkāreṇaivrotprekṣāyā utthānāt /
evamiti /
yathoktagatyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That' refers to the one whose elaboration has been stated. 'Of the generality' means: because the word '<s>aṅganā</s>' (woman) denotes merely womanhood. 'Through the force of <s>śleṣa</s>' means: because '<s>payodhara</s>' has ambiguity [meaning both 'breast' and 'cloud']. 'Gender-distinction' means: the activity called 'resorting to' [applies to] the sun and <s>saṃdhyā</s> in their male and female forms. He also shows the mixture of this [<s>samāsokti</s>] with other figures, beginning with 'ākṛṣṭi' etc. 'That' refers to the <s>utprekṣā</s>. 'Simultaneous' means: because the <s>utprekṣā</s> arises only through the incorporation of <s>samāsokti</s> at that very moment. 'Thus' means: in the manner stated.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 33:
<s>Parikara</s> (attendant expression) is the intentional purposefulness of qualifications. [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 33]
Therefore, because of having clear yet profound words, this is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion).

children.text: evaṃ ca pratīyamānāṃśasya vācyonmukhatvātparikara iti sārthakaṃ nāma /
children.translated_text: And thus, since the suggested aspect is on the verge of becoming expressed, the name '<s>parikara</s>' (attendant) is meaningful.

children.text: 'rājño mānadhanasya kārmukabhṛto duryodhanasyāgrataḥ pratyakṣaṃ kurubāndhavasya miṣataḥ karṇasya śalyasya ca /
children.translated_text: "Before king <s>Duryodhana</s>, a treasury of pride, a bearer of the bow, in the direct presence of the kinsman of the <s>Kurus</s>, while <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Śalya</s> looked on,

children.text: pītaṃ tasya mayādya pāṇḍavavadhūkeśāmbarākarṣiṇaḥ koṣṇaṃ jīvata eva tīkṣṇakarajakṣuṇṇādasṛgvakṣasaḥ' //
children.translated_text: I have today drunk the warm blood from the chest -- crushed by sharp nails -- of that one who dragged the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> wife by her hair and garments, while he was still alive."
Since the variety of qualifications has been the topic, this [figure] is taught here. The intentional purposefulness of qualifications means the incorporation of a suggested meaning.

children.text:
atra rājña ityādau sotprāsatvaparaṃ prasannagambhīrapadatvam /
evam-
'aṅgāja senāpate rājavallabha droṇopahāsin karṇaṃ, sāṃprataṃ rakṣainaṃ bhīmād duḥśāsanam' ityādau jñeyam /
children.translated_text: Here, in 'of the king' etc., the clear yet profound quality of the words is directed toward mockery. Similarly, in '<s>Aṅgaja</s>! O commander of the army! O favorite of the king! O one who mocks <s>Droṇa</s>! Protect him, <s>Karṇa</s>! Now save this <s>Duḥśāsana</s> from <s>Bhīma</s>!' -- and similar cases, the same should be understood.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 33:]

children.text:
viśeṣaṇetyādi /
iheti samāsoktyānantaram /
viśeṣaṇānāṃ cātra bahutvameva vivakṣitam /
anyathā hyapuṣṭārthasya doṣatvābhidhānāt tannirākaraṇena svīkṛtasya puṣṭārthasyāyaṃ viṣayaḥ syāt /
evamevaṃvidhānekaviśeṣaṇopanyāsadvāreṇa vaicitryātiśayaḥ saṃbhavatītyālaṅkāratvam /
pratīyamānārthasya vācyonmukhatvena prādhānyābhāvādgabhīṅkārastadantaḥ kṛtatvam /
ata eveti pratīyamānārthasya prādhānyābhāvāt /
prasaccatvaṃ vācyasyaiva prādhānyena nirdeśāt /
gambhīratvaṃ pratīyamānasyāpyarthasya guṇībhāvena garbhīkārāt /
yatra ca pratīyamānaṃ prati upasarjanīkṛtasvarthayoḥ śabdārthayoravasthānāṃ sa dhvaneḥ sa eva viṣayaḥ ' iti /
atra ca na tathātvamityuktaṃ nāyaṃ dhvanerviṣaya iti /
ata eva nāmāpyasya yaugikamityāha-evaṃ cetyādi /
sotprāsatvaparamiti /
tathā ca rājño jagad rakṣitavyamasya punaranujamātrarakṣaṇāsiddheranyadeva nāmamātreṇa rājātvamityupahāsaparatvam /
evamanyeṣāmapisvayamevaitadavagantavyam /

children.translated_text: By the word 'ādi' (etc.):

children.text: 'yasyaikasyaiva doṣṇāṃ jayati daśaśatī sānvayo dvāri rudraḥ kārāgāre surāṇāṃ patarapi ca śacī cāmaravyagrahastā /
children.translated_text: "He whose ten hundred arms alone are victorious, at whose door <s>Rudra</s> stands with his lineage, in whose prison <s>Śacī</s> herself stands holding a fly-whisk, servant to the gods,

children.text: kanyā tasyeyamekā rajanicarapatereṣa śuddhāntameko bālo niḥśaṅkamasyāḥ praviśati ca namaste 'se vaiṣṇavāya' //
children.translated_text: This is his one daughter, the <s>Rākṣasa</s> king's; this is his sole inner chamber -- the boy enters it fearlessly; salutations to you, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (follower of <s>Viṣṇu</s>)!"

'Qualifications' etc. 'Here' means after <s>samāsokti</s>. And what is intended here is specifically the multiplicity of qualifications. For otherwise, since the insufficiency of a single qualifier's meaning would be stated as a defect, and since <s>puṣṭārtha</s> (enriched meaning), accepted through the rejection of that [defect], would be the domain of this [figure], [multiplicity is essential]. Thus, through the presentation of many such qualifications, an excess of variety becomes possible -- hence it constitutes a figure of speech. The suggested meaning, not having primacy due to being on the verge of the expressed, is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion), made subsidiary within it. 'Therefore' means: because of the lack of primacy of the suggested meaning. 'Clarity' is because the expressed meaning alone is presented with primacy. 'Profundity' is because the suggested meaning too is incorporated in a subordinate role. And 'where the word-meanings stand as subordinated to the suggested meaning, that is the domain of <s>dhvani</s>.' But here that is not the case -- hence it is said 'this is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s>.' Therefore, even the name of this [figure] is etymologically significant -- thus he says 'evaṃ ca' etc. 'Directed toward mockery' means: thus, 'of the king' -- his duty is to protect the world, yet he cannot even protect his own younger brother; therefore his kingship is merely nominal -- this is the mocking intent. Similarly, one should understand the others by oneself.
In such cases too, the clear-yet-profound quality of the qualifications should be understood.
START <s>Sūtra</s> 34:
When there is similarity of the qualified [thing] too, and both are presented, it is <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning). [<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 34]

children.text:
kevalaviśeṣasāmyaṃ samāsoktāvuktan /
viśeṣyayuktaviśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ tvadhikṛtyedamucyate /
tatra dvayoḥ prākaraṇikayoraprākaraṇikayoḥ prākaraṇikāprakaraṇikayor vā śliṣṭapadopanibandhe śleṣaḥ /
tatrādyaṃ prakāradvayaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasāmya eva tṛtīyastu prakāro viśeṣaṇasāmya eva bhavati /
viśeṣyasāmye tvarthaprakaraṇādinā vācyārthaniyame 'rthāntaragatadhvanerviṣayaḥ syāt /
ādye tu prakāradvaye dvayorapyarthayorvācyatvam /
ata evātra - 'dvayorvopādāne' iti tṛtīyaprakāraviṣayatvenoktam /
'viśeṣyasyāpi sāmye' iti tu śiṣṭaprakāradvayaviṣayam /
children.translated_text: Similarity of qualification alone was stated in <s>samāsokti</s>. But this [<s>śleṣa</s>] is stated with reference to similarity of qualification conjoined with the qualified. Here, when both contextual [subjects], or both non-contextual, or one contextual and one non-contextual, are bound together through ambiguous words, it is <s>śleṣa</s>. Of these, the first two types involve similarity of both qualification and qualified, while the third type involves similarity of qualification alone. In the case of similarity of the qualified alone, when the expressed meaning is restricted by context of meaning etc., it would be the domain of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) pertaining to another meaning. In the first two types, however, both meanings are expressed. Therefore, the phrase 'when both are presented' is stated with reference to the third type. And 'when there is similarity of the qualified too' pertains to the remaining two types.
[Commentary on <s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 34:]

children.text:
viśeṣyasyāpītyādi /
idamiti śleṣalakṣaṇam /
ādyamiti /
prākaraṇikagatatvenāprākaraṇikagatatvena ca /
evakāraścātra bhinnakramo draṣṭavyaḥ /
tena prakāradvayameveti vyākhyeyam /
ataśca tṛtīyaḥ prakāro viśeṣaṇasāmya eva bhavatīti vyāvacchredaphalam /
anyathā hi prakāradvayasyāsya viśeṣyasāmyābhāve 'pi darśanādavyātpiḥ syāt /

children.translated_text: For example: 'the interiors purified by passage' etc.
Here, there is absence of similarity of the qualified for the two contextual subjects, <s>prabhā</s> (radiance) and <s>dhenu</s> (cow).
"With splendor reaching the edges of the circle from their arms, with armored chests, hot-breathed, wounded, uprooting the hearts of enemies, rough,

children.text: utsṛtṣṭāmbaradṛṣṭavigrahabharā yasya smarāgresarā yodhā daivavadhūstanāśca na dadhuḥ kṣobhaṃ sa vo 'vyājjinaḥ' //
children.translated_text: With garments cast aside revealing their massive forms, his warriors, forerunners of <s>Smara</s> (Love), and the celestial women's breasts did not give him agitation -- may that guileless conqueror protect you!"

'Of the qualified too' etc. 'This' means the definition of <s>śleṣa</s>. 'The first' means: through belonging to the contextual and through belonging to the non-contextual. And the word 'eva' (alone) here should be understood in a reversed order. Thus, it should be explained as 'only these two types.' Consequently, 'the third type involves similarity of qualification alone' states the result of exclusion. For otherwise, since these two types are seen even in the absence of similarity of the qualified, there would be no definitive scope.

children.text:
atra stanayodhayoraprakṛtayorviśeṣyayoḥ sāmyābhāvaḥ /
viśeṣaṇasāmya eveti na punarviśeṣyasāmye /
etadapi viśeṣyasāmye kiṃ na bhavatītyāśaṅkyāha-viśeṣyasāmye tvityādi /

children.translated_text: For example:
"Of the <s>Laṅkā</s>-dwellers, O son, who have gained free range in the month of spring,
People fear the <s>palāśas</s> (Butea trees / demons), which are yellow and red."

Here, there is absence of similarity of the qualified for the two non-contextual subjects, breasts and warriors. 'In similarity of qualification alone' means: and not in similarity of the qualified. Anticipating the objection 'why does this not also occur in similarity of the qualified?', he says 'but in similarity of the qualified' etc.
[Sanskrit reconstruction:] "Of the <s>Laṅkā</s>-dwellers, O son, who have gained free range in the spring month,
People fear the <s>palāśas</s>, which are yellow and red."

children.text:
atra palāśānāmiti viśeṣyasyāpi śliṣṭatvam /
prakaraṇavaśācca vṛkṣaviśeṣaṇamevavācyatvaniyamātprastutatvena niśācarāṇāmaprastutānāṃ vyaṅgyatvam /
atra copamāyā eva vyaṅgyatvaṃ yuktaṃ nātiśayokteriti prakṛtānupayogādiha noktam /
nanu ca yathaivāyaṃ dhvanirviṣayastathaivādyamapi bhedadvayaṃ kiṃ na bhavatītyāśaṅkyāha-ādya ityādi /
vācyatvamiti,ata eva na dhvanerviṣayaḥ /
tasya vācyātiriktanvarūpatvāt /
tṛtīyaprakāraviṣayatveneti prādhānyāduktam /
ādyasyāpi prakāradvayasya dvayorupādānasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Here, the qualified '<s>palāśa</s>' itself is ambiguous. And due to the force of context, only the tree-meaning is restricted as expressed, while the <s>Rākṣasa</s> meaning, being non-contextual, is suggested. And here, it is appropriate that only simile is suggested, not hyperbole -- hence this is not stated here as irrelevant to the topic. Now, anticipating the objection 'just as this is the domain of <s>dhvani</s>, why are the first two types not also [domains of dhvani]?', he says 'the first' etc. 'Are expressed' -- therefore it is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s>, since <s>dhvani</s> by nature goes beyond the expressed. 'With reference to the third type' is stated with emphasis. Since in the first two types also, both [meanings] being presented is possible.
[<s>Ruyyaka</s>'s <s>Alaṃkārasarvasva</s> 34/1:]
In order, for example:

children.text: 'yena dhvastamanobhavena balijitkāyaḥ purāstrīkṛto yaścodvṛttabhujaṅgahāravalayo gaṅgā ca yo 'dhārayat /
children.translated_text: "He by whom, having destroyed <s>Manobhava</s> (Kāma), the body of <s>Balijit</s> (Indra) was formerly made into a woman; who bore <s>Gaṅgā</s> while wearing <s>Bhujaṅga</s> (serpent) necklaces with raised hoods;

children.text: yasyāhuḥ śaśimacchirohara iti stutyaṃ ca nāmāmarāḥ pāyātsa svayamandhakakṣayakarastvāṃ sarvadomādhavaḥ' //
children.translated_text: Whose praiseworthy name the gods call '<s>Śaśimacchirohara</s>' (bearer of the moon on his head / slayer of enemies) -- may that <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s> / <s>Śiva</s>), the destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s>, himself protect you, the conqueror of all!"
"Of those brought to confusion by greedy hunters with many arrows,
The sight of the lotuses of those forest-elders is comparable."

children.text: 'svecchopajātaviṣayo 'pi na yāti vaktuṃ dehīti mārgaṇaśataiśca dadāti duḥkham /
children.translated_text: "Although his desire arises spontaneously, he does not ask 'give!', yet through hundreds of entreaties he gives suffering.
Out of delusion he snatches away life itself untimely -- alas, cruel like <s>Manobhava</s> (Kāma), the ill-skilled lord!"

children.text:
atra hariharayorddhayorapi prākaraṇikatvam /
padmānāṃ mṛgāṇāṃ copamānatvādaprākaraṇikatvarm /
iśvaramanobhavayoḥ prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikatvam /
evaṃ ca śabdārthobhayagatatvena vartamānatvāttrividhaḥ /
tatrodāttādisvarabhedātprayantabhedācca śabdānyatve śabdaśleṣaḥ /
yatra prāyeṇa padabhaṅgo bhavati /
arthaśleṣastu yatra svarādibhedo nāsti /
ata eva na tatra sabhaṅgapadatvam /
saṃkalanayā tūbhayaśleṣaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:
"Displaying red leaves, being fully bloomed, not being sufficiently connected with water,

children.text: nirasya puṣpeṣu ruciṃ samagrāṃ padmā virejuḥ śramaṇā yathaiva' //
children.translated_text: Having cast away all charm among flowers, the <s>padmas</s> (lotuses / ascetics named Padma) shone forth just like <s>śramaṇas</s> (wandering monks)."

Here, <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) and <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) are both contextual. Lotuses and deer are non-contextual because they are objects of comparison. <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) and <s>Manobhava</s> (Kāma) represent one contextual and one non-contextual. Thus, since it occurs in word, meaning, and both combined, it is threefold. Among these, <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal double meaning) arises from differences in accent such as <s>udātta</s> etc. and from differences in articulation, where generally word-splitting occurs. <s>Arthaśleṣa</s> (meaning-based double meaning), however, is where there is no difference of accent etc., and therefore no word-splitting occurs there. And through combination, there is <s>ubhayaśleṣa</s> (both types combined).

children.text:
atra raktacchadatvamityādāvarthaśleṣaḥ /
nālamityādau śabdaśleṣaḥ /
ubhayaghaṭanāyāmubhayaśleṣaḥ /
granthagauravabhayāttu pṛthaṅnodāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: Here, in 'displaying red leaves' etc., there is <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (meaning-based double meaning). In 'nālam' (not sufficiently / by the stalk) etc., there is <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal double meaning). When both are combined, there is <s>ubhayaśleṣa</s> (both types of double meaning). However, due to fear of making the text too lengthy, they have not been illustrated separately.
